paragraphs: A composition about a current. The arc rises at one end, sags in the middle and lifts again; the petals are turned along that line, in layers. Density grows toward the centre and falls toward the ends, where single elements break away and hang alone — a flock moving as one.
The surface is smooth, without texture of any kind: only form and finish are at work. White gloss and polished gold — two ways of meeting light, and nothing more.

By day it is the pure contrast of two surfaces: opaque gloss beside mirrored gold, read through silhouette and highlight. In the evening the gold petals reflect the light and flare into radiant stars, while the white ones diffuse it and stay soft patches. A current in which every second element burns.
LC0001.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, lobbies, meeting rooms, reception areas. The curve of the arc is calculated for the length of the zone.
LC0001.style: Contemporary Art Deco and minimalism: two finishes, not one superfluous element. The message is representative — a piece for an interior that rests on proportion.
LC0001.madeToOrder: The length, the arc pattern, the number of petals and the ratio of white to gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about three behaviours of one beam. White gloss, polished gold and clear are mixed without system, so at any point in the composition all three fall side by side. That is exactly what keeps the mass uneven: it never looks flat.
The bowl is deep, the mass dense below and thinned above, where single petals break away and hang alone among the hatching of threads with small point lights.

By day it is an armful of petals suspended below the ceiling: white, gold and clear intermixed, read through the plasticity of the crumpled edge. In the evening the white petals diffuse the light and glow evenly, the gold ones reflect and flare hot, the clear ones transmit it and throw icy sparks. A cloud in which light behaves differently at every point.
LC0002.whereItWorks: Formal spaces — lobbies, double-height living rooms, banquet and wedding halls, atria. The deep bowl needs height: pressed to the ceiling it loses its volume.
LC0002.style: Contemporary Art Deco and Hollywood glamour: three finishes instead of ornament. The message is festive — a piece for an interior that loves shine.
LC0002.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of petals, the ratio of the three finishes and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a planet with a core. At the centre of each disc sits a gold hemisphere — at once heart and source: the light spreads from it toward the rim, losing strength exactly as it does around a star with a centre and a fading corona.

The discs are set at varied angles: some almost flat, some on edge, some obliquely. The bowl is shallow, the discs overlap here and there, and through the front layer you can see the second and the third.

By day it is a scatter of soap bubbles — clear circles with a bluish, iridescent cast, read through highlights. In the evening a fine glowing line flares at the rim of each disc, and because the layers overlap, each one lights its neighbour: the composition reads as a volume filled with light, not as a set of lamps. A cluster of planets with burning cores.
LC0003.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms, zones above a round table. The layering reads from below: the piece is hung above the area where people stand or sit.
LC0003.style: Cosmic minimalism and mid-century: the circle and the point as the entire vocabulary. The message is contemporary and clear — a piece for an interior of pure geometry.
LC0003.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of discs, the calibres and the finish of the cores are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the drop. The form is perfectly smooth, with a clean transition from the narrow neck to the heavy base — the shape water takes in free fall, when nothing touches it. Here it is held and repeated in the hundreds.
The mass hangs from a round mirrored base and descends in a dense array, tiered, level at the top and deeply sagging at the centre: a cone pointing downward.

By day it is a cluster of honey drops — a mirrored surface with a warm golden-honey tint, heavy and rich. In the evening the light enters at the neck, travels the full body and gathers in the broad lower section, so each drop fills from within to deep amber; the mirrored surface reflects its neighbours and a constant exchange of highlights runs inside the composition. Rain frozen mid-fall.
LC0004.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, dining rooms, stairwells, lobbies, banquet halls. The sagging centre sets the minimum height above a table.
LC0004.style: Grand classicism in contemporary execution: a cascade without a single faceted drop. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a space that receives guests.
LC0004.madeToOrder: The base diameter, the number of drops, the suspension lengths and the depth of the honey tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about plumage. The plates within each row are inclined identically, while the rows themselves rise, fall, twist and straighten again — together they give the effect of a feather or a crest laid down by the wind. The form changes completely with the viewpoint: the piece has no principal face.
There are hundreds of plates, each fixed at its own angle. Uniformity within the row and freedom between rows — the whole plasticity rests on that.

By day it is a surface built from scales: white ribbing read through light and shadow, calm and dense. In the evening the light grazes the plates at a sharp angle and brings out the ribbing — some rows light up entirely, others stay in shadow, and a wave of light and shade runs the whole length. There are no hard points: only grazing light. A wing across which light runs.
LC0005.whereItWorks: Large spaces — atria, lobbies, conference halls, retail galleries, double-height living rooms. Grazing light means the piece gives little general illumination and works as an architectural element.
LC0005.style: Parametric design and contemporary architecture: the array rather than the object. The message is monumental — a surface-piece, not a luminaire.
LC0005.madeToOrder: The overall size, the wave pattern, the number of plates and the surface finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about opposing movement. Below, large clear leaves hang low and flat, forming the main mass; above, small gold ones break away alone and rise high toward the ceiling. The heavy falls, the light ascends — read from below upward, the piece is movement, not arrangement.
The cables vanish into darkness, so the leaves appear to hang unsupported.

By day it is a leaf-fall caught halfway: a dense clear lower body veined with fine lines, and sparse gold points above. In the evening the light passes through several lower layers and reveals the whole venation in silhouette, while the gold leaves above reflect it and throw rare warm flares into the void. Most of the upper zone stays dark — a crown lit only in its lower tiers.
LC0006.whereItWorks: Generous rooms with high ceilings — atria, lobbies, stairwells, double-height living rooms. The upward scatter needs height: without it the opposing movement does not read.
LC0006.style: Organic modernism and contemporary installation: autumn as movement rather than colour. The message is poetic — a piece that tells a story.
LC0006.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of leaves, the ratio of calibres and the share of gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about venation. A fine net of veins is pressed into the surface of every leaf — what in a real leaf is a supply system, not a drawing. The author uses that literally: in the evening it is precisely along the veins that the light runs.
The composition is drawn out on the diagonal: the leaves are turned at random, overlapping in places, elsewhere breaking away alone far from the group. The upper edge is ragged.

By day it is an armful of leaves caught in flight: clear mixed with amber, the composition read right through, with real depth. In the evening the clear ones pass the light and flare along the net of veins, while the amber ones fill with copper from within. A crown whose venation is alight.
LC0007.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, double-height living rooms, winter gardens. Transparency gives depth when seen from the side: the piece is not hung tight to the ceiling.
LC0007.style: Art Nouveau and botanical modernism: the leaf as a classic motif. The message is natural and warm — a piece for an interior with greenery.
LC0007.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of leaves, the share of amber and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a thicket in bud. Inside — a dense stand of fine clear rods, a bristling hatch; outward and downward run curved stems, each ending in a large matte drop. Hard within, soft without: the structure of almost any plant.
The stems carry the drops well beyond the main volume, and a fringe forms around the edges. Inside the stand the drops hang closer and lower.

By day it is a thicket in bloom: clear hatching and white spheres on curved arcs, read through silhouette. In the evening the light lives in two places — the rods carry it along their length and flare at the ends as points, while the drops glow from within in an even milky tone, without flare. A bristling hatch inside and soft glowing spheres around the edge: a swarm of fireflies around a clear column.
LC0008.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, atria. The fringe extends beyond the main envelope: allow clearance to the sides.
LC0008.style: Art Nouveau and organic modernism: a plant with a different character inside and out. The message is alive — a piece for an interior that loves natural forms.
LC0008.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of stems, the calibre of the drops and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an organ. The tubes in each cluster are cut to different heights, so the upper contour is stepped — the same logic as organ pipes, where length determines pitch. Here length determines the depth at which the glowing point hangs.
The clusters hang at varied levels and almost touch — together they read both as an organ and as a stalagmite forest. The material is clear and colourless, with occasional bubbles inside.

By day it is a transparent forest — clear verticals read through highlights, the composition visible right through. In the evening the light enters from above and travels down each cylinder like a lightguide: the cylinder itself stays almost invisible, while the lower cut flares into a bright point. Hundreds of glowing circles hang at varied depths — rain stopped mid-fall.
LC0009.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, stairwells, double-height living rooms, banquet halls. The multi-level arrangement reads from below and from the side: it needs volume.
LC0009.style: Contemporary minimalism and architectural classicism: the vertical as the only motif. The message is austere and ceremonial — a piece for a formal space.
LC0009.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of clusters, the tube lengths and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a sheaf. The ribbons stand almost upright, layered and overlapping, ragged at the top and tapering below — this is how a sheaf is tied: caught at the base and left to open above.
Each ribbon is bent and twisted in its own way, with sharp cut ends. The ribbing is hidden on the reverse; outside there is only clean gloss — the piece shows its face and hides its lining.

By day it is a sheaf of paper ribbons: white gloss read through light, shadow and overlap, light and graphic. In the evening the light escapes through the narrow gaps and lights the ribbed undersides — a white glow stands inside the composition while the outside stays glossy, and at the cut ends the light flares into bright points. A reed bed lit from within.
LC0010.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, atria. The vertical sheaf needs height rather than floor area.
LC0010.style: Scandinavian minimalism and organic modernism: the sheaf as a form without decoration. The message is clean and bright — a piece for a white palette.
LC0010.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of ribbons, their lengths and the surface finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a cross-section. Concentric arcs around an off-centre point draw close, then open to reveal the ground — a tree ring, a fingerprint, ripples on water. The ambiguity is deliberate: what all three share is that the pattern cannot be repeated; it is always unique.

The form is broken open: the composition occupies not a full circle but a crescent with one side cut away. Because of that it never reads as a closed target — it reads as a fragment of something larger.

By day the panel works as metalwork graphics: polished bronze with gold and copper shifts, a mirrored surface in which each band reflects its neighbour, so an endless exchange of highlights builds up in the depth. In the evening the backlight emerges from behind the plates and grazes them at a sharp angle, bringing out the whole relief: a cross-section lit from within.
LC0011.whereItWorks: Feature walls — halls, stair landings, private living rooms, reception areas, gallery spaces. The open form suits a long wall: the cut side runs out beyond the field of view.
LC0011.style: Art Deco and contemporary sculpture: the concentric pattern as a classic motif. The message is expressive — a picture-object for a wall that needs nothing else.
LC0011.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of bands, the ring spacing and the metal finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a wingbeat. Two broad wings open upward and outward; between them the mass thickens and trails downward, where the rods thin to singles. All of them run along the movement — one beat, caught in a frame.
The rods hang almost horizontally, layered and overlapping. The large irregular faceting gives each its own pattern of refraction; colourless ice mixes with warm gold.

By day it is an icy flock — a clear mass with gold inclusions, read through the shape of the wing. In the evening the faceting breaks the light and scatters it along each rod, so the layers glow in strokes: the gold sections fill with warmth, the icy ones flash white. At the fold of the wing, where the rods are densest, the glow is at its strongest — a wing assembled out of light.
LC0012.whereItWorks: Generous rooms with high ceilings — atria, lobbies, stairwells, double-height living rooms. The wingspan needs width: the piece is designed for the specific volume.
LC0012.style: Contemporary sculptural installation and grand classicism. The message is monumental — a piece that sets the scale of a room.
LC0012.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of rods, the share of gold and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about wind. The mass runs from the upper left corner down to the right, thinning as it goes; the last feathers hang alone, far from the group. All of them are turned along that movement — you read a current, not an arrangement.
The feather is narrow, with a wavy edge and close longitudinal scoring. Warm amber-honey mixes with clear silver; a few feathers carry a red accent at the tip.

By day these are feathers caught in a current: a diagonal band read through colour and inclination. In the evening the light enters at the quill and spreads along the scoring — each feather glows in strokes, the amber ones fill with copper, the clear ones throw white sparks, the red tips flare as points. A flock crossing the room on the diagonal.
LC0013.whereItWorks: Generous rooms and irregular geometry — stairwells, atria, curved halls, double-height living rooms. The diagonal is designed for the specific volume.
LC0013.style: Art Nouveau and natural romanticism: the feather as a classic motif of lightness. The message is poetic — a piece that fills a room with movement.
LC0013.madeToOrder: The length and pitch of the current, the number of feathers, the palette and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a pond in the rain. The discs hang almost flat — leaves on water; the threads run to the ceiling in dense hatching — the downpour above them. Two images laid over one another: a rainstorm with leaves suspended inside it.
The pyramid is wide at the top and narrows below, where single discs drop far down on their own. Small faceted beads are scattered between them.

By day it is a pool with floating leaves: deep blue-violet mixed with colourless, read through colour and ribbing. In the evening light enters each disc at the rim and runs out along the ribs, so every one glows radially from centre to edge — the blue ones fill with dense ultramarine, the colourless flash white, and the beads break the light into sparks. Night water lit from beneath.
LC0014.whereItWorks: Generous rooms with high ceilings — atria, lobbies, stairwells, pools and spas. The pyramidal build needs height.
LC0014.style: Art Nouveau and Japanese water aesthetics: the water lily as a classic motif. The message is contemplative and cool — a piece for interiors near water.
LC0014.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of discs, the proportion of blue and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a body that is barely there. The moon jellyfish shows only its ribs: everything else is transparent enough to read as emptiness. The author takes that literally — a flat, rounded dome with fine radial ribbing along the edge and a short tail.
Hundreds of domes hang mixed with tiny bubble-beads at varied heights and tilts; some trail down on long threads with sparse beads, like tentacles. What you read is not an object but a medium.

By day the composition is all but invisible: a cool bluish cast, a cloud of small clear things that is easy to overlook. In the evening the light enters the ribbing and traces every dome with a glowing net of ribs, while the bubbles flash as small points. The room becomes a body of water full of jellyfish.
LC0015.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, pools and spas, panoramic living rooms, meeting rooms. Transparency needs a dark backdrop: against a white ceiling the piece disappears by day.
LC0015.style: Marine modernism with a scientific edge: biological accuracy without stylisation. The message is contemplative — a piece you look into.
LC0015.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the density of the bubbles and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the outline. A fine gold band runs along the rim of every petal, tracing the form and flaring at each bend. The device comes from jewellery: this is how cloisonné enamel is bounded so the colour cannot run. Here it holds nothing — it only draws.

The mass is gathered into a lens shape: wide at the centre, tapering to sharp points at both ends. The petals are layered, each turned differently; the upper half is given over to the hatching of the suspension threads, the whole mass sits below.

By day it is an armful of petals caught on a gold thread: milky white with a hot contour, a graphic piece. In the evening the white diffuses the light and glows evenly, without a single flare, while the gold rims intercept it and trace every petal with a burning line. The source is never visible — the mass itself glows, drawn out by hundreds of gold outlines. A cloud with burning edges.
LC0016.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, banquet and wedding halls, lobbies, meeting rooms. The soft glare-free light is comfortable directly above a table.
LC0016.style: Art Deco and jewellery-inflected modernism: the outline as the only ornament. The message is festive and restrained at once — a piece for an interior that celebrates quietly.
LC0016.madeToOrder: The length, the number of petals, the width of the gold rim and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a wingbeat. The mass is gathered into a lens — broad at the centre, tapering to sharp points at both ends; the petals are turned along the axis, in layers. You read an open fan, or a wing at the top of its span: a form that exists for a single instant.
Each petal is narrow and pointed, twisted on its axis, each with a slightly different bend. Crimson-purple is mixed with polished gold.

By day it is an open fan: deep wine colour with a mirrored sheen beside gold, dense and ceremonial. In the evening the purple transmits the light and fills from within to wine, while the gold reflects it and flares hot — the glow comes out uneven, cool sitting next to burning, and the composition shimmers. A firebird's feather stretched above a table.
LC0017.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, reception rooms, restaurant floors. Saturated colour needs a calm setting.
LC0017.style: Art Deco and Eastern opulence: purple with gold as a classic pairing. The message is vivid and regal — a piece for an interior unafraid of colour.
LC0017.madeToOrder: The length, the number of petals, the depth of the purple tone and the share of gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an enfilade. The frames are nested one inside another like a matryoshka, and the light passes through several outlines in a row — a perspective opens that a flat composition could never hold. The eye travels inward, as through a run of open doors.
The array is stepped, level at the top and deeply sagging below; the silhouette recalls terraces. The frames stand vertically, layered and overlapping.

By day it is a set of empty frames — mirrored gold mixed with clear ones read only at their edges. In the evening the gold reflects the light and fills from within, the clear frames transmit it and flare along their rims, and the nesting multiplies the glow. A system of luminous openings receding into depth — an enfilade with lit windows.
LC0018.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, lobbies, meeting rooms, reception rooms. The perspective reads from the side: the piece is designed for a view along its length.
LC0018.style: Art Deco and architectural minimalism: the opening as a decorative motif. The message is representative — a piece for a formal space.
LC0018.madeToOrder: The length, the number of frames, the calibres and the ratio of gold to clear are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a field seen from above. The mass is packed element to element without a single gap — this is how a flowering field looks from height, where individual plants merge into unbroken colour. Closed buds, half-open cups and small berry spheres are mixed together: flowering is shown in every phase at once.
White butterflies are set across the field — there are few of them, they are larger than the rest and they work as pale accents in the dark mass. Gold beads are scattered between the elements.

By day the panel reads as a botanical specimen under magnification: deep violet-blue with a glossy glaze, dense and saturated. In the evening the backlight emerges as points between the elements — the glaze reflects it, the beads flare, the butterflies glow softly, and the surface begins to shimmer without losing the density of its colour. A field at dusk full of fireflies.
LC0019.whereItWorks: Feature walls — halls, living rooms, bedrooms, private studies, reception areas. The dense dark mass needs a clear wall and directional ambient light.
LC0019.style: Botanical modernism and jewellery miniature: a field assembled by hand. The message is contemplative — a piece people come close to.
LC0019.madeToOrder: The panel diameter, the glaze palette, the number of butterflies and the frame finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about what draws them in. The light is hidden inside the tangle, the butterflies sit outside — the piece literally shows the reason they are here: a swarm come to the flame. Cause and effect are shown at once.

The rods are woven into a sphere with no order at all, crossing and jutting outward to form an open cage. The butterflies have settled unevenly: clustered in one place, leaving the cage bare in another.

By day it is a gold tangle covered with white figures — dense, sculptural, read through silhouette. In the evening the light escapes from within through every gap between the rods, lighting the butterflies from below and behind; the wings turn translucent and fill with milky white, and the rods flare into lines. From outside you see a sphere whose surface does not glow — its core does.
LC0020.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, wedding and banquet halls. The sphere reads from every side — it is hung in the volume, not against a wall.
LC0020.style: Art Nouveau and romantic classicism: the moth drawn to light as an eternal subject. The message is poetic — a piece with a story inside it.
LC0020.madeToOrder: The sphere diameter, the number of butterflies, the density of the cage and the metal finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about backlight. A real shoal seen from below looks exactly like this: some fish flare, others stay silhouettes, and it depends not on them but on the angle. The author reproduces the effect through finishes — scoring on the silver bodies breaks the light into a shimmer along the whole flank, while polished gold reflects it sharply.
Every figure faces the same way: what you read is the movement of a shoal, not a set of objects. Density is uneven — thicker at the centre, with strays at the edges.

By day it is a shoal below the ceiling: gold mixed with softly shimmering silver, read through silhouette. In the evening some fish glow and others stay shadow — a shoal running just beneath the surface of the water.
LC0021.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, pools and spas, panoramic living rooms, restaurants. The direction of the shoal sets an axis: the piece is oriented along the flow of people.
LC0021.style: Marine modernism and contemporary installation: natural behaviour reproduced precisely. The message is narrative — a piece that makes a scene.
LC0021.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of fish and the ratio of gold to silver are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a surface that answers. Every scale rotates freely on its own axis, and so the wall is alive: it responds to moving air and to anyone passing by. This is not decoration but behaviour — the screen can never be caught looking the same twice.

The palette is deliberately uneven: plates of differing tones are mixed, so there is always a ripple in the surface. It exists in two versions — warm, running from bronze and brass to dark copper, and cool, in silver, pewter and steel.

By day the screen works as a textured surface with a soft metallic sheen: the ripple is visible but calm. In the evening the backlight in the frame edges grazes the scales at a sharp angle, and wherever a plate has turned toward the light a bright point flares. The pattern of highlights never repeats — the wall shifts like water, or like fish scales.
LC0022.whereItWorks: Zoning and wall treatment — lobbies, restaurants and bars, reception areas, stage backdrops, showrooms, photo zones. The movement needs a gap: the screen is not fixed flat against a wall.
LC0022.style: Contemporary Art Deco and kinetic art: movement as a material. The message is striking — a piece for a space that must be remembered.
LC0022.madeToOrder: The screen dimensions, the palette and calibre of the scales and the lighting scheme are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an inverted crown. The bowl opens upward and tapers below to a sharp point: a cone standing on its tip — a crown set on the head, or a flower head caught by the stem. The form of authority, turned inside out.

Hundreds of small elements hang from a fine hoop — clear faceted drops and gold petals, mixed without system. The base is a cone of black stone with a bright white vein, and between it and the shade runs a slender stem reduced to a minimum. The contrast of heavy stone below and shimmering mass above holds the whole structure.

By day it is a sculptural object: a shimmering mass on black stone, expensive and dense. In the evening the light from deep in the bowl refracts in the drops and scatters into sparks, while the petals reflect it in warm patches. Not one source is visible directly — the mass itself glows, and the stone below picks up the reflection.
LC0023.whereItWorks: Living rooms, halls, reception rooms, showrooms, restaurant floors. The light goes upward and sideways — the lamp gives volumetric illumination, not only an accent.
LC0023.style: Art Deco and Hollywood glamour: stone, gold, shimmer. The message is representative — a piece that states the level of an interior.
LC0023.madeToOrder: The height, the bowl diameter, the number of elements and the stone of the base are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about what was broken and set again. Inside every medallion lies a net of cracks and shards compressed into a single layer: ice split by frost and then caught back together. Destruction is not depicted here, it is recorded.
The discs stand on edge, gathered into one dense row — a crest, or a rank of shields. The calibres vary and the tilts differ slightly, so the row never looks machined.

By day it is a rank of icy plates in a fine gold setting: the white net inside reads as graphics, the setting draws the outline of every disc. In the evening the light enters at the rim and travels inward along the cracks like lightguides — each crack flares along its own line, the whole disc glows with a net of white veins, and the setting rings it with a warm contour. Medallions with frozen lightning inside.
LC0024.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, reception areas. Discs on edge read end-on: the piece is oriented along the line of sight.
LC0024.style: Contemporary Art Deco and natural aesthetics: the fracture as a drawing. The message is dramatic — a piece for an interior that likes a strong detail.
LC0024.madeToOrder: The length, the number of discs, the calibres and the finish of the settings are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about balance. A horizontal rod passing straight through a disc, with collars at both ends — a scale beam, a propeller, a spindle laid on its side. A form from the world of mechanics, which always has a fulcrum and two symmetrical sides.
The spiral descends, thinning downward — the last elements hang alone. Every one is turned differently, so the composition has no principal face.

By day it is a set of clear mechanisms — precise forms with gold details, read through highlights. In the evening the disc gathers the light and flares along its rim, while the ends give directed points with radiant haloes; because the elements are turned at random, the glowing points face every direction. From each floor the piece looks different — a swarm of beams descending in a spiral.
LC0025.whereItWorks: A vertical format — stairwells, atria, shafts between floors, double-height living rooms. It is designed to be seen from several levels at once.
LC0025.style: Industrial minimalism and precision mechanics as an aesthetic. The message is rational and contemporary — a piece for an interior with an engineer's taste.
LC0025.madeToOrder: The overall height, the number of elements, the pitch of the spiral and the finish of the collars are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about brushwood. The rods hang almost horizontally at varied angles and cross one another, forming a three-dimensional lattice — the way gathered deadwood lies, where no branch repeats another's direction.
The layers run one beneath the other through the full height of the opening, twisting into a spiral. Density is uneven: in places the rods bunch together, elsewhere they hang alone.

By day it is brushwood suspended in the air: clear lines with gold collars, read graphically. In the evening light enters at the collar and runs both ways, flaring at the ends as points. Hundreds of horizontal glowing strokes at varied heights give the effect of a pencil drawing built in space — not a mass but a net of lines descending between floors.
LC0026.whereItWorks: A vertical format — stairwells, atria, shafts between floors, double-height living rooms. The spiral is designed for the specific height and route of ascent.
LC0026.style: Contemporary minimalism and the graphic school: the stroke as the only element. The message is intellectual — a piece for a space that thinks.
LC0026.madeToOrder: The overall height, the number of rods, the pitch of the spiral and the finish of the collars are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the candle. The form reads unambiguously, with no stylisation at all: a cylinder in a gold sleeve. The author does not hide the reference — on the contrary, it is carried through to the end, giving every "candle" its own gradient from bright to dark, exactly as a real one burns hot at the top and stays cool below.
The cylinders hang closely at several levels, level at the top and ragged below. The calibres are identical, only the lengths differ: the candles have burnt down unequally.

By day it is a set of gold sleeves — a dense row read through metal and the matte white beneath it. In the evening the light runs down the cylinder: the matte section diffuses it and glows evenly, the clear lower part transmits it and almost fades out, while the transverse scoring breaks the glow into horizontal strokes. A row of burning candles suspended in the air.
LC0027.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, stairwells, lobbies, meeting rooms. The downward light lifts the surface beneath it — the piece works above a table.
LC0027.style: Contemporary classicism: the candle without the candelabrum. The message is warm and ceremonial — a piece for a table where people gather.
LC0027.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of candles, the cylinder lengths and the finish of the sleeves are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the spindle. A rod with a thickening at its middle is among the oldest tools there is, and its form has not changed in thousands of years because there is nothing in it to change. The author takes it as it stands and adds only what the spindle never had: light.
Some rods carry two thickenings, some one — the rhythm is uneven. The composition is vertical, the rods hanging in a dense group at several levels.

By day it is a set of clear instruments — precise, cool forms with gold collars and finials. In the evening light enters from above and below and travels along the rod to meet in the middle: the transverse scoring breaks it into close horizontal strokes, while the thickened disc gathers it and flares into a bright ring. A double graphic — fine hatching along the rod and a bright point at the swell.
LC0028.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, meeting rooms. The vertical group builds downward: allow for height.
LC0028.style: Industrial minimalism and craft aesthetics: the tool as form. The message is rational — a piece for an interior that values how things are made.
LC0028.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of rods, the number of swells and the finish of the collars are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a scarf picked up at its centre. The material is suspended from a single point and falls freely in folds — a form that cannot be designed, only allowed. Each element settles its own way: two folds here, four there, a corner lifted somewhere else.

The longitudinal ribbing reads clearly and serves the image: this is how ribbed fabric hangs. The elements sit on fine rods with conical holders above and gather in a dense group at varied levels, with a wavy lower edge.

By day it is fabric frozen in the act of falling: a warm smoky tone, translucent, with clear hatching and its own shadows inside the folds. In the evening the light enters from above and runs down along the ribbing — every fold glows in strokes and flares more brightly at the breaks. A row of glowing scarves.
LC0029.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, dining rooms, lobbies, banquet halls. The folds read from the side: the piece is hung at eye level rather than overhead.
LC0029.style: Contemporary sculpture and Baroque drapery in a minimalist reading. The message is expressive — a piece for a space that needs a gesture.
LC0029.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the pattern of the folds and the depth of the smoky tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a crumpled sheet. Each plate has been crushed and smoothed out again — creases, folds and torn corners preserved entirely. The author fixes the moment when the sheet has already been spoiled but not yet thrown away.
The plates stand vertically, slightly turned, laid in layers. The top is ragged — individual sheets rise above the main mass — and the bottom is wavy; the array is deliberately uneven.

By day it is a heap of sheets thrown into the air: mirrored gold mixed with matte white, a random pattern of highlights. In the evening the crumpled gold reflects the light unevenly, in bands along the folds, flaring sharply, while the white diffuses it softly and holds a calm ground. The composition reads as an alternation of hot and cold rather than a single mass.
LC0030.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, lobbies, meeting rooms, reception areas. The ragged upper edge needs clearance to the ceiling.
LC0030.style: Contemporary art and minimalism: chance as form. The message is bold — a piece for an interior with no taste for the smooth.
LC0030.madeToOrder: The length, the number of plates and the ratio of gold to white are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a line folded into a loop. A long pin bent into a half-circle at the end reads both as a paper clip and as the tubing of a wind instrument. What they share is a path travelled by something invisible — paper in one case, air in the other. Here that path carries light.
The loops hang vertically, layered, threaded through one another and overlapping, level at the top and deeply sagging below. Because everything is clear, you see straight through.

By day it is an interlacing of clear tubes with gold insets — graphics read through outline. In the evening the light enters a loop and runs its whole length like a lightguide, rounding the bend and bursting out at the cut end as a bright point; the gold loops reflect and give warm bands. What you read is not form but a net of glowing lines nested inside one another.
LC0031.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms. Transparency in depth works when seen from the side — the piece is not pushed up against the ceiling.
LC0031.style: Contemporary minimalism and industrial graphics: the line instead of the volume. The message is spare — a piece for an interior that rests on structure.
LC0031.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of loops and the ratio of clear to gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the broken link. No ring is closed — a section is missing from each, and it is precisely in that gap that the light bursts out as a bright point. A chain that holds nothing, because every one of its links has been cut.

The shapes vary: some rings are round, some drawn into ovals, some almost hexagonal. They hang at varied levels, threaded through one another to form couplings; the upper half is taken by a sparse hatching of bare cables, with the whole mass gathered below.

By day it is a set of clear links — thick outlines on gold holders, read through highlights. In the evening the light enters at the fixing point and travels the whole ring like a lightguide, tracing it with a fine glowing line, then bursts out as a point at the break. An interlacing of luminous loops suspended in emptiness — a chain assembled out of light.
LC0032.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, lobbies. The couplings read in the round: the piece is designed for a view from the side.
LC0032.style: Contemporary minimalism and jewellery modernism: the link as the unit of composition. The message is spare — a piece for an interior that chooses one strong idea.
LC0032.madeToOrder: The length, the number of rings, the calibres and the finish of the holders are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about emptiness in a setting. Square and diamond frames are closed along their outlines while their centres stay empty — the piece consists of borders and of what is not inside them. Because the middles are hollow, the mass reads right through: behind the front layer you see the second and the third.
The frames are turned at varied angles, threaded through one another in places, overlapping in others; short gold rods with luminous ends are set between them.

By day it is a drawing carried into space: clear faceted outlines mixed with amber ones, read as lines. In the evening the light enters the frame at its fixing points and travels the outline like a lightguide, tracing every figure with a glowing line, while sharp sparks flare on the facets. The frames themselves disappear — what remains is an interlacing of luminous squares.
LC0033.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, meeting rooms, lobbies, reception areas. Transparency in depth works from the side: the piece is hung at eye level rather than at the ceiling.
LC0033.style: Bauhaus and contemporary minimalism: geometry without mass. The message is intellectual — a piece for an interior that rests on structure.
LC0033.madeToOrder: The length, the number of frames, the calibres and the share of amber are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a deep wave. The line drops sharply at the centre and lifts at the ends — not a gentle ripple but a full trough. The petals hang closer along the crests and sparser in the trough, so the wave is stated twice: by form and by density.

Each element is a broad crumpled petal with a rolled edge, each with a slightly different bend. Mirror-bright gold is mixed with matte white; above the mass runs a net of bare cables that sets the volume.

By day it is the crest of a wave: the mirrored petals catch daylight and invert it, the white ones stay calm, and the line reads as plasticity. In the evening the level of light travels along the length of the composition — brighter on the crests, subdued in the trough: this is real chiaroscuro, not an even wash. A current lit from within.
LC0034.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, lobbies, meeting rooms. The trough at the centre sets the minimum height above a table.
LC0034.style: Contemporary Art Deco and organic modernism: the wave as a classic motif of movement. The message is dynamic and ceremonial — a piece for a table meant to impress.
LC0034.madeToOrder: The length, the depth of the wave, the number of petals and the ratio of gold to white are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a thrown handful. The elements are laid out in a free circle — denser at the centre, sparser toward the edge, each turned differently. There is no strict grid, only a general circular field: the piece reads as a handful cast onto a plane, not as a set pattern.
The form is an elongated curved grain with faceted sides, slightly twisted, its planes meeting at random angles. Warm polished gold is mixed with cool mirrored silver.

By day the object works through reflection: the polished facets catch the light of the room and give each grain its own band of highlight, and because the facets face different ways the composition shimmers and shifts as the viewer moves. Warm and cool reflect differently, and a temperature rhythm appears across the field. In the evening, under directional light, the wall turns into a field of sparks.
LC0035.whereItWorks: Feature walls — halls, living rooms, stair landings, reception areas, dressing rooms. The effect depends on directional light: allow for a track or spots.
LC0035.style: Contemporary Art Deco and minimalism: a scattering rather than a composition. The message is light and expensive — a piece for a wall that needs no subject.
LC0035.madeToOrder: The area of the layout, the number of elements, the calibres and the ratio of gold to silver are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a shaving. A narrow twisted ribbon with close transverse scoring along its length — a curl taken off by a blade. A form from the workshop, not from nature: it arises only as a by-product of work, and the author makes it the subject.
The ribbons hang vertically, slightly turned, in tiers, level at the top with a wavy lower edge. The upper third is taken up by the hatching of bare cables with cool point lights.

By day it is a shaving taken off a block of ice: clear, read through ribbing and highlights on the coils. In the evening the light enters from above and spreads along the ribbing, so each ribbon glows in strokes rather than as a patch; transparency opens all the layers at once, the front one and everything behind it. The composition reads right through and looks like a mass made entirely of light.
LC0036.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, lobbies, meeting rooms. Transparency needs a dark backdrop: against a white ceiling the piece disappears by day.
LC0036.style: Industrial minimalism: a production form treated as an aesthetic object. The message is contemporary — a piece for an interior that values honesty of form.
LC0036.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the depth of the ribbing and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a vortex. The mass begins broad at the top, twists into a spiral and descends, narrowing to single elements. The cables vanish into darkness and do not read, so the scales seem to hang unsupported, caught in a current.
The elements are small, no larger than a palm, and mean nothing individually — only the mass works. Clear, gold and dark bronze are intermixed: three ways of meeting light in one current.

By day it is the trace left by a whirlwind: a drawing in the air, living on reflections, all but imperceptible. In the evening not every element glows but one in ten — the gold ones give warm flares, the clear ones cold sparks, the bronze ones almost extinguish. Most of the mass stays dark, and that is exactly why the composition reads as movement rather than object: a current of sparks descending between floors.
LC0037.whereItWorks: A vertical format for tall openings — stairwells, atria, shafts between floors, double-height living rooms. The spiral is designed for the specific height.
LC0037.style: Contemporary sculptural installation: the composition as an event within a volume. The message is dynamic — a piece that makes people look up.
LC0037.madeToOrder: The height of the vortex, the pitch of the spiral, the number of elements and the palette of finishes are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about what has fallen. The magnolia sheds its petals whole — they lie on the ground uncrumpled and stay beautiful for another day or two. The author takes exactly that moment: an armful of fallen petals lifted into the air.

Each petal is elongated, twisted on its axis and pointed at the tip, each with a slightly different bend — the mass looks alive. Hundreds of elements are laid in layers, level at the top and ragged below; the upper third holds a sparse hatching with small points.

By day it is an armful suspended in the air: milky white, calm, read through silhouette and soft shadow. In the evening the matte surface diffuses the light, each petal glows along its whole length in an even warm tone without flare, and because the layers are dense the glow passes onward. The composition gives soft light with not a single hard point — a cloud lit from within.
LC0038.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, banquet and wedding halls, lobbies, meeting rooms. Glare-free light is comfortable where people eat and work beneath it.
LC0038.style: Romantic modernism and contemporary classicism: bloom at the point of fading. The message is tender — a piece for a bright interior.
LC0038.madeToOrder: The length, the number of petals, the tone of the glow and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a wreath drawn out into a spiral. The laurel is a symbol whose form has always been closed: wreath, ring, circle. The author unwinds it into a vertical, and the sign turns back into a plant.

The leaves sit in pairs and groups: white beside gold, then two gold in a row, then white again — the alternation is free, with no pattern. The spiral narrows below, where single leaves descend alone.

By day it is a wreath drawn into a spiral: white gloss with drawn veining beside mirrored gold, graphic and ceremonial. In the evening the white leaves transmit the light and glow from within in soft milk, while the gold ones reflect and flare sharply; each leaf lights the one below it, and a constant exchange of warm and cool runs through the crown. A laurel that burns in every other leaf.
LC0039.whereItWorks: A vertical format — stairwells, atria, double-height living rooms, reception rooms. The spiral needs height and a view from several levels.
LC0039.style: Classical antiquity in a contemporary reading: the wreath without the pathos. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a representative space.
LC0039.madeToOrder: The overall height, the number of leaves and the ratio of white to gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a thicket. The rods are woven freely, with no geometry at all: they bend, cross and separate like branches in undergrowth. Density is uneven — in places the tubes bunch together, elsewhere the branch stays bare.
The tubes point in every direction and at every angle — up, sideways, down — so the composition has no clear silhouette: it reads as a cloud of glowing strokes rather than an object.

By day it is a thicket of budding branches — gold graphics read through lines and highlights on the ribbing. In the evening the light lives at the end of each tube: the ribbing gathers it into fine vertical hatching, while the holders throw sharp flares. Hundreds of points form an unbroken warm field with the gold frame showing through. A bush full of lights.
LC0040.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, lobbies. Having no silhouette, the piece does not argue with the interior — it works through light, not form.
LC0040.style: Organic modernism and contemporary classicism: a thicket instead of a chandelier. The message is alive and informal — a piece for an interior with no taste for ceremony.
LC0040.madeToOrder: The length, the number of tubes, the planting density and the metal finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same spiral, with flowers instead of fruit. White cups with two or three reflexed petals, opaque outside and glowing within — closer to bindweed or calla, simplified down to a few planes. The author simplifies deliberately: this flower needs no botanical accuracy, only silhouette.
The flowers sit in clusters, facing every direction: some down, some sideways, some up. The spiral narrows below and ends in single buds.

By day it is a thicket of white bindweed on a chromed branch — cool, clean, graphic. In the evening the light emerges through the open mouth as a warm patch and lights the petals from within, so they fill with cream while the outsides stay cool and matte; the chromed branches reflect that light and turn into glowing lines between the flowers. A garland of luminous cups wound into a spiral.
LC0041.whereItWorks: A vertical format — stairwells, atria, double-height living rooms, winter gardens. The spiral reads as you walk around and climb: the piece is designed for a moving viewer.
LC0041.style: Art Nouveau and Scandinavian minimalism: a botanical motif pared back to planes. The message is light and bright — a piece for a cool palette.
LC0041.madeToOrder: The overall height, the number of flowers, the density of the clusters and the finish of the branches are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the vine. The branches curl freely and interweave into a vertical spiral — a vine grows by clinging, and its form always follows a support. Here there is no support, so the vine winds around itself.

Berries of differing shapes, from small and round to large and elongated, are set in dense clusters like real fruit. The composition begins broad at the top and narrows below, where single bunches hang alone.

By day it is a vine with ripened clusters: clear berries mixed with copper-rose, a mirrored surface with a metallic sheen. In the evening light enters each berry at its base and fills it from within — the clear ones flash white, the copper ones fill with a dense warm tone, and each reflects its neighbour in its depth. The clusters signal to one another: a vineyard lit from inside.
LC0042.whereItWorks: A vertical format — stairwells, atria, double-height living rooms, shafts between floors. The spiral is calculated for the specific height and viewpoint.
LC0042.style: Art Nouveau and Mediterranean classicism: the vine as one of the oldest decorative motifs. The message is generous and warm — a piece for an interior that speaks of abundance.
LC0042.madeToOrder: The overall height, the number of clusters and the ratio of clear to copper are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same twisted drop read in graphite. The device rests on a division of temperatures: outside everything is cold — grey smoke, steel highlights, white points above; inside each drop is a hot orange core, visible only through the openings of the twist.
The form is identical, the palette its opposite — and the piece changes in mood. Instead of warmth, a smouldering restraint.

By day it is a cluster of smoky drops, almost black against the light, with a mirrored surface: a dark, heavy, graphic mass. In the evening what you see from outside is a dark mass in which dozens of embers are smouldering — narrow orange bands breaking through the twist. A fire cooling under ash.
LC0043.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, private living rooms, lounges in a dark palette. The dark mass gives little general light: the piece sets a mood rather than illuminating.
LC0043.style: Dark luxury and contemporary minimalism: smoke outside, heat within. The message is intimate and adult — a piece for an evening interior.
LC0043.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the depth of the smoky tone and the colour of the cores are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the snowflake. No two are ever alike, and the piece is built precisely on that: more rays here, longer ones there, an off-centre hub elsewhere. Not one element repeats another, and this is not decoration but a condition of truth.
The mass is sparse: there is plenty of air between the elements and the whole depth is visible. The stars hang at varied levels and orientations, some flat, some edgewise.

By day it is a set of crystals suspended below the ceiling: clear rays read through highlights at their ends. In the evening the light enters each ray at its inner end and travels outward, flaring at the tip as a bright point with a radiant halo. Every star gives its own glow, in proportion to its rays — a swarm of flashes at varied depths. Snowfall caught by a camera flash.
LC0044.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, double-height living rooms, banquet halls. The sparseness needs volume: compressed, the composition loses its depth.
LC0044.style: Nordic modernism and contemporary classicism: winter as motif, the crystal as form. The message is festive and cool — a piece for a light palette.
LC0044.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the ray lengths and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about full bloom. The flowers sit close, in whole clusters, with gaps between them — the crown reads as grown rather than set out on a grid. This is a botanical principle: plants do not flower evenly but in sprays, and the author keeps to it.

The form is small, with three or four sharp reflexed petals and an open cup — closer to jasmine or lilac than to a large garden flower. The band sags at the centre and rises at the ends, like a real branch under its own weight.

By day it is a branch in full bloom: pearlescent on gold, bright and festive. In the evening the light passes through the thin petals and lights them from within — they fill with a warm milky tone and take on an iridescent cast at the rim, while the branches pick up the reflection and glow in fine lines through the mass of flowers. A cloud of luminous sprays.
LC0045.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, banquet and wedding halls, reception areas. The sag sets the lower limit above a table.
LC0045.style: Art Nouveau and romantic classicism: the flowering branch as a classic motif of celebration. The message is ceremonial and bright — a piece for an occasion.
LC0045.madeToOrder: The length, the number of flowers, the density of the sprays and the finish of the branches are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about flame set in depth. Each drop is twisted on its vertical axis: the wall spirals around the core, the sharp tip staying above and below. The shape of fire with its movement taken away — something that does not occur in nature and can only be made this way.
The mass is packed in tiers with a wavy lower edge; the upper third is given over to the hatching of bare cables with point lights.

By day it is a cluster of amber drops — warm, translucent, with visible thickness, living on the refraction of daylight. In the evening the light runs along the spiral of the twist, reflecting off the walls, and emerges already broken into several bright bands; a glowing core appears within the body, and because the mass is dense the light passes from element to element. A field of small flames.
LC0046.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, lobbies, meeting rooms. The dense mass gives plenty of warm light: the piece works as the main illumination of a zone.
LC0046.style: The Murano tradition in a contemporary reading: colour and torsion held in depth. The message is warm — a piece for an interior that values comfort.
LC0046.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the depth of the amber tone and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a bird drawn in a single stroke. The simple tick — two blades diverging at an angle, with uneven edges — is how a child draws a bird and how a bird is seen at a distance. The author takes the most economical of signs and multiplies it into a flock.
The pyramid is dense, thicker toward the centre and the base, thinned at the edges and above. Over the mass runs a net of bare cables with glowing points — the sky above the flock.

By day it is a flock sketched in strokes alone: clear mixed with polished gold, read through silhouette. In the evening the irregular facets refract the light and scatter it in white sparks, the gold ticks reflect it and flare warm, and because the array is dense the glow passes from element to element — the whole flock shimmers. A swarm seen against the light.
LC0047.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, double-height living rooms, banquet halls. The pyramid needs height: pressed to the ceiling it loses its silhouette.
LC0047.style: Contemporary minimalism and the graphic school: the sign instead of the image. The message is light — a piece for an interior that likes things left unsaid.
LC0047.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the share of gold and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about tension released. Each plate sags in an arc between two fixing points — the form fabric takes when you stop pulling it. The edges lift into sharp corners here and hang in triangular points there, so the line is ragged rather than smooth.
The panels run in two tiers, one beneath the other, close together, forming two undulating bands. The texture is large and scaled — worked hide or bark.

By day it is a row of stretched panels: the scaling catches daylight and gives a soft play of light and shade across the whole plane. In the evening the light runs along the upper edge and grazes the texture at a sharp angle, bringing out the entire relief: the surface comes alive and every scale gets its own shadow. Almost nothing escapes outward — only the grazing light works, and the composition reads as a garland lit along its top.
LC0048.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, meeting rooms, lobbies, restaurant floors. Grazing light means the piece gives little general illumination and works as an accent.
LC0048.style: Brutalist luxury and contemporary sculpture: texture instead of shine. The message is tactile — a piece whose chief quality is its surface.
LC0048.madeToOrder: The length, the number of panels, the texture and the number of tiers are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a vein of amber. The stones are irregular and tumbled, with faceted sides and dents — not one repeats its neighbour, the surface smooth and mirrored in places, welling up in others. The tone is honey-amber, almost colourless here and dense there: resin never has an even colour.
The cloud is dense, level at the top with a ragged lower edge — a few stones descend deeper than the rest. Enough air is left between the elements to see the depth.

By day it is a scatter of amber — warm, translucent, living on the refraction of daylight. In the evening the light passes through several layers, gathering temperature, and emerges already dense with honey; each stone works as a lens for its neighbour, and the source is impossible to locate. A vein glowing inside rock.
LC0049.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, lobbies, meeting rooms. The layering is seen from the side and below: the piece is hung fairly low.
LC0049.style: Organic minimalism and the Baltic amber tradition: the stone exactly as it is. The message is warm and collector-minded — a piece chosen by feel rather than from a catalogue.
LC0049.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the calibres and the depth of the honey tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same botany without the fireflies and at a larger calibre. There are fewer leaves, they are markedly bigger, and each one reads on its own — instead of a mass you get a herbarium, where the specimen matters.
The composition is sparse: wide gaps between the leaves, visible cables, the whole mass looking light. The leaves are turned at random, some flat, some on edge.

By day it is a herbarium suspended in the air: a matte surface with worked venation, green patina beside warm bronze. In the evening the light falls on the leaves from below and from the side — the patina absorbs it and gives a subdued glow, the bronze edges flare sharply and trace each leaf with a hot line, and the veins read as relief. A crown lit from beneath.
LC0050.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, meeting rooms, reception areas, winter gardens. The sparseness gives little light: the piece is an accent, not a main source.
LC0050.style: Botanical modernism and mid-century: the plant as a graphic object. The message is restrained and natural — a piece for a warm palette.
LC0050.madeToOrder: The length, the number of leaves, the palette of the patina and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a summer night in a vineyard. The roles here are strictly divided: the foliage gives form and shadow, the fireflies give light. The leaves stay subdued and reflect only what reaches them from below — exactly as real foliage does in the dark.
The leaf form carries drawn lobes and venation, each one slightly crumpled and rolled at the edge. Small winged figures are set among them, unevenly distributed.

By day it is a vine thicket lifted to the ceiling — subdued green patina mixed with warm bronze and gold wear. In the evening every figure gives its own bright point with a radiant halo, while the foliage around it stays dark and is only lit from beneath. A vineyard full of fireflies.
LC0051.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, winter gardens, double-height living rooms, restaurant floors, terraces. Sparse point sources give atmospheric rather than working light.
LC0051.style: Art Nouveau and natural romanticism: the grapevine as a classic motif. The message is lyrical — a piece that brings back a memory of summer.
LC0051.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of leaves, the number of fireflies and the palette of the patina are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a greenhouse quarter. Rectangular cases and cylinders of differing heights stand in a dense array at varied levels and together read as a city skyline of towers and blocks — only with greenery instead of windows.

Sealed inside each are fern fronds, leaves and shoots; the walls carry condensation, so the plants are seen indistinctly, as through the side of a terrarium. The upper line of the composition is ragged — a city is never level.

By day it is a collection of herbaria under clear covers: transparent volumes through which everything is visible, the front row and what stands behind it. In the evening the light in the upper part of each case runs downward and lights the greenery from within: the leaves fill with acid green and the walls glow along their edges. A quarter of glasshouses lit all at once.
LC0052.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, meeting rooms, restaurants, winter gardens, showrooms. Transparency works when seen through: the piece is placed within the volume, not tight to the ceiling.
LC0052.style: Biodesign and urban modernism: nature set into a city grid. The message is contemporary — a piece for an interior with an agenda.
LC0052.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of cases, the plant selection and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the fogged window of a greenhouse. The pane here is not perfectly clear but carries condensation and fine droplets on its inner face — and that is the key decision. The greenery is seen indistinctly, as through a morning conservatory window: neither a picture nor a plant, but a condition.
Inside the round case dense greenery is laid in layers — ferns, monstera, fronds of several kinds. The backlight is hidden around the inner perimeter and runs as a ring.

By day the panel works as a decorative inset of calm green: a circle of green on the wall, read through colour. In the evening the ring light strikes the plants from the side, the front leaves come into focus and the far ones dissolve into a luminous haze — and a round window into a winter garden opens in the wall.
LC0053.whereItWorks: Interiors without windows — corridors, dressing rooms, washrooms, meeting rooms, lift lobbies, spas. The piece solves a specific problem: it gives a view where there is none.
LC0053.style: Biodesign and the Victorian conservatory tradition: the plant under a bell as a collector's object. The message is convivial — a piece for a room that needs bringing to life.
LC0053.madeToOrder: The case diameter, the plant selection, the planting density and the colour temperature of the backlight are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about prayer beads. The beads are strung several to a rod — larger above, smaller toward the bottom — and each strand ends in a drop. Diminishing calibre is an old device of rosaries and necklaces: it gives the strand direction and weight.
The array is dense, level at the top with a wavy lower edge. Above the composition runs a sparse net of bare rods with point lights, receding to the ceiling.

By day it is a row of hanging rosaries — a honey tone, large irregular faceting with planes of differing size, read through shine. In the evening the light enters the topmost bead and is passed down the whole strand from stone to stone, refracting on every facet: the amber fills from within, the composition gives a warm honey glow with no direct source at all, and the holders between the beads flare as sharp points. Drops of resin lit right through.
LC0054.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, reception areas. The wavy lower edge sets varying heights above the table.
LC0054.style: Art Deco and Eastern opulence: the strand of stones as a classic of formal decoration. The message is warm and rich — a piece for a table where people linger.
LC0054.madeToOrder: The length, the number of strands, the range of calibres and the depth of the honey tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a shoreline. Several different forms meet here — broad discs with a thick lens at the centre, curved white crescents, narrow curls, occasional gold bowls — and they are mixed without system. This is how the tideline lies: the unrelated ends up side by side.
The elements hang in layers, turned at random; the composition is drawn out horizontally with a ragged lower edge and a few pieces descending deeper than the rest.

By day it is a heap of shells — clear, white and gold intermixed, read through form. In the evening one and the same beam behaves in three ways: the clear discs gather it and give bright cores within their bodies, the white crescents diffuse it into soft patches, the gold bowls reflect it and flare hot. A shoreline lit from beneath.
LC0055.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, dining rooms, double-height living rooms, meeting rooms. The multi-level arrangement sets a lower limit: allow clearance beneath.
LC0055.style: Marine modernism and eclecticism in the best sense: the unrelated gathered on a single principle. The message is alive — a piece for an interior with no taste for uniformity.
LC0055.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the ratio of finishes and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same form, stripped of contrast. The wings are entirely clear, and giving up the second finish changes the piece fundamentally: instead of the interplay of white and mirror, what remains is pure optics.

The wings hang at random and are laid in a spiral, with the sources standing between them. The body of each wing works as a lens: a glowing core appears in the hollow and a bright thread runs along the rim.

By day the composition is all but invisible and shows itself only in highlights — a clear mass that is easy to overlook. In the evening every layer is visible at once, the front one and everything behind it: the piece reads right through, with real depth, and never looks solid. A cloud of lights, each in its own setting.
LC0056.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, dining rooms, lobbies, stairwells. Transparency needs a dark backdrop: against a white ceiling the piece disappears by day.
LC0056.style: Contemporary classicism and minimalism: light as the only material. The message is clean — a piece for an interior that refuses colour.
LC0056.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of wings, the suspension lengths and the colour temperature are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the difference between finishes. The wings themselves give no light here — the sources stand between them, on gold holders. The wings only receive the light, and the whole piece is built on how differently they do it: the opaque white ones diffuse it into a soft patch, the mirrored ones reflect and pass it onward to their neighbours.
The form is a curved wing with a sharp tip and a deep hollow. The bowl is dense, the assembly spiral, the wings turned in every direction and overlapping in places.

By day it is a flock stilled below the ceiling: white mixed with mirror, read through silhouette and reflection. In the evening one half of the composition is always calm and the other sparkling, and as you walk around they change places — a swarm that burns in every other wing.
LC0057.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, lobbies, stairwells, banquet halls. The spiral assembly asks to be seen in the round: the piece is not placed against a wall.
LC0057.style: Contemporary Art Deco and glamorous minimalism: two behaviours of a single beam. The message is festive — a piece for a formal space.
LC0057.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements and the ratio of white to mirror are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a paper cone. An elongated cone with an open mouth below and a sharp apex above, thin walls, a wavy fire-polished rim — a rolled cone or a bindweed flower. The simplest of forms, and that is its strength: it is recognised instantly and needs no explanation.
The cones hang at several levels, slightly turned and overlapping, with a wavy lower edge. The upper zone stays empty — only the hatching of cables.

By day the composition is all but invisible: clear and colourless, it reads through highlights along the wavy rims alone. In the evening the light travels from the apex down to the mouth, reflecting off the walls, and a glowing column appears within the body; it escapes through the open base. Dozens of luminous funnels hang in the air with not a single lamp in sight.
LC0058.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms, zones above a long table. The light is directed downward through the mouth — the piece lights the table, not the room.
LC0058.style: Scandinavian minimalism and organic modernism: the simplest form without decoration. The message is light — a piece for an interior that refuses weight.
LC0058.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of cones, the suspension lengths and the calibres are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a thrown handful. The rods hang at wildly varied angles — horizontal, oblique, crosswise — and intersect to form a lattice with no centre and no symmetry. A handful of matches thrown into the air and frozen: there is no order, because there was none at the moment of the throw.
Some rods bunch into tight clusters, others hang alone far from the mass. The cables vanish into darkness and are barely visible.

By day it is a drawing carried into space: polished lines read graphically, with occasional flares on the faceted heads. In the evening the light enters each rod at its upper end and travels to the sphere — which gathers it, breaks it on the facets and flares into a point, while the rod itself stays a cold stroke. Only the glowing heads are visible: a swarm of sparks suspended in the air.
LC0059.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, meeting rooms. The lattice builds in the round and has no principal face — it is designed for the specific room.
LC0059.style: Contemporary minimalism and the graphic school: line and point, nothing more. The message is intellectual — a piece for an interior that rests on an idea.
LC0059.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of rods, the metal finish and the calibre of the heads are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a colony. Every element differs from its neighbour — three offshoots here, five there, a wider mouth on one, a narrower one on another. This is not variety for its own sake but accuracy: a colony consists of individuals, not of parts.
The pyramid is dense, the elements almost touching, thicker at the centre and thinned at the edges. From below the mass reads as continuous, like a real growth on a rock.

By day it is a limestone colony — white, matte, read through relief and the shadows between the offshoots. In the evening the light emerges through the open mouths as a warm milky patch and shows through the thin walls from inside, so the white fills with cream while the outer surfaces stay cool and opaque. The mouths face every direction — a reef lit from within.
LC0060.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, pools and spas, double-height living rooms, winter gardens. The dense pyramid needs height; the soft glare-free light suits positions above water.
LC0060.style: Marine modernism and organic minimalism: a biological form without stylisation. The message is calm — a piece for an interior where people rest.
LC0060.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the tone of the glaze and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about growth. Segments with rounded sides are stacked one on another, each throwing off short offshoots — the form reads at once as coral, as a spine and as a cactus. The ambiguity is deliberate: the author takes the general principle of growth rather than any single species.

The glaze runs unevenly, with drips, and the object looks grown rather than cast. Openings of varying calibre are cut through the whole body — from fist-sized down to small points — and their inner surfaces are gold.

By day it is a dense sculpture: warm white with a cream cast or deep blue with a grey undertone, opaque and matte. In the evening the light emerges from the openings in narrow warm beams while the column itself stays dark — the same device as a coal: cold shell, burning core. The base is reduced to a minimum, so the mass seems to stand of its own accord.
A second finish exists, faced in preserved moss, where a living green texture replaces the glaze.
LC0061.whereItWorks: Halls, living rooms, spas, showrooms, reception rooms, restaurant interiors. Fragmentary light gives atmosphere rather than illumination: a second source is needed nearby.
LC0061.style: Biodesign and organic modernism: growth as the form-giving principle. The message is natural and contemporary — a piece for an interior with character.
LC0061.madeToOrder: The height, the number of segments, the glaze colour and the number and calibre of the openings are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about freezing rain. The rods are overgrown with small crystals along their whole length — uneven accretions, thicker in places, sparser in others. This is how a branch looks the morning after rain has frozen in flight: the crust builds not evenly but wherever it managed to.
The rods hang at varied angles — almost horizontal, oblique, crosswise — and intersect to form a three-dimensional lattice with no centre and no symmetry. A thicket of bare branches caught by frost.

By day it is an interlacing of branches — graphic, cold, living on the highlights along the crystals. In the evening every accretion lights its own point, and an uneven glowing line runs along each branch: where the crystals are denser, it is brighter. The polished ends flare as separate hard highlights. A thicket covered in luminous frost.
LC0062.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, double-height living rooms, stairwells, winter gardens, restaurants. A lattice without a centre is built for the specific volume and has no principal face.
