LC0062.style: Nordic modernism and organic aesthetics: winter as motif. The message is cool and clean — a piece for an interior in a cold palette.
LC0062.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of branches, the density of the crystals and the metal finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the fruit and its medium. Large pomegranates with faceted sides and a dimple on top are rare and heavy; around them falls a dense vertical rain of small drops on clear threads, even and uniform. The whole composition rests on that contrast: a few large events within a uniform medium.
The form of the fruit is taken almost literally. The tone is deep scarlet with gold runs, the surface mirrored: the fruits reflect and glow from within at the same time.

By day it is an orchard with ripened fruit — red against clear, read through colour and highlight. In the evening the light passes through the body and fills it to ruby, while the rain picks up the reflection and scatters it as pinpoint sparks through the whole volume. The source cannot be found — both the fruit and the medium around it glow. Rubies suspended in a cloud of sparks.
LC0063.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, double-height living rooms, banquet and wedding halls, restaurants. The rain sets the vertical envelope: allow for height.
LC0063.style: Grand classicism and Eastern opulence: the fruit as a symbol of abundance. The message is festive and generous — a piece for a space where guests are received.
LC0063.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of fruits, the density of the rain and the depth of the scarlet tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a horn with a crystal. The element is double: a cone rolled into a bell with an open mouth, and a faceted cube at its wide end. It reads both as a horn with a mouthpiece and as a flower with a crystal for its heart — a form from the world of machinery and a form from the world of minerals in one object.
The elements hang at varied angles: some mouth up, some down, some sideways. The bowl is shallow, and in places the elements interlock into clusters.

By day it is a cluster of gold flowers with icy hearts: the bells work through reflection, the cubes through refraction. In the evening the light leaves the bell for the crystal, which gathers it, refracts it on the facets and flares from within, while the cone remains a reflector — lit, but not luminous itself. The orientations vary, so the glowing crystals face every direction.
LC0064.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, dining rooms, lobbies, banquet halls. The absence of a principal view means the piece is placed at the centre of a zone, not against a wall.
LC0064.style: Art Deco and industrial luxury: a mechanical form with a precious filling. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a formal space.
LC0064.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the calibres of the crystals and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a city. Arches, windows, portals, rectangular plates — some with rounded tops, some stepped, some flat: the vocabulary of architecture broken down into signs. Each element is turned at its own angle, and from a distance the mass reads as a city skyline with roofs, spires and windows receding into depth.
The array is dense: hundreds of plates at varied levels, overlapping, level at the top and deeply sagging below.

By day it is graphics made of mirrored silhouettes — flat, sharp, read through outline. In the evening the mirrored plates reflect the light and pass it to one another: an endless exchange of highlights builds inside the composition, the source is impossible to locate, and every arch reflects its neighbour. A panorama with lit windows — a city reflected in itself.
LC0065.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, lobbies, meeting rooms, reception areas. The skyline reads from a distance: the piece is designed for a view from the entrance, not from directly beneath.
LC0065.style: Art Deco and urban modernism: architecture as ornament. The message is metropolitan — a piece for an interior that loves the city.
LC0065.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the set of forms and the metal finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about dark water. Concentric waves of deep black with a mirrored gloss spread from an off-centre point, welling over one another — rings from a stone thrown into water at night.

The finish is wholly glossy, without a single matte area: the frame reflects everything around it and all but disappears in the dark, leaving only bands of highlight. That sets it apart from the gold versions in principle — here it is not colour that works but pure reflection.

By day the object reads graphically, black against the wall; the convex plate with its warm golden cast draws the room into a compact frame, and against the black waves that reflection looks like a window cut into a dark surface — the only warm patch in the whole object. In the evening the frame all but dissolves, and only the glowing circle of the reflection remains, hanging on its own.
LC0066.whereItWorks: Interiors in a dark palette — entrance halls, private studies, bars, living rooms, gallery walls. Against a pale wall the disappearing act does not work.
LC0066.style: Dark luxury and contemporary minimalism: black gloss as the principal language. The message is austere — a piece for an interior that does not flirt.
LC0066.madeToOrder: The diameter, the depth of the waves, the finish and the size of the sphere are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the point everything gathers toward. The sphere here is polished rather than matte: it gives no light of its own but collects and redirects the glow running along the inner rim of the ring. Source and accent are separated — one thing shines, another is looked at.

The band is broad and crushed into soft waves, the circle wandering slightly along its contour, the inner opening alive with swellings. The inner surface is polished with particular care: it is the reflector.

By day it is a metal hoop with a sphere — polished gold with cool blue-green reflections along the crests of the folds. In the evening what remains is a ring of light with one bright point in the upper left. The opening stays empty: the wall is visible through it, and that is part of the intent — the piece frames a void.
LC0067.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, corridors, private living rooms, stair flights, reception areas, showrooms. An empty opening means the wall beneath the fitting is part of the composition: its texture and colour matter.
LC0067.style: Contemporary sculpture and minimalism: a frame around nothing. The message is conceptual — a piece for an interior that values the idea.
LC0067.madeToOrder: The ring diameter, the width of the band, the metal finish and the calibre of the sphere are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a mirror that is barely there. The opening is very small and set deep into the frame: almost the entire area is given to relief, and only enough reflective surface remains for a reflection to register. The proportion is inverted — here the frame is the subject and the mirror is secondary.

The relief is built from soft broad folds spiralling toward the centre in uneven coils: they well over one another, break, and lift into a sharp crest in places. Crumpled fabric, a rose, a cabbage leaf — the ambiguity is deliberate.

By day the object works through light and shade rather than reflection: warm bronze with a matte surface, bluish veining in the shadows, bright gold wear on the crests, very little shine. In the evening, under directional light, the folds throw deep shadows and the frame becomes almost a relief sculpture, while the deeply recessed convex plate reads as a look down a tunnel — distant, compressed, barely real.
LC0068.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, bedrooms, living rooms, corridors, gallery walls — wherever a sculptural object is wanted rather than a functional mirror. It was never conceived as a working mirror.
LC0068.style: Organic modernism and wabi-sabi: a subdued palette, irregularity as a virtue. The message is quiet — a piece for an interior that avoids shine.
LC0068.madeToOrder: The diameter, the depth of the folds, the size of the opening and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a whirlpool. The folds run in coils around an off-centre opening, welling over one another and narrowing toward the middle: a funnel, fabric twisted into a rope, a section through a shell — the form reads several ways at once and none of them to the end.
The surface is mirrored, so every coil reflects its neighbour and the frame acquires its own depth, independent of the reflection in the plate. The piece turns out to be dimensional twice over.

By day it is polished gold with cool blue-green reflections deep in the folds and wear along the crests — the frame lives on the reflections of the room. In the evening a small matte sphere lights up in the lower fold: it gives a soft glow from below and grazes the whole spiral, bringing out the relief. Reflection and frame together pull the eye into a single point.
LC0069.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, living rooms, boudoirs, private studies, gallery walls. The asymmetry needs a clear wall — the piece is not hung in a row.
LC0069.style: Baroque plasticity in a contemporary reading: movement set in metal. The message is dramatic — a piece for an interior that likes strong forms.
LC0069.madeToOrder: The diameter, the depth of the spiral, the metal finish and the position of the sphere are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the mark of the hammer. Uneven dents, grooves and swellings run across the whole frame — as though the metal had been struck while still soft. The pattern is irregular, without a single repeat: handwork is shown as it is, not smoothed away.
The chief difference from the other mirrors in the line is the backlight. It is hidden in a ring recess between frame and mirror and emerges as a narrow band.

By day the frame works through texture: pale antiqued silver with gold wear and dark patina in the hollows, a matte surface with visible grain. In the evening the light comes from within and grazes the relief — every dent takes a shadow, the frame gains volume, and the mirror itself sits inside a glowing ring. The convex plate meanwhile draws the room into a compact frame with strong distortion at the edges.
LC0070.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, corridors, bedrooms, bathrooms, dressing rooms. The backlight makes the mirror functional for the zone, but the convexity distorts the reflection — it is not a mirror for getting ready.
LC0070.style: Brutalist luxury and hand forging: the marks of work as decoration. The message is honest and craft-driven — a piece that shows how it was made.
LC0070.madeToOrder: The diameter, the character of the forging, the metal finish and the brightness of the backlight are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same solution in hard plasticity. Instead of soft waves — large planes meeting at angles, and an inner opening with sharp projections and hollows. The form is closer to a nugget or a fragment of ore than to an organic fold.

The device is identical but the result is different: on the flat facets the highlights are broad and calm, on the breaks they flare sharply, and the object reads more graphically than the round version.

By day it is metal melted and set again — polished gold with cool reflections, heavy and angular. In the evening the light runs along the inner rim and lights the ragged contour: you see not the shape of the object but the outline of the hole in it. On angular geometry the device works more dramatically than on soft — an opening with fire behind it.
LC0071.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, private studies, bars, lounges, gallery walls. The hard plasticity needs a dark or neutral backdrop.
LC0071.style: Brutalist luxury and contemporary art: the fracture instead of the line. The message is hard — a piece for an interior that does not soften.
LC0071.madeToOrder: The dimensions, the character of the geometry, the metal finish and the lighting scheme are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a ring that burns only at its edge. The band is broad, its surface wavy, crushed and twisted along its whole length; the inner opening is not a circle but a living contour with swellings and lobes. There is no correct geometry anywhere.

A small matte sphere sits in the upper part, slightly off centre — and it is the only source. Its light runs along the inner rim, tracing the opening with a hot line, while the outer surface stays reflective.

By day it is a metal ring-sculpture: each wave carries its own elongated band of highlight, and as you walk past they shift — the object looks mobile. In the evening the outer part falls into shadow, and what remains is a hoop burning along its inner edge — the glowing contour of an emptiness.
LC0072.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, corridors, bedrooms, private living rooms, stair flights, reception areas. The light is directed into the ring and onto the wall — the fitting works as an accent rather than as illumination.
LC0072.style: Contemporary sculpture and organic modernism: a ring without a single straight line. The message is spare — a piece for a wall that needs one object only.
LC0072.madeToOrder: The ring diameter, the width of the band, the metal finish and the calibre of the sphere are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same shell set upright. The layers no longer run in circles but converge upward toward a pointed apex, with the pearl shifted into the upper third: the form becomes teardrop-like, with a clear direction. The folds are larger and softer — a few broad waves instead of close accretions.
Direction changes the piece fundamentally. The round version is static; this one reaches upward.

By day the object reads as a mussel shell stood on end: polished gold with cool pearlescent reflections along the rims, pure sculpture. In the evening the light from the matte pearl runs down the folds and spreads across the full height — the lower part stays in shadow and works as form, the upper part burns. A drop of light in a metal setting.
LC0073.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, narrow corridors, bedrooms, stair flights, private reception rooms. The vertical format goes where there is no width: in piers and along flights.
LC0073.style: Art Nouveau and organic modernism: a natural form with direction. The message is aspiring — a piece for a narrow space that needs height.
LC0073.madeToOrder: The dimensions, the depth of the relief, the metal finish and the position of the pearl are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the pearl in the shell. A shell grows in annual accretions — several nested layers with wavy edges, spiralling toward an off-centre core, with swellings and folds. There is no regularity, because growth knows none.
The finish is mirrored, and every layer reflects its neighbour: an endless exchange of highlights builds up in the depth of the shell, something no matte form could produce.

By day the object reads as a sculptural shell on the wall — polished gold with cool blue-green reflections along the rims, giving a pearlescent effect. In the evening a matte pearl lights up at the centre: it illuminates all the surrounding layers from within, the gold around it grows hot, and the outer coils stay subdued. The light never strikes the eye — it is always reflected.
LC0074.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, corridors, bedrooms at the bedhead, bathrooms, private living rooms, spas. Reflected light without direct glare suits positions beside a mirror or a bed.
LC0074.style: Art Nouveau and marine modernism: the shell as a classic motif of preciousness. The message is intimate — a piece for a private space.
LC0074.madeToOrder: The dimensions, the depth of the relief, the metal finish and the calibre of the pearl are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a chain that holds nothing. Large irregular links are threaded one through another, each crumpled and twisted, none repeating its neighbour. Together they sag freely and twist about their own axis — a chain stripped of its function and left as form.
Traces of forming remain on the surface — dents and waves — and they read as drawing, not as flaw. The piece has no principal view: from the side and from below it is two different compositions.

By day it is warm gold with greenish and coppery shifts in the shadows, a sculpture working through the plasticity of the link. In the evening the light emerges along the inner rim of each ring and traces it with a glowing line; because the rings pass through one another and face different ways, those lines cross and layer. An interlacing of luminous loops.
LC0075.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, lobbies. The sag sets a lower limit: allow clearance beneath.
LC0075.style: Brutalist luxury and contemporary Art Deco: the link as a unit of opulence. The message is strong and direct — a piece for an interior with character.
LC0075.madeToOrder: The length of the chain, the number of links, their calibres and the metal finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a single line. There is no set of elements here — there is one continuous strip, twisted and crushed into a loose knot: it folds over, crosses itself and returns, never repeating a previous bend. The piece reads whole and at once, as a single movement.
The surface is polished, with facets and dents left by working hot metal: light does not slide evenly across it but breaks into dozens of highlights, and every bend acquires its own line of light.

By day it is a metal sculpture — warm gold with greenish shifts in the shadows, plastic and heavy. In the evening light wakes deep inside the knot: it escapes through the gaps between the coils, lighting the inner faces of the strip, and the knot begins to glow without a single visible lamp. A ribbon heated from within.
LC0076.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, reception rooms, zones above a long table. The knot has no principal view: the piece is placed where people walk around it.
LC0076.style: Contemporary sculpture and brutalist luxury: one gesture instead of a composition. The message is artistic — a piece that exists as an object of art.
LC0076.madeToOrder: The length of the strip, the pattern of the knot, the metal finish and the drop height are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a piece of earth lifted into the air. The volume is entirely covered in preserved moss — dense, velvety, with an uneven living surface; the form is irregular, with projections and hollows. This is not an abstraction but a fragment: a part of forest taken out and hung up.

Openings are cut through the body, framed by metal craters with ragged rims, like a drilled bore. The device rests on a collision of textures: soft matte organic matter that absorbs light entirely, and hard mirrored metal that throws it out.

By day it is a fragment of forest suspended in the air — deep green, light-absorbing, with occasional metallic flashes at the craters. In the evening all the sources hidden inside the mass emerge only through the openings: craters of differing calibre face different ways, and the light spreads unevenly, in patches. Rock with holes burnt through it.
LC0077.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, restaurants, winter gardens, spas, showrooms, meeting rooms. Preserved moss needs no care or watering, but dislikes direct sun.
LC0077.style: Biodesign and brutalist modernism: living texture against metal. The message is ecological and hard at once — a piece for an interior with a contemporary agenda.
LC0077.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of craters, their calibres and the metal finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a drawing carried into space. The frame of fine ties joined into an irregular polyhedral net is not concealed — it is the principal form. Triangles of varying size meet at the nodes: a structure that holds nothing but itself.

Glowing points sit at the nodes, and small polished discs are fixed along the ties, turned in different directions. There are exactly enough of them to stop the net being only geometry — and not one more.

By day the object looks like a molecular model or an architectural grid: a transparent structure read through lines. In the evening the light flares at the nodes as stars, the discs reflect and invert it, and a small cloud of secondary highlights forms around each point. The frame is transparent, so foreground and background glow at once — a patch of night sky with its connections drawn in.
LC0078.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, double-height living rooms, meeting rooms, showrooms. The depth reads only when seen through: the piece is set within the volume, not up at the ceiling.
LC0078.style: Bauhaus and scientific minimalism: structure instead of decoration. The message is intellectual — a piece for a space that thinks.
LC0078.madeToOrder: The overall size, the density of the net, the number of lights and the palette of the discs are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a shell enlarged many times over. The form curls in two opposing waves with a deep hollow between them, and close linear hatching runs across the whole surface — annual layers, the grooves on a mollusc valve. Scale turns the familiar into the unfamiliar: what once fit in a palm now fills a corner of a room.
The object gives no light — it is pure sculpture, made for viewing in the round: from every side a different form reads.

By day the colour does the work: from pale pink and cream on the crests to deep coral and near-burgundy in the shadows, with a warmed golden band at the very depth of the fold. The transition is gradual, without boundaries — and it brings out the volume better than any light could. In the evening, under side light, everything becomes a play of folds and shadows: the hatching intensifies, the hollow deepens, and the object reads almost as relief.
LC0079.whereItWorks: Halls, gallery spaces, private living rooms, showrooms, spas. Viewing in the round means the object is placed at the centre or on a plinth, not against a wall.
LC0079.style: Contemporary sculpture and organic modernism: a natural form at the wrong scale. The message is artistic — a work of art rather than a furnishing.
LC0079.madeToOrder: The dimensions, the palette and the character of the hatching are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a ripple on water. Soft undulating folds spread from the centre in uneven circles of varying depth and width, welling over one another and never repeating. The frame looks laid by hand rather than cast — this is how water spreads from a thrown stone.
The opening is irregular, with soft lobes along its contour: the frame approaches it as a wave, without a hard boundary. The transition between reflection and relief is blurred.

By day the palette is restrained, almost beige — pale antiqued gold with cool bluish veining deep in the folds and wear on the crests. The object does not read as gilding; more as weathered wood or plaster. In the evening side light brings out the full depth of the folds, and the frame spreads around the compressed convex frame of the reflection.
LC0080.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, bedrooms, living rooms, boudoirs, corridors. The restrained palette suits bright interiors where gold would be too loud.
LC0080.style: Organic modernism and wabi-sabi: irregularity and fading as virtues. The message is quiet — a piece for an interior that avoids shine.
LC0080.madeToOrder: The diameter, the depth and number of folds and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a single fold. There is no fine detailing here: a broad band wraps the mirror in a circle and turns back on itself, leaving the cut visible. One gesture across the whole frame — and that is the entire intent.

The opening is strongly displaced toward the upper edge and has an uneven, multi-faceted contour. The symmetry is broken deliberately: the piece reads as a shell or a rolled leaf, not as a classical round frame.

By day the frame works through plasticity — pale leaf gold with wear and fine cracks, almost white on the raised sections, drifting into copper in the shadows. In the evening, under directional light, the single fold throws a deep dramatic shadow and the volume doubles in strength. The convex plate gathers the room into a compact reflection with strong distortion at the edges.
LC0081.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, living rooms, private studies, boudoirs, gallery walls. The asymmetry needs clear space around it: the piece does not sit in a row with others.
LC0081.style: Contemporary sculpture and organic modernism: one form instead of ornament. The message is spare — a piece for an interior that chooses a single strong detail.
LC0081.madeToOrder: The diameter, the depth of the fold, the displacement of the opening and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a whirlpool. Instead of even rings the frame is wound into a large spiral fold — the surface rotates around the centre like a funnel, or fabric twisted into a rope. The relief is deep, with pronounced crests and troughs.
The opening is not perfectly round but slightly faceted: the frame encroaches on it with uneven projections, so the boundary between relief and reflection is alive rather than drawn with a compass.

By day the piece reads through plasticity: leaf gold with heavy patina, pale and almost white on the crests, drifting into dark bronze in the hollows, with bluish veining between the folds. In the evening, under directional light, the spiral throws long twisting shadows and the frame begins to rotate before your eyes. The convex plate draws the whole room into itself — a whirlpool with a window at its centre.
LC0082.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, living rooms, boudoirs, private studies, reception areas. The effect depends on side light: allow for a directional source.
LC0082.style: Baroque plasticity in a contemporary reading: movement set in the frame. The message is dramatic — a piece for an interior that likes strong forms.
LC0082.madeToOrder: The diameter, the depth of the relief, the gilding finish and the shape of the opening are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about growth rings. The frame is built from concentric rings of varying thickness, and the rings are irregular — they wander in width and sit slightly off centre. This matters in principle: a tree section and ripples on water are never regular, and turned geometry would kill the image.

The mirror itself is convex, and that changes what it is for. It gathers a whole room into a small circle — window, ceiling, furniture, the view beyond — and the reflection comes out compressed, as through a fisheye lens. The piece is not for checking how you look; it is for seeing a space entire.

By day the frame reads through texture: antiqued gold with patina, almost white in places, elsewhere drifting into warm ochre, with fine bluish veining between the rings. In the evening, under side light, the rings throw deep shadows and the frame gains volume — turning from graphics into relief.
LC0083.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, living rooms, studies, bedrooms, corridors — wherever an accent is wanted rather than a functional mirror. The convexity distorts the reflection: it does not serve for getting ready.
LC0083.style: Organic modernism and antique classicism: the Flemish convex mirror in a contemporary reading. The message is collector-minded — an object, not a household item.
LC0083.madeToOrder: The diameter, the number of rings, the gilding finish and the depth of the convexity are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about hatching. Short clear rods hang horizontally, the rows running in tiers, curving as they rise and fall. Hundreds of lines oriented one way and layered over each other give the effect of pencil hatching — a volume built out of separate strokes.
Density is uneven: in places the strokes bunch into tight packs, elsewhere they hang alone far from the mass. That is how a hand hatches, not a machine.

By day the composition is all but invisible — the colourless rods read only through highlights, and the drawing in the air is barely guessed at. In the evening the light enters a rod at one end and travels its whole length, so every stroke lights up as an even line. What remains is a drawing suspended in the air — a sketch made in light.
LC0084.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, double-height living rooms, stairwells, meeting rooms. Transparency needs a dark backdrop: against a white ceiling the piece disappears by day.
LC0084.style: Contemporary minimalism and the graphic school: the line as the only element. The message is intellectual — a piece for an interior that rests on an idea.
LC0084.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of rods, the wave pattern and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about two halves that behave in opposite ways. The left is white, glossy, reflective, without a single pattern. The right is bronze with botanical etching, where branches and grass heads emerge against the light. Between them a mixing zone, where the sails alternate.
The device lies in the fact that the difference is not immediately apparent. By day it is a transition from pure geometry to ornament — the piece reads as a gradient, calm and decorative.

In the evening the halves separate for good: the white reflects the light and stays opaque, only the rims glowing; the bronze transmits it and the etched pattern lights up from within, revealing the whole botanical graphic. One half falls into shadow, the other burns — the composition literally splits in two.
LC0085.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, double-height living rooms, banquet and restaurant halls, atria. The asymmetry sets a direction: the burning half is oriented toward the principal position.
LC0085.style: Contemporary Art Deco and botanical modernism: minimalism and ornament in one object. The message is contrastive — a piece for an interior that likes surprise.
LC0085.madeToOrder: The overall size, the point of transition, the etching pattern and the number of tiers are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about structure visible only against the light. Thin plates with a pronounced fibrous structure read by day as simply pale — all their complexity is hidden and opens up only when lit from behind.

Each plate is bowed in an arc, several overlapping to form a single sail. The tiers are laid over one another, overlapping in places. The palette drifts from cool milky grey to warm honey — the transition runs horizontally, left to right.

By day the composition reads as a heap of shells: soft, pale, working through form and overlap. In the evening the light passes through the material and reveals the whole fibrous structure — every plate becomes a map of veins. Outward the light emerges soft and diffuse, without a single bright point: a cloud in which every scale glows.
LC0086.whereItWorks: Generous rooms with high ceilings — atria, lobbies, double-height living rooms, banquet halls. The tiering needs height: in a low room the layers merge.
LC0086.style: Organic minimalism and the Japanese aesthetics of paper: light through the material rather than light within it. The message is quiet — a piece for an interior that does not argue.
LC0086.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of sails, the number of tiers and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a current. The mass runs from the upper left corner to the lower right in a broad band, with every leaf turned along that direction. The diagonal is no accident: the horizontal reads as rest, the vertical as falling, and only the diagonal reads as movement.

The large elements gather in the upper part, the small ones below, where the current breaks into single leaves. The colour drifts from golden ochre to deep bottle green, with translucent passages here and there.

By day it is a current caught in a frame: a diagonal band living on colour and inclination. In the evening the light enters the body and spreads across the whole plane of the leaf, filling the green from within and flaring on the gold passages; the cables vanish into darkness and do not read, so the leaves seem carried by the current. A shoal crossing the room on the diagonal.
LC0087.whereItWorks: Generous rooms and irregular geometry — stairwells, atria, curved halls, double-height living rooms. The diagonal is designed for the specific volume and entrance point.
LC0087.style: Organic modernism and contemporary installation: movement as the principal subject. The message is dynamic — a piece that leads you through a space.
LC0087.madeToOrder: The length and pitch of the current, the number of leaves, the palette and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about what is inside a flower. From outside the piece is closed — only the white matte surface of the petals, laid in overlapping layers. From within something quite different opens up: a dense net of fine spokes and rods radiating outward, with the light node at the centre. A flower head whose entire core structure is on view.
The form changes completely with the viewpoint: from the side it is a flat disc with a fringe, from below an open flower with a burning centre. One piece and two different objects.

By day the composition reads through form: a white half-open bowl, calm and graphic, concealing how it is built. In the evening the light emerges from the centre through the gaps between the petals, lighting them from within, while the frame casts fine vein-like shadows across them. The flower turns out to be transparent to its own light.
LC0088.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, reception rooms, zones above a round table. The principal view is from below, so the piece is hung above an area where people stand or sit rather than pass through.
LC0088.style: Organic modernism and mid-century: a natural form with its structure exposed. The message is rational and warm — a piece for someone who values how a thing is made.
LC0088.madeToOrder: The disc diameter, the number of petals, the tone of the finish and the drop height are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the way soft coral grows. Long curved stems with a swelling at the tip are each turned differently: some hook over, some stay almost straight. This is not ornament but behaviour — it is how everything living reaches toward light, each shoot on its own.
The array is dense, level at the top and deeply sagging below. Among the white mass are a few coral-orange elements, scattered unevenly, like fish in a thicket.

By day it is a coral colony — matte, white, calm, read through silhouette and a few points of colour. In the evening the matte surface diffuses the light and every stem glows along its full length in an even milky tone without flare, while the orange ones fill with dense colour and work as accents. A thicket lit from the depths.
LC0089.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, pools and spas, double-height living rooms, atria. Soft light with no hard points suits rest zones and water.
LC0089.style: Marine modernism and organic minimalism: growth as the only motif. The message is calm — a piece for an interior where people unwind.
LC0089.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of stems, the share of coloured elements and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same technique in a hot palette. Scarlet, brick, orange and ochre — and among them a few single green leaves: the ones that have not yet turned. That single detail converts an ornament into a moment in time: autumn is shown as a process, not a state.
The forms are maple and oak, with deep lobes and sharp teeth. The mass is denser to left and right and thinner at the centre; below, individual leaves fall alone, drawn out into a chain.

By day it is a scattered armful of leaves — dense colour read against the light, a living composition without symmetry. In the evening the palette comes alive: the scarlet segments deepen to ruby, the orange to amber, the ochre lightens to gold, and the gold seams read as veins traced in light. A bonfire broken down into separate embers.
LC0090.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, double-height living rooms, restaurant floors, winter gardens. The saturated palette needs a calm backdrop.
LC0090.style: Art Nouveau and autumn classicism: stained glass as a way of catching colour. The message is warm — a piece for an interior in a natural range.
LC0090.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of leaves, the palette of the segments and the pattern of the soldering are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a dismantled stained-glass window. Every leaf is assembled from coloured segments joined by gold soldering, and the seams work as veins and as load-bearing frame at once: pattern and structure are one and the same thing here, so the leaf reads even without light.
The forms vary — some broad and five-lobed, some narrow with sharp teeth. The leaves are turned at random and hang at varied levels; below, a few break away and fall alone.

By day it is a thicket of ivy — from grass green to dark olive and almost black, read through colour against the light. In the evening the light passes through the segments, each filling with its own tone — pale green beside bottle green — while the gold seams flare as a graphic net laid over the colour. A crown lit from within.
LC0091.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, winter gardens, double-height living rooms, restaurant floors. Stained glass is made to be seen against the light: the piece is placed where people look up at it.
LC0091.style: Art Nouveau and the Tiffany stained-glass tradition: a plant motif in coloured mosaic. The message is collector-minded — a piece for an interior that values handwork.
LC0091.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of leaves, the palette of the segments and the pattern of the soldering are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a dismantled stained-glass window. Every feather is assembled from separate coloured segments joined by silver soldering, and the seams form the pattern of the vane: they work as veins and as frame at once. Structure and drawing are one and the same thing here.
The feathers are turned in different directions and hang at varied levels; the main mass gathers at the centre, and below individual feathers break away and fall alone.

By day it is a flock of blue feathers — from cobalt and ultramarine to turquoise, read through colour against the light. In the evening the light passes through the segments and each fills with its own tone — blue beside turquoise, ultramarine beside near-black — while the silver seams flare as a graphic net over the colour. The pattern reads more clearly than by day: a stained-glass window taken apart and suspended in the air.
LC0092.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, double-height living rooms, spas and pools, gallery spaces. The technique is made to be seen against the light: the piece is placed where people look up at it.
LC0092.style: Art Nouveau and the Tiffany stained-glass tradition in a contemporary reading. The message is collector-minded — a piece for an interior that values handwork.
LC0092.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of feathers, the palette of the segments and the pattern of the soldering are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about fragility in quantity. One butterfly is a detail; a hundred butterflies are an event. The author uses that: the mass is denser below and at the centre, while at the edges individuals fly far off alone — and it is they that make the flock alive.
The wing form differs by species — some broad, some narrow with long tails; the veins are drawn. The figures are turned in different directions, some hanging flat, some edgewise.

By day it is a flock stilled below the ceiling — white, matte, faintly translucent, read through silhouette. In the evening the light passes through the thin wings and they begin to glow from within in a soft milky tone with the veins showing through. Not a single hard highlight: the glow reads as a property of the butterflies themselves, not as backlighting.
LC0093.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, double-height living rooms, winter gardens, wedding and banquet halls, children's spaces. Soft diffuse light suits zones where people spend time.
LC0093.style: Art Nouveau and romantic classicism: the butterfly as a classic motif of fragility. The message is light and bright — a piece for a space that wants to give pleasure.
LC0093.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of figures, the range of wing forms and the tone of the glow are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a split mineral. The facets meet at random angles, without symmetry — the way a stone looks when it has been broken rather than cut. The author deliberately refuses jewellers' regularity: what is valued here is the rock, not the workmanship.

The crystals hang at varied levels, bunching into a dense mass in places and falling away alone, far down or to the side, in others. The depth of colour depends on thickness: the more massive, the more saturated.

By day it is a scatter of minerals in the air — turquoise with a greenish cast, read through volume and refraction. In the evening the light enters the body and refracts on every facet, filling the colour from within: in the thick passages it deepens to emerald, in the thin ones it lightens almost to clear. Not one source is visible directly — a vein lit from inside the rock.
LC0094.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, spas and pools, double-height living rooms. Saturated colour needs a neutral setting.
LC0094.style: Organic minimalism and geological aesthetics: the stone exactly as it is. The message is collector-minded — a piece for someone who values the material.
LC0094.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of crystals, the calibres and the depth of the turquoise tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about tearing. The fragments are torn and crushed: ragged edges, deep creases, not one correct geometric line. The object must read as what is left after a tear, not as something assembled — and every decision serves that.
The fragments hang at varied levels, turned at random, arranged in no order at all. The calibres differ, from large down to fine crumbs: a scatter always sorts by mass.

By day it is an explosion of foil — gold mixed with matte silver, a random pattern, nothing predictable. In the evening not every fragment glows but one in five: the crumpled gold reflects the light in bands along the folds, the silver subdues it, and most of the mass stays dark. It is precisely that selectiveness that creates the impression of movement — a field of shards with occasional flares.
LC0095.whereItWorks: Generous rooms with high ceilings — lobbies, atria, gallery spaces, double-height living rooms. A scatter needs air: pressed together, the composition turns into a heap.
LC0095.style: Contemporary art and brutalist luxury: the aesthetics of destruction, executed expensively. The message is bold — a piece for an interior unafraid of being abrupt.
LC0095.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of fragments and the ratio of gold to silver are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a leaf that has already lain a while. Each element is slightly crumpled and rolled at the edge — not flat, but the shape a leaf takes after a day on the ground. The author takes not the moment of falling but what comes after: leaf-fall already settled.

The leaves hang at varied levels, turned at random, bunching in places and flying off alone far from the mass in others. Warm gold with patina is mixed with cool matte silver — a difference in age, not in species.

By day it is a leaf-fall caught in a frame: the crumpled surfaces give ragged highlights, and the composition shimmers as the viewer moves. In the evening the gold leaves reflect the light and flare warm, the silver ones diffuse it and stay subdued. A heap of leaves with light breaking out from beneath.
LC0096.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, stairwells, double-height living rooms, winter gardens. The scattered elements extend beyond the main envelope: allow clearance to the sides.
LC0096.style: Organic modernism and autumn classicism: fading as an aesthetic. The message is melancholy and warm — a piece for an interior that loves the season.
LC0096.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of leaves and the ratio of gold to silver are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an armful. The stems spread from a round base outward and downward, each bending its own way: not a bouquet set in a vase but an armful thrown open in every direction. Between them runs a dense fringe of straight rods — what remains of the stems that have no flower.
The cups with their ragged wavy rims are open like a poppy, or like a flower that has just unfurled. The tone is pomegranate-crimson, almost opaque in places, lightening to pink in others.

By day the composition reads as a bouquet — saturated colour on gold, dense and painterly. In the evening the light passes through the body of the colour and the petals fill from within: the tone becomes deeper and hotter than by daylight, while the stems pick up the reflection and glow as fine lines. An armful of embers on gold legs.
LC0097.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, reception rooms, restaurant floors, boudoirs. The saturated tone needs a calm backdrop: against a coloured wall the flower is lost.
LC0097.style: Art Nouveau and romantic classicism: the flower as the principal subject of an interior. The message is passionate and warm — a piece for a space with character.
LC0097.madeToOrder: The base diameter, the number of flowers, the stem lengths and the depth of the pomegranate tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a thicket growing downward. From a round mirrored base runs a dense fringe of fine rods, and monstera leaves sit along its lower edge, forming a wreath. The middle stays open: you can see the rods receding, and the thicket reads as having a root.
The leaf form is taken almost literally — a broad plate with deep splits, through-holes and drawn venation. Warm gold with patina is mixed with cool oxidised turquoise: one plant at two ages.

By day it is a metal thicket on the ceiling — dense, graphic, living on the reflections in the mirrored base. In the evening the light emerges through the splits in the plates and lights the neighbouring leaves from below: a warm glow stands inside the wreath, the rods reflect and multiply it upward toward the base, and the outer surfaces stay subdued. A bush lit from within.
LC0098.whereItWorks: Living rooms, winter gardens, spas, restaurant floors, reception rooms. Ceiling mounting needs no height — the piece suits places where a pendant is impossible.
LC0098.style: Tropical modernism and mid-century: fifties botany without the kitsch. The message is buoyant — a piece for an interior that loves greenery.
LC0098.madeToOrder: The base diameter, the number of leaves and the ratio of gold to turquoise are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a ripple on metal. The line rises and falls in two crests with a trough between them — a wave set by the length of the suspensions. Each narrow curved tongue is turned on its own axis, so the mass never reads as flat: it has depth and shimmer.
Cool silver and warm gold are intermixed, the surface polished. The upper part of the composition stays almost dark — only the hatching of cables.

By day it is a ripple: the mirrored tongues catch daylight and invert it, and the pattern changes with every step the viewer takes. In the evening the light rolls out along the full length of each element and a glowing rib lights up — gold gives warm flares, silver cool ones. A wave full of sparks.
LC0099.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, lobbies, meeting rooms. The wave pattern is calculated for the length of the table.
LC0099.style: Contemporary Art Deco and glamorous minimalism: two metals, no colour at all. The message is representative — a piece for a table where people are received.
LC0099.madeToOrder: The length, the wave pattern, the number of elements and the ratio of gold to silver are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about density. Hundreds of drops hang almost touching, in layers — a mass so thick that it stops reading as individual elements. The upper zone is left empty, only the hatching of cables; everything gathers in the lower half with a ragged edge.
Each drop is twisted on its axis: a sharp tip below, an open hollow at the middle. The thickness works as a lens, and once the light has entered the mass it never leaves in a straight line.

By day it is a wall of ice — clear, dense, read through highlights and the refraction of daylight. In the evening the light passes from element to element, refracting at every twist, and the source cannot be found: the volume itself glows. Because the mass is dense the illumination comes out even and diffuse, without a single hard highlight. A downpour frozen in the air.
LC0100.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, double-height living rooms, banquet halls. Even glare-free light is comfortable where people spend time beneath it.
LC0100.style: Contemporary classicism and minimalism: mass instead of pattern. The message is monumental — a piece that works through volume, not detail.
LC0100.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the density of the array and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a cave. A stalactite grows drop by drop over thousands of years — a form made entirely of time. The upper edge of the composition is level, the lower one wavy: a section through a cave where growth has been uneven.
Each faceted drop with its slight twist hangs on its own rod with a glowing point at the end, the rods varying in length. Bare rods are set between them — they work as hatching and give depth.

By day the composition reads graphically, through hatching alone: clear forms, fine lines, almost a technical drawing. In the evening the light travels from the point straight into the body, refracts on every rib and flares at the base of the drop, while the rod itself stays invisible. Because the array is dense, the light passes from drop to drop and the whole volume begins to glow — a row of icicles hung above the table.
LC0101.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, reception areas. The wavy lower edge sets varying heights above the table: the piece goes where people sit beneath it.
LC0101.style: Organic minimalism and contemporary classicism: a geological form without decoration. The message is restrained — a piece for an interior that avoids ornament.
LC0101.madeToOrder: The length, the number of drops, the length of the rods and the calibres are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the berry and the thorn. Thousands of faceted spheres form a soft pale mass, among which narrow bronze petals with sharp tips are scattered. Berry and claw in a single thicket — the way any real bush is built.

The spheres hang densely, in layers, with a ragged lower edge; the metal elements are turned in different directions and work as dark accents in a pale field. Above, a net of fine cables with point lights holds the composition.

By day it is a cloud of berries — pale, sparkling, with a few dark strokes inside it. In the evening the light passes through the clusters and breaks on every facet: the mass sparkles and loses its source entirely, while the bronze petals reflect it directionally and give rare warm flares. The contrast is set by temperature — a cool white scatter with hot strokes inside it. A thicket full of sparks.
LC0102.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, banquet and wedding halls, double-height living rooms, atria. Light that breaks up gives plenty of glare: this is a ceremonial piece, not a working one.
LC0102.style: Grand classicism and Art Deco: the scatter as a symbol of abundance. The message is festive — a piece for a space where people celebrate.
LC0102.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of spheres, the share of metal elements and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same spinning top, but in a dense array. Here the elements stand close together, layered, with a wavy lower edge: not a swarm but a mass. A flattened disc at the middle, a short cone above, a long sharp spike below — a top stopped in the air, multiplied by the hundred.
Above the mass runs a net of bare cables with point lights, receding to the ceiling: it adds volume and stops the composition reading as a flat band.

By day the object is all but invisible — entirely clear, it shows itself only in highlights. In the evening a double rhythm establishes itself: the discs diffuse the light and flare along their rims in a horizontal layer of reflections, while the spikes carry it downward and light up at their very tips in a vertical rain. A volume filled with hanging lights on two levels.
LC0103.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, lobbies, meeting rooms. A dense mass gives more light than a sparse composition of the same length.
LC0103.style: Contemporary classicism and precise minimalism: geometry instead of ornament. The message is austere — a piece for an interior that holds its form.
LC0103.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the length of the spikes and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about dropped fabric. The panel is crushed and folded in large pleats — the form matter takes when you let it go. The author fixes chance: the pattern of the folds cannot be repeated twice, and that is the whole piece.

Close parallel ribbing runs across the entire surface, with a fine gold thread carrying point lights along the rim. The elements are large — each several times the size of an ordinary pendant — and hang at varied heights, in places running one into another.

By day it is fabric frozen in the air: the ribbing catches the light in bands, the folds give real chiaroscuro, and the surface reads as volume. In the evening the light runs along the gold rims and enters the ribbing, scattering across it in strokes — some passages burn brightly, others fall into shadow. The trace left by light rather than the fabric itself.
LC0104.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, double-height living rooms, long dining halls. It exists in two formats: an elongated horizontal band and a multi-tier volumetric composition.
LC0104.style: Contemporary sculpture and Baroque drapery in a minimalist reading: the fold as a classic motif without classic decoration. The message is expressive — a piece for a space that wants a gesture.
LC0104.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of panels, the pattern of the folds and the number of lights along the rim are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a summer evening. The firefly is the only insect people find beautiful, and only because it glows. The author builds the whole piece on that: the sources are hidden in the rods, yet it seems the swarm itself is alight.

Rods of varying length hang in dense hatching and set the volume — some gold, some clear. Hundreds of small winged figures are set among them, unevenly distributed: denser below, sparser above, with individuals straying far from the mass.

By day the composition reads graphically — a rain of lines in which the figures are barely distinguishable. In the evening every rod ends in a point that flares as a star, and the thin amber wings transmit that light and fill with it. The hatching stays cool and almost invisible, and in the dark all you see is a swarm of fireflies over water.
LC0105.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, stairwells, panoramic living rooms, winter gardens. Vertical hatching works with height: it establishes a volume that a low room does not have.
LC0105.style: Art Nouveau and natural romanticism: the insect as a precious thing, light as its property. The message is lyrical — a piece that brings back a memory.
LC0105.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of figures, the length of the rods and the tone of the wings are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a creature without a skeleton. The jellyfish is a body held together by water; taken out of its medium it stops being a form at all. The author gives it its medium back: a vertical rain of small pendants hangs around the figures, and the shoal exists inside it.

The dome is faceted, assembled from triangular plates with visible ribs — like a geodesic dome or a carapace. The tentacles do not hang straight down but stream sideways and below: the jellyfish is being carried by a current, and you can see it.

By day it is a shoal of creatures suspended in the air — amber bells with runs and patches of differing density, a fine clear fringe beneath them. In the evening the light passes through the amber, the domes glow from within with their net of ribs showing through, the tentacles pick it up and carry it their whole length, flaring at the tips, while the rain around catches the reflections and shimmers. An immersion into deep water.
LC0106.whereItWorks: Generous volumes — atria, lobbies, pools and spas, double-height living rooms, children's spaces. The streaming tentacles need height: the space beneath must be clear.
LC0106.style: Marine Art Nouveau and contemporary sculptural installation. The message is narrative, almost theatrical — a piece that turns a room into a stage.
LC0106.madeToOrder: The number of figures, the calibre of the domes, the length of the tentacles and the density of the rain are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a caught drop. Every inverted drop with its sharp tip hangs on a fine hook bent like a question mark — a thing that ought to be falling turns out to be suspended. The whole tension of the composition rests on that.
The upper zone is left empty: only the hatching of threads, with small beads hanging between them — gold and cool blue. The mass of drops gathers in the lower third, with a wavy lower edge.

By day the composition reads graphically — hatched threads and clear forms, almost a technical drawing. In the evening the light passes through the body of each drop and bursts out at the tip as a bright point, the gold hook above it picks up the reflection and outlines it from above, and the beads give scattered sparks between the main elements. Only the glowing drops remain, hanging from gold loops.
LC0107.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, lobbies, meeting rooms. The light gathers into points below: the piece lights the table, not the room.
LC0107.style: Jewellery modernism and contemporary classicism: the suspension as a subject in its own right. The message is refined — a piece for a table where people sit close.
LC0107.madeToOrder: The length, the number of drops, the palette of the beads and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a rain of stones. The curtain is not regular: some strands descend deep, others break off high, and the spacing of the beads differs on each. The top is level, the lower edge ragged — this is how something heavier than water falls, at differing speeds.

The main mass is a subdued green, with colourless clear beads set among it. The calibres vary — from large spheres to fine crumbs — and that too is about falling: large things fall differently from small ones.

By day it is a green veil — dense, subdued, working through colour and reflection. In the evening the light runs down the strands from above and enters every bead: the facets break it and scatter it in sparks, the green ones fill with a deep tone, the colourless flare white. The light passes through several layers and loses its source — the whole volume glows. A rain of precious stones.
LC0108.whereItWorks: Generous volumes — atria, lobbies, stairwells, banquet and wedding halls. The curtain is installed without interfering with the walls and covers tall openings easily.
LC0108.style: Art Deco and Eastern opulence: stones on a strand as a classic of formal decoration. The message is generous — a piece for a space that celebrates.
LC0108.madeToOrder: The overall size, the strand spacing, the palette of the beads and the calibres are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a scree slope. Large crumpled stones hang almost touching, at varied levels, and the mass reads as continuous and heavy — a rockfall suspended in the air a moment before it lands. The density here is not decorative but semantic: scree is never sparse.
Every stone is pressed and folded in its own way, none repeating its neighbour. The polish is unbroken, without matte areas, so the object works purely through reflection.

By day it is a cluster of gold boulders — heavy, rich, read through ragged highlights on the crumpled surfaces. In the evening the light emerges only in the gaps between the stones, strikes the gold flanks and reflects repeatedly, boulder to boulder: the mass fills from within and looks red-hot. Rock just taken out of the furnace.
LC0109.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, lobbies, private studies, bars, showrooms. A dense heavy mass needs height and clear surroundings — everything else nearby should stay silent.
LC0109.style: Brutalist luxury and contemporary Art Deco: a mass of gold instead of filigree. The message is direct and generous — a piece for an interior unembarrassed by force.
LC0109.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of stones, the calibres and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about what is inside. The oyster is a thing whose entire value is hidden: a rough layered shell outside, a nacreous layer with speckling and marbling within. The author opens the valves and lays them out on the wall face outward.
Valves of varying calibre lie in a dense circle: large at the centre, small at the edges, all turned differently, so the pale insets face different ways and the composition reads as volumetric.

By day the piece rests on three contrasts: the dark rough shell, the pale smooth core and the fine gold line along the rim. In the evening the backlight emerges from behind the valves and traces the gold rim, while the nacreous insets reflect it softly, without glare. A colony lit from beneath.
LC0110.whereItWorks: Feature walls — halls, private living rooms, spas, restaurants, reception areas. The circular layout needs a clear wall: neighbouring objects break the form.
LC0110.style: Marine Art Nouveau and natural opulence: the shell as a symbol of hidden value. The message is tactile — a piece you want to touch.
LC0110.madeToOrder: The area of the layout, the number of valves, the calibres and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the nugget. The face is polished to a mirror while the sides and back drift into dark patina — each stone reads as an ingot lifted from the ground and burnished on one side only. This is not an ornament but a find: the piece shows both the gold and the rock it came out of.

The stones are laid out in an elongated horizontal group: large at the centre, small at the edges, with breaks and clusterings. The composition is deliberately asymmetrical — it has not been arranged, it has been poured out.

By day it is a scatter of nuggets: gold on crumpled folds gives complex warm highlights, while the dark patina around the edges outlines each stone and separates it from its neighbour. In the evening, under directional light, the composition flares as a whole; under diffuse light it stays calm and almost graphic. Gold found in the rock.
LC0111.whereItWorks: Feature walls — halls, private living rooms, studies, reception areas, bars. The effect depends on directional light: allow for a track or spots.
LC0111.style: Brutalist luxury and contemporary art: the precious alongside the unworked. The message is direct and masculine — a piece for an interior with a strong character.
LC0111.madeToOrder: The area of the layout, the number of stones, the calibres and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about mercury. Crumpled stones of irregular geometry, each with a pressed-in surface — as though fingers had been drawn across something soft — are covered in unbroken mirrored silver without a single matte area. The object has no appearance of its own: it shows only what is around it.
Stones of varying calibre are laid out in a free circle, denser at the centre and sparser toward the edge. No pattern and no order — a natural distribution, like shingle on a shore.

By day it is a scatter of mercury drops: the mirrored surface catches the light of the room and inverts it in the crumpled folds, so each stone acquires its own complex highlight that shifts at the slightest movement of the viewer. In the evening, under directional light, the composition becomes a gathering of mirrors throwing light across the wall — and the wall comes alive.
LC0112.whereItWorks: Feature walls — halls, living rooms, stair landings, reception areas, dressing rooms. The composition depends on its surroundings: it is hung where there is something to reflect.
LC0112.style: Contemporary art and minimalism: an object with no image of its own. The message is conceptual — a piece for an interior that values the idea.
LC0112.madeToOrder: The area of the layout, the number of stones, the calibres and the character of the mirrored finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the valve. In a scallop the fan pattern is not decoration but structure: the ribs hold the thin valve together. The author takes that logic — here the ribbing works too, and what it carries is light.
The elements are turned in different directions: some lie almost flat, others stand on edge. The bowl is shallow, denser at the centre and thinned at the edges.

By day it is a scatter of shells below the ceiling — white, matte, read through the light and shade across the fan of ribbing. In the evening the light from the gold heart spreads along the ribs toward the wavy rim, and the whole structure of the valve emerges against the light. The glowing centres face different ways, and the composition looks different from every point — a field of luminous fans.
LC0113.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, double-height living rooms, dining rooms, spas and pools. Because the elements face every direction the piece has no "front": it is placed where people walk around it.
LC0113.style: Marine Art Nouveau and Mediterranean classicism: the shell as one of the oldest decorative motifs. The message is light and coastal — a piece for a bright interior near water.
LC0113.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the calibres and the tone of the glow are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about soft and hard. Rounded scaled buds — and straight rods set obliquely between them. Two forms with nothing in common: one grew, the other was drawn. The author sets them against each other on purpose.

The buds form a dense lower mass with a ragged upper contour, a few rising high above it. The rods, by contrast, pierce the upper zone at varied angles and work as hard graphics against the rounded forms.

By day it is a botanical study laid over a drafting grid: white matte cones and gold lines. In the evening the light lives in two places at once — it emerges from under the scales, lighting the buds from within in a warm milky tone, and runs as a line along the rods, turning them into glowing strokes. Diffuse and linear glow together: a field of fruit stitched through with gold.
LC0114.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, lobbies, stairwells, restaurant floors. The rods extend beyond the envelope of the main mass: allow clearance to the sides.
LC0114.style: Contemporary sculpture and Bauhaus graphics: nature against geometry. The message is intellectual — a piece for an interior that likes contradiction.
LC0114.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of buds and the length and number of rods are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about something grown rather than assembled. The branches curve in a broad loop in the horizontal plane, divide, and on every stalk sits its own rosette at its own angle. The composition reads as something that developed by itself — not one position is repeated.
The rosettes, with fine radial pleating and a slightly rolled, uneven rim, differ a little from one another in calibre and inclination. The fibrous texture gives the material visible veining.

By day it is a field of paper flowers on a gold loop — bright, light, almost weightless. In the evening light from the nodes of the branches passes through the thin structure and the discs begin to glow from within, entire, with their veining showing; the gold shows through them as a warm thread. Not one direct source is visible — a cloud of luminous rosettes.
LC0115.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, double-height living rooms, dining rooms, banquet and wedding halls. The horizontal loop reads from above and from the side: the piece is hung over a table or a gathering zone.
LC0115.style: Art Nouveau and romantic classicism: flowering as the subject, gold as the setting. The message is festive and bright — a piece for a ceremonial space.
LC0115.madeToOrder: The overall diameter, the number of rosettes, the calibres and the finish of the branches are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a gaze from the depths. A large disc with dense radial pleating — hundreds of fine petals running from the centre to an uneven rim — holds a round mirror at its middle. The reflection is set inside a living form: whoever looks sees themselves inside an anemone.

Beside it two smaller satellite discs without mirrors, and around them crumpled "stones" with a mirrored glaze — some gold, some chrome. They scatter from the centre in uneven groups and give the whole composition movement.

By day the object works as a sculptural mirror with satellites: a deep tone running from charcoal grey to plum, coppery shifts along the petal rims, mirror and glaze catching the room. In the evening the backlight emerges along the contours of the discs, brings out the relief of the pleating and reflects in the glaze of the stones — a colony lit on the wall.
LC0116.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, dressing rooms, bathrooms, boudoirs, private living rooms. The mirror is functional, so mounting height is set by the user, not by the composition.
LC0116.style: Marine Art Nouveau and contemporary decorative sculpture. The message is intimate — a piece for a space where people are alone with themselves.
LC0116.madeToOrder: The mirror diameter, the number of satellite discs, the number of stones and the glaze palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the gills beneath a cap. The pattern radiating from the centre is taken from a mushroom — from the part of it people never look at: gills exist precisely not to be examined. The author turns the thing over and makes the underside the face.

The discs hang almost flat, in layers, densely — the caps overlap with almost no gaps, and from below the field reads as continuous. The composition is drawn out as a rectangle: not a cloud but a canopy.

By day it is a colony seen from beneath — a smoky grey-beige tone, the ribbing read through light and shade. In the evening a gold heart lights up at the centre of each disc, the light spreads along the rays, and every cap glows radially, from a bright centre to a subdued rim. Hundreds of radial glows give an even warm field of luminous rosettes.
LC0117.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, dining rooms, meeting rooms, panoramic living rooms, reception areas. A continuous field gives even light: the piece works as principal illumination, not as an accent.
LC0117.style: Organic modernism and mid-century: a natural form in a rectangular grid. The message is calm and warm — a piece for working and dining spaces.
LC0117.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of discs, the calibres and the depth of the smoky tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about descent. The colour changes with height: clear and colourless above, drifting into smoky blue lower down, near-graphite at the very bottom. The transition is gradual, without boundaries — this is how light diminishes in a body of water, and it diminishes here in the same way.
Clusters of differing height and diameter form a dense diamond-shaped volume, broad at the middle and pointed at top and bottom. The whole mass reads as one body, not as a set of parts.

By day it is organ pipes suspended below the ceiling — vertical hatching, austere and resonant. In the evening the upper tiers glow bright and white while the lower ones absorb the light and stay cold: from below the composition looks like a cloud lit only at the top. An iceberg lit from its summit.
LC0118.whereItWorks: Generous volumes — atria, lobbies, stairwells, double-height living rooms, banquet halls. The gradient exists only across a substantial vertical: in a low room it has no space to unfold.
LC0118.style: Contemporary minimalism and Nordic aesthetics: the vertical, the cold and monotony as devices. The message is monumental — architecture rather than decoration.
LC0118.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of clusters, the element lengths and the depth of the tinting are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about two temperaments. Soft and sharp meet here: broad crumpled caps with wavy rims and long faceted spikes drawn downward. The author mixes them without system — cap, spike, cap again — and the composition keeps changing its mood.
The bowl is shallow, denser at the centre, sparser at the edges, with single spikes descending below. No element repeats its neighbour in form or in orientation.

By day the object is all but invisible: clear and colourless, it shows itself only in highlights, and in a bright room it is easy to miss. In the evening the difference between the forms comes fully into play — the caps gather the light and diffuse it into a broad soft patch, the spikes carry it their whole length and flare at the tip. A gathering of luminous forms suspended in emptiness.
LC0119.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, zones above a table. Transparency needs a dark or saturated backdrop: against a white ceiling the piece is lost.
LC0119.style: Contemporary classicism and minimalism: contrast of form instead of colour. The message is spare — a piece for an interior built on nuance.
LC0119.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the ratio of caps to spikes and the suspension lengths are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same wreath, but shedding downward. The direction is reversed: instead of wind carrying feathers sideways, weight and fall do the work. The stream separates below, thinning as it goes, and the last feathers hang alone far from the mass.
The palette is cool — subdued moss green, silver-grey, matte white, with gold inclusions around the ring. The transition between tones is gradual, with no boundaries.

By day the panel reads as graphics: the worked shafts and barbs give a continuously ribbed surface that catches the light in bands. In the evening the ring lights up along its contour while the falling feathers stay dark — and the movement becomes more legible than it is by daylight. Light here works as direction rather than decoration.
LC0120.whereItWorks: Feature walls — halls, living rooms, stair landings, reception areas, private studies. The vertical shedding needs clearance below the ring.
LC0120.style: Nordic modernism and contemporary classicism: a cool palette, a natural motif. The message is restrained — a piece for an interior that dislikes volume.
LC0120.madeToOrder: The wreath diameter, the number of feathers, the length of the fall and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a wreath coming apart. The main mass is laid in a dense overlapping ring, but on the right the feathers break away one after another: first in a group, then in pairs, then alone. The last of them — the palest, almost white — hang far from the wreath and act as the point the eye is led toward.
A closed form with one side opened always reads as a process. The author uses that: the wreath is not broken, it is flying away.

The palette is warm and autumnal — copper, burnt bronze, dark ochre, with gold and near-white feathers across the field. By day the panel reads through colour and gradient: the ribbed surface of close barbs catches the light in bands. In the evening the backlight emerges along the rims and traces every feather with a fine gold line — the mass gains volume, and the departing tail lights up separately from the ring.
LC0121.whereItWorks: Feature walls — halls, stair landings, private living rooms, reception areas, gallery spaces. An open composition needs room to the right: the tail must run into empty space rather than into a corner.
LC0121.style: Art Deco and autumn classicism: the feather as a motif of opulence, movement as the subject. The message is poetic — a picture-piece for a wall that leads the eye.
LC0121.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of feathers, the length of the departing tail and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same device, opened out. The feathers are laid not in a ring but in a spiral: a dense coil above unwinds downward and runs off to the right as a tail, shedding feathers along the way. The last ones hang alone, apart from the mass — movement shown together with its fading.

The palette is olive and gold: from subdued moss green above to warm ochre and old gold in the tail. The transition is gradual, without boundaries, so the spiral reads as a single gesture rather than two halves.

By day the panel works through silhouette and gradient: the ribbed surface of close barbs catches the light in bands and changes with the sun. In the evening gold lines light up along the rims and the spiral becomes volumetric — you can see the layers, the overlaps and the way the tail loses density toward its end.
LC0122.whereItWorks: Feature walls — halls, stair landings, private living rooms, reception areas, gallery spaces. The open form sits well on a long wall and along a stair flight.
LC0122.style: Art Nouveau and contemporary decorative sculpture: movement inscribed into a plane. The message is dynamic — a piece for a wall that should lead the eye.
LC0122.madeToOrder: The overall size of the spiral, the number of feathers, the palette and the lighting scheme are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about plumage. The feathers are laid overlapping in a ring, their tips facing outward and inward at once: the outer row sets a radiant contour, the inner one closes the middle, leaving a dark opening at the centre. The piece reads both as a wreath and as an open wing curled into a circle.
