The palette is built on transition: one part of the wreath in deep blue-green with a metallic sheen, the opposite in warm ochre and gold, with a gradual flow between them. The colour changes around the circle exactly as it does in the plumage of a real bird — not in patches but by shift.

By day the panel works through pure graphics and colour: the finely worked barbs give a ribbed surface that catches the light in bands. In the evening the backlight emerges along the rims and traces every feather with a gold line — the mass gains volume, and you can see where the feathers lie two deep and where only one.
LC0123.whereItWorks: Feature walls — halls, living rooms, private studies, reception areas. The round form asks for a clear wall with no neighbouring objects: the panel works as the sole object.
LC0123.style: Art Deco and jewellery modernism: the feather as a classic motif of opulence. The message is decorative and expensive — a picture-piece rather than a luminaire.
LC0123.madeToOrder: The wreath diameter, the number of feathers, the palette and the lighting scheme are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a knot. Broad ribbons are rolled into loops and figures of eight, twisted freely, each in its own way: some form a closed ring, others break off in a sharp end. The incompleteness is deliberate — a knot still being tied.
The reverse of the ribbons is gold, the face white, with faceted clear fragments set between them. The pyramid is dense at the centre, thinned at the edges, with single elements descending below.

By day it is a tangle of ribbons — white with gold and cold sparks, plastic and volumetric. In the evening three finishes give three different glows within one mass: the light strikes the gold linings and emerges in warm patches, the faceted fragments pick it up and scatter it in hard white sparks, and the white face stays cool and matte. A knot with gold burning inside it.
LC0124.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, lobbies, stairwells, banquet halls. The pyramid needs height — pressed to the ceiling it loses its volume.
LC0124.style: Contemporary Art Deco and Hollywood glamour: ribbon, gold, shine. The message is dressy — a piece for a space that likes an effect.
LC0124.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the ratio of finishes and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a shell that holds light. A broad bowl with a wavy rim and a deep dent at its centre: copper-rose and calm outside, mirrored within. One form, two opposite roles — restrained without, hot within.
The elements hang at varied levels, tilted at different angles, overlapping in places, but with enough air between them: the mass never congeals.

By day it is a cluster of copper forms — warm, quiet, working through soft reflections. In the evening a point lights up inside each shell: the light reflects off the mirrored layer, takes on copper and spreads across the whole inner surface, while the outer face stays rose and even. The mouths face different ways, and the composition looks different from every point.
LC0125.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms, zones above a long table. The varied tilts mean the piece is best assembled for a specific plan.
LC0125.style: Warm Art Deco and contemporary classicism: copper and rose gold rather than yellow. The message is intimate and rich — a piece for a warm palette.
LC0125.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the depth of the copper tone and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about living fabric. The spacing on every strand is different — in places the elements sit close, elsewhere long empty stretches remain. The irregularity is deliberate: the curtain must read as cloth, not as a grille, and cloth always has gatherings and gaps.
The elements are tumbled and smooth, without facets: copper-rose, clear, with small gold spheres between them. Not one repeated rhythm.

By day the curtain works as a translucent screen — it subdues the view without closing it, and lives on the reflections of daylight. In the evening the light runs down the strands from above and enters every element: the clear ones flare as white sparks, the rose ones fill with a honeyed tone, the gold spheres give sharp star-points. Moving air makes the plane shimmer and shift — a wall of hanging lights that never stands still.
LC0126.whereItWorks: Zoning and decoration — dividing zones in a living room, a screen at a window, a backdrop in a restaurant, the treatment of a stairwell opening, wedding and banquet halls. The suspended structure is installed without interfering with the walls.
LC0126.style: Art Deco and Eastern opulence: strands with stones as the oldest way of dressing an opening. The message is festive — a piece for a space where things happen.
LC0126.madeToOrder: The curtain dimensions, the strand spacing, the set of elements and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the surface of water seen from below. The plates hang almost horizontally, in layers, and the composition is gathered into a broad oval with a sparse centre — this is how water looks when you are beneath it.

The whole surface carries the texture of ripples: close undulating folds of the kind wind leaves behind. The form is oval with uneven edges — no plate repeats its neighbour, because ripples do not repeat.

By day it is a set of ice floes suspended below the ceiling: saturated turquoise, clear and opaque passages intermixed, the piece read through colour. In the evening light is fed into the rim and spreads along the ribbing, so the ripples begin to glow in strokes, while the thickness gathers the light at the edges and traces every plate with a bright line. The gold fixings stay warm points in a cold field. Water lit from the depths.
LC0127.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, pools and spas, panoramic living rooms, dining rooms. The horizontal set reads only from below: the piece is hung over an area where people stand or sit.
LC0127.style: Marine Art Nouveau and organic modernism: water as motif, colour as argument. The message is cool and refreshing — a piece for an interior in a cold palette.
LC0127.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of plates, the depth of the turquoise tone and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about two directions. Two forms work in opposite ways here: the bells open upward and give their light to the ceiling, the icicles hang down and carry it to the table. One object lights both up and down, and that is not a technical solution but a subject.

The bells are gathered into a dense group at the centre — a field of flowers or a rank of gramophone horns. Icicles with ragged fire-polished surfaces form a fringe at the edges. The tone is amber at varying densities: almost colourless in places, thickening to honey in others.

By day it is a thicket of clear flowers — warm, translucent, read against the light. In the evening the light from deep in the bells rises and settles on the ceiling as a soft warm patch, while the icicles pick it up and carry it down, flaring at their tips. A field from which sparks are falling.
LC0128.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, lobbies, meeting rooms. Light reflected upward makes the composition a source of general illumination, not merely an accent.
LC0128.style: Art Nouveau and warm contemporary classicism: a botanical motif in an amber palette. The message is hospitable — a piece for a table where people gather.
LC0128.madeToOrder: The length, the number of bells, the length of the icicles and the depth of the amber tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about rain. Fine rods of varying length, each with a large drop at its end, stand in a dense array — you see through them as through a downpour. Hundreds of elements almost touching: the composition does not depict rain, it reproduces it.

The top is level, the centre deeply sagging — the silhouette is funnel-like, as though the mass were drawn down by its own weight. The drops are elongated and heavy, with a perfectly smooth surface: the shape water takes as it falls.

By day it is pure hatching — vertical lines read graphically, almost a technical drawing. In the evening the rod works as a lightguide: it stays almost invisible while the drop at its end flares. The composition becomes a volume filled with hanging luminous points at varied depths — a downpour with its movement taken away.
LC0129.whereItWorks: Generous volumes — atria, lobbies, stairwells, double-height living rooms, banquet halls. The depth of the array needs height: in a low room the funnel does not read.
LC0129.style: Contemporary classicism and minimalism: the vertical instead of ornament. The message is ceremonial and austere — a piece for a formal space without excess.
LC0129.madeToOrder: The overall size, the rod lengths, the calibre of the drops and the density of the array are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a moment. Every element is inclined the same way at the same angle — like grass laid down by wind. That single device turns the object into an event: the composition reads not as a thing but as the instant in which it was caught.
The line sags at the centre and rises at the ends — the arc of a crest. Above it runs a net of bare cables with small glowing points: spray above the wave, broken away from the mass.

By day it is a crest caught in a frame: white feathers mixed with bronze, the pure graphics of the inclination. In the evening the light grazes along each feather and emphasises the angle — the white ones glow evenly, the bronze give warm highlights, the points above scatter as sparks. A wave lit from within.
LC0130.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, reception areas. The inclination sets a direction: the piece is oriented along the line of sight from the entrance.
LC0130.style: Organic modernism and contemporary classicism: movement as the only decoration. The message is dynamic — a piece for a space that does not stand still.
LC0130.madeToOrder: The length, the arc pattern, the number of elements and the ratio of white to bronze are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same shoal, but moving in one direction. There is no ring here — a dense horizontal mass, hundreds of individuals in tiers, all heading the same way. The shoal is not defending itself; it is migrating.
The upper zone of the composition is left empty: only the net of cables. The device makes the shoal appear to be moving under its own power rather than hanging.

By day it is graphics on the ceiling — narrow silhouettes read through outline, a silvery subdued mass. In the evening it turns out there are markedly fewer gold fish than clear ones, and they read as individuals that have caught the sun: they light up whole while the rest give only a flare along the rim. This is exactly how a real shoal looks in a body of water — a handful flare, thousands stay shadow.
LC0131.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, pools and spas, panoramic living rooms. The composition is drawn along one axis, so it is oriented along the main line of movement.
LC0131.style: Marine modernism and contemporary installation: natural behaviour reproduced precisely. The message is calm and narrative — a piece for a space people move through.
LC0131.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the share of gold and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about undergrowth. The pods are gathered in groups of three to five, in the manner of an inflorescence — neither singly nor as a solid mass. That is a botanical principle: a plant always grows in nodes, and the author keeps to it.

The column is uneven: it thickens in places and almost breaks off in others. Bare cables with small white beads run between the clusters, working as hatching. The vertical reads as grown rather than assembled.

By day it is a botanical study — milky white mixed with clear green from grass to olive, a clean graphic form. In the evening the sources sit in the nodes rather than in each element, and the glow is distributed in patches: the white pods diffuse it milkily, the green ones fill with a grassy tone. This is how sunlight breaks through real undergrowth — unevenly.
LC0132.whereItWorks: A vertical format — stairwells, atria, double-height living rooms, winter gardens. It needs height rather than width: the composition builds downward in a single stream.
LC0132.style: Organic modernism and botanical aesthetics: the plant without stylisation. The message is fresh and alive — a piece for an interior that loves greenery.
LC0132.madeToOrder: The overall height, the number of clusters and the ratio of white to green are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same galaxy taken at scale. Here the dishes are gathered not into a sparse group but into a dense multi-tier mass — several dozen elements, broad at the top, narrowing below.

Density changes the piece in substance: where the smaller version left emptiness between dishes, here one overlaps another and the light passes through two or three layers in a row. The spirals of bubbles lay over one another and give a depth no single element possesses.

By day it is a cloud of clear forms — many-layered, read through highlights, almost colourless. In the evening a sky full of galaxies opens from below: hundreds of glowing spirals at varied distances, the near ones sharp, the far ones blurred. From above, only the net of cables receding to the ceiling. A star chart hung overhead.
LC0133.whereItWorks: Generous rooms with high ceilings — atria, lobbies, double-height living rooms, stairwells. The layering exists only when seen from below at a distance.
LC0133.style: Contemporary sculptural installation with a scientific motif. The message is large-scale — a piece for a space that should astonish.
LC0133.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the number of tiers and the density of the spirals are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a galaxy in your hand. Thousands of the finest bubbles are sealed within the body of each dish, gathered into a spiral around the centre. This is not decoration but structure: a spiral of air fixed in a clear mass, repeating the pattern by which star systems are built.

The dishes are irregular and asymmetrical, each with its own geometry. There are few of them, they hang at varied heights and are tilted at different angles. The voids between them are as much part of the composition as the elements.

By day it is a set of clear bowls: the spirals of bubbles are visible against the light and the piece reads through detail. In the evening a point lights up at the centre of each dish, the light scatters along the spiral and a luminous galaxy appears around it — denser toward the centre. The light emerges both upward and downward, so table and ceiling are lit at once. A cluster of nebulae.
LC0134.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, meeting rooms, lobbies, zones above a round table. The sparse arrangement does not overload the ceiling — it suits medium heights too.
LC0134.style: Scandinavian minimalism with a cosmic motif: a simple form with complex content. The message is contemplative — a piece you look into.
LC0134.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the calibres of the dishes, the density of the spiral and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a root. A long winding tube with smooth turns and swellings — a form with no geometry: neither a root nor a stem nor a weed ever has any. The author refuses repetition, and every element is bent its own way.
The mass descends from a round mirrored base and narrows below. The stems interweave and touch here and there: the thicket reads as continuous, yet every individual stem is visible.

By day it is a mass of white coral suspended below the ceiling — dense, calm, monochrome. In the evening the light enters a stem at its end and travels its whole length, and the milky surface diffuses it so that not a point but the entire stem glows, evenly and softly. A thicket lit underwater.
LC0135.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, lobbies, spas, stairwells. The composition builds downward, so what matters is not floor area but clear height beneath it.
LC0135.style: Organic modernism and marine aesthetics: a line without a single angle. The message is soft and enveloping — a piece for an interior where people rest.
LC0135.madeToOrder: The base diameter, the number of stems, the element lengths and the tone of the glow are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about movement in a circle. The shoal runs in a closed loop around an empty centre — and that emptiness is the point: the fish are circling around something that is not there. The device comes from the behaviour of real shoals, which gather into a torus when they defend themselves.

The ring is not flat: on one stretch the shoal rises, on another it drops, and the loop turns out to be twisted through space. Density is uneven — in places the fish move in a wall, elsewhere they break away alone.

By day it is graphics on the ceiling: narrow forked-tail silhouettes, clear mixed with gold, read through outline. In the evening the level of light shifts around the circle — one arc burns bright, the opposite one is nearly in shadow: the clear bodies give white flares along their rims, the gold ones light up whole. A shoal circling an invisible centre.
LC0136.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atria, double-height living rooms, pools and spas. The ring reads only from above at a distance: it needs volume, not a ceiling close overhead.
LC0136.style: Marine modernism and contemporary sculptural installation. The message is narrative — a piece that tells a story rather than decorating.
LC0136.madeToOrder: The ring diameter, the number of elements, the share of gold and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a ripple. The line of elements rises and falls, forming two crests with a trough between them: on the crests the elements bunch closer, in the trough they thin out. The wave is stated twice — by the length of the rods vertically and by the density of the spacing horizontally.

Each element is a narrow twisted ribbon with a ragged edge, crushed freely, with no repeats. It hangs on its own rod with a point source at the end: the light arrives from above, from outside, not from within the form.

By day it is a ripple on water — amber ribbons beneath the silver hatching of the rods, a pattern that changes with every step. In the evening the light travels from the point straight into the body, the ribbon picks it up and carries it through all its folds, and a burning core appears inside every element. Hundreds of cores give an unbroken warm field, while the rods above them stay cold. A golden wave suspended above the table.
LC0137.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, lobbies. The wave pattern is calculated for the length of the table.
LC0137.style: Contemporary classicism and organic modernism: water as motif, light as material. The message is warm and hospitable — a piece for a table where people sit long.
LC0137.madeToOrder: The length, the wave pattern, the number of elements and the depth of the amber tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about interlock. The rings pass through one another and form couplings — the composition is held not by its suspensions but by its own connections. The form is deliberately irregular: every ring has its own geometry, closer to an oval here, to a triangle with rounded corners there. Not one true circle among them.
Straight gold crossbars are set between the rings — they work as graphic pauses and stop the mass turning into a jumble.

By day it is a sculpture of interlocked rings — a gold band, a clear inset with a grainy texture, the piece read through outline. In the evening the light travels the entire perimeter and flares on the grainy texture in fine sparks, while the band reflects it and traces every ring with a hot line. What remains is an interlacing of luminous loops suspended in emptiness.
LC0138.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, lobbies, stairwells, reception rooms. The couplings read in the round — the piece is designed to be walked around rather than viewed frontally.
LC0138.style: Jewellery modernism and contemporary sculpture: the link as the unit of composition. The message is spare and expensive — a piece for an interior that rests on one strong detail.
LC0138.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of rings, the calibres and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a crown. The elements stand vertically around the perimeter, tips upward, and lean outward — the silhouette comes out exactly like a diadem or the cup of an opened flower. The form is old and unambiguous: a crown, a bud and a defensive palisade are all built this way.
Inside the bowl the elements are denser and shorter, along the rim taller and sparser — the mass grows from centre to perimeter, and the object reads as opening.

By day it is a clear sculpture: the thick walls work as lenses, and the composition catches daylight from the window and scatters it across the table. In the evening the light enters each hook from below, travels the curve and gathers in the drop-shaped finial, which flares into a gold core. Every layer is visible right through — the crown seems filled with light entirely.
LC0139.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, dining rooms, lobbies, banquet halls, zones above a round table. A round bowl asks for a round table beneath it — form answers form.
LC0139.style: Grand classicism in contemporary execution: a diadem without a single ornament. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a table where people are received.
LC0139.madeToOrder: The bowl diameter, the number of elements, the height of the hooks and the depth of the setting are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same colony, but with something to hold on to. The anemones are set not on cables but on a tubular branch curved into a broad loop in the horizontal plane: the branch divides into short stalks, and on each sits a figure at its own angle.

The mass reads as grown on its support — the colony has covered the branch the way polyps cover a sunken tree. Density is uneven: in places the elements bunch into clusters, elsewhere the branch stays bare. That matters more than symmetry: growth is never even.

By day it is a coral colony — clear bodies on a gold line, graphic and light. In the evening two levels of glow appear at once: cold points at the tips of the tentacles, and the warm vein of the branch showing through the clear mass beneath them. A branch overgrown with luminous creatures.
LC0140.whereItWorks: A horizontal format — long tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, spas, reception areas. The curved loop reads from above and from the side, so the piece is hung lower than usual.
LC0140.style: Marine Art Nouveau: a natural form on a natural support, without geometry. The message is organic — a piece for an interior that avoids straight lines.
LC0140.madeToOrder: The length of the branch, the number of elements, the density of the colony and the metal finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a colony. The sea anemone is a creature that does not move and does not look alive until it starts to glow. The author takes that form: a rounded body with a grainy core and dozens of tentacles radiating in every direction. Each is drawn out its own way and curved separately — there are no identical elements.
The composition is vertical, wound into a spiral. Some anemones break away from the mass and hang alone, with gaps between them: the colony looks grown rather than assembled.

By day the object is all but invisible — entirely clear, it shows itself only in highlights, a gathering of transparent creatures easy to overlook. In the evening the light enters the base of each tentacle and travels to its tip, flaring there as a point. From below the composition reads as a swarm of glowing stars with radiating rays — a colony lit in the depths.
LC0141.whereItWorks: A vertical format — stairwells, atria, double-height living rooms, spas. Transparency needs a dark backdrop: against a pale wall the colony is lost by day and by night alike.
LC0141.style: Marine modernism and scientific aesthetics: a biological form reproduced precisely. The message is investigative — a piece for someone who loves nature unstylised.
LC0141.madeToOrder: The overall height, the number of elements, the length of the tentacles and the density of the colony are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the stroke. Close longitudinal grooves run the whole length of the leaf, and that changes everything: the surface shifts in density as it turns, and light travels across it in lines rather than patches. The form acquires graphics of its own — the ribbing works like hatching in an etching.

The pyramid is dense toward the centre and thinned at the edges, with single leaves descending below. Bare cables with glowing points are set between them — they establish the volume and stop the mass congealing.

By day it is autumn foliage lifted to the ceiling: amber leaves mixed with clear ones, a warm mass living on the reflections along the grooves. In the evening the light enters at the stalk and spreads along the ribbing — every leaf glows in strokes, the amber ones fill with copper, the clear ones throw white sparks along their ribs. The sources are lost among the layers and the whole crown glows.
LC0142.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, double-height spaces. The dense pyramid needs height — otherwise the silhouette is lost.
LC0142.style: Art Nouveau and organic modernism: the leaf as a classic motif, the ribbing as the author's device. The message is warm and autumnal — a piece for an interior in a natural palette.
LC0142.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of leaves, the share of amber and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about directed sound. The bell is a form from the world of sound, not light: a horn, a gramophone trumpet, a megaphone. The author uses its chief property — a bell does not diffuse, it aims.

Outside, the bodies are opaque, graphite and matte — in the dark they do not read at all. Inside, polished gold or mirrored silver. The elements are turned at random: some mouth down, some sideways, some almost up.

By day it is a cluster of metal flowers — a dark, dense, graphic mass below the ceiling. In the evening the bodies disappear and only the open mouths remain: the gold ones give a warm honeyed glow, the silver a cool white one, and each throws a narrow directed beam. A gathering of luminous funnels suspended in emptiness — a swarm of spotlights facing every way.
LC0143.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, lobbies, restaurants, stairwells, zones above a round table. Directed light lets you pick out specific points: a table, a bar counter, a picture.
LC0143.style: Industrial luxury and steampunk minimalism: a technical form presented as something precious. The message is bold — a piece for an interior with character.
LC0143.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of bells, the ratio of gold to silver interiors and the colour of the outer surface are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a whirlwind. The cascade is wound into a spiral: it begins high as a narrow stream, widens at the middle and narrows again below, curving around an invisible axis. The form is taken not from an object but from a movement — this is how leaves fall in a rising current.

The elements are small, no larger than a palm, and read almost not at all on their own: only the mass works. The cables vanish into darkness and are invisible, so the petals appear to hang unsupported.

By day it is the trace left by a whirlwind — a drawing in the air, living on reflected light, all but imperceptible. In the evening the principal device takes over: not all the elements glow but one in ten. The gold backings give warm flares, the clear fragments cold sparks, and the rest of the mass stays dark. It is precisely that selectiveness that creates the sense of movement: a current of sparks descending between floors.
LC0144.whereItWorks: A vertical format for tall openings — stairwells, atria, shafts between floors, double-height living rooms. The spiral is designed for the specific height and viewpoint.
LC0144.style: Contemporary sculptural installation: the composition as an event within a volume. The message is dynamic — a piece that makes people look up.
LC0144.madeToOrder: The height of the cascade, the pitch of the spiral, the number of elements and the share of gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about monochrome. There is no gold here and no contrasting inset — only white, and all the work falls to form and light. This is deliberate self-restraint: by removing the palette, the author makes you look at the plasticity.

A broad bowl with a rolled edge, one side raised and the other lowered, the rim wavy — an opened flower or a shell curled in water. The elements face in different directions: some open their mouths downward, others show a smooth back.

By day it is a field of white flowers below the ceiling — a quiet, almost soundless mass read through light and shade. In the evening the light emerges through the open mouths in soft warm patches and lights the thin walls from within, so the white fills with cream. From outside the elements stay cool and opaque: what you see is not form but a net of glowing mouths. A pool lit from beneath the water.
LC0145.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, double-height living rooms, spas and pools, banquet and wedding halls. Monochrome works in any interior palette, so the composition is universal.
LC0145.style: Minimalism and organic modernism: form without decoration. The message is clean and ceremonial — a piece for a bright interior that does not want to argue with itself.
LC0145.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the tone of the glow and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about sparseness. What matters here is not what is present but what is absent: the elements lie almost flat, in layers at varied levels, barely overlapping. Between them, large voids. The flock is stretched through the whole body of water rather than packed into a shoal.
The form is a narrow feather with a wavy edge and a slight twist, repeated in three finishes: clear turquoise with internal marbling, opaque milky white, and gold with patina.

By day it is a flock suspended below the ceiling: sparse, light, read through individual silhouettes. In the evening one and the same beam behaves in three ways — the turquoise feathers transmit it and glow a cool green-blue, the white ones diffuse it softly, the gold ones reflect it sharply. Some elements burn, others merely gleam, others stay dark: a current lit from the surface.
LC0146.whereItWorks: Generous volumes — atria, lobbies, pools and spas, double-height living rooms. Sparseness needs area: compressed, the composition turns into an ordinary chandelier.
LC0146.style: Marine modernism and contemporary sculpture: the movement of water as the principal motif. The message is calm and immersive — a piece for a space where people unwind.
LC0146.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the ratio of the three finishes and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a nest. Hooks with turned tips interweave into a tangle — a mass with neither top nor bottom, only interlock. Between them, on separate threads, hang small faceted spheres that descend lower: drops running off the hooks.
Some elements are opaque and white, with a gold hollow inside; others are entirely clear, read only through highlights along the rim. One form in two readings: visible and nearly absent.

By day it is a tangle of clear horns — a pale sculptural mass in which the transparent elements all but dissolve. In the evening a chain builds itself: the light emerges reflected from the gold hollows, enters the clear hooks, which carry it onward along their curve, and the faceted spheres gather it and give it back as pinpoint flares. A nest with sparks falling out of it.
LC0147.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, zones above a round table. The trailing pendants set a lower limit — allow clearance beneath.
LC0147.style: Art Nouveau and jewellery modernism: a complex interweaving that works as a setting. The message is collector-minded — a piece for someone who looks closely.
LC0147.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the ratio of white, gold and clear, and the pendant lengths are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a break. The surface is uneven, with cavities and matte patches — not a product but a splinter of ice or a slab of rock salt. The author deliberately avoids smoothness: what is valued here is looking found rather than made.

Plates of differing size are laid in vertical bands offset in height — the masonry is uneven, with steps and gaps. Dark slots run between them, passing air and some light. The slim frame is visible but does not argue with the mass: it works as hard rhythm against ragged masonry.

By day the screen looks like a wall of ice — cold, white-grey, almost opaque, living on texture alone. In the evening light is fed in at the rim and spreads unevenly across each plate, emphasising the relief: thicker means duller, thinner means brighter. A glacier lit from within.
LC0148.whereItWorks: Zoning — separating a living room from a dining room, a panel in spas and pool areas, a partition beside a staircase, a backdrop behind reception. A nearly opaque plane gives full privacy while still glowing.
LC0148.style: Nordic minimalism and organic architecture: cold, stone and irregularity as an aesthetic. The message is severe and clean — a piece for an interior without embellishment.
LC0148.madeToOrder: The screen dimensions, the number of plates, the depth of the relief and the lighting scheme are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about rock above fire. Below, a living flame; above it a tall cylinder built from hundreds of overlapping flat plates, like masonry or tiling. A gap is left between bowl and cylinder: the fire is visible from every side and works not as decoration for the column but as its source.
No plate repeats its neighbour — runs, cavities, patches of differing density. The column looks laid by hand out of found material rather than assembled from parts: rock, not product.

By day it is a sculptural volume — warm amber, read through texture and reflection, calm and dense. In the evening the fire below lights the masonry from beneath, the light passes through the amber and emerges warm and diffuse. The column begins to glow like heated rock — stone with the heat still in it.
The same object exists in a rose-copper palette, where the tone shifts toward fired clay and terracotta.
LC0149.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, lobbies, spas, restaurants, winter gardens, terraces. A live flame needs ventilation and a clear perimeter — the object stands at the centre, not against a wall.
LC0149.style: Organic minimalism and the archaic: fire as the oldest centre of a dwelling. The message is primal and luxurious at once — a piece for a space people gather around.
LC0149.madeToOrder: The column dimensions, the plate palette, the burner type and the drop height are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a curtain. The lozenges are strung on fine vertical cords — the construction is closer to a bead curtain than to a wall: it hangs rather than stands. Offsets in both directions break the grid: there is no strict pitch, only rhythm.

Three kinds of lozenge — clear with internal marbling, smoky grey with a frosted texture, and dense amber. Each is faceted irregularly, so the facets catch the light differently and no two points in the field are alike.

By day the outline of whatever is behind the screen is visible through the gaps, but not the detail: the panel divides without cutting off. In the evening light runs down the gold cords and enters the facets at the fixing points — the clear ones give white flares, the smoky ones glow subdued, the amber ones fill with copper and become the brightest points. A curtain of lights hung on threads.
LC0150.whereItWorks: Zoning — separating a living room from a kitchen, a screen in a lobby, a partition beside a staircase, a backdrop behind a bar counter, an inset in a window opening. A suspended structure goes where permanent fixing is impossible.
LC0150.style: Art Deco and jewellery modernism: faceting, thread, light at a point. The message is dressy — a piece for an interior where the screen should be an event.
LC0150.madeToOrder: The screen dimensions, the number of lozenges, the ratio of the three kinds and the layout pitch are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about dried time. Real fern fronds are sealed inside the plates — a fine silhouette with every pinna drawn, held in the body for good. The device is old and botanical: plants were pressed between pages exactly this way, to keep the form once colour and scent had gone.

Triangular plates are set point down and laid in offset rows — the plane reads as scales or as roof tiling. The impressions are scattered across the field irregularly: a herbarium gathered without system, not an ornament.

By day the screen works as a translucent panel — smoky, almost clear in places, drifting into graphite in others, with internal marbling. The view behind it is subdued but not closed. In the evening light enters at the rim, the plates fill from within, and the ferns emerge as dark silhouettes against a glowing ground. A botanical archive lit from behind.
LC0151.whereItWorks: Zoning — separating a living room from a dining room, a screen at an entrance, a panel in a spa, a backdrop behind reception, an inset in a restaurant wall. Translucency gives privacy without a solid wall.
LC0151.style: Botanical modernism and Art Nouveau: the plant as the principal subject, transparency as the means of holding it. The message is contemplative — a piece for an interior that loves detail.
LC0151.madeToOrder: The screen dimensions, the number of plates, the selection of botanical inserts and the depth of the smoky tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about depth. The tinting is uneven: almost colourless in places, thickening to honey in others, with visible runs in the body. This is not a flaw but a condition — because of that unevenness every element changes the light passing through it in its own way.

Twisted ribbons with sharp ends hang in layers, turned at random. The mass reads right through: behind the front layer you see the second and the third, and the depth of the composition becomes part of its drawing.

By day it is a cloud of crumpled forms — clear, warm, working on the refraction of daylight from a window. In the evening the light passes through several layers and gathers temperature on the way: where it goes through the colourless it stays white, where it crosses dense amber it fills with copper. The source cannot be found — the whole mass glows, and every element works as a lens for its neighbour.
LC0152.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, double-height spaces. The layering is visible only from the side and below — the composition is built for a specific height.
LC0152.style: The Murano tradition in a contemporary reading: colour held in the body rather than on the surface. The message is warm and collector-minded — a piece chosen by feel rather than from a catalogue.
LC0152.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the depth of the amber tone and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about ash and heat. The outer face is opaque, dark grey and rough — as though covered in ash or oxide. The inner hollow is gilded and polished to a mirror. The contrast is set hard and holds the whole piece on a single device: from outside the object is almost invisible, from inside it is white-hot.

The elements are turned in different directions — some show a grey back, others open a burning interior. The bowl is dense, without gaps: the mass reads as something already burnt through on the surface.

By day the composition is restrained and graphic — a sculpture in unworked metal, a dark silhouette below the ceiling. In the evening the figures vanish into the dark entirely and what remains is a net of glowing gold triangles suspended in emptiness. You see not the form but its lining.
LC0153.whereItWorks: Interiors in a dark palette — private living rooms, bars, lounges, lobbies, restaurants. The device only works against a dark ground: against a pale wall the grey face stops disappearing.
LC0153.style: Brutalist luxury and contemporary art: rough texture outside, something precious within. The message is strong and masculine — a piece for an interior built on contrast.
LC0153.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the texture of the outer surface and the depth of the gilding are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a hidden core. An elongated lozenge is twisted on its long axis, and the twist creates pockets — inner folds you cannot see into from outside. It is these that glow, not the elements themselves: the composition is built so that the source always hides in the fold.
The pyramid is dense at the centre and thinned toward the edges, with single lozenges descending below. All are turned at random, and the mass reads as volumetric, with hollows and gatherings.

By day it is a swarm of twisted ribbons — white with gold, a form without light, living on plasticity alone. In the evening the outer surfaces stay opaque while the inner folds fill with light: what burns is not the mass but its core. A cloud with fire hidden inside it.
LC0154.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, banquet halls. The pyramidal build needs height: pressed to the ceiling, it loses its silhouette.
LC0154.style: Contemporary Art Deco: the twisted ribbon as the principal motif, white with gold as the palette. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a formal space.
LC0154.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements and the ratio of white to gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about braking. An open fan with sharp tips and a deep hollow — the silhouette reads both as a bird's tail as it kills its speed before landing and as an opened bud. What the two readings share is opening: the form is shown at the moment it is most fully unfurled.
The elements are turned in different directions and hang in layers. The upper contour is uneven: individual figures rise above the main mass or drop below it, and the flock never looks drawn up.

By day the object reads as a flock stilled below the ceiling — white with gold, a dense sculptural mass. In the evening the light emerges through the open mouths in narrow warm patches: the white bowls are lit from within, the gold ones flare. From outside the elements stay opaque — only the opened sides glow, and the composition looks different from every point.
LC0155.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, double-height living rooms, dining rooms, atria. The directional glow means the piece should be oriented along the principal line of sight.
LC0155.style: Contemporary classicism with an organic motif: movement caught in sculpture. The message is lively and dynamic — a piece for a space where something is happening.
LC0155.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the ratio of white to gold and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about two sides. The element is twisted a half-turn on its central axis, so it shows both faces at once: one white and opaque, the other gold with the texture of leaf. No element is ever wholly warm or wholly cool — the twist will not let you choose.
The bowl is broad and shallow, the mass thinned above and denser below. The elements hang at varied levels and overlap in places — a cloud with a solid floor.

By day it is a cloud of crumpled foil: uneven highlights, a random pattern, the piece read through texture. In the evening the light strikes the gold faces and reflects outward in warm patches, while the white ones stay cool and matte. On one sail you see white, on the next gold — the composition shimmers at the slightest shift of the eye, as though burning in every other element.
LC0156.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, double-height spaces. The bowl builds downward, so allow for height.
LC0156.style: Glamorous minimalism and contemporary Art Deco: gold and white, no geometry at all. The message is festive — a piece for an interior that loves shine.
LC0156.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements and the ratio of white to gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about light broken across facets. The triangular sails are slightly bowed, so a soft chiaroscuro without hard highlights appears across the plane — the screen becomes dimensional while staying pale and calm.
There are few gold triangles, set in free diagonal groups. The proportion is chosen so that gold reads as an accent rather than a pattern: the mass stays white, and the gold within it is an event.

By day the screen is nearly monochrome: the white faces catch daylight differently, and the whole difference rests on light and shade. In the evening a second life begins — the white diffuses the light into an even glow across the whole surface, while the gold sails intercept it and flare in hot patches. A calm wall turns out to be lit from within.
LC0157.whereItWorks: Bright interiors — zoning a living room, a screen in spas and pool areas, a partition in a reception room, a backdrop behind reception, a wall inset. Soft light without glare suits zones where people spend time.
LC0157.style: Contemporary minimalism with a gold accent: a white field, pinpoint opulence. The message is light — a piece that brightens a space rather than weighing it down.
LC0157.madeToOrder: The screen dimensions, the number of elements, the share of gold and the lighting scheme are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about chainmail. The same device of four-pointed elements joined at their tips, but executed entirely in polished gold. Dropping the second colour changes the piece fundamentally: instead of graphics in white and gold you get a continuous metal fabric that works only through light and shade.
Every point is slightly concave, and a complex chiaroscuro appears across the surface — some faces burn, others fall into shadow. The screen reads as forged mail or as scales: armour hung on a wall.

By day it is a dense gold mass living on reflected daylight: the pattern changes with the sun. In the evening the light comes from deep in the net, emerges through the openings, strikes the sails and reflects repeatedly, element to element. The plane fills from within and looks red-hot.
LC0158.whereItWorks: Formal spaces — a hotel lobby, a reception room, a private study, a backdrop behind a bar counter, a wall inset. Unbroken gold demands restrained surroundings: everything else nearby should stay silent.
LC0158.style: Art Deco and Eastern opulence: metal fabric as a symbol of wealth. The message is direct and generous — a piece for an interior unembarrassed by richness.
LC0158.madeToOrder: The screen dimensions, the number of elements, the gilding finish and the lighting scheme are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the reflected room. Triangular elements with an undulating polished surface are each bowed differently, so the reflections on them stretch and break up as they do on water. The screen does not show itself — it shows what stands before it, distorted.
The main mass is cool, grey with a greenish cast; the gold triangles are gathered not into a pattern but into free diagonal groups — they read as gleams breaking through the metal.

By day it is a mirror without a subject: the screen changes with every step the viewer takes, and it never holds a static reflection. In the evening the light passes through the slots between the faces and flares in the gold cells, while the grey ones stay cold mirrors and go on reflecting the room. The plane lives in two ways at once — by its own light and by borrowed light.
LC0159.whereItWorks: Zoning — a partition in a lobby, a screen in a restaurant, a divider beside a staircase, a backdrop behind a bar or reception. A reflective surface visually expands a room: it works where volume is lacking.
LC0159.style: Industrial modernism and brutalist luxury: metal as the principal language. The message is contemporary and urban — a piece for an interior with character.
LC0159.madeToOrder: The screen dimensions, the number of elements, the share of gold and the metal finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about weaving. A four-pointed star whose tips converge toward the centre, with concave sails forming between them — joined at their points, the elements give a continuous lozenge net. The device is taken from textiles: the screen is not assembled but woven.

The gold elements are scattered across the white field not evenly but in groups, on the diagonal. The pattern reads as random flashes within the mass, and that enlivens the strict geometry — the net stops being mechanical.

By day the screen works through light and shade: each sail is slightly concave and catches the light its own way, so the plane never looks uniform. In the evening the light emerges through the openings of the net — the white sails diffuse it and glow softly, the gold ones intercept it and throw hard highlights. The fabric begins to shimmer from within.
LC0160.whereItWorks: Zoning — separating a living room from a dining room, a screen at an entrance group, a partition in a spa, a backdrop behind reception. The open-work net steals almost no light, so it suits darker zones.
LC0160.style: A Moorish motif in a contemporary reading: the mashrabiya grille without ornamental overload. The message is decorative but restrained — a piece that adorns without dominating.
LC0160.madeToOrder: The screen dimensions, the number of elements, the share of gold and the lighting scheme are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a thicket. The calla is a flower that does not open but wraps itself around: a funnel with a turned rim and a drawn-out tip. The author repeats it dozens of times, sets each on its own rod and gathers the rods into a bundle — the result is not a bouquet but a thicket that has grown on its own.

The flowers run the full height of the column in tiers, turned in different directions and overlapping. The lower half is left bare: only rods on a round disc — stems without foliage, as real callas have.

By day it is a clear sculpture of a thicket — milky white on chrome, cool and graphic. In the evening the light passes through the thin walls of the funnels and lights every flower entire in a soft milky tone; the chromed rods reflect that light and multiply it deep inside the column. A field of flowers glowing from within.
LC0161.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, spas, reception rooms, winter gardens. Soft diffuse light without glare — the lamp works as a source of mood rather than as working light.
LC0161.style: Art Nouveau and Scandinavian minimalism: a botanical motif stripped of decorativeness. The message is lyrical — a piece for an interior that loves quiet.
LC0161.madeToOrder: The column height, the number of flowers, the tone of the glow and the finish of the rods are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about masonry made of grain. Elongated forms with rounded sides — a grain, a pill, a river stone — are laid in dense rows offset by half a step. The author takes the logic of a brick wall and replaces the brick with an organic form: strict construction, soft element.

The gaps are narrow: the screen comes out almost continuous but not solid — air and light pass through the slots. The elements are turned slightly at random, and that stops the row from being machine-made.

By day the surface is calm and almost monochrome — white with occasional gold insets, a wall as a wall. In the evening the backlight emerges from behind the plane along the contour of every element: the white grains read as separate volumes with a halo, the gold ones catch the light across their whole surface and flare. The monolith breaks up into hundreds of outlined forms.
LC0162.whereItWorks: Zoning generous rooms — a partition between living room and kitchen, a screen at an entrance, a wall in a reception area, a backdrop behind a bar counter. An almost continuous plane gives more privacy than an open-work screen.
LC0162.style: Organic modernism: a natural form in a strict grid. The message is calm and architectural — a background piece, not an accent.
LC0162.madeToOrder: The screen dimensions, the number of elements, the ratio of white to gold and the lighting scheme are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an optical illusion. Every element is presented corner-forward, with three faces visible, and so reads now as a cube, now as a hexagon — depending on where you stand. This is the classic optical game known from parquet and mosaic: a volume that may turn out to be a plane.

The layout of finishes is not subordinated to any pattern — gold with patina, white and graphite are mixed freely. The surface looks alive rather than ornamental: there is no motif, only distribution.

By day the screen works through light, shade and reflection: the faces catch light differently and the plane shimmers of its own accord. In the evening the contour takes over — a fine glowing line traces every face, and the wall becomes a three-dimensional net hanging in the air. The gold cubes give a warm reflection, the white ones glow softly, the graphite ones stay voids.
LC0163.whereItWorks: Zoning without a solid wall — separating a living room from a dining room, the entrance to a private area, a partition beside a staircase, a screen in a restaurant or hotel foyer. The gaps between elements pass air and light, so space is marked out rather than divided.
LC0163.style: Art Deco and optical modernism: geometry as the principal subject. The message is architectural — a piece that works with the structure of a space rather than its finishes.
LC0163.madeToOrder: The screen dimensions, the number of elements, the layout of finishes and the lighting scheme are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a paper bird. Two triangular sails meeting at an angle, sharp tips, a short keel — the form is folded, not modelled: what you read in it is a crease, not a volume. Origami lifted into the air and multiplied into a flock.
The top of the composition is left empty — only a net of cables with point lights. The device is simple and precise: with no support above, the whole mass appears to hover rather than hang.

By day it is a flock of paper birds below the ceiling — gold and clear intermixed, light graphics. In the evening the difference between the finishes sets the rhythm: gold rolls the light across the whole plane of the sail in warm patches, while the clear wings flare only along their ribs in cold sparks. A swarm whose wings are alight.
LC0164.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, panoramic living rooms, dining rooms, atria. The empty upper zone only works with a high ceiling: otherwise the hovering trick does not read.
LC0164.style: Japanese minimalism and contemporary sculpture: the fold instead of ornament. The message is light and poetic — a piece for an interior that refuses to look heavy.
LC0164.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements and the ratio of gold to clear are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the crack as ornament. Crazing is usually counted a defect: a net of fine cracks across a surface. Here it is rubbed with gold, and damage turns into drawing. The device is Japanese in spirit — kintsugi, where the break is not hidden but emphasised.
The branches are woven into a long horizontal band with side shoots. The leaves are turned at random: some show a white crazed back, others open a hot gold interior. Every lining is gilded in full.

By day it is a branch with whitened foliage — frost, old glaze, something time has touched. The crazing reads as graphics on white. In the evening the light strikes the gold linings and emerges reflected and warm; the white stays cool while the gold in the cracks catches the light and traces a glowing net across every leaf. A crown with gold burning between its leaves.
LC0165.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long tables, kitchen islands, meeting rooms, reception areas. The crazing is seen close to, so the piece is hung lower than usual.
LC0165.style: Wabi-sabi and European classicism in one: the marks of time presented as value. The message is collector-minded — a piece for someone who values texture over shine.
LC0165.madeToOrder: The length of the branch, the number of leaves, the density of the crack pattern and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the seed. An elongated grain with pointed ends — a form in which everything is compressed to the limit: it is a pip, a spindle and a drop caught in flight all at once. The author does not specify which, because what all three share is concentration, a readiness to unfold.

The mass is arranged freely, without an array: denser at the centre, sparser at the edges, the lower edge wavy. Gold takes up most of it, with clear and opaque green set in as occasional accents — the way a crown carries leaves of a different age.

By day it is a scatter of seeds in the air: warm, calm, read through silhouette. In the evening the three finishes begin to behave differently — the gold flares sharply, the clear throws white sparks, the green fills with an opaque tone without a single highlight. The composition shimmers unevenly, like a crown in wind.
LC0166.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, lobbies. The free layout needs length to spare: compressed, it loses its randomness.
LC0166.style: Organic modernism with a jewellery accent: a natural form in an expensive finish. The message is warm — a piece for an interior that loves gold but dislikes ceremony.
LC0166.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the ratio of finishes and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same scatter, assembled from modules. The composition is counted in elements: each is a finished form, and any number of them makes up a field of the required size. There is no set arrangement — there is a principle from which both an intimate group above a table and a field across the whole ceiling can grow.
A free layout is essential: denser at the centre, sparser at the edges, with a wavy lower edge. Rank and file would kill the image — seeds are not laid out in rows.

By day it is a warm scatter in the air: the elements read through silhouette and overlap, the field calm and even. In the evening the finishes begin to behave differently — gold flares sharply, clear gives white sparks, green fills with a mute tone — and the mass shimmers unevenly, like a crown in the wind.
LC0166-1.whereItWorks: Long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, lobbies, retail galleries. The modularity allows the composition to be assembled for any geometry: a dense group, a drawn-out line or a continuous field.
LC0166-1.style: Organic modernism with a jeweller's accent: the module instead of ornament, natural form instead of decor. The message is warm — a piece for an interior that loves gold but does not love ceremony.
LC0166-1.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the area of the field, the ratio of finishes and the height of the suspensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A handful of seeds left on the wall. A few elements from the great scatter are gathered into a compact vertical bunch — what read as a crown in the composition has become a branch pressed to the plane here.
The ratio of finishes is kept: gold holds the main mass, clear and opaque green are set in as rare accents. At small size that proportion reads more precisely — every inclusion counts.

By day it is a warm graphic silhouette on the wall: elongated grains with sharp ends, read through contour and highlight. In the evening the three finishes part in character — gold flares sharply, clear gives white sparks, green fills with a mute tone and no highlight at all — and the bunch shimmers unevenly, like a branch in the wind.
LC0166-2.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, corridors, bedrooms, staircase flights, zones by a mirror. It works solo, in a pair beside a doorway or in a series along a wall — then the wall lights carry on composition LC0166-1, repeating its rhythm on the vertical.
LC0166-2.style: Organic modernism with a jeweller's accent: a natural form, an expensive finish. The message is warm — a piece for an interior that loves gold but does not love ceremony.
LC0166-2.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the ratio of finishes and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a ribbon of fire. Boats with sharp raised prows stand close and overlap, so the line reads as a continuous mass rather than a row of separate objects. The lower edge is wavy, the upper level — together they give the silhouette of a ribbon stretched below the ceiling.
Gold and pearl-white elements are mixed without system and turned at random: some show a burning interior, others a cool back. The rhythm is set not by spacing but by those orientations.

By day it is a ridge of shells — dense, metallic, read through silhouette. In the evening the hollows begin to work: the gold turns light into hot patches, the pearlescent diffuses it into a soft glow. Because the mass is dense the source never reads — what glows is the ribbon itself, a band of fire stretched above the table.
LC0167.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, reception areas. A continuous mass gives more light than a sparse composition of the same size.
LC0167.style: Contemporary Art Deco: white with gold, a streamlined form, rhythm instead of ornament. The message is representative — a piece for a table where people are received.
LC0167.madeToOrder: The length of the ribbon, the number of elements, the ratio of gold to pearlescent and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the setting. The petal here is placed inside a second, clear form: an opaque grey-white core surrounded by an amber shell, with an air gap between them and a visible boundary along the rim. The device is a jeweller's — this is how a stone is set into a collet so it never touches the metal.

The form is elongated, pointed at both ends, with a slight twist. The composition is a dense shallow bowl: the elements are laid in layers, denser at the centre and sparser at the edges, with single petals descending below.

By day it is a cluster of layered petals — the double structure is visible along the contour and every element reads separately. In the evening the light divides between the layers: the amber shell flares along its contour as a warm line, the grey-white core stays a calm matte patch. The mass never merges into a continuous glow — it is a multitude of outlined forms, a swarm of luminous cocoons.
LC0169.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, lobbies, stair landings, zones above a round table. The double structure is visible close to — the composition is made to be examined.
LC0169.style: Jewellery modernism and contemporary classicism: the setting as a device rather than a finish. The message is collector-minded — a piece for someone who looks at detail.
LC0169.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the tone of the core and the depth of the amber are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the passage from dawn to dusk. White and gold are not mixed here but drawn apart to the ends: the white boats gather on one side, the gold on the other, and in the middle they blend. The arc reads not as a pattern but as a timeline — a cold field warming toward gold.
The element is a narrow boat with high sharp prows and a deep hollow. The arc rises from one side, the elements lying in tiers and layers with a gradual gain in height.

By day the gradient reads calmly: white all but dissolves against a pale ground while gold holds the accent. In the evening the difference intensifies — the white diffuses the light into a soft even glow, the polished gold reflects it sharply and throws highlights. The transition becomes more legible than it is by daylight: the composition literally heats up toward one edge.
LC0170.whereItWorks: Generous rooms with irregular geometry — stairwells, curved halls, atria, double-height living rooms. The rise of the arc is designed for the specific volume.
LC0170.style: Contemporary classicism with an Art Deco accent: white with gold, movement as the principal motif. The message is formal — a piece for a space where the first impression matters.
LC0170.madeToOrder: The length and rise of the arc, the number of elements and the point of transition from white to gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a flower made of a single leaf. The calla is a rare case in botany: its "flower" is one leaf wrapped around itself. The author takes precisely that peculiarity: a funnel with a sharp tip below, the inner spiral clearly visible and not concealed.

The composition is drawn out horizontally: the flowers hang on gold tubes of varying length, with empty tubes set between them to establish the rhythm. The elements are turned at random — some show an open mouth, others a smooth back.

By day it is a field of clear flowers, read through rims and highlights; the thick fire-polished edges give a sharp contour. In the evening the light travels the spiral of the funnel, reflecting off the walls, and bursts out at the tip as a bright point, while the body works as a lens — a gold core of its own appears inside every flower. Not a single direct source is visible: a swarm of luminous funnels above the table.
LC0172.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, reception areas. The light is gathered into points, so the composition gives directed rather than general illumination.
LC0172.style: Art Nouveau and contemporary classicism: a botanical motif in pure clear execution. The message is elegant — a piece for an interior that holds its form.
LC0172.madeToOrder: The length, the number of flowers, the suspension lengths and the finish of the tubes are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the moment of stopping. A spinning top exists only while it spins; a stationary top falls over. The author catches it in an impossible state: motionless and upright at once, suspended in the air.

The form is built from three parts: a flattened disc with a broken-ice texture at the middle, a short cone above, a long sharp spike below. The elements hang on gold tubes of varying length, with empty tubes between them — they work as hatching and give the composition depth, hollows and gatherings.

By day it is a set of clear instruments — precise, cool, almost laboratory forms. In the evening every element gives two different glows at once: the icy texture of the disc scatters light in fine sparks, while the smooth spike carries it onward and lights up at the very tip. A swarm of tops glowing in the dark.
LC0173.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, zones above a round table. The multi-level arrangement needs height — the composition builds in depth, not in width.
LC0173.style: Contemporary classicism and precise minimalism: geometry instead of decoration. The message is intellectual — a piece for someone who values the idea over the effect.
LC0173.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the suspension lengths and the finish of the tubes are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about what is left. The fragments are crushed and smoothed out again: folds, creases and torn edges are all preserved. The author does not assemble a form, he records a consequence. The object must look like what remains after something, not like something carefully put together.

The cloud is broad, the fragments at varied levels, turned at random, with no array and no symmetry. Large pieces with polished gold alternate with pearlescent ones, and small scraps are scattered between them.

By day it is scattered foil: uneven highlights, a random pattern, nothing predictable. In the evening the light flares as stars between the fragments — the crumpled gold reflects it unevenly, in bands along the folds, while the pearlescent diffuses it softly. No evenness at all, only patches and flares. A field of shards, each with its own highlight.
LC0174.whereItWorks: Generous rooms with high ceilings — lobbies, double-height living rooms, stairwells, gallery spaces. The cloud needs air around it: pressed to the ceiling, it loses its depth.
LC0174.style: Contemporary art and brutalist luxury: the aesthetics of destruction, executed expensively. The message is bold — a piece for an interior unafraid of being uncomfortable.
LC0174.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of fragments and the ratio of gold to pearlescent are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a shell with light sounding inside it. A broad bowl with a rolled rim — a section like a shell or a petal curled by heat. Copper-rose and calm outside, mirrored within: one and the same form behaves in two different ways depending on which side you look at it from.
The cluster is vertical, broad above and tapering below. The elements are turned at random: some show a mirrored interior, some a clear back.

By day it is a cluster of rose forms — warm, quiet, working through reflection. In the evening light kindles inside each bowl, takes on copper and emerges through the open edge as a narrow hot patch. The mouths face different ways, and the composition reads differently from every point — a swarm of copper lights with no principal view.
LC0175.whereItWorks: A vertical format — stairwells, atria, double-height living rooms, shafts between floors. It is designed to be seen from several levels at once.
LC0175.style: Warm Art Deco and contemporary classicism: copper and rose gold rather than yellow. The message is intimate and rich — a piece for an interior with a warm palette.
LC0175.madeToOrder: The cluster height, the number of elements, the depth of the copper tone and the finish of the inner surface are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the time that tumbles things smooth. These stones have no facets and no correct geometry — only rounded flanks and a matte surface, as though the sea had carried them for a long while. The author deliberately refuses cutting: what is valued here is not the work of a maker but the work of the elements.

The stones hang individually, gathered into a broad shallow bowl. Density is uneven: they mass together at the centre and thin to a scatter at the edges. No array at all — a natural distribution, like shingle on a shore.

By day it is a scatter of sea stones suspended in the air: cobalt blue beside cloudy white, the palette of a northern coast. In the evening the glow comes from within — the matte surface does not transmit light but glows as a soft subdued patch: the blues deepen to ultramarine, the whites to opal. Not a single hard highlight. A night sea lit from beneath.
LC0176.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, spas and pools, panoramic living rooms, dining rooms. Even diffuse light without glare is comfortable where people spend time beneath it.
LC0176.style: Organic minimalism and Nordic aesthetics: imperfection as a virtue. The message is contemplative — a piece for an interior that calms.
LC0176.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of stones, the ratio of blue to white and the calibres are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the trace of wind. There is no cloud here and no symmetry — there is a line: the leaves run in a broad arc that winds into a spiral, and density falls from the centre toward the ends. Single elements remain on the tails, strays from the current.

The leaf form is narrow, with sharp ends and a twist on its axis, the rims thickened. Some are clear, some carry a gold backing that gives a warm mirrored interior — and that determines how each element will behave with light.

By day it is a trace left by wind: a drawing in the air, read through highlights. In the evening the leaves begin to burn selectively — the clear ones transmit and diffuse, the gold ones reflect and flare, and as you walk around the composition the brightly burning elements change, because they depend on the angle. The cables vanish into darkness and the leaves seem to hang unsupported. A current of sparks curving around the room.
LC0177.whereItWorks: Large volumes and irregular geometry — stairwells, atria, curved halls, double-height living rooms. The arc is designed for the specific volume: it does not fit into a space, it runs through it.
LC0177.style: Contemporary sculptural installation: the composition as an architectural gesture. The message is authorial — a piece that makes a space recognisable.
LC0177.madeToOrder: The length and pattern of the arc, the number of leaves, the share of gold and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a frozen downpour. Hundreds of needles point downward, gathered into a dense shallow bowl — thicker at the middle, sparser at the edges. This is rain with its time taken away: the drops have already drawn out in falling but have never touched the floor.
The element is double: a gold cone tip-up above, a clear spike below on a base textured like broken ice. A spindle, an icicle grown under a metal cap — the form reads several ways at once.

By day it is a gold field: from below only the cones are visible, and the composition looks metallic and dense. In the evening the light passes from the gold into the clear spike, which carries it the whole length and flares at the point, while the icy base scatters part of it sideways. The field of needles becomes a downpour caught an instant before it lands.
LC0178.whereItWorks: Generous rooms with high ceilings — lobbies, atria, double-height living rooms, banquet halls. It is seen from below, so height matters more than area.
LC0178.style: Grand classicism in contemporary execution: the same logic as a large cascade chandelier, but without a single faceted drop. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a space that makes an impression.
LC0178.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the length of the spikes and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the outline. These leaves have no body — only a closed thickened rim, with emptiness or the thinnest membrane inside. The author keeps the boundary of the form and removes its content: the leaf is reduced to its own contour.

The leaves hang flat, in layers, turned at random; through the upper ones you see the lower. Some are turquoise, some carry a milky haze, and the colour is drawn into the body unevenly, in bands — traces of hand-drawing are visible and nowhere concealed.

By day it is a flock of leaves lifted by wind: the mass is transparent right through, and the composition reads as light to the point of weightlessness. In the evening the principal device engages — the light runs along the thickened contour like a lightguide and traces every leaf with a glowing line. The turquoise fill with colour, the clear ones give a white flare. In the dark only the outlines remain.
LC0179.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, panoramic living rooms, dining rooms, meeting rooms. The layering reads at a distance; in a tight room the contours merge.
LC0179.style: Art Nouveau in a contemporary idiom: a natural motif reduced to line. The message is graphic — a piece for an interior that loves drawing.
LC0179.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of leaves, the share of turquoise and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a support that disappears. The frame here is graphite-black and matte — deliberately made invisible, so that when lit the gold sails seem to hang in emptiness. The author plays with what the piece shows and what it conceals: switched off, it honestly displays its structure; switched on, it denies it.
Every element is bowed like a sail, with sharp ends and a deep hollow, and none repeats its neighbour. This is the pure plasticity of a leaf, fixed at the moment of bending.

By day the object reads as a metal sculpture — gold on graphite, heavy and composed. In the evening the black frame falls entirely into shadow, the light strikes the gold hollows and reflects outward in hot patches. What remains is a column of gold sparks, resting on nothing.
LC0180.whereItWorks: A dark palette — living rooms in deep tones, bars, private studies, showrooms, restaurant interiors. The vanishing-support trick works only against a dark ground.
LC0180.style: Contemporary Art Deco and dark luxury: black with gold, drama instead of ornament. The message is theatrical — a piece designed for effect.
LC0180.madeToOrder: The column height, the number of elements, the gilding finish and the colour of the rods are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same ear of grain, read in winter. The geometry is kept but everything else is inverted: the leaves thin toward their tips to full transparency, the offshoots are longer and finer, the rods chromed instead of gold. The palette moves into cold — silver, white, icy highlights.
One and the same form in a warm and a cold reading gives two different objects. Here the silhouette comes out open-work and the object loses weight: a sheaf from which density has gone.

By day it is an ice sculpture — the rims glow along their contour even without a source, because they catch daylight on their edges. In the evening the light passes through the body and makes every leaf glow entire, from base to tip, not only through the gaps. The column becomes dimensional right through: you see both the front layer and what stands behind it.
LC0181.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, spas, reception rooms, interiors in a cold palette. Transparency needs a dark or neutral backdrop — against a white wall the piece loses its outline.
LC0181.style: Scandinavian minimalism and Nordic modernism: cold as an aesthetic position. The message is clear and ascetic — a piece for an interior without excess.
LC0181.madeToOrder: The column height, the number of elements, the degree of transparency and the finish of the rods are all made to order.
