paragraphs: A composition about ripeness. The ear of grain is a form with a season: it exists only at the end of summer. The author takes a pointed leaf with two short offshoots at its base and repeats it hundreds of times, tips upward — the result is a sheaf raised on a gold stem.
The rows are offset from one another by half a step, so the column reads as plaited rather than stacked. The lower half is left bare: the mass gathers at the top, at eye level, like grain on a stalk.

By day it is pure form — white gloss on gold, a sculptural ear of grain with no visible source of light. In the evening the light emerges from deep in the column through the gaps between the leaves, lights the rods from within, and the vertical fills with a warm glow while staying white on the outside. A sheaf with the sun hidden inside it.
LC0182.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, reception rooms, lounges, showrooms. The soft diffuse glow without direct glare suits rest areas and bedrooms.
LC0182.style: Organic modernism and rustic luxury: a natural motif presented without folklore. The message is warm and domestic — a piece for an interior that speaks of plenty rather than status.
LC0182.madeToOrder: The column height, the number of elements, the tone of the glow and the finish of the rods are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about cold flame. An elongated lozenge twisted on its axis is a form you cannot draw at rest: the half-turn makes the eye complete the movement upward. The author sets the elements in a dense array, slightly turned toward one another, and the row reads as the crest of a wave or as tongues of fire rising all at once.
Clear, turquoise and opaque white elements are mixed with no system whatever. It is precisely the absence of system that keeps the mass alive: there is an array, but it has not been drawn up.

By day it is a ridge of ice — cold, sharp, with hard highlights on the twisted faces. In the evening the row begins to shimmer: the clear ones flare at the rim, the turquoise fill with colour entire, the white stay soft patches. Brightness wanders from element to element, and the flame turns out to be made of ice.
LC0183.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, reception areas. It is viewed along its length, so what it needs is extent, not height.
LC0183.style: Contemporary minimalism with a Murano note: clean geometry, colour as the only decoration. The message is restrained and design-led — a piece for an interior that rests on form.
LC0183.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the ratio of clear, turquoise and white, and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about how light is caught. Here the sources are not hidden inside the elements — they stand separately, on fine gold rods, while clear caps with rolled rims hang around them and gather their light. The relation between light and form is inverted: the form does not glow, it catches.
The caps — broad, crumpled, with a wavy rim — hang at varied levels and are turned at random. The thickness of each wanders, so every one has its own runs and lenses: no two are alike.

By day the composition is all but invisible — read only through highlights, like dew on a web. In the evening the body works as a lens: a bright gold core appears deep inside every cap, and a glowing thread runs along the wavy rim. A cloud of fires, each one caught in its own bowl.
LC0184.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, zones above a round table, lobbies. The layering reads only with height to spare — in a low room the composition flattens.
LC0184.style: Organic modernism and the Scandinavian school: a natural form, warm light, no symmetry. The message is contemplative — a piece looked at long and close.
LC0184.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of elements, the density of the layers and the tone of the glow are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about shedding. The garland sags at the centre and opens upward — the form of something stretched between two points, alive, with a sag from its own weight. Large flowers with sharp radiating petals sit on the arcs, with leaves scattered between them.

The essential thing here is that some of the leaves break away from the mass and hang lower, singly, on fine threads. A light train forms beneath the composition: flowering is shown not at its peak but at the moment it has already begun to fall. Beauty with a stated term.

By day it is a flowering branch lifted to the ceiling — white with gold, festive graphics. In the evening the petals light up entirely, from within, with no visible source; the gold leaves give pinpoint flares, the white ones stay soft patches. The garland becomes a cloud of light with sparks slowly falling from it.
LC0185.whereItWorks: A format for formal spaces: lobbies, double-height living rooms, banquet and wedding halls, atria. It asks for length — hung along a table or across a volume, between two fixing points.
LC0185.style: Romantic Art Nouveau and ceremonial classicism. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a space where people gather for an occasion.
LC0185.madeToOrder: The span of the garland, the number of flowers, the length of the train and the ratio of white to gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about recognition. A monstera cannot be mistaken for anything else: the deep splits and through-holes are its signature. The author takes the form almost literally, with the venation drawn, and does not stylise it — because all the force of the image lies in instant recognition.

White leaves alternate with gold ones of the same geometry, turned in different directions and laid in layers into a dense vertical thicket. The lower half is bare stem only: the plant is raised above the floor, as in a shot taken from below.

By day it is a sculpture of a plant — white gloss with gold insets, graphic and flat. In the evening the thicket begins to glow from within: the light emerges through the splits, lights the gold linings of the neighbouring leaves and draws patches on them that have passed through the holes. A tropical noon, folded into a room.
LC0186.whereItWorks: Living rooms, winter gardens, spas, reception rooms, restaurant interiors. It suits a corner or a position beside a column, where the thicket reads as silhouette.
LC0186.style: Tropical modernism and mid-century: the same botany as in fifties interiors, but without the kitsch. The message is buoyant — a piece for a space that loves greenery and light.
LC0186.madeToOrder: The column height, the number of leaves and the ratio of white to gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the body of water. Discs with a deep funnel at the centre — a section like a lens: they are not merely coloured a marine shade, they accumulate it. The rim betrays the thickness, and within it the colour moves from azure to deep blue, the way water moves away from a shore.

Discs of varying calibre are set in layers and at random: some face straight ahead, some are turned edgewise, some overlap their neighbours. At the centre of every funnel is a gold hemisphere, the only warm point in a cold palette.

By day it is a sculpture in colour: the discs work through reflection and the colour reads as flat. In the evening the light lives in the gold cores: it enters from the centre, spreads to the edges and refracts through the body — one disc reflects inside another, and not a single source reads directly. The column becomes a pillar of water lit from beneath.
LC0187.whereItWorks: Living rooms, spas, reception rooms, restaurant interiors, spaces with a marine theme. Saturated colour needs a neutral ground — against a pale wall it reads more precisely.
LC0187.style: Art Nouveau and the Murano tradition of coloured work in a contemporary reading. The message is collector-minded — a piece bought for its colour and examined close to.
LC0187.madeToOrder: The column height, the number of discs, the calibres and the depth of the marine tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about structure that does not hide. Chromed rods run right through the column, and the author does not mask them — on the contrary, broad gaps are left between the gold blades so the frame stays visible. The piece honestly shows how it is made.

The blades — a broad leaf with a sharp tip and a slight twist — run in tiers from bottom to top, overlapping. Each is turned on its axis its own way: the column comes out transparent despite the density of metal.

By day it is a sculpture in two metals: cool chrome inside, warm gold outside, and the contrast holds the object. In the evening the light comes from below, strikes the underside of every blade and reflects upward — the belly lights up while the top stays dark. Deep inside the column the chrome catches the gold reflections and multiplies them.
LC0188.whereItWorks: Living rooms, halls, reception rooms, bars, showrooms. Light reflected upward lifts the ceiling — the lamp works as a source of volume, not only as an accent.
LC0188.style: Industrial luxury and Art Deco: exposed structure, expensive finish. The message is technical — a piece for someone who cares how a thing is made.
LC0188.madeToOrder: The column height, the number of blades, the metal finish and the height of the light unit are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a flock that has already scattered. The same sickle form — a narrow wing with sharp ends and a twist — but read quietly: a white matte mass with gold elements strewn through it as rare flares.

The elements are turned at random, some rising above the main mass, others breaking away below. The flock reads as sparse and mobile rather than drawn up — the moment after take-off, before the formation has settled.

By day it is a cloud of leaves or birds below the ceiling — light, almost incorporeal. In the evening the white field gives a soft even glow without highlights, while the gold reflects sharply, in points. The difference between the two finishes creates the rhythm: a calm luminous ground with occasional hot sparks in it.
LC0189.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long tables, meeting rooms, reception areas, panoramic living rooms. Soft light without direct glare is convenient where people work or eat beneath the composition.
LC0189.style: Scandinavian minimalism with a jewellery accent: a restrained base, pinpoint opulence. The message is calm — a piece for an interior that does not raise its voice.
LC0189.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the share of gold and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the upstroke. A narrow curved sickle with sharp ends and a slight twist on its axis — the form reads both as a wing at the moment of lift and as a leaf caught by wind. The author does not specify which: what matters is not the nature of the thing but the phase of the movement.

The composition is drawn out horizontally and built in tiers: the elements hang at varied heights, turned in different directions, overlapping in places. The mass is not flat — it has depth, and the flock reads as volumetric.

By day it is gold graphics on the ceiling — mirrored strokes living on reflected daylight. In the evening a glowing rib flares on every wing: the light rolls out along the full length of the sickle, reflections multiply from element to element, and the composition begins to shimmer at the slightest shift of the eye. A flock caught at the moment of lift.
LC0190.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, lobbies. It works where people pass beneath it and look along it, not across.
LC0190.style: Contemporary Art Deco and glamorous minimalism: pure form, mirrored finish, no ornament at all. The message is representative — a piece that sets the standing of a space from the doorway.
LC0190.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the gilding finish and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about morning. The same device as the dark version, read in full light: gold cast branches woven into a sphere, and on them large flowers with a delicate rose-cream shift from the base of the petal to its edge. The surface is velvety, without a single highlight.

The only difference from the twilight version is colour, but it turns the piece over entirely: instead of heavy bronze, a tree in full bloom. The crown looks light and airy, the petals almost translucent. Buds are set among the open flowers — the flowering is still going on.

By day it is a sculptural tree in bloom: rose on gold, a festive and open piece. In the evening the light passes through the thin petals, they light up from within, the rose tone fills and intensifies, and the gold branches pick up the reflection. The crown burns almost entirely — not in separate points but as a cloud.
LC0191.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, bedrooms, stairwells, wedding and ceremonial halls. It asks for a pale ground: against a white or cream wall it reads more precisely than against a dark one.
LC0191.style: Romantic Art Nouveau and contemporary classicism: flowering as the principal subject of an interior. The message is festive and feminine — a piece for a space that wants to give pleasure.
LC0191.madeToOrder: The crown diameter, the number of flowers, the depth of the rose tone and the finish of the branches are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about dusk. The magnolia flowers before its leaves — a bare branch on which large cups open straight away. The author takes that moment and carries it into evening: the palette is deliberately subdued, grey instead of white, and the crown reads as heavy, like a garden at the hour when colour has already left the petals but the form still holds.
Branches with a rough cast texture are woven into a sphere. Closed buds alternate with half-open and fully open ones — flowering is shown not as a state but as a process.

By day it is a bronze sculptural branch: heavy, dark, almost archaeological. In the evening a few flowers light up within the crown — the light emerges from the cups in warm patches, lights the neighbouring petals from within and flares on the gold of the branches. Most of the crown stays in darkness, and it is precisely that restraint that holds the drama.
LC0192.whereItWorks: A voluminous crown asks for height — living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, private studies, lobbies in a dark palette. It suits a position above a round table or in an opening where people walk around it.
LC0192.style: Dark luxury and Art Nouveau in an evening reading: a natural form presented as something precious. The message is intimate and adult — a piece for an interior with character.
LC0192.madeToOrder: The crown diameter, the number of flowers, the depth of the grey tone and the finish of the branches are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same magnolia at another hour. The crown is loosened, the branches are drawn apart, and the garden turns from a dense sphere into a spreading branch — the twilight is the same, but there is more air in it.
The proportion of open to closed has shifted: there are more open cups, and the crown stops being mute. There the drama rested on darkness, here it rests on the pauses between the flowers.

By day it is a sculptural branch with a rough cast texture: heavy, muted grey, read through silhouette and gaps. In the evening light comes out of the cups in warm patches, lights the neighbouring petals from within and flares on the gold of the branches — the flowering appears in turn rather than all at once.
LC0192-1.whereItWorks: Sitting rooms with high ceilings, stair flights, lobbies, private studies. A spreading branch is built across: it needs the length of a wall or a zone, not height alone.
LC0192-1.style: Dark luxe and Art Nouveau in an evening reading: a natural form served as a jewel. The message is intimate and grown-up — a piece for an interior with character.
LC0192-1.madeToOrder: The spread of the branch, the number of flowers, the depth of the grey and the finish of the branches are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about weightlessness. The manta is the only large creature that does not swim but flies: its movement is closer to a bird's gliding than to a fish. The author strips the form of everything surplus and leaves a pure silhouette — a broad triangular wing, drawn-out tips, a curved tail.

The shoal runs in tiers, some rising, some sliding low, the figures turned at random. Glowing points hang between them — plankton, bubbles, suspended matter. It is they, not the figures, that carry the light: on one individual a wing edge flares, on another only a shadow is visible.

By day it is a sculptural shoal below the ceiling — white with occasional dark mirrored accents, graphics on the plane of the ceiling. In the evening immersion sets in: the figures recede into darkness, leaving the luminous suspension and the silhouettes passing through it. The room becomes a body of water.
LC0193.whereItWorks: A format for large volumes — atria, lobbies, pools and spas, double-height living rooms, children's spaces. It needs height: the shoal reads only from above, at a distance.
LC0193.style: Contemporary sculptural installation, closer to a museum than to an interior piece. The message is narrative — a piece that creates a scene rather than complementing one.
LC0193.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of figures, the ratio of pale to mirrored and the density of the light points are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the depth of water. Elongated leaves of deep bottle green shading into transparency at the rim — a colour that belongs to a body of water, not to its surface. Large smooth curves catch and stretch reflections, so the object never looks the same from two positions.

The leaves are laid in overlapping layers in a spiral. The top is dense, below the rim breaks off cleanly and only bare rods continue — the thicket is lifted above the floor, like weed torn loose from the bed.

By day it is a clear sculpture: the green reads as dense, almost stone-like. In the evening light enters the body from the edge and spreads across the whole plane of the leaf — the green fills from within and turns emerald, while the gold of the rods shows through, adding a warm vein to a cold colour. The thicket comes alive.
LC0194.whereItWorks: A saturated colour needs a calm ground — living rooms, winter gardens, spas, reception rooms, restaurant interiors. It works well by a window, where daylight is added to the artificial.
LC0194.style: Art Nouveau and organic modernism: the same line as the vases of Gallé and Daum. The message is collector-minded — a piece for someone who chooses colour as the principal argument.
LC0194.madeToOrder: The column height, the number of leaves, the depth of the green tone and the metal finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about coal. Black outside, heat within — a device as old as a campfire, brought here to a form. Crumpled discs of deep black with a mirrored gloss: each pressed in at the middle and rolled at the edge, as though a finger had been laid on it while the form was still soft. The load-bearing structure is polished gold, and it shows only in the gaps.
The discs are set in layers, turned in different directions, covering the gold with themselves. The column reads as a black mass with metal breaking through from beneath.

By day it is a dark monolith — a thing that absorbs light rather than giving it back. In the evening the mass opens: narrow hot bands emerge, lighting the gold linings. A pair of these lamps flanking a sofa in a dark room gives no general light — they set two vertical columns of glow with the scene held between them.
LC0195.whereItWorks: A dark palette and dramatic light — living rooms in deep tones, private studies, bars, lounges, showrooms. They work better in pairs than singly.
LC0195.style: Dark luxury and brutalist modernism: black with gold, no lightness at all. The message is masculine and club-like — a piece for an interior that does not flirt.
LC0195.madeToOrder: The height, the number of discs, the gilding finish and the depth of the black are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the lining. Every element is a broad sickle with a deep hollow: white and opaque outside, polished gold within. The author turns each element on its axis its own way, and the column begins to play at openness: one shows a white back, the next reveals a gold interior.

The tiers run unevenly, with gatherings and gaps — you read a branch with large leaves, or an inflorescence opening upward. The stem and base are in the same gold: the structure is reduced to a single vertical, all attention on the crown.

By day it is graphics — white silhouettes on a gold shaft, sculpture without light. In the evening the gold within heats to a honeyed tone and throws reflected light outward: not one direct point, only a warm radiance out of the hollows. The white outside stays cool. The piece literally glows from inside.
LC0196.whereItWorks: A large crown and soft reflected light — living rooms, halls, reception rooms, showrooms, restaurant areas. It needs height to spare and a clear wall behind it.
LC0196.style: Hollywood glamour and contemporary Art Deco: white with gold, the contrast of opaque and mirrored. The message is representative — a piece for an interior that receives guests.
LC0196.madeToOrder: The height, the number of elements, the gilding finish and the colour of the outer surface are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the unopened. A pine cone, a bud, a cocoon — a form in which everything already exists but nothing has yet been shown. The author takes the image literally: pointed petals with a soft twist are laid overlapping in a spiral, each course covering the one before, the rim breaking off below in sharp tips.
The lower half of the column is deliberately left empty — bare rods only. The mass gathers at the top, at eye level: the object does not grow from the floor, it hangs like fruit on a branch.

By day it is a dense milky sculpture — opaque, cool, without a single highlight. In the evening a core wakes inside: through the slots between the petals a warm orange burning is visible, while the petals themselves stay milky and cold. That difference is the whole character of the piece: calm outside, heat within.
LC0197.whereItWorks: Soft diffuse light and a vertical silhouette — living rooms, bedrooms, reception rooms, lounges, hotel rooms. It suits places that need not general light but a point of presence.
LC0197.style: Scandinavian minimalism and organic modernism: a pure natural form without ornament. The message is quiet and intimate — a piece for an interior that values silence and material clarity.
LC0197.madeToOrder: The column height, the number of petals, the tone of the glow and the finish of the rods are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about light stacked like a wall. Links with an opening at their centre are laid in offset layers — the device is taken from masonry, where strength rests not on mortar but on order. The author pushes it to a paradox: the masonry comes out transparent.
Clear links alternate with mirror-gold ones, and there is no system to the alternation — the column reads as built by hand rather than cast. Gaps remain between the courses: the mass breathes.

By day it is an architectural fragment — a column lifted out of a portico and set down in a room. In the evening the masonry opens from within: light passes through the clear links, flares on their rounded ribs, and is intercepted by the gold ones and thrown outward in warm patches. The wall becomes a sieve of light.
LC0198.whereItWorks: A vertical on a slender stem needs a free corner and a view from a distance — living rooms, halls, reception rooms, lounges, showrooms. It works well in pairs flanking an axis: a sofa, a fireplace, an entrance.
LC0198.style: Art Deco and contemporary classicism: the same language as the bronze floor lamps of the thirties, but with no ornament — only module and rhythm. The message is architectural: a piece for someone who values structure over decoration.
LC0198.madeToOrder: The column height, the number of links, the ratio of clear to gold and the metal finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A weave that reads differently from every side. A white ribbon runs inward, a gold rod comes out, the next ribbon covers it again — volume is built by alternation rather than by thickness.
The lower half is left empty: bare rods only. All the mass and all the light gather at the top, at the eye level of a standing person, while the lower part works as a leg.

By day it is a sculptural column with rich plasticity — you can see how one and the same ribbon is white at one edge and shows a gold lining at the other. In the evening the light emerges through the cells of the lattice, and the column begins to glow from within, evenly, without a single direct point.
LC0199.whereItWorks: Living rooms, halls, reception rooms, lounges, showrooms, hotel lobbies.
LC0199.style: Contemporary Art Deco and Eastern luxury: brass, deep tones, rugs, carving. The message is craft — a composition about the maker's hand, legible in every interlacing.
LC0199.madeToOrder: The column height, the density of the weave, the finish of the rods and the colour of the ribbons are all made to order.

paragraphs: A column shedding feathers. The column is dense at the middle and thinned at its ends: below, individual feathers break away from the mass and hang on their own, as though they had only just fallen.

The light runs along the axis and spreads into the grooves of the vane: every feather glows in strokes rather than as a patch. The amber ones fill from within, the clear ones give highlights — one structure, two behaviours.

By day the lamp reads as a clear sculpture at human height — all but invisible, only contours and flares along the ribs. In the evening the spiral lights up from bottom to top, and the column becomes a shaft of light that is losing feathers.
LC0200.whereItWorks: Living rooms, halls, private reception rooms, showrooms, restaurant areas, lobbies.
LC0200.style: Art Nouveau and contemporary opulence: flowing lines, gilding, natural textures. The message is moulting — a composition about plumage renewing itself while the bird stays.
LC0200.madeToOrder: The column height, the number of feathers and the ratio of amber to clear are all made to order.

paragraphs: A pod in motion, not a set of figures. The dolphins run in waves, some higher, some lower, all turned the same way — you read direction and speed.

The form is reduced to a pure silhouette, without detail: only the line of movement works. The light falls on the polished flanks and rolls out along the body — a glowing rib flares on every figure from nose to tail.

By day it is graphics against a dark ground — silhouettes, rhythm, pure line. In the evening not one source is visible directly: only the metal glows, and the pod moves through a body of water lit from the surface.
LC0201.whereItWorks: For generous volumes: atria, lobbies, pools and spas, panoramic living rooms, children's and family zones.
LC0201.style: Marine modernism and contemporary minimalism: white walls, water, pale timber. The message is the joy of movement — a composition about animals that swim not out of need but because they can.
LC0201.madeToOrder: The length, the number of figures, the direction of the pod and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A wall of rain caught in a single frame. The rods stand in a dense array, the lower edge wavy from the difference in heights — a downpour in which every thread is visible.

The light runs down the rod like a lightguide: the rod itself glows faintly while the drop at its end flares. The form of the drop is taken from a real one — at the moment of release, when it has left the surface but is not yet falling.

By day the composition reads graphically, as pure hatching against a pale ceiling. In the evening the rods vanish altogether and a row of bright points remains, suspended in the air: rain with the lines erased and only the drops left.
LC0202.whereItWorks: For large spaces: lobbies, atria, stairwells, double-height living rooms, banquet halls.
LC0202.style: Contemporary minimalism and high-tech: clean planes, transparency, an absence of decoration. The message is reduction — a composition about how one drop is enough to stand for rain.
LC0202.madeToOrder: The overall size, the rod lengths, the calibre of the drops and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A meadow with fewer flowers in it than it seems. There are not many buds, but hundreds of small beads between them — the density is created not by the flowers but by what has not yet bloomed.
The light is distributed in patches: some hearts burn, others stay dark. That is how a real meadow looks, with the sun breaking through unevenly — evenness here would be a falsehood.

By day it is a botanical study — fine, pale, almost weightless. In the evening the meadow rises to the ceiling and lights up from within: the flowers do not all come on at once, and the field begins to shimmer in patches.
LC0203.whereItWorks: For living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, winter gardens, wedding venues.
LC0203.style: Romantic modernism and eco-classicism: pale walls, living greenery, natural fabrics. The message is the first bloom — a composition about early spring, when not everything is flowering yet.
LC0203.madeToOrder: The overall diameter, the number of flowers, the ratio of pearlescent to gold and the density of the buds are all made to order.

paragraphs: A ridge of ice floes forced to the surface. The shards stand vertically in a dense array, slightly turned toward one another — the way ice rises into pressure ridges when a field is squeezed.

The surface is uneven, as if split; some elements are colourless, others richly turquoise, and there are transitions where colour is drawn into the clear body as an uneven patch. Brightness wanders from element to element because of the differing thickness.

By day it is a section through a glacier — cold, faceted, with internal shadows. In the evening the light runs from above along the whole plane, the clear elements flare white at their bases, the turquoise fill entirely: an aurora brought down to the table.
LC0204.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — for long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, reception areas, restaurant floors.
LC0204.style: Nordic minimalism and contemporary luxury: concrete, pale timber, a cold palette, panoramic windows. The message is austere beauty — a composition about ice that does not melt.
LC0204.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the share of turquoise and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same crown on a light base — and the object changes character. You can move it with one hand; it does not bind a zone to itself the way the stone versions do.
The light emerges reflected off the gold faces: no direct source is visible from any position. For a lamp standing at the eye level of a seated person, that matters.
By day it is a decorative sculpture on a stem — mobile, almost weightless. In the evening it gives a soft warm patch around a chair: not illumination for a room, but a circle in which people sit.
LC0205.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, studies, zones beside a chair or sofa, hotel rooms, reading corners.
LC0205.style: Contemporary classicism and comfortable minimalism: pale walls, textiles, timber. The message is personal space — a composition about light for one person.
LC0205.madeToOrder: The height, the crown diameter, the number of ribbons and the base finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A ribbon that changes colour as it turns. Every element is twisted a half-turn on its axis: white gloss on one side, gold on the other — and the crown never looks the same twice.
The lower edge is ragged: individual ribbons descend deeper than the rest. The base is a dark wedge with a bright white vein along its face, and between it and the crown there is almost nothing.

By day it is a sculpture in twisted metal — dense, rhythmic, with the interplay of two finishes. In the evening the light falls on the gold faces and reflects in warm patches while the white ones stay cool: a vortex of sparks hangs above black stone.
LC0206.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, reception rooms, lounges, studies, hotel rooms.
LC0206.style: Contemporary Art Deco and graphic modernism: contrasting combinations, black with gold, mirrors. The message is duality — a composition about a thing with two sides, both of them true.
LC0206.madeToOrder: The height, the crown diameter, the number of ribbons and the stone of the base are all made to order.

paragraphs: An icy bush on a stone plinth. The crown looks accreted rather than manufactured: uneven branches with runs, descending in layers of varying length.

The scale shows in the photograph with a model: the lamp stands a head above waist height, the crown reaching the shoulder. This is not a side light but an object in its own right, holding the zone around it.

By day it is a sculpture — a clear crown on pale stone with grey veining, pure geometry. In the evening the light travels down into the branches from above, the tips flare brighter than the rest, and the bush gives soft diffuse light without a single direct highlight.
LC0207.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, halls, private rest zones, showrooms, boutique hotel lobbies.
LC0207.style: Nordic minimalism and Alpine luxury: pale stone, timber, spare detailing, plenty of air. The message is clarity — a composition about winter without a single superfluous colour.
LC0207.madeToOrder: The height, the crown diameter, the branch lengths and the stone of the base are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same cone, but set on stone — and a different object because of it. Instead of a light disc beneath the shade there is now a heavy wedge, and the lamp becomes substantial, almost architectural.
The difference in mass is the device: stone below, air above, a slender stem between them. The shade meanwhile stays as it was — airy, layered, full of gaps.

By day it is a stone column with a cluster on top — a contrast of weight read instantly. In the evening the clear elements transmit the light, the mirrored ones reflect it, and the stone below picks up the reflection until the white vein within it begins to glow.
LC0208.whereItWorks: Living rooms, halls, private studies, reception rooms, lobbies, showrooms.
LC0208.style: Brutalist luxury and contemporary classicism: unworked stone, dark timber, brass. The message is support — a composition about lightness needing weight.
LC0208.madeToOrder: The height, the shade diameter, the ratio of clear to mirrored and the stone of the base are all made to order.

paragraphs: Frost settled on rock. Below, stone with violet, ochre and golden veining — the most colourful element in the whole structure; above, a colourless mass working purely through refraction.

The light passes from pendant to pendant, refracting at each: from outside it is impossible to tell where the source is — the cone itself glows. Onto the stone the light falls from above and lights the veining, so it fills with colour.
By day it is a stone column with an icy cap — heavy below, clear above. In the evening the cap lights up from within and the stone answers from below: two glows moving toward each other.
LC0209.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, private reception rooms, rest zones, studies, hotel rooms.
LC0209.style: Alpine luxury and contemporary classicism: stone, timber, large windows, a cold palette. The message is a mountain winter — a composition about frost on rock on the first sunlit morning.
LC0209.madeToOrder: The height, the shade diameter, the set of pendants and the stone of the base are all made to order.

paragraphs: A bush lit from within. The branches are uneven, knotted, dividing — a form taken from a coral colony or from driftwood tumbled by the sea.

The light hides inside the fringe and emerges only through the gaps, in narrow warm slots. The grain of the finish will not let a beam slide across it: the light breaks up, and the crown shimmers instead of gleaming.
By day it is a metal sculpture on a stem — warm, dense, richly textured. In the evening the cool stem recedes into darkness and only the glowing bush remains, grown out of nothing.
LC0210.whereItWorks: Living rooms, halls, lounges, private studies, showrooms, restaurant areas.
LC0210.style: Eco-luxury and organic modernism: natural stone, timber, a subdued palette. The message is growth — a composition about a form that branches by laws of its own.
LC0210.madeToOrder: The height, the crown diameter, the branch lengths and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A cluster filling with light. The petals are crushed as though squeezed in a fist — the form was not calculated but obtained, and that is what makes it convincing.
Clear and mirrored are mixed without system: the cone shimmers in patches — cool transparency here, a warm flare there. The stem is deliberately reduced to a minimum so the shade appears to hover.

By day it is a sculptural object on a stem — light, almost invisible against a pale ground. In the evening the light catches between the layers, the source is lost, and the cone becomes a cluster filled to the brim.
LC0211.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, lounges, private reception rooms, hotel rooms, studies.
LC0211.style: Contemporary classicism and soft modernism: pale walls, rounded furniture, brass. The message is ripening — a composition about something filling up rather than something shining.
LC0211.madeToOrder: The height, the cone diameter, the number of petals and the ratio of clear to mirrored are all made to order.

paragraphs: A structure held together by a difference in weight. Below, a heavy dark block with a white vein; above, a weightless fringe — and between them a stem that all but disappears in the dark.

The branches are uneven, with runs and swellings: an icicle grown in layers, or a fragment of coral. The fringe is set at varying lengths — shorter at the outside, deeper toward the centre — so the lower edge comes out alive.

By day it is a sculpture on a stone plinth — a clear crown, a dark base, the pure graphics of the stem. In the evening the branches glow along their whole length and most brightly at their tips: the fringe looks as though it is thawing, about to start dripping.
LC0212.whereItWorks: Living rooms, halls, private studies, hotel rest zones, lounges, reception rooms.
LC0212.style: Nordic modernism and brutalist luxury: stone, dark timber, a cold palette, large volumes. The message is the thaw — a composition about the moment winter begins to give way.
LC0212.madeToOrder: The height, the crown diameter, the branch lengths and the stone of the base are all made to order.

paragraphs: Velvet below, thorns above. The contrast is set hard: an opaque matte base across which light does not slide but settles in bands, and a bristling luminous crown where every rib catches a beam.
Spiral ribbing winds around the body through its full height — a vertical that rotates slightly while standing still. Three tiers of the crown descend in steps, repeating that movement from above.

By day the lamp reads as a sculptural vessel with a large crown — dark, dense, almost stone-like. In the evening the light passes through the crown in vertical hatching and lights the neck: the violet fills and deepens, while the crown above it flares into sparks.
LC0213.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, studies, private reception rooms — wherever light is needed without a ceiling fixing.
LC0213.style: Art Deco and contemporary opulence: deep colours, velvet, mirrors, brass fittings. The message is a jewel on a plinth — a composition about stone and faceting, set one upon the other.
LC0213.madeToOrder: The height, the tone of the base, the number of tiers and the calibre of the crown are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same architecture, translated into geometry. Instead of a flowing botanical motif — a strict repeat: lozenges, meanders, broken bands running in a spiral around the body.

The only difference between the two versions is the graphic on the body, but it decides everything: the botanical drawing gives classicism, the geometric one gives modernity with an Eastern accent. One silhouette, two eras.

By day it is a decorative vessel with a large crown — dense, rhythmic, almost architectural. In the evening the light emerges as even hatching and settles on the shoulders of the vase: a column with engraved metal burning at its foot.
LC0214.whereItWorks: Living rooms, studies, lounges, private reception rooms, showrooms, hotel rooms.
LC0214.style: Contemporary Art Deco and Eastern minimalism: sharp graphics, metal, monochrome. The message is order — a composition about ornament as a system rather than as decoration.
LC0214.madeToOrder: The height, the graphic of the repeat, the finish and the number of tiers are all made to order.

paragraphs: An Eastern engraving hidden in a mirror. The ornament is matte on a mirrored ground, so it reads only at an angle and changes as you walk around — the pattern appears, then vanishes.
The shade is stepped: three tiers descending in steps, each smaller than the last. The silhouette comes out like a collar or a headdress — a thing with bearing rather than with a shade.

By day the lamp works as a sculptural vessel with a large crown, and the ornament is visible only close to. In the evening the lantern comes on: the lower tier lights the neck, the mirror kindles, and the pattern emerges as a contour — an engraving that appears when it gets dark.
LC0215.whereItWorks: Living rooms, studies, bedrooms, private rest zones — wherever light is needed without a ceiling fixing.
LC0215.style: Eastern luxury and Art Deco: deep colours, brass, rugs, carving. The message is a cipher — a composition about a pattern that does not reveal itself at once.
LC0215.madeToOrder: The height, the etching pattern, the finish and the number of tiers are all made to order.

paragraphs: A leaf that changes colour as it turns. One side is cool and matte, the other warm and mirrored — the element switches over entirely at the slightest swing.
The composition hangs at random, some leaves dropping below the main mass. The upper zone stays transparent — only the net of cables — so the object looks as if it were hovering, for all its size.

By day it is a leaf-fall stilled in the air: silver and gold intermixed, not one identical inclination. In the evening the light scatters unevenly, reflecting now cool, now warm, and the composition shimmers the moment you shift a step: a swarm of sparks that lives off the viewer's movement.
LC0216.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — for long dining tables, bar counters, lobbies, meeting rooms, restaurant floors.
LC0216.style: Contemporary classicism and soft Art Deco: mirrors, brass, pale walls. The message is variability — a composition about a thing that never shows the same face twice.
LC0216.madeToOrder: The length, the number of leaves, the ratio of cool to warm and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: Marked Award Winning — the badge appears on the brand photography for this item.
Pure plasticity of line. Two bands run one above the other, rising, falling, twisting at their ends and parting — not one repeated passage along the whole length.
The ribbing changes density as it turns: the ribbon almost disappears, then fills with colour. The lights along the rim are set unevenly and emphasise the curves precisely where the line turns.

By day it is two smoky bands frozen in the air — nearly graphics, nearly a technical drawing. In the evening the light runs along the rim and scatters across the ribbing in fine highlights: what remains is a trace left by light in the dark — a stroke with no visible hand behind it.
LC0217.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format for long spaces: dining halls, meeting rooms, lobbies, reception areas, galleries.
LC0217.style: Contemporary minimalism and gallery aesthetics: empty walls, large planes, an absence of small decoration. The message is the gesture — a composition about the movement of a hand rather than about an object.
LC0217.madeToOrder: The length of the bands, the wave pattern, the tone and the number of lights along the rim are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same line, released to any length. The composition is counted in running metres: the ribbon is extended section by section, and the pattern of the wave is composed for the particular room — a flourish with no set size.

The device of the line is kept whole: the ribbing changes density as it turns, and the lights along the edge are spaced unevenly, stressing the bends where the line turns. No section repeats its neighbour, because repetition would kill the gesture.

By day it is a smoky band frozen in the air — almost graphic work, almost a drawing, read through its trajectory and the hatching of the ribbing. In the evening light runs along the edge and scatters over the ribbing in small flecks: what remains is a trace left by light in the dark.
LC0217-1.whereItWorks: Long spaces — dining halls, meeting rooms, lobbies, receptions, galleries, corridors. The length is chosen for the zone: the composition can run the whole length of a table or follow the perimeter of a room.
LC0217-1.style: Contemporary minimalism and gallery aesthetics: bare walls, large planes, no small decor. The message is a gesture — the composition is about the movement of a hand, not about an object.
LC0217-1.madeToOrder: The length of the ribbon, the pattern of the wave, the shade and the number of lights along the edge are all made to order.

paragraphs: A grove, not a row. The leaves hang at varied levels and orientations, and between them run bare rods with glowing points: hatching that establishes volume where there is no foliage.

The colour is subdued and olive: in places the surface is almost colourless, in others it thickens to bottle green. The faceted planes catch light differently, and one and the same green reads now warm, now cold.

By day the composition is restrained, almost graphic — dark foliage against a pale ground. In the evening the green fills from within, the tips flare as points, and the chrome reflects it all upward: a deep green tone rarely seen in ceiling light.
LC0218.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — for long tables, meeting rooms, bar counters, reception areas, winter gardens.
LC0218.style: Mediterranean modernism and eco-luxury: pale stone, timber, living plants, a subdued palette. The message is a southern grove — a composition about dry warmth and shade beneath a canopy.
LC0218.madeToOrder: The length, the number of leaves, the tone of the green and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: The regular hatching of water and the free movement of living things inside it. The whole idea rests on that contrast: the rain is dense and even, the shoal sparse and unruly.
The fish give no light: the gold ones reflect, the white ones stay silhouettes. What glows is the medium, not its inhabitants — the reverse of the usual device, and memorable for it.

By day the composition reads as a shoal in clear water: you see both the fish and the hatching. In the evening the water lights up and the fish recede into shadow — the medium comes forward and crowds out those who live in it.
LC0219.whereItWorks: For generous volumes with high ceilings: atria, lobbies, pools and spas, double-height living rooms, children's spaces.
LC0219.style: Marine modernism and resort luxury: water, white stone, pale timber. The message is that the medium matters more than the figure — a composition about how water defines everything within it.
LC0219.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of fish, the ratio of gold to white and the density of the rain are all made to order.

paragraphs: A meadow seen from below. The flowers face downward, each hanging at its own cable length, denser below and sparser above — an inverted pyramid the viewer looks into from underground.

The light hides in the gold hearts and runs down into the tassels, flaring at their tips as bright points. The white form gives no light at all — it works as silhouette, while all the brightness gathers in the hearts and threads.
By day it is a field of flowers hung from the ceiling — white, matte, calm. In the evening a luminous fringe of its own hangs beneath every flower: a swarm of fireflies, each with its own cup.
LC0220.whereItWorks: For generous spaces with high ceilings: atria, lobbies, double-height living rooms, winter gardens, spas.
LC0220.style: Romantic modernism and eco-classicism: pale walls, living greenery, natural textures. The message is the first bloom — a composition about what pushes through before anything else and is valued for it.
LC0220.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of flowers, the length of the tassels and the finish of the hearts are all made to order.

paragraphs: A column of bubbles in a glass. The composition looks as though it were rising rather than hanging: the top is held by an even net of cables while the spheres are grouped in clusters, as if pushed up from below.

Each sphere refracts in its own way, so no two are alike. The light hides in only a few and is passed onward: the neighbours pick it up, refract it and diffuse it — the whole mass glows and the sources never read.
By day it is a scatter of honey drops suspended in the air. In the evening the amber gives a warm aura that settles on ceiling and walls: the room ends up inside the glass rather than beneath it.
LC0221.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — for long tables, bar counters, lobbies, panoramic living rooms, wine rooms.
LC0221.style: Warm modernism and gastronomic luxury: timber, brass, subdued light, deep tones. The message is a celebration at the table — a composition about that point in an evening when the second round has been poured.
LC0221.madeToOrder: The overall size, the calibres of the spheres, the density of the clusters and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: Water striking an invisible obstacle. Above, the ribbons run strictly vertical in a tight bundle; lower down they separate and curve gently outward — a jet that has met something you cannot see.
Below, the composition grows luminous steps: narrow vertical plates at varying heights form an uneven toothed border — where the jets end, light begins.

By day it is a metal curtain — austere, graphic, with a clean vertical. In the evening the ribbons reflect light along their whole length and turn into glowing lines, while the plates burn from within as even warm rectangles: a flow frozen at the moment of falling.
LC0222.whereItWorks: For living rooms, halls, zones above a round table, stair landings, reception rooms.
LC0222.style: Art Deco and contemporary opulence: gilding, vertical divisions, symmetry. The message is a waterfall indoors — the force of an element brought to strict geometry.
LC0222.madeToOrder: The base diameter, the length and number of ribbons, the set of plates and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: Marked Award Winning — the badge appears on the brand photography for this item.
A crown that grew rather than being assembled. The petal form is deliberately irregular: rolled, broken, slightly twisted at the edge — not one repeats its neighbour.
Density is uneven: thick at the middle, sparse toward the ends of the branch. That is how real flowering behaves, where resources never stretch to everything at once.

By day it is a branch in bloom — white, light, with occasional gold accents. In the evening the light goes inside the buds: the white shows through in warm milk, the gold reflects in hard highlights, and from below the composition reads as an inflorescence lit from within.
LC0223.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — for long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, reception areas, wedding venues.
LC0223.style: Contemporary classicism and romantic modernism: pale walls, brass, a pastel palette. The message is flowering — a composition about spring stopped at its best point.
LC0223.madeToOrder: The length of the branch, the number of flowers, the share of gold buds and the density of the crown are all made to order.

paragraphs: A wood in autumn sun. Some elements are almost invisible, others burn amber — the mass never reads as dense, it shimmers in patches, like a crown with low sunlight striking through it.
Inside every element clear and gold are mixed in uneven runs: on some the gold takes almost the whole area, on others it stays a thin vein. No two are alike.

By day it is a cloud of crumpled film — light, rustling, almost transparent. In the evening the light passes through several layers and changes temperature on the way: through the clear it stays white, through the amber it fills with copper — a swarm of burning autumn leaves.
LC0224.whereItWorks: For living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, zones above a table, winter gardens.
LC0224.style: Eco-modernism and warm classicism: timber, brass, natural fabrics, a subdued palette. The message is an Indian summer — a composition about the short season when light turns golden.
LC0224.madeToOrder: The overall diameter, the number of elements, the share of amber and the drop height are all made to order.

paragraphs: Ripple instead of surface. The mosaic is set so that neighbouring facets face different ways: dense green here, almost white there, drifting into sea blue elsewhere — the colour is not fixed, it fluctuates.
The ribbon is rolled into a free loop and never repeats itself at any point. The only firm line in the whole form is the fine edging along the rim, which is also what holds it.

By day it is a sculpture in broken ice — cold, faceted, scattering highlights. In the evening the turquoise fills from within, the edging flares along the contour, and the ice becomes a wave lit from beneath.
LC0225.whereItWorks: For living rooms with high ceilings, lobbies, zones above a round table, spas and pools, restaurant floors.
LC0225.style: Contemporary modernism and a marine theme without literalness: pale stone, water, panoramic glazing. The message is the movement of water — a composition about how the surface of the sea is never level.
LC0225.madeToOrder: The dimensions of the ribbon, the pattern of the curve, the tone of the turquoise and the finish of the edging are all made to order.

paragraphs: Shell and burning core. From outside the element stays white and opaque; inside it burns — the light emerges through a narrow warm slot at the fold.

The flock is not drawn up but scattered: rods of varying length, elements at varying angles, as though the wind had just caught them. The upper zone stays transparent — only rods running to the ceiling.

By day it is a cloud of white paper: folded sheets, wings, sails — the form reads as all of these at once. In the evening only the linings glow, and the swarm becomes a flock burning on the reverse of its wings.
LC0226.whereItWorks: For large horizontal spaces: lobbies, dining rooms, meeting rooms, panoramic living rooms, banquet halls.
LC0226.style: Contemporary minimalism and Japanese aesthetics: paper, timber, clean planes, an absence of ornament. The message is origami — something complex obtained by one fold of something simple.
LC0226.madeToOrder: The area of the composition, the number of elements, the density of the flock and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A spiral still unwinding. The top is almost empty, the whole mass below — the composition is caught at the beginning of a movement, not at its end.

Every petal is crumpled, like one that has fallen and dried at the edge. The inner face is gilded, the outer matte white: the light strikes the lining and emerges already reflected — warm, soft, without direct points.

By day it is a vortex of fallen petals — white, dry, almost graphic. In the evening gold flares deep within the white mass: two colours live on every element at once, and a cool surface turns out to be lit from inside.
LC0227.whereItWorks: A vertical format for tall openings: a stairwell, an atrium, a double-height living room, a lift shaft, a bay window.
LC0227.style: Contemporary classicism and soft modernism: pale walls, gilded details, rounded furniture. The message is the moment of falling — a composition about beauty that has already begun to leave.
LC0227.madeToOrder: The height of the spiral, the number of petals, the pitch of the twist and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: Marked Award Winning — the badge appears on the brand photography for this item.
A skirt in movement. The tiers are laid in a wave: the hems run not in a circle but along a free line, rising and falling — the same curve fabric takes from a step.
The colour chosen is one on its way out: tea rose caught at the moment of fading. Not a fresh pink but the kind that will turn brown by tomorrow — and that is the whole character of the piece.

By day it is smoky fabric folded in the air — dense, matte, almost textile. In the evening the light runs down into the tubes from above, every tier lights up as vertical hatching, and dark divisions stay between the tiers: a dress put on over light.
LC0228.whereItWorks: A large format for formal spaces: double-height living rooms, lobbies, banquet halls, atria, theatre foyers.
LC0228.style: Theatrical classicism and neo-Baroque: velvet, drapery, mouldings, deep tones. The message is a stage gesture — a composition about costume rather than about a luminaire.
LC0228.madeToOrder: The number of tiers, the length and pattern of the wave, the tone and the finish of the hems are all made to order.

paragraphs: Ink released into water. Cobalt is drawn into the clear body in uneven bands and swirls — a pattern water makes for itself and never repeats.
From a distance the composition reads as a single shoal moving as one; close up it breaks into separate bodies, each with its own marking. Scale decides what you see — the shoal or its members.

By day the object is restrained and almost graphic: cool silhouettes against a pale ground. In the evening the blue comes on at full strength, the light passes through several layers and emerges as a cold radiance — the room goes underwater entirely.
LC0229.whereItWorks: For generous spaces with high ceilings: atria, lobbies, pools, spas, double-height living rooms, restaurant floors.
LC0229.style: Marine modernism and contemporary minimalism: white walls, water, natural stone, panoramic windows. The message is depth — the composition changes not the lighting of a room but its medium.
LC0229.madeToOrder: The overall size, the number of figures, the depth of the cobalt tone and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: Shards, not blanks. The edges are torn, cut at random angles, the surface undulating — every plate reflects light unevenly, in bands, like foil smoothed out by hand.

One and the same set gives two characters: a free circle with gaps reads as an explosion, a regular grid as order. The composition changes its meaning with the layout while staying identical in content.

By day it is graphics made of highlights: the undulating surface catches the light of the room, and the pattern never repeats — it depends on what is happening around it. In the evening a contour lights up behind the plates and the wall becomes a scatter of luminous mirrors.
LC0230.whereItWorks: Feature walls, fireplace surrounds, stair flights, reception areas, private studies.
LC0230.style: Contemporary art and brutalist minimalism: large planes, concrete, unworked stone. The message is the trace of destruction — a composition about the beauty of what was once whole.
LC0230.madeToOrder: The area of the layout, the number of plates, the layout scheme and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A snowfall with no lower boundary. The mass is dense at the centre and thins toward the edges, the top empty — only a net of cables. The object seems to hover rather than hang.

The shards are of varying calibre and scattered with no grid at all: from large plates down to crumbs. The light refracts on every facet and travels onward to the neighbours — the whole composition glows and the source is impossible to find.

By day it is snow stilled in the air — cold, silvery, almost soundless. In the evening rare warm points appear among the cold sparks, and the snowfall becomes a swarm of fireflies over water: a winter with summer loose inside it.
LC0231.whereItWorks: For large horizontal spaces: lobbies, dining rooms, meeting rooms, panoramic living rooms, banquet halls.
LC0231.style: Nordic minimalism and contemporary classicism: pale walls, plenty of air, a subdued palette. The message is quiet — a composition about snow that falls while everyone sleeps.
LC0231.madeToOrder: The width and depth of the composition, the density of the shards and the share of warm points are all made to order.

paragraphs: Plasticity fixed at the moment the material was still yielding. Every element is twisted and rolled into a funnel, and the form is never repeated — this is not a series but a multitude of individual decisions.
The tinting is deep: on the curves the surface gives a mirrored gleam, against the light a warm amber. A single element reads as dense and transparent at once, depending on where the eye falls.

By day it is a cloud of crumpled gold foil — light, seemingly rustling. In the evening the light passes through several layers in a row, the source is lost, and the cloud becomes a swarm of burning petals with not a single visible lamp.
LC0232.whereItWorks: For living rooms with high ceilings, stairwells, lobbies, zones above a round table, banquet halls.
LC0232.style: Art Deco and contemporary opulence: gilding, deep tones, large scale. The message is the generosity of the material — a composition about abundance presented without symmetry.
LC0232.madeToOrder: The overall diameter, the number of elements, the depth of the tinting and the drop height are all made to order.

paragraphs: A branch that has wound itself around a space. The base is curved into a broad loop in the horizontal plane — it reads not as a structure but as something that grew and took the place.

The foliage comes in three kinds: clear with relief, opaque white and mirrored gold. They are mixed without system, so the crown looks grown rather than assembled. A second reading also exists — wholly clear, where the entire mass becomes almost colourless.

By day it is a branch taken from a tree and gilded — dry, graphic. In the evening the foliage lights up unevenly: the clear glows right through, the matte smoulders in patches, the mirrored reflects its neighbours — one crown, three different fires.
LC0233.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — for long tables, kitchen islands, meeting rooms, reception areas, restaurant floors.
LC0233.style: Eco-modernism and contemporary classicism: warm timber, brass, living plants. The message is natural disorder — a composition about how nature never lines its elements up in a row.
LC0233.madeToOrder: The length of the branch, the composition of the foliage, the palette and the density of the crown are all made to order.

paragraphs: The birds do not glow — the flowers do. The division of roles is strict: source below, reflector above, and the whole scene rests on the hunter being lit by its prey.
The form of the birds is reduced to a few planes but is recognised instantly. Part of the flock is mirrored and gold, part matte and graphite — the variety keeps it alive rather than stamped out.

By day it is sculpture: dark silhouettes, polished flanks, pure plasticity. In the evening a flower lights up beneath every bird, and warm patches appear on the polished metal — a flock hovering above the field that lights it.
LC0234.whereItWorks: For living rooms, stairwells, lobbies, winter gardens, restaurants, rest zones.
LC0234.style: Art Nouveau and organic modernism: living greenery, natural textures, brass fittings. The message is the moment before contact — a composition about an instant that lasts because it has been stopped.
LC0234.madeToOrder: The number of birds, the ratio of mirrored to matte, the form of the cup and the drop height are all made to order.

paragraphs: A lens instead of a lamp. The elements do not glow of themselves — they gather light arriving from above and from the side, and work as optics rather than as a source.

The curvature of every crescent is arranged so that a gold core appears in its depth while a glowing thread runs along the thickened rim. The form is transparent to the point of invisibility, yet the light within it is visible — the object disappears and the effect remains.
By day the composition barely reads: only highlights and contours against a pale ground. In the evening it becomes a cloud of warm lights, each set into an invisible mount.
LC0235.whereItWorks: An elongated horizontal format — for long dining tables, bar counters, meeting rooms, generous halls, restaurants.
LC0235.style: Contemporary minimalism and optical design: white walls, clean lines, an absence of ornament. The message is light without a luminaire — the composition gives all attention to the effect and removes the object.
LC0235.madeToOrder: The length, the number of elements, the density of the layers and the colour temperature are all made to order.

paragraphs: Marked Award Winning — the badge appears on the brand photography for this item.

Mass gives form, light gives movement. The whole idea rests on that division: the white bodies are motionless and silent, while the trail beneath them lives and stirs at the slightest movement of air.

The threads glow only at their tips, so a cloud of shimmering points hangs beneath every figure — the wake of particles behind a creature moving through water. The body does not glow at all: it only casts a shadow onto its own trail.

By day it is a flock of white sculptures below the ceiling — dense, matte, without a single highlight. In the evening the bodies recede into shadow and only the luminous rain remains: the flock disappears while its wake stays.
LC0236.whereItWorks: For large volumes: atria, lobbies, double-height living rooms, pools and spas, banquet halls.
LC0236.style: Contemporary minimalism and biophilic design: white walls, water, natural textures, plenty of air. The message is the presence of the invisible — a composition about how movement is more visible than whatever is moving.
LC0236.madeToOrder: The number of figures, the length of the trails, the area and the height of the composition are all made to order.

paragraphs: Marked Award Winning — the badge appears on the brand photography for this item.
A view from the bottom of a pond. The composition is built to be looked at from below: only then does the view open through several layers of turquoise toward the surface, toward the light.
The colour is not uniform — dense, almost emerald at the stalk, lightening toward the edge to clear water. This is the gradient of a real body of water: the closer to the surface, the paler.

By day the object stays calm and graphic — foliage laid out in tiers. In the evening the water switches on: the turquoise glows from within, the gold of the branches picks up the reflection, and the composition acquires an underwater aura it did not have by day.
Two vertical variants are shown, differing in height and in the density of the tiers.
LC0237.whereItWorks: For stairwells, double-height living rooms, zones beside panoramic glazing, spas, pools, winter gardens.
LC0237.style: Eco-modernism and resort luxury: water, natural stone, living greenery, pale walls. The message is immersion — the composition puts the viewer underwater rather than in front of an aquarium.
LC0237.madeToOrder: The height, the number of leaves, the tone of the turquoise and the finish of the branches are all made to order.

paragraphs: A column with no boundary. Density is distributed unevenly: the mass is thick at the middle, thinner toward the edges, with individual fragments hanging on their own — the object does not end, it dissolves into the air.
The shards are small, with torn edges: this is not a cut stone but a splinter of ice, with internal cracks and matte patches. Perfection here would be a mistake.

By day it is a frozen waterfall — heavy, cold, stopped. In the evening the light runs down the shards from above, refracting on every facet, and the waterfall becomes a shaft of light with neither beginning nor visible source.
LC0239.whereItWorks: A narrow vertical format for stairwells, shafts between floors, piers beside tall windows, bay windows.
LC0239.style: Nordic minimalism and Alpine luxury: stone, pale timber, a cold palette, panoramic windows. The message is water stopped by frost — a composition about force held in a pause.
LC0239.madeToOrder: The column height, the diameter, the density of the shards and the calibre of the fragments are all made to order.

paragraphs: A vortex pressed to the ceiling. The tiers are offset from one another around the circle, and the mass winds into a spiral, forming a shallow funnel — movement with no height at all.

The light enters the rods at their ends and bursts out at the tip as a bright point: from below the composition reads as a swarm of luminous needles converging on a centre. A warm base above and icy tips below give a temperature difference within a single object.

By day it is a decorative rosette on the ceiling — flat, calm, almost unnoticed. In the evening the spiral switches on and a funnel appears overhead: the room gets a whirlpool where usually nothing happens at all.
LC0240.whereItWorks: A compact surface-mounted format for rooms with low ceilings, where a full chandelier is impossible: bedrooms, studies, dressing rooms, corridors, lift lobbies.
LC0240.style: Contemporary classicism and soft Art Deco: pale walls, gilded fittings, symmetry. The message is opulence in tight quarters — the composition brings ceremony where there is no height.
LC0240.madeToOrder: The disc diameter, the number of tiers, the rod lengths and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: Tiling on a tower, scales on a tail. The elements are set overlapping and offset — a construction invented independently by nature and by builders, each for their own purpose.

Two finishes give two different objects from one geometry: in warm gold the column reads as heavy, cast, almost jewel-like; in cool silver as fish-like, mobile, aquatic. The choice here determines the whole scene around it.

By day it is a sculptural column — dense, rhythmic, architectural. In the evening the light creeps from top to bottom through the gaps between the layers, and the column becomes a shaft assembled out of burning plates.
LC0241.whereItWorks: For stairwells, narrow tall openings, entrance groups, zones beside panoramic glazing, piers.
LC0241.style: Art Deco and contemporary opulence: vertical divisions, metal, symmetry. The message is armour — a composition about protection that is beautiful precisely because it is functional.
LC0241.madeToOrder: The column height, the number of scales, the finish and the overlap pitch are all made to order.

paragraphs: Knowledge escaping its binding. The image reads at once and without explanation: the volumes open, the pages separate and fly downward, and the lower you look the more of them there are.
The contrast is set hard: a heavy dark top and a weightless luminous base. The books stay opaque, the pages glow — the object gives out light only when it stops being an object.

By day it is a frozen explosion of paper — graphics, shadow, volume. In the evening the pages light up and the falling becomes luminous: a blizzard in which every snowflake is a page that has been read.
LC0242.whereItWorks: Libraries, studies, lobbies of educational institutions, book-lined staircases in private houses, stairwells, atria.
LC0242.style: Intellectual classicism and the contemporary library: dark timber, leather, tall shelving. The message is enlightenment — a composition about content mattering more than the medium.
LC0242.madeToOrder: The number of volumes, the density of the page blizzard and the height of the fall are all made to order.

paragraphs: One form at a distance, a hundred forms from two steps away. From afar it is a dense sphere; come closer and it breaks into separate elements, each at its own angle.

The light comes not from the caps but from the stems: the tubes glow along their whole length, and the composition becomes a tangle of luminous lines with discs laid over it. The caps reflect that light and invert it — hot from below, cool from above.

By day it is a sculpture read through mass and silhouette. In the evening it is a mycelium lifted out of the earth and hung from the ceiling: what grows in darkness, carried into the light and still glowing on its own.
LC0243.whereItWorks: For living rooms, stairwells, zones above a round table, restaurants, lounges.
LC0243.style: Organic modernism and eco-luxury: natural textures, a warm palette, timber. The message is hidden life — a composition about what happens beneath the surface and usually goes unseen.
LC0243.madeToOrder: The sphere diameter, the number of elements, the finish of the caps and the length of the stems are all made to order.

paragraphs: A panel that failed to hold its contents. The central gesture is that the fish do not fit inside the frame: part of the shoal has already crossed the edge and is swimming across the bare wall.

The ground works as a seabed lit through water: the colours run into one another in uneven patches, the surface rough and streaked. Above it the shoal moves diagonally, set on rods of differing height — a flat panel turns out to be three-dimensional.

By day it is a fragment of reef shot close up: texture, relief, a subdued palette. In the evening the ground recedes into darkness and only the silver of the scales remains — night water in which you see nothing but what moves.
LC0244.whereItWorks: Feature walls in halls, on stair landings, in private living rooms, restaurants, lobbies.
LC0244.style: Art Nouveau and organic modernism: natural textures, subdued tones, large planes. The message is freedom — a composition about how living things do not stay within the boundaries assigned to them.
LC0244.madeToOrder: The panel dimensions, the number of fish, the palette of the ground and the direction of the shoal are all made to order.

paragraphs: A panel that failed to hold its contents. The shoal has crossed the boundary of the circle and swims across the bare wall — the composition loses its closure deliberately, and that is its principal gesture.

Below, a mass of cones grows out of the plane like the tubes of marine worms or the mouths of volcanoes; at the centre a gold sphere around which they thicken. The shoal breaks away from that mass and leaves — movement from below upward, out of the dense into the empty.

By day it is a section of reef raised onto a wall: texture, relief, runs of colour. In the evening the glow emphasises the relief, the fish begin to throw highlights, and the shoal seems to accelerate.
LC0245.whereItWorks: Feature walls in generous rooms: a hall, a stair landing, a private living room, a lobby, a restaurant.
LC0245.style: Art Nouveau and organic modernism: natural textures, a subdued palette, large planes. The message is escape — a composition about how living things will not stay inside a frame.
LC0245.madeToOrder: The panel diameter, the number of fish and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: A moon risen over a field. The sphere is set off centre, and around it the elements grow smaller and denser — as though drawn in by the gravity of a body heavier than any of them.
The main mass is matte white and rough; gold grains are scattered through it. The light emerges from beneath the sphere and spreads across the white field, emphasising the relief with a grazing beam.

By day it is a biological specimen under magnification — a colony, spores, something growing out of a plane. In the evening it is a moon over a plain: the same relief, read as a landscape rather than as a microcosm.
LC0246.whereItWorks: Feature walls in a hall, a bedroom, a private study, a meeting room, a gallery space.
LC0246.style: Contemporary art and organic minimalism: white walls, an absence of ornament, sculptural furniture. The message is a change of scale — one and the same form reads through a microscope and through a telescope alike.
LC0246.madeToOrder: The diameter of the circle, the density of the elements and the share of gilding are all made to order.

paragraphs: A find lifted out of a dig. The figure is wrapped in bands carrying signs — pictograms, symbols, something like writing that cannot be read and makes you want to.
The plasticity rests on contrast: a heavy dense top and an almost weightless base, where the figure balances on a small stand. It stands as though it were about to rock — and does not.
By day it is an archaeological object: faded stone, pale signs on dark, a dry texture. Under directional light the signs gain contrast and begin to read as an inscription that means something.
Three viewpoints are shown: the pattern of signs differs on every side and walking around is essential.
LC0247.whereItWorks: Halls, gallery spaces, private living rooms, showrooms, libraries, studies.
LC0247.style: Ethnic and contemporary art: unworked textures, blank walls, pinpoint lighting. The message is antiquity — a piece for someone who values the question more than the answer.
LC0247.madeToOrder: The height, the colour and the set of symbols are all made to order.

paragraphs: Two elements in one vertical. Damp greenery behind a matte pane above, an open flame below — water and fire set one above the other with no intermediary.

The flame reflects in the pane of the case and lights the leaves from beneath, so the greenery looks warmed through. Conservatory and hearth do not merely coexist, they work for each other: without the fire the greenery would be nothing but a display case.
By day the object reads as a decorative case of plants — calm, green, humid. In the evening the fire becomes the protagonist and the conservatory turns into its backdrop: the tropics, lit from below.
LC0248.whereItWorks: Living rooms, lounges, restaurants, winter gardens, spas, hotel lobbies.
LC0248.style: Eco-luxury and tropical modernism: living plants, natural stone, dark timber. The message is joining the unjoinable — a composition about opposites holding each other up.
LC0248.madeToOrder: The dimensions, the contents of the case and the burner type are all made to order.

paragraphs: A hearth in the middle of a cliff. The upper part hangs above the fire — an opaque mass suspended so that a gap remains between it and the hearth, through which the flame is visible from every side.

The texture is weathered: vertical cracks, chips, patches of moss. The object looks like a fragment of a cliff face lifted out of a landscape and set down in a room together with the fire that burned at its foot.
