By day it is a sculptural column — heavy, stony, silent. In the evening the hearth is lit and the composition becomes what it was conceived as: a campfire beneath an overhanging rock, the oldest interior there is.
LC0249.whereItWorks: Living rooms with high ceilings, lobbies, spas, terraces, winter gardens, restaurant floors.
LC0249.style: Brutalist luxury and organic modernism: unworked stone, timber, large volumes. The message is the primal — fire and rock, the things people gathered around before there were houses.
LC0249.madeToOrder: The dimensions, the character of the rock and the fuel type are all made to order.

paragraphs: A form that refuses to be named. A shell, a sail, a petal, a wave — the object reads as all of these and as none in particular, and that ambiguity is deliberate.
The polish is taken to a mirror, so the sculpture changes with the sky: silver in the morning, gold at sunset, almost gone at night. It has no permanent appearance — the weather supplies it.
A mirrored sphere in the lower bowl gathers everything around it into a single globe: the park, the sky, the viewer. By day the object reflects the world; in the evening it dissolves into it.
LC0250.whereItWorks: Parks, the grounds of private residences, entrance groups, embankments, forecourts of hotels and offices.
LC0250.style: Contemporary sculpture and landscape minimalism: gravel, clipped greenery, the clean geometry of a setting. The message is a dialogue with the sky — a piece that works not on its own but together with the light of the day.
LC0250.madeToOrder: The height, the surface finish and the material of the plinth are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same device taken to drama. Here the light does not diffuse but strikes in patches, and the leaves read as shadows against it — charcoal silhouettes on a blazing ground.
This is a tropical evening at a precise moment: the sun already behind the foliage but not yet down. A state that lasts ten minutes in nature stays switched on here for as long as you want it.
By day the panel looks restrained, almost graphic — a dark rectangle with a drawing on it. In the evening it becomes the principal source of mood: the room takes its temperature from a single wall.
LC0251.whereItWorks: For lounges, bars, private studies, bedrooms in a dark palette, restaurants, smoking rooms.
LC0251.style: Dark modernism and colonial luxury: timber, leather, deep tones, subdued light. The message is a tropical evening — a composition about heat on its way out.
LC0251.madeToOrder: The panel dimensions, the density of the foliage and the colour of the backlight are all made to order.

paragraphs: A window where there is no window. The panel solves a problem a picture cannot: it gives not an image but a condition — the view into a conservatory early in the morning.
The effect rests on blur: the near leaves read sharply, the far ones dissolve into a luminous haze. The matte face removes definition, and the greenery stops being an object and becomes atmosphere.
By day the panel works as a decorative inset in the wall — calm, almost unnoticed. In the evening the backlight brings it forward, and a windowless room acquires a window into a winter garden.
LC0252.whereItWorks: For interiors without windows: corridors, dressing rooms, washrooms, meeting rooms, lift lobbies, basement areas.
LC0252.style: Eco-modernism and biophilic design: natural textures, greenery, a pale palette. The message is air — the composition expands a room without touching its walls.
LC0252.madeToOrder: The dimensions of the case, the planting and the colour temperature of the backlight are all made to order.

paragraphs: Presence without a face. The figure is reduced to silhouette, pose and drapery — there are no hands and no features, and because of that the object stops being a portrait and becomes a sign.

The drapery is rigid yet looks fluid: you can see the tension at the hip, the sag at the feet, the turn of the shoulder. The gold ornament along the hem is applied with blackening and reads in relief — the one detail permitted to speak.
By day it is a sculpture of pure plasticity — dark, quiet, demanding to be walked around. Under directional light the folds gain depth and the figure seems to take a step.
Three viewpoints are shown: the object is made for viewing in the round and has no reverse.
LC0253.whereItWorks: A boutique hall, a private living room, a showroom, a gallery space, a hotel lobby, a reception room.
LC0253.style: Eastern luxury and contemporary art: deep colours, minimal furniture, large planes. The message is mystery — a piece for an interior that does not explain itself at once.
LC0253.madeToOrder: The height, the colour of the drapery and the ornament pattern are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same water lily, turned invisible. The discs are so transparent that they read only through relief and highlights along their rims — the form exists, the surface does not.

Matte white spheres are scattered between them — pearls, or roe caught in the foliage. The light passes through several layers in a row, refracting and diffusing: the source is lost and a radiance without an address remains.

By day it is a cloud of clear leaves with pearl inclusions, barely distinguishable against a pale ground. In the evening it is a luminous pool whose bottom cannot be made out: the light comes from everywhere and from nowhere.
LC0254.whereItWorks: For formal spaces with high ceilings: atria, lobbies, double-height living rooms, banquet and wedding halls.
LC0254.style: Contemporary classicism and romantic minimalism: pale walls, plenty of air, light fabrics. The message is transparency — the composition is vast in volume and weightless in presence.
LC0254.madeToOrder: The number of discs, the share of pearls and the depth of the layers are all made to order.

paragraphs: A horn with light pouring out of it. The form is taken from a wind instrument: a bell rolled from a sheet, its rim crumpled differently on every element.

The contrast decides everything: a cold blue back and a hot gold interior with a hammered texture. The light goes downward as a warm patch while the top stays blue and opaque — the object shows two temperatures at once.
By day it is a group of metal flowers — blue, dense, sculptural. In the evening it is a rank of horns pouring gold: sound you cannot hear but can see.
LC0255.whereItWorks: For long tables, bar counters, generous halls, restaurants, lobbies, meeting rooms.
LC0255.style: Industrial luxury and contemporary modernism: dark walls, metal, large planes. The message is force and warmth — cold armour with fire hidden behind it.
LC0255.madeToOrder: The number of bells, the tone of the blue and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: Pleating that works as venation. The relief radiates from the centre, and when light passes through the thin wall the folds emerge like the veins of a real leaf.

The edges are all uneven and slightly rolled: the composition looks grown rather than stamped out. The discs hang in layers, overlapping — the way water lilies lie when there is not quite enough room on the water.
By day it is a field of white leaves, calm and almost graphic. In the evening it is a pool lit from beneath the water: the light comes from below, from where a real pond has nothing but silt.
LC0256.whereItWorks: For large horizontal spaces: lobbies, panoramic living rooms, dining rooms, spas, meeting rooms.
LC0256.style: Eco-modernism and Japanese minimalism: pale timber, paper, water, emptiness as a material. The message is stillness — a composition about water without movement and about time that has stopped.
LC0256.madeToOrder: The number of discs, their calibres and the area of the composition are all made to order.

paragraphs: Black outside, sun within. The whole object is built on a single device: the sphere stays dark and matte on the outside while the light lives deep inside and emerges only through the bells.
The petals are rolled into funnels and form a tangle with deep pockets. The light reflects off the gold inner surfaces and bursts out in narrow warm beams — it does not diffuse, it strikes.
By day it is a sculpture in crumpled metal — dense, opaque, absorbing. In the evening it is a spent coal that still holds its heat: blackness outside, a blast furnace within.
LC0257.whereItWorks: A compact format for bedrooms, studies, zones above a round table, private living rooms, bars.
LC0257.style: Brutalist luxury and dark modernism: graphite walls, leather, timber, subdued light. The message is hidden force — the composition shows nothing on the outside and holds everything within.
LC0257.madeToOrder: The sphere diameter, the number of petals and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A mosaic that does not hang down. The composition spreads beneath the ceiling as a flat layer — it does not occupy volume, it marks out a plane.

The pearlescence shifts from blue-violet into green, like a beetle's wing or a mussel shell: the colour is not fixed and changes with the angle of view. The light hides behind the elements and emerges at their edges, tracing every drop with a contour.

By day it is a scatter of pearls on dark velvet — dense, quiet, almost jewel-like. In the evening the contours light up and the mosaic becomes a star chart in which every pearl is ringed by its own orbit.
LC0258.whereItWorks: For ceilings of medium height where compactness matters: bedrooms, studies, lift lobbies, dressing rooms, corridors.
LC0258.style: Soft Art Deco and contemporary classicism: pearlescence, mirrors, subdued tones. The message is preciousness in small compass — the composition needs no height and works where a chandelier is impossible.
LC0258.madeToOrder: The overall diameter, the number of drops and the tone of the pearlescence are all made to order.

paragraphs: Metal caught in the act of flowing. The form has run and crumpled — it looks not made but happened, as though it had been stopped a second before it flowed further.

Some drops are opaque and mirrored, others glow from within. Because of that the cluster burns in every other element: the light here is selective rather than general, and the composition reads as a branch on which half the berries have ripened.
By day it is a gathering of mercury bubbles with a cool blue-steel shift. In the evening gold kindles inside them — a warm patch amid cold metal, like fire seen through ice.
LC0259.whereItWorks: A horizontal format for long tables, generous living rooms, lobbies, restaurants, private studies.
LC0259.style: High-tech and contemporary opulence: polished surfaces, transparency, a dark palette. The message is a controlled element — a composition about a material that was once liquid and remembers it.
LC0259.madeToOrder: The number of drops, the ratio of mirrored to luminous and the span of the branches are all made to order.

paragraphs: A score for three voices. The clear rings carry light along the arc and flare at the breaks, the gilded ones reflect and work as accents, the matte ones glow evenly — three behaviours of one beam in one composition.
The rings are open and hang in a vertical stream, catching at each other by eye but never touching. A gap always remains between them: the piece is about connection that requires no contact.
By day it is a scattering of bracelets laid out through the air. In the evening it becomes a stream of glowing arcs twisted into a spiral, where every arc burns in its own way.
LC0260.whereItWorks: A vertical format for stairwells, double-height spaces, bay windows, tall entrance halls.
LC0260.style: Contemporary luxury and soft Art Nouveau: rounded forms, brass, pale walls. The message is consonance — three different characters gathered into one piece without argument.
LC0260.madeToOrder: The number of rings, the ratio between the executions and the height of the stream are all made to order.

paragraphs: Chainmail woven out of light. Links are joined into chains, chains into a fabric, and the lattice comes out alive because every link is slightly irregular.
Three executions change the character entirely: clear — light, almost invisible; milky — soft and diffusing; white-and-gold — formal, with a metallic shine. One structure, three different rooms.

By day the screen reads as chainmail — dense in its drawing, transparent in fact. In the evening, lit from the side, the links act as lenses and scatter hundreds of oval highlights across the wall: the lattice stops being a border and becomes a projector.
LC0261.whereItWorks: Zoning and decorative screens: entrance halls, restaurants, showrooms, private areas, hotel lobbies, window displays.
LC0261.style: Contemporary classic with a softened Art Deco accent: mirrors, brass, velvet, subdued light. The message is shelter without isolation — a border you can see straight through.
LC0261.madeToOrder: The dimensions of the panel, the execution of the links and the density of the weave are all made to order.

paragraphs: Pebbles from a river shallow, lifted into the air. The form is worn down to complete simplicity: not one corner, not one detail, only a smooth volume.

The light floods the stone entirely and a bright rim appears along its edge. Varying the drop height turns the field into a relief: waves, shallows, depths — a map of the riverbed carried up to the ceiling.

By day it is a scattering of amber set in mid-air, warm and heavy to the eye. In the evening every element burns with a fire of its own, and the field becomes a shallow in which the sun got tangled and cannot get out.
LC0262.whereItWorks: Large horizontal spaces: lobbies, long tables, panoramic living rooms, restaurants, winter gardens.
LC0262.style: Eco-modern and warm minimalism: wood, linen, natural stone, a soft palette. The message is simplicity — the composition makes do with a single form and proves that it is enough.
LC0262.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the area of the field and the depth of tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A form wrapped around emptiness. The loops are coiled around nothing — what holds the object together is inside it and does not exist.

The cocoons hang in a dense sphere, and through the near ones you see the far ones: repeated refraction creates a depth in which the gaze gets lost without finding a bottom. The light is hidden inside individual elements and reflected in all the rest.

By day it is a cluster of bubbles or spawn — clear, almost indiscernible against a pale background. In the evening it becomes a glowing tangle whose source cannot be located: the whole sphere burns at once.
LC0263.whereItWorks: Central positions: above a round table, in a rotunda, in a double-height living room, in an entrance hall, in a reception room.
LC0263.style: Contemporary minimalism and optical design: white walls, clean forms, no ornament. The message is birth — the composition is about what happens inside, before it becomes visible.
LC0263.madeToOrder: The diameter of the sphere, the number of cocoons and the density of the assembly are all made to order.

paragraphs: A shoal held still in the current. Every wing is curved in its own way: some folded almost in half, others barely bent — phases of a single movement laid out through the air.

The light spreads along the concave surface from inside: from below you see a glowing underside, from above the plate stays dark. The composition shows itself only to whoever stands beneath it — from above it barely exists.

By day it is a shoal mid-turn — smoky pink, iridescent, with inner currents running through the mass. In the evening it becomes a cloud of glowing wings at different heights with darkness falling away between them.
LC0264.whereItWorks: Generous halls with high ceilings: lobbies, double-height living rooms, restaurants, spas, pools.
LC0264.style: Soft Art Nouveau and resort luxury: a pastel palette, pale fabrics, natural stone. The message is fluidity — the composition is about slow movement through a dense medium.
LC0264.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the spread of the shoal and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: An object with no appearance of its own. The mirrored drops reflect the surroundings and each other — the composition consists entirely of what is around it.
The light is hidden underneath and aimed downward: a narrow beam escapes while the surface stays mirrored. The piece both shines and disappears — it works without showing itself.

By day it is a gathering of mercury beneath the ceiling, in which the room is reflected taken apart into fragments. In the evening dark mirrors remain above and points of light burn below: the object vanishes, the light stays.
LC0265.whereItWorks: Contemporary interiors with clean architecture: concrete, glazing, minimalism. Lofts, offices, galleries, showrooms, meeting rooms.
LC0265.style: High-tech and radical minimalism: no ornament, large planes, monochrome. The message is self-effacement — the composition gives up an appearance of its own in favour of the space.
LC0265.madeToOrder: The number of drops, their calibres and the density of the group are all made to order.

paragraphs: A thicket translated into the vertical. Stalks with swollen joints reproduce bamboo down to the rings at the nodes — a replica taken to botanical accuracy.
Gaps remain between the stalks: the screen lets through both light and sight, yet it still divides. It does not cut the space off; it turns the passage between zones into a walk through a grove.

By day it is a thicket set in the transparent — a graphic of verticals with a honeyed cast. In the evening light from below makes the stalks glow along their full height, and the grove becomes a wall of light with a rhythm.
LC0266.whereItWorks: Zoning: between a living room and a dining room, in a spa, in a restaurant, in a private area, beside a staircase, in a hotel lobby.
LC0266.style: Eastern minimalism and eco-modern: natural textures, wood, stone, a muted palette. The message is a natural border — dividing space with something that grows rather than something that is built.
LC0266.madeToOrder: The dimensions of the panel, the number of stalks and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A field suspended in weightlessness. There is a great deal of air between the elements — the composition does not press down with mass, it is distributed through the volume so that the gaze passes right through.

The light is hidden in only some of the flowers; the rest pick it up and pass it on. There are therefore many times fewer glowing points than elements, and the composition shimmers unevenly, like a real field at dusk.

By day the object is almost transparent and reads only through highlights — it is easy to miss. In the evening the key flowers light up and the clear ones flare with borrowed light: the result is a starfield with warm thickenings.
LC0267.whereItWorks: Very large spaces: atriums, lobbies, panoramic double-height halls, banqueting venues.
LC0267.style: Romantic classicism and light Art Nouveau: pale walls, plenty of air, a minimum of heavy furniture. The message is weightlessness — the composition occupies an enormous volume without creating any weight.
LC0267.madeToOrder: The number of flowers, the area of the field and the proportion of lit elements are all made to order.

paragraphs: A fabric that does not bend. The petals are laid in dense overlapping rows and the surface reads as embroidered cloth, though it will not give by a millimetre.

At the centre the pattern parts — dark rounded fragments emerge through the gold, like pebbles laid bare on the bed of a stream. It is the only event on the whole plane, and it keeps the composition from monotony.

By day the panel looks like a relief of gold cloth — calm, almost a background. Under directed light the relief comes alive: shadows begin to travel across it, and the motionless surface starts to move.
LC0268.whereItWorks: An accent wall: an entrance hall, behind a bedhead, in a meeting room, in a showroom, in a private study.
LC0268.style: Contemporary luxury and Eastern opulence: deep colours, velvet, an abundance of metal. The message is the tactile — the panel asks to be touched, and that is its main action.
LC0268.madeToOrder: The dimensions of the panel, the density of the petals and the pattern of the openings are all made to order.

paragraphs: A sun that has a reflection. A crown of petals radiates from the centre, and in the middle there is a mirror: the object is a luminary and a window at once.

Each petal reads as a volume thanks to the darkened recesses, and the whole crown shimmers at the slightest movement of the viewer. The backlight is hidden behind the frame and escapes along the contour, drawing a halo on the wall.

By day it is a classic sunburst mirror in a formal frame — a piece you notice first and look into second. In the evening the halo turns it into a glowing disc and the reflection recedes: the mirror stops being a mirror.
LC0269.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, dressing rooms, accent walls in a living room, boudoirs, reception rooms.
LC0269.style: Art Deco and neo-baroque: gilding, symmetry, mouldings, deep tones. The message is ceremony — the object greets whoever comes in and sets the tone for the whole house.
LC0269.madeToOrder: The diameter, the number of rows of petals and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: An armful of branches thrown into the air and caught before it reached the floor. The angles are accidental, the crossings uncalculated — the whole piece is about disorder being more precise than composition.
Inside each tube a thread of light runs, and the bubbles in the mass flare along its full length. The stick turns into a glowing rod; the joints hold the structure together and double as accents.

By day it is strict graphic work: intersecting straight lines, nothing surplus, almost a draft drawing. In the evening the lines catch fire and begin to live on their own — the structure disappears and what remains is a sketch of light hanging in the air.
LC0270.whereItWorks: Contemporary interiors: lofts, offices, minimalist living rooms, co-working spaces, showrooms.
LC0270.style: Industrial minimalism and constructivism: concrete, exposed services, monochrome. The message is freedom of gesture — the composition looks accidental and is alive for exactly that reason.
LC0270.madeToOrder: The number of tubes, their lengths and the density of the crossings are all made to order.

paragraphs: A backwater under the moon. The glow is silvery and cold — the same form in warm light would read as decorative; here it stays graphic.

The plates lie flat, slightly tilted, like leaves on the surface of still water. The composition is flat in silhouette and deep in layers: the elements hang at different levels and the eye passes straight through them.
By day it is a scattering of shells laid out beneath the ceiling. In the evening it becomes a backwater lit by a cold moon, where both the surface and what lies under it are visible.
LC0271.whereItWorks: Large flat ceilings: lobbies, conference halls, spa areas, pools, meeting rooms.
LC0271.style: Minimalism and Nordic modern: a cold palette, stone, smooth surfaces, subdued light. The message is stillness — the composition does not warm the room, it calms it.
LC0271.madeToOrder: The number of plates, their calibres and the area covered are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same pattern, but with the structure left open. The bar is not hidden — it cuts the circle in half and becomes part of the drawing rather than a service detail.
The discs overlap, and the light passes through several layers in a row. The relief is laid over itself and a moiré appears — a moving pattern that exists in no single element.
By day it is a bundle of flowers on gold stems, dense and sculptural. In the evening it becomes a cascade of glowing rosettes with every facet alight and a ripple running between the layers.
LC0272.whereItWorks: Stairwells and double-height spaces where the cascade is seen from two levels at once, and halls with a mezzanine.
LC0272.style: Art Deco and grand classicism: gilding, mouldings, large scale. The message is generosity of form — the composition economises on neither mass nor shine.
LC0272.madeToOrder: The number of discs, the depth of the cascade and the finish of the bars are all made to order.

paragraphs: A frost pattern seen against the light. The disc glows not by its surface but by its drawing: the light enters at the centre and runs out along the relief, igniting every facet separately.

The discs hang at different angles: some face the viewer and burn whole, others are seen edge-on and all but vanish. The composition shows itself and hides by turns, depending on which door you came through.
By day it is a collection of rosettes read through relief and shadow. In the evening it becomes a constellation of glowing circles where half the stars face you and half look away.
LC0273.whereItWorks: Generous horizontal spaces: lobbies, dining rooms, meeting rooms, reception rooms, galleries.
LC0273.style: Contemporary classic with a softened Art Deco accent: pale walls, mirrors, symmetry. The message is winter clarity — the composition brings the cold graphic of a frosted window indoors.
LC0273.madeToOrder: The number of discs, their calibres and the density of the composition are all made to order.

paragraphs: A nugget given a transparent shell. The gold lives inside the mass — it creases, catches the light and glows through from within, while staying out of reach.

No two elements are alike: each has its own twist and its own inner pattern of foil. The composition alternates fully gilded pieces with half-clear ones, and because of that the mass reads as a volume with deep hollows between the layers.

By day it is a collection of nuggets lifted into the air and laid out on invisible shelves. In the evening the light ignites the foil from inside and the group begins to shimmer red-gold — gold that burns rather than glints.
LC0274.whereItWorks: Stairwells, bay windows, living rooms with high ceilings, private studies, wine rooms.
LC0274.style: Art Deco and contemporary luxury: deep tones, dark wood, gilded detail. The message is treasure — a piece about value hidden inside and visible only against the light.
LC0274.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the proportion of gilding and the height of the group are all made to order.

paragraphs: An ingot cast into a transparent shell. The gilding is applied from the inside, so the element stays clear on the outside and burns with metal within — the form shows its contents without opening.
The clear elements between the gilded ones work as air: without them the composition would become a solid mass, with them it breathes. The proportion matters more here than the count.

By day it is a collection of precious drops laid out through the air. In the evening it becomes a stream of molten gold arrested at the moment of pouring: a movement that never happened and is nonetheless visible.
LC0275.whereItWorks: A horizontal format for long tables, generous halls, lobbies, banqueting rooms, restaurants.
LC0275.style: Art Deco and contemporary luxury: gilding, deep tones, symmetry, large scale. The message is value — the composition speaks of wealth through substance rather than ornament.
LC0275.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the share of gilded ones and the spread of the group are all made to order.

paragraphs: Resin with something caught in it for good. Gold foil lives in the mass, and when the light comes on it passes through, scattering warm sparks inside the body of the piece.
The white elements provide pauses and keep the composition from overheating on colour. Without them the honey tone would turn cloying — with them it reads as amber rather than syrup.
By day it is a cluster of honeycomb or drops of resin — dense, heavy to the eye, warm in colour. In the evening it becomes a swarm of glowing cocoons with something happening inside each one.
LC0276.whereItWorks: Stairwells, dining rooms, living rooms in a warm palette, restaurants, wine rooms.
LC0276.style: Eco-luxury and warm Art Nouveau: wood, leather, natural fabrics, subdued light. The message is time preserved — the composition is about warmth being something you can put up in a jar.
LC0276.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the balance of honey to white and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: Ice with whatever was in it frozen in place. Bubbles and swirls remain in the mass, so under light the piece looks like a genuine block rather than a coloured shape.
The white elements damp down the intensity of the colour and keep the composition from becoming decorative — they work as pauses, without which the aquamarine would sound insistent.
By day the object recalls a cluster of stalactites — dense, cold, mineral. In the evening it becomes a cave of ice flows lit from somewhere deep inside, where there should be no light at all.
LC0277.whereItWorks: A vertical format: staircases, narrow double-height spaces, spa areas, pools, bathrooms.
LC0277.style: Nordic Art Nouveau and spa aesthetics: stone, water, subdued light, a cold palette. The message is coolness and depth — the composition lowers the temperature of a space and slows it down.
LC0277.madeToOrder: The number of spindles, the depth of tone and the height of the group are all made to order.

paragraphs: Icicles under an eave. The lower edge is ragged and the elements differ in length — the composition is deliberately not levelled, because levelled icicles do not exist.

Every spiral is its own: tight in one place, barely started in another. The light enters from above through the tip and fills the form entirely — the matte pieces glow evenly, the clear ones throw sharp highlights off the facets of the twist.
By day it is a collection of ice figures laid out through the air. In the evening it becomes a frozen waterfall lit from within: water that has stopped and goes on glowing.
LC0278.whereItWorks: Stairwells, bay windows, double-height spaces, winter gardens, spa areas.
LC0278.style: Nordic minimalism and alpine luxury: pale wood, stone, large windows, a cold palette. The message is winter as a state — the composition brings the clarity of a frosty day rather than festive decor.
LC0278.madeToOrder: The number of elements, their lengths and the balance of clear to matte are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same ribbon in mirror — and the opposite character because of it. Where the matte version is soft and diffused, this one is sharp, flaring, cold.
The ribbing works as an optical grating: reflections break into hundreds of vertical strokes and the surface never shows a whole picture. The room is reflected in it taken apart into stripes.

By day it is a sculpture of mercury — heavy, fluid, gathering the interior into itself. In the evening the backlight surfaces through the slots and glowing stripes run along its whole length, as though the metal had cracked from inside.
The composition holds an international award.
LC0279.whereItWorks: Interiors with strong architecture: concrete, glazing, stone, double height. Lobbies, atriums, galleries, offices, showrooms.
LC0279.style: High-tech and industrial luxury: large planes, exposed structure, monochrome. The message is precision of substance — a piece about metal being capable of flow.
LC0279.madeToOrder: The length, the depth of the bends and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A sheet of paper caught in flight. The pleating reads as folds in cloth, and the form as something a draught picked up and would not let fall.

The light escapes only through the slots between the ribs, so the ribbon glows in fine longitudinal lines while staying dense and sculptural. This is not a glowing object but an object with light inside it — the difference is fundamental.
By day it is a giant sheet of pleated paper frozen halfway through its fall. In the evening it becomes a glowing wave with close hatching, as though a comb had been drawn along it.
The model holds an international award.
LC0280.whereItWorks: A horizontal format for generous halls: dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms, galleries, showrooms.
LC0280.style: Minimalism and Japanese aesthetics: paper, wood, emptiness, no ornament. The message is simplicity of gesture — one form, one movement, nothing beyond.
LC0280.madeToOrder: The length of the ribbon, the character of the bends and the density of the ribbing are all made to order.

paragraphs: A ring that outlines a space rather than filling it. The inner part is empty — and that emptiness works on equal terms with the material.

The petals are laid overlapping in several layers, like roof tiles, each turned with its gold reverse facing inward. The light collects in the cavity and comes out reflected, without a single direct beam: the source is invisible from anywhere.
By day it is a wreath — dense, white, with gold glimmers deep inside. In the evening it becomes a glowing hoop suspended in the air, in which not the surface burns but the interior.
LC0281.whereItWorks: A ring format for round tables, rotundas, the central zone of a living room, private dining rooms, wedding venues.
LC0281.style: Contemporary classic and neo-baroque: symmetry, mouldings, gilding, formal proportions. The message is ceremony — the composition draws a circle inside which the main thing happens.
LC0281.madeToOrder: The diameter of the ring, the number of petals and the depth of the layering are all made to order.

paragraphs: A fold with gold hidden inside it. From the outside the form is restrained and white; inside there is a gilded cavity with the source: the piece shows its interior only to those who approach from the right side.
The composition runs as a diagonal stream, from a dense core to sparse edges. The elements overlap and depth accumulates in layers — as in a wave, where you see both the crest and what is beneath it.

By day it is a sculpture of rich plasticity, read through relief and shadow. In the evening it becomes a scattering of warm glowing pockets with darkness between them: the light here does not flood, it peers out.
LC0282.whereItWorks: Long spaces: above a table, along a bar counter, in a gallery hall, in a restaurant, in a reception room.
LC0282.style: Contemporary classic and a softened baroque: pale walls, gilded detail, rounded furniture. The message is restrained luxury — the composition does not put its gold in the window, it hides it.
LC0282.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the depth of the stream and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: Foam that was not allowed to burst. Every element differs in size and is slightly irregular in form — like a real bubble, which has no two identical siblings.

The coating produces interference: the colour is not fixed, it shifts with the viewing angle, flowing from blue to green and pink. The composition has no permanent palette — it depends on where you are standing.

By day it is a cluster of soap foam suspended in the air, light and almost invisible. In the evening the shells glow across their whole surface, and the foam becomes a cloud of small moons with iridescent shifts.
LC0283.whereItWorks: Interiors with a playful character: children's rooms, spas, pools, lounges, bathrooms, window displays.
LC0283.style: Soft futurism and optical design: smooth surfaces, a pale palette, no sharp corners. The message is lightness and play — the composition takes the seriousness out of a space without making it childish.
LC0283.madeToOrder: The number of bubbles, their calibres and the palette of the coating are all made to order.

paragraphs: A whirlwind coiled around a spiral staircase. The composition does not hang in the shaft, it passes through it — from the top floor to the bottom, accompanying whoever is coming down.

The light enters the end of each rod and runs downward: the result is rain falling along a spiral — a movement that does not occur in nature. Because of the helical geometry the piece reads differently from every floor: a funnel from below, a cascade from the side, an open rose from above.

By day it is an architectural structure — precise, engineered, with a legible frame. In the evening the frame disappears and what remains is a whirlwind of light with neither axis nor fixings in sight.
LC0284.whereItWorks: Tall verticals only: stairwells, atriums, panoramic halls of several levels, double-height lobbies.
LC0284.style: Contemporary luxury and high-tech: open staircases, glazing, metal, large scale. The message is the vertical — the composition turns moving between floors into the main event of the house.
LC0284.madeToOrder: The height of the spiral, the number of turns and the density of the fringe are all made to order.

paragraphs: Two different lights in one field. Some elements glow evenly and softly, others brightly and in points, with a highlight deep inside; the composition is built on that difference rather than on form.
Varying the drop height turns a flat field into a relief: waves, crests, hollows. The eye travels it as it would travel terrain, finding now a dense stretch, now a gap.

By day it is a garden of white flowers with amber inclusions — calm, almost monochrome. In the evening the matte pieces fade to a warm glow and the clear ones flare: the garden becomes a field of fireflies that have settled on the blooms.
LC0285.whereItWorks: Long tables, lobbies, generous dining rooms, meeting rooms, restaurant halls.
LC0285.style: Contemporary classic with a botanical note: warm wood, brass, pale textiles. The message is hospitality — the composition reads as a table laid before anyone has laid it.
LC0285.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the ratio of matte to clear and the area of the field are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same flock, but gathered before take-off. If the sparse version is about flight, this one is about mass: a cloud in which the individual bird no longer matters.

The light is distributed through the whole volume, and warm hollows open up in the depth where the gaze travels in layers. Gilded figures among the white ones work by reflection and set a rhythm, keeping the mass from going uniform.

By day it is a sculptural group with gold inclusions — dense, legible, almost monolithic. In the evening it becomes a glowing cloud in which the figures can be guessed at but not made out: the flock turns into light.
LC0286.whereItWorks: Formal spaces with high ceilings: hotel lobbies, banqueting halls, double-height living rooms, atriums.
LC0286.style: Contemporary classic and grand luxury: mouldings, pale stone, gilded detail. The message is abundance — the composition speaks of generosity outright, without resorting to hints.
LC0286.madeToOrder: The number of birds, the density of the flock and the ratio of white to gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A form taken all the way to a sign. A body, two wings, not one detail — recognition rests on silhouette and tilt, and that turns out to be enough.

The gold is applied in points, only to the wingtips and the beaks: an accent within the drawing, not a finish. The light is hidden under each bird and lifts the wings from below, which leaves the edges half-transparent.

By day the flock reads as a sculptural group — white on white, pure plasticity. In the evening the birds glow from within and a wave of light travels the whole arc from end to end, the way movement travels through a real flock.
LC0287.whereItWorks: Large horizontal spaces: lobbies, conference halls, panoramic living rooms, banqueting halls, wedding venues.
LC0287.style: Contemporary classic and minimalism: pale walls, simple forms, a minimum of colour. The message is clarity and peace — the composition reads as a symbol without turning into an allegory.
LC0287.madeToOrder: The number of birds, the span of the arc and the proportion of gilding are all made to order.

paragraphs: A bird simplified to two strokes. A forked tail, sharp wings — a silhouette in a dive with everything removed except recognisability.

The flock travels in echelons: some higher, some lower, a few broken away and heading off to the side. Point sources light the elements from the flank and inner currents surface in the mass — swirls invisible under direct light.

By day the composition reads graphically: dark silhouettes on a pale ceiling, almost a draft drawing. In the evening the green deepens to emerald and the flock is no longer flying through air but through water — the medium changes together with the light.
LC0288.whereItWorks: A horizontal format for generous halls, double-height living rooms, lobbies, restaurants, winter gardens.
LC0288.style: Eco-modern and natural minimalism: natural textures, muted green in the finishes, plenty of air. The message is freedom of movement — the composition is about those who fly, not those who watch.
LC0288.madeToOrder: The number of birds, the echeloning of the flock and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A contour drawing carried out into the air. The metal traces the form the way a setting traces a stone, and the middle stays empty — the piece consists of a line and of what that line encloses.

The elements stand close together and slightly rotated relative to one another. A moiré arises from that: move along the composition and the contours overlap and part again, and the field begins to waver while staying perfectly still.

By day it is graphic work — fine gold lines hanging against a transparent ground. In the evening the light sets every contour alight along its edge, and the drawing turns into a bonfire in which only the outlines burn and there is no fire inside.
LC0289.whereItWorks: Long spaces: above a table for ten or more, in a lobby, in a gallery, in a meeting room, in a banqueting hall.
LC0289.style: Contemporary minimalism and graphic Art Nouveau: white walls, clean lines, no small-scale decor. The message is understatement — the composition shows the boundary of the object and leaves the contents to the imagination.
LC0289.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the spread of the field and the finish of the contours are all made to order.

paragraphs: Spring taken as a colour. The lime green is cold and young — the shade that stays on foliage no more than a fortnight a year.

The half-transparency with its milky clouding spreads the light evenly along the full length of each element, with no bright patches. Every "leaf" glows entire — like a real one against the light, with the sun behind it rather than in front.
By day it is a stand of sedge lifted to the ceiling. In the evening it becomes a flock of glowing wings held in flight: the form is the same and the image turns into its opposite.
LC0290.whereItWorks: A horizontal format for long tables, lobbies, wide-plan halls, winter gardens, spas.
LC0290.style: Eco-modern and Scandinavian freshness: pale wood, linen, live plants, plenty of air. The message is renewal — the composition brings in the beginning of the season rather than its height.
LC0290.madeToOrder: The spread of the flock, the number of elements and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A spiral as a way of leading the eye. The elements turn around a shared axis and the gaze travels them from top to bottom as it would travel steps — the composition sets its own viewing route.

Every wing is lit along its curve, so the light also moves along a spiral. The piece is built so that standing in front of it is awkward: it wants to be walked around, or passed on the way down a staircase.
By day it is a stream of gold petals frozen mid-turn. In the evening it becomes a vortex with every coil alight and the centre left dark, like the throat of a funnel.
LC0291.whereItWorks: A vertical format that requires height: stair shafts, atriums, double-height spaces, galleries with a mezzanine.
LC0291.style: Art Deco and contemporary luxury: gilding, deep tones, grand staircases, large scale. The message is ascent — the composition turns climbing between floors into a passage through light.
LC0291.madeToOrder: The height of the spiral, the number of elements and the intensity of the gilding are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition made entirely of reflections. It has no colour of its own and almost no surface — only a mirror in which the interior, the light and the cluster itself converge.

Switched on, the object loses its form: the spheres turn into a gathering of bright patches and it becomes impossible to make out where one berry ends and the next begins. The piece disappears inside its own glow.
By day it is a jeweller's sculpture — precise, cold, every stem legible. In the evening it becomes a cluster of molten metal with neither boundaries nor detail.
The composition holds an international award.
LC0292.whereItWorks: A vertical format for stairwells, tall entrance halls, bay windows, double-height living rooms, showrooms.
LC0292.style: High-tech and glamour at once: polished surfaces, glazing, no textiles. The message is shine without apology — the composition was made to impress and does it head-on.
LC0292.madeToOrder: The height of the cluster, the number of spheres and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: An object with two faces. Outside, white modesty with not a single highlight; inside, solid gold. Walk around it and the piece changes completely, from matte restraint to baroque opulence.

Each cup is tilted so as to reveal its interior only from one particular position. The composition decides for itself to whom and when it will open — and that is built into the geometry, not left to chance.
By day it is a collection of white cups, calm and almost monastic. In the evening the gold flares from within, and the cascade becomes a cloud of warm light in which the white can no longer be seen.
LC0293.whereItWorks: A vertical format for staircases, bay windows, double-height living rooms, tall entrance halls, private dining rooms.
LC0293.style: Contemporary classic and neo-baroque: pale walls, mouldings, gilded detail. The message is restraint with opulence behind it — the piece makes no announcement but rewards whoever comes closer.
LC0293.madeToOrder: The number of cups, the depth of the cascade and the gilding finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A flock flying out of light into shadow. Half the feathers glow right through, half work as silhouette — and the transition between them sets the direction of travel.
Because of that the composition appears layered, although every element hangs in one plane. The depth here is optical rather than spatial — a deception that holds from any position.

By day it is a flock caught mid-turn: dark and pale figures intermixed. In the evening the clear feathers light up and the dark ones vanish altogether — the flock thins before your eyes, as though half of it had already gone.
LC0294.whereItWorks: A horizontal format for long spaces: dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms, galleries, restaurant halls.
LC0294.style: Contemporary classic and graphic Art Nouveau: contrasting combinations, dark wood, brass. The message is movement and departure — the composition is about a flock always being half elsewhere already.
LC0294.madeToOrder: The number of feathers, the balance of lit to dark and the spread are all made to order.

paragraphs: A form that is barely there. The elements are so clear that what you see is not them but the pattern of scoring, hanging in the air.

The scoring works as a diffraction grating: light breaks on the ridges into rainbow highlights, and the feather begins to shift colour without a single drop of pigment in it. The rainbow here is not applied — it is computed.

By day the composition reads as a collection of transparent feathers laid out through the air. In the evening point sources ignite the scoring and the group shimmers the way a slick of oil shimmers on water.
LC0295.whereItWorks: Generous interiors with a quiet background — pale walls, minimal decor around: living rooms, dining rooms, galleries, reception rooms.
LC0295.style: Minimalism and optical design: clean planes, no ornament, precise light. The message is physics instead of decor — beauty obtained from the properties of a substance rather than from a pattern applied to it.
LC0295.madeToOrder: The number of feathers, their calibres and the density of the group are all made to order.

paragraphs: A garland that does not end. The composition is built like a line of text: it runs the length of the table and has neither a beginning nor a full stop — only rhythm.

The rhythm is set by alternation: some leaves glow evenly and softly, others flare with sharp highlights. The light is hidden at the base of each and lifts it from below, leaving the upper side in shadow — foliage as seen by someone standing under the canopy.
By day it is a botanical garland, fine and graphic. In the evening it becomes a ribbon of light drawn across the room with every second leaf alight.
LC0296.whereItWorks: A linear format for very long tables, bar counters, galleries, banqueting halls, elongated meeting rooms.
LC0296.style: Contemporary classic with a classical note: laurel, symmetry, noble proportions. The message is celebration — the composition reads as a wreath stretched above the gathering.
LC0296.madeToOrder: The length of the garland, the number of leaves and the balance of the two finishes are all made to order.

paragraphs: A glacier at sunset — two states of water in one composition. The blue crystals read as ice, the amber ones as arrested sun, and together they give what the mountains give for ten minutes a day.
The faceting is large, with broad planes, as on an unworked mineral. Every crystal is lit from within, so the colour lives in the mass itself rather than lying on the surface.
By day it is a mineralogical display case — cold, precise, collectable. In the evening it becomes a wall of ice lit through its whole thickness, with something warm sensed behind it.
LC0297.whereItWorks: A vertical, formal format: staircases, atriums, entrance groups, double-height living rooms, hotel lobbies.
LC0297.style: Contemporary luxury and alpine opulence: stone, wood, large windows, long views. The message is the grandeur of nature brought down to domestic scale.
LC0297.madeToOrder: The number of crystals, the ratio of the colours and the depth of the cascade are all made to order.

paragraphs: Gold that lives in the depth rather than on the surface. Foil is fused into the mass — the leaf looks transparent and metallic at once, and the contradiction is never resolved from any viewpoint.
The veins are etched from the reverse and flare under light. Every leaf is turned its own way: some flat, some edge-on, some mid-turn — a fall recorded at a long exposure.

By day it is a herbarium lifted into the air: the dry graphic of veins seen against the light. In the evening the leaves catch fire from within, and the cascade becomes an autumn rain whose gold is not reflected but its own.
LC0298.whereItWorks: A vertical format for stairwells, double-height living rooms, bay windows, tall entrance halls.
LC0298.style: Contemporary classic and soft Art Nouveau: warm wood, brass, quiet walls. The message is the generosity of autumn — the composition brings in the state of harvest and late light.
LC0298.madeToOrder: The number of leaves, the balance of clear to gold and the height of the cascade are all made to order.

paragraphs: A system of beacons, each with a beam of its own. The cups work as parabolic mirrors: light bounces off the concave surface and leaves as a directed cone — wherever the element is turned.

Because the tilts differ, the composition draws pools of light on the ceiling and walls while at the same time delivering working light downward. It is a rare case of an art object solving the artistic and the technical task with no compromise on either.
By day it is a scattering of gold mirrors, each reflecting the room in its own way. In the evening it becomes a constellation of directed beams that have ruled the space into sections.
LC0299.whereItWorks: Generous halls and double-height spaces: lobbies, atriums, banqueting halls, galleries, showrooms.
LC0299.style: Art Deco and contemporary luxury: gilding, mirrors, large planes, formal proportions. The message is theatricality — the composition places accents in a space the way stage lighting places them on a set.
LC0299.madeToOrder: The number of cups, their diameters and the angles of tilt are all made to order.

paragraphs: The ripple from a drop that fell a few seconds ago. Rings run out from the centre of each disc and overlay the rings of their neighbours — a drawing that water holds for an instant.

The discs are layered at several levels, so the gaze passes through three or four layers at once and the ripple multiplies against itself. The composition reads through optics alone: there is almost no form, there is refraction.

By day the object is barely noticeable against the ceiling — a transparent cloud that is easier to miss than to see. In the evening it appears in full: the surface of water lit from below, suspended overhead.
LC0300.whereItWorks: Large horizontal spaces: lobbies, dining rooms, panoramic living rooms, meeting rooms, spas.
LC0300.style: Minimalism and Japanese aesthetics: emptiness as a material, pale tones, natural textures. The message is contemplation — the composition does not demand attention, it rewards it.
LC0300.madeToOrder: The area of the composition, the number of discs and their calibres are all made to order.

paragraphs: An artefact raised from the sea floor. An irregular trunk, a porous rough surface with runs down it, gold trumpet-cups grown into it like polyps — the object looks found rather than made.
Hanging strands with hundreds of sparks at their ends give a second light part: the trumpets throw directed light, the strands shimmer diffusely. Two lights with different characters in one object.

By day it is a biological specimen scaled up to the size of a chandelier. In the evening it becomes a reef in a diver's torch beam: you see only what the light has caught, the rest goes off into blackness.
LC0301.whereItWorks: A horizontal format for long tables, generous halls with character, restaurants, private clubs, galleries.
LC0301.style: Art Nouveau and natural surrealism: dark walls, antiques, collected objects. The message is discovery — a piece for someone who collects the unusual and is not put off by the strange.
LC0301.madeToOrder: The length of the trunk, the number of strands and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: Stones split by hand rather than worked on a machine. The faceting is deliberately irregular — the piece is about chance being more precise than symmetry.

Inside each element its own lamp burns, and the facets work as prisms: the light comes out in bundles, breaks up, reflects in its neighbours. Varying the drop height gives the scattering volume — a cloud of jewels suspended in the air.
By day it is a collection of minerals laid out on invisible shelves. In the evening it becomes the heat of coals lifted to the ceiling and left there to burn down.
LC0302.whereItWorks: A flexible format: a compact group above a table or a wide field in a hall, a lobby, a restaurant, a private living room.
LC0302.style: Contemporary luxury and brutal opulence: rough stone, dark metal, leather. The message is possession — the composition speaks of value directly, without circumlocution.
LC0302.madeToOrder: The number of stones, their calibres and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: A surface that flows into itself. The form folds and unfolds without a single corner — the tail of a fish, the wing of an insect, a wave at the moment it turns over: everything is recognised at once and nothing separately.
Every scale reflects light at its own angle, so moving along the composition sends waves of highlights running across it. The object does not move, yet it never looks frozen.
By day it is armour — dense, cold, blue-steel in cast, like blued metal. In the evening the light sets the scales alight from within, and the armour turns into a fish heading for deep water.
The composition holds an international award.
LC0303.whereItWorks: Large spaces: atriums, lobbies, panoramic halls, pools, spa areas, showrooms.
LC0303.style: Contemporary luxury and biomimicry: large volumes, smooth surfaces, a dark palette. The message is natural mechanics — beauty derived from the way living things are built.
LC0303.madeToOrder: The dimensions, the number of scales and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: Light hidden inside something that absorbs light. The surface is matte, downy, almost textile — it kills highlights completely, and that is the whole calculation.

Hundreds of points scattered through the mass read against such a background with full contrast, like sparks deep in moss. The composition does not shine — it smoulders, and that is a rare state for a light object.

By day it is a warm patch of colour with a rich texture, a piece you sense by touch rather than by glow. In the evening the mass disappears and what remains is a constellation suspended in the air with nothing holding it.
LC0304.whereItWorks: Generous interiors with high ceilings: lobbies, lounges, spas, private clubs, living rooms with a fireplace.
LC0304.style: Eco-luxury and comfortable minimalism: natural fabrics, wood, a muted palette. The message is warmth and shelter — the composition reads as something alive and soft that asks to be touched.
LC0304.madeToOrder: The diameter of the dome, the density of the pile, the tone and the number of light points are all made to order.

paragraphs: A thicket seen from below — the way a fish sees it. The rods vary in length and are slightly curved; they sway to the eye even in complete stillness.

Density is the point here: there are so many elements that the composition reads as a single body rather than a set of parts. Light gets inside and runs down the rod, so each tip glows as a separate drop — thousands of points within the mass of green.
By day the object looks like a dense green canopy; in the evening, like a thicket lit from a depth the eye cannot reach.
LC0305.whereItWorks: Large spaces with high ceilings: atriums, spa areas, lobbies, pools, winter gardens.
LC0305.style: Eco-modern and biophilic design: living greenery, natural stone, water. The message is immersion — the composition places the viewer inside an environment rather than in front of it.
LC0305.madeToOrder: The diameter of the dome, the density of the rods and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A net sagging under its own weight. The form is set not by a designer but by physics — the mesh falls the way any net stretched between fixed points will fall.

The light enters at a knot and runs along the tape to the next one, so what glows is not a point but the whole thread: the lattice turns out to be drawn entirely in light. A bluish cast in the mass adds to the likeness with water — a net raised while still wet.
By day the object throws diamond shadows on the floor and reads as graphic work; in the evening it becomes a glowing web beneath the ceiling.
LC0306.whereItWorks: Large flat ceilings: lobbies, conference halls, panoramic living rooms, co-working spaces, exhibition spaces.
LC0306.style: Contemporary minimalism and a marine theme kept from the literal: pale tones, natural textures, plenty of air. The message is simplicity of solution — one idea carried through to the end, with not one surplus detail.
LC0306.madeToOrder: The dimensions of the mesh, the cell pitch and the depth of the sag are all made to order.

paragraphs: Wind made visible. The ribbons are twisted helically and drawn out in one direction — the whole stream is moving, though no element will shift from its place.
The light enters at the tips and runs the length of the ribbon, flaring at the turns. Pink and gold alternate, setting a soft rhythm of colour — not a contrast but a gradation, as in a morning sky.
By day the composition is almost weightless: only highlights and contours are visible. In the evening it appears in full — warm air that has become noticeable.
LC0307.whereItWorks: A horizontal format for long tables, bar counters, generous entrance halls, restaurant rooms, bedrooms with high ceilings.
LC0307.style: Soft Art Nouveau and romantic classicism: a pastel palette, light fabrics, pale wood. The message is lightness — the composition weighs nothing down, it lifts.
LC0307.madeToOrder: The length of the stream, the number of ribbons and the balance of tones are all made to order.

paragraphs: Cold fire — a contradiction placed at the base of the piece. The colour is not a warm pink but a crimson with violet depth: the elements look lit even with the light switched off.
The form, meanwhile, is entirely of fire: twisted tongues reaching upward, a dense vertical group. The eye reads flame while the colour says the opposite, and the object stays inside that mismatch.
Fine gold rods between the elements provide a second light part — pointed, sharp, keeping the composition from going vague.
By day it is a sculpture of dense, almost jewel-like colour. In the evening it is a bonfire burning crimson: a fire whose warmth has been taken away and whose light has been left.
LC0308.whereItWorks: A vertical format for stairwells, boudoirs, dressing rooms, private living rooms — interiors that are not afraid of colour.
LC0308.style: Glamour and contemporary Art Deco: velvet, deep shades, mirrors, bold combinations. The message is character — a composition for someone who chooses pieces rather than maintains neutrality.
LC0308.madeToOrder: The height, the number of elements and the depth of tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: Driftwood raised out of the forest and hung from the ceiling. The trunks are worked down to their cracks, knots and burls — the texture is real, found rather than invented.

Beneath the branches hangs rain: thousands of the finest threads with points of light at their ends, of varying length, answering the least movement of air. The light lives only at the tips — hundreds of white sparks in several layers.

By day it is graphic work: dark branches and silver fringe. In the evening the branches dissolve into darkness and what remains is glowing rain with no source — the effect the whole thing was built for.
LC0309.whereItWorks: Very large spaces: atriums, hotel lobbies, panoramic halls, banqueting spaces, winter gardens.
LC0309.style: Eco-luxury and natural Art Nouveau: stone, wood, live plants, large volumes. The message is a forest after rain — the composition brings the state of nature into a room, not a picture of it.
LC0309.madeToOrder: The length of the branches, the density of the threads and the number of light points are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same fire, divided in two. Half the tongues burn evenly and softly, half flare with sharp highlights — one flame shown at two temperatures at once.

The light is hidden in the upper part of each element and runs down the spiral — against the usual logic of fire. Because of that the composition reads not as a bonfire but as a torch, inverted and hung.
The sheaf narrows toward the bottom and ends in a few solitary tongues, the way a real torch ends in sparks.
By day it is a sculptural group: two textures arguing over one form. In the evening the argument ends — every tongue burns separately, and the whole vertical becomes a single flame.
LC0310.whereItWorks: A vertical format for staircases, bay windows, double-height living rooms, tall entrance halls.
LC0310.style: Contemporary classic and neoclassicism: pale walls, mouldings, brass. The message is festive restraint — the composition is dressed up exactly enough not to become excessive.
LC0310.madeToOrder: The height of the sheaf, the number of elements and the balance of lit to reflecting are all made to order.

paragraphs: A bonfire arrested at the moment of the flare. The tongues are twisted into spirals and drawn upward — the movement runs against gravity, and that is the only thing the composition asserts.

A mirrored coating on the inside changes the nature of the elements: they read as metallic rather than clear, and reflect one another, creating an endless gold echo inside the ring. The light lifts the tongues from below — from where a real fire burns.
By day the composition looks like a giant brooch; in the evening, like a flame that was not allowed to go out.
LC0311.whereItWorks: A ring format for round tables, rotundas, the central zone of an entrance hall, banqueting halls, restaurants.
LC0311.style: Art Deco and grand opulence: gilding, mirrors, deep colours, symmetry. The message is celebration — the composition was made for occasions and does not hide it.
LC0311.madeToOrder: The diameter of the ring, the number of elements and the intensity of the gilding are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same structure turned opaque — and by that turned from a diagram into a sculpture. Every bend, every tension in the surface is visible; what could only be guessed at in the transparent version is here declared at full voice.

The polish gathers reflections of the neighbouring elements, and the structure seems endless, folding back into itself. Cold and warm elements alternate, setting a rhythm of temperature inside a single geometry.
The light strikes the concave surfaces and only reflected glow escapes.

By day it is a net of mercury — heavy, dense, reflecting everything around it. In the evening it loses its weight: what remains is a glowing frame suspended with no support, like the diagram of a molecule drawn in the air. The composition holds an international award.
LC0312.whereItWorks: Interiors with strong architecture: concrete, panoramic glazing, metal, double height. Lobbies, atriums, offices, galleries.
LC0312.style: Industrial luxury and constructivism: large volumes, exposed structure, a restrained palette. The message is the force of engineering — beauty derived from calculation rather than from ornament.
LC0312.madeToOrder: The dimensions, the ratio of cold to warm elements and the density of the lattice are all made to order.

paragraphs: A soap film stretched on a frame and never burst. The membranes sag and pull taut between the rods, forming concave surfaces — a form that in nature lives for seconds.

The films are all but invisible: they neither reflect nor obscure, they gather light along their edges and flare as fine ribs. By day the composition reads as a scientific model — a molecular lattice, a crystal structure; in the evening it disappears as mass and remains as a net of glowing lines.
The model holds an international award. The intent is to make lasting what is by nature instantaneous.
LC0313.whereItWorks: Generous contemporary interiors: atriums, lobbies, galleries, meeting rooms, showrooms, offices.
LC0313.style: High-tech and scientific minimalism: concrete, glazing, metal, exposed engineering. The message is precision — the composition speaks the language of a formula and does not pretend to be an ornament.
LC0313.madeToOrder: The dimensions of the lattice, the number of membranes and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A bird's tail at the moment of opening. The bands are angled and overlap one another — the movement is stopped halfway and the eye completes what it cannot see.

Every band catches the light at its own angle, so the wreath shimmers around its whole circumference without one static highlight. The composition changes with every step the viewer takes — it does not depict movement, it creates it.
The light lifts the reverse of the bands and only a radiant contour escapes. A dark core at the centre keeps the form from scattering.
By day it is metal: the room taken apart into shards of reflection. In the evening it is a ring of light around emptiness, with neither a source nor a centre.
LC0315.whereItWorks: Works on the ceiling and on the wall: an entrance hall, above a round table, on an accent wall, in a reception room, in a showroom.
LC0315.style: Contemporary minimalism and gallery aesthetics: white walls, large planes, no small-scale decor. The message is pure plasticity — there is no subject here, only form, light and the pause between the elements.
LC0315.madeToOrder: The diameter, the number of bands and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A leaf crumpled and smoothed out again. Every crease is left in place — that is the work: a piece about the trace of effort rather than about a smooth surface.

The gilding is applied unevenly, with darkening in the recesses, so the relief reads with contrast: the raised parts burn, the hollows go to shadow. The mirror at the core distorts the room like a fisheye lens, drawing the space into the flower.
The light escapes from under the petals around the perimeter and draws the contour. The result is a sun with a dark pupil — a form that radiates and absorbs at once.
By day it is relief: creases, shadow, the room reflected in the pupil. In the evening it is an eclipse stopped at the second when the corona is already visible and the disc is still black.
LC0316.whereItWorks: An accent wall: an entrance hall, above a console, in a study, in a private living room, in a gallery space.
LC0316.style: Art Deco and contemporary art: large empty planes, dark walls, minimal furniture. The message is preciousness — the object works like a brooch scaled up to the size of a panel.
LC0316.madeToOrder: The diameter, the character of the crumpling and the finish of the mirror are all made to order.

paragraphs: The corolla of a giant flower seen from inside. The plates are angled toward the centre and downward — the composition opens upward while the viewer looks at it from below, standing inside the flower.

The thickness produces strong optics: each plate holds the refracted reflection of its neighbours, and the ring seems endless. The pink chosen is a cold one, amethyst — it keeps the piece in an adult register and stops it turning sweet.
The light strikes upward and only a glimmer along the edges escapes. The core stays dark — a device that makes you look inside.
By day it is a crown, faceted and cold. In the evening it is a flower glowing from deep within, never showing where it burns.
LC0317.whereItWorks: A ring form for round tables, rotundas, the central zone of a living room, boudoirs, private dining rooms.
LC0317.style: Softened Art Deco and feminine Art Nouveau: velvet, mirrors, deep muted tones. The message is intimacy — the composition draws a closed circle of light you want to stay inside.
LC0317.madeToOrder: The diameter of the ring, the number of plates and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A flowering with half the blooms still closed. Some corollas glow from within, others stay blind and merely reflect their neighbours — a garden caught halfway through the process.

The edge of every corolla is uneven, with folds, like a real flower after rain. One and the same form is rendered in two textures, and their alternation gives the composition a depth that neither one gives on its own.
The spiral of the cascade leads the eye downward and never lets it settle: however long you look, there is always a flower you have not yet made out.
By day it is a botanical sculpture — relief, shadow, two textures in dialogue. In the evening it is a garden where half the bush has come into bloom and the other half has gone into the dark.
LC0318.whereItWorks: A vertical format made for stairwells, double-height living rooms, bay windows, tall entrance halls.
LC0318.style: Contemporary classic and soft Art Nouveau: pastel walls, rounded furniture, brass fittings. The message is generosity — the composition reads as an armful just carried into the house.
LC0318.madeToOrder: The height of the cascade, the number of flowers and the balance of lit to blind are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same branch with the sign reversed. Where the neighbouring model reflects light, this one lets it through — and the result is the opposite character from identical geometry.

The light enters at the stalk and spreads through the body of the leaf, igniting it entire; highlights flare at the bends and a green shadow holds in the depth. The composition reads as underwater — weed in the body of the water, swaying with the current.

By day the branch is almost transparent and visible only as a contour; in the evening it fills with turquoise and becomes the principal patch of colour in the room. The composition holds an international award.
LC0319.whereItWorks: A horizontal format for large spaces with a quiet background: above a table, in a lobby, in a spa area, beside a pool, in a winter garden.
LC0319.style: Eco-modern and resort luxury: pale walls, natural stone, water nearby. The message is coolness — the composition drops the temperature of a room by several degrees while changing nothing in it.
LC0319.madeToOrder: The spread, the number of leaves and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: An object with no colour of its own. The composition shows nothing that belongs to it — it gathers up the interior around it and gives it back distorted, the way a drop of water gives back a room.

Because of that the piece never looks the same twice: in the morning it holds the reflection of the window, in the evening the warm light of the lamps; in winter it is grey, in summer green from the garden outside. The owner acquires not an object but a mirror of their own space.

The light is hidden in the joints and strikes the underside of the leaves — only reflected glow escapes, without a single direct beam. By day it is a sculpture in arrested metal; in the evening it is a glowing canopy with not one lamp in sight. The model holds an international award.
LC0320.whereItWorks: A horizontal format — above a long table, in an entrance hall, over a reception desk, in a meeting room, in a showroom.
LC0320.style: High-tech and contemporary minimalism: clean planes, glazing, polished stone. The message is intellectual restraint — an object that declines to take the solo and is remembered for exactly that.
LC0320.madeToOrder: The spread of the branch, the number of leaves and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A rare format for the brand: not a luminaire but a piece of architecture. Here the light is built into a structure people run a hand along — and that changes the relationship with it.
The intent is to make an event of the passage rather than of a point. A staircase is usually what you walk through; here it is what you climb for.

By day the leaves work as stained glass: the cold blue reads against the light while the warm metal of the handrail keeps its own temperature. In the evening the light from the treads washes the whole flight in blue, and the contrast of the two lights carries the staircase entire.
LC0321.whereItWorks: Private residences, boutique hotels, showrooms, galleries — anywhere a staircase should be an event rather than a transit.
LC0321.style: Contemporary luxury and Art Deco: marble, brass, deep colours, formal proportions. The message is ceremony — climbing a staircase like this becomes a staged gesture.
LC0321.madeToOrder: The length of the flight, the number of elements, the tone of the leaves and the metal finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A tropical plant cast whole. The leaves are twisted helically, with a sharp tip and a deep lens in the body — a form taken from nature and carried through to an optical instrument.

Within the thickness of each leaf the reflections of its neighbours gather, and the canopy comes out layered: through the near leaf you see the far one, refracted and enlarged. The green is saturated, botanical, with a cold undertone.

By day it is the opposite: the graphic of the stems and leaves that are almost transparent. In the evening the foliage fills with light while the stems go into shadow — what remains is greenery hanging in the air with nothing to hold it.
LC0322.whereItWorks: A vertical format made for stairwells, bay windows, narrow double-height spaces, winter gardens.
LC0322.style: Eco-modern and tropical luxury: live plants, natural textures, warm wood. The message is vitality — the composition brings into a house the sense of something growing rather than something arranged.
LC0322.madeToOrder: The height of the branch, the number of leaves and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A curtain after the performance. The panels are thrown over rings and set in different phases: some sag, others are caught up and raised — movement stopped halfway.
The rings work as both fixing and source: light comes out from inside each one and lifts the drapery from below, the way footlights lift the wings.
The model holds an international award.

By day the illusion deceives the eye: you see folds, tension, the weight of cloth — although the object is rigid and holds its form for years. In the evening the light comes out from inside each ring and lifts the drapery from below, the way footlights lift the wings — the curtain turns out to be on stage.
LC0323.whereItWorks: A format for wide spaces with high ceilings: lobbies, banqueting and theatre halls, double-height living rooms, grand staircases.
LC0323.style: Theatrical classicism and neo-baroque: velvet, drapes, mouldings, deep colours. The message is the stage — the composition turns entering a room into stepping onto the boards.
LC0323.madeToOrder: The number of panels, the palette and the spread of the composition are all made to order.

paragraphs: A form caught at the moment of compression. The body looks crushed by hand — uneven facets, creases, the marks of pressure — and that is the only thing happening in it.
Three versions differ in the character of the crumpling, and no frame repeats another. Repeatability here would be a defeat — the piece is built on every example being the only one of its kind.

By day the body reads as crumpled: uneven facets, creases, the marks of pressure — the piece works through plasticity alone. In the evening the light escapes only around the perimeter, from under the edge, drawing the contour as a fine line, while the core stays dark: a window into a room where the light has already been switched off.
LC0324.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, corridors, private studies, stair flights, gallery walls — wherever a wall light works as an accent rather than as a source of general light.
LC0324.style: Brutal minimalism and contemporary art: concrete, rough stone, large empty planes. The message is the force of the substance — an object about the trace of effort being worth more than a smooth surface.
LC0324.madeToOrder: The size, the depth of the relief and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A backwater seen from above. The bowls are laid overlapping, like leaves on still water — with no order and no centre, arranged the way the current arranged them.
Traces of working are left deliberately: scratches, streaks, an uneven patina. The composition is meant to look touched by time rather than to look as though it came off a line.

By day the object stays dark and matte: darkened bronze with the marks of working, scratches and an uneven patina. In the evening the light strikes upward into the underside of the neighbouring leaves and only a glimmer escapes — bronze on the outside, hidden gold within.
LC0325.whereItWorks: A ceiling or wall format; works as an independent art object: an entrance hall, a private living room, a spa area, a study, a restaurant.
LC0325.style: Art Nouveau and vintage luxury: antique furniture, dark wood, aged surfaces. The message is noble ageing — a piece that will only improve over the years.
