LC0325.madeToOrder: The number of bowls, the character of the patina and the points of illumination are all made to order.

paragraphs: A knot whose beginning cannot be found. The loops enter one another, cross, break off — a topology the eye tries to untangle and cannot.
The pink is muted almost to haze, and the ribbing adds a metallic cast.
The composition holds an international award.

By day the composition has to be walked around: each side reads as a new drawing and none of them gives the whole picture. In the evening the lights overlay each other where the ribbons cross, and bright knots appear there — a map the eye tries to travel.
LC0326.whereItWorks: It asks for space around it: the centre of a living room, an atrium, a generous lobby, a gallery hall, a showroom.
LC0326.style: Contemporary art and gallery aesthetics: minimal furniture, maximum air, walls as a background. The message is an intellectual game — a piece that poses a question and does not answer it.
LC0326.madeToOrder: The dimensions of the tangle, the number of ribbons and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A bridge thrown across where a bridge has nothing to come from. Two ribbons meet at the apex and part toward the edges, breaking off at a crumpled edge — an arch resting on nothing.
The green here is deep, bottle-dark, with a cold undertone — a rare colour for large light objects and memorable for that reason.
The model holds an international award. The intent is architectural gesture: the composition does not hang over a space, it spans it like a vault.

By day the ribbing breaks the deep bottle tone into dozens of shades: in one place the ribbon is almost black, in another it glows grass-green. In the evening the vault lights up from within, and the arch that rests on nothing turns out to be glowing as well.
LC0327.whereItWorks: A format for wide spaces: above a long table, in an entrance hall, in a restaurant room, in a lobby, in a winter garden.
LC0327.style: Eco-modern and contemporary classic with a botanical note: live plants, natural textures, muted green in the finishes. The message is natural force — the colour of a forest brought into architectural form.
LC0327.madeToOrder: The span of the arch, the tone and the drop height are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same ribbon in a dark reading — and that changes its nature. Here it lets almost no light through and works as silhouette; only a chain of lights along the edge gives away that this is a luminaire.
The composition holds an international award. The device is built on refusal: the colour is removed, the transparency is removed, only the trajectory is left.

By day the form reads as silhouette — a sail, the wing of a ray, a sheet of paper caught by a draught; the double fold gives the eye nowhere to settle. In the evening only the chain of lights along the edge remains: the body disappears and a single trajectory hangs in the dark.
LC0328.whereItWorks: Good in interiors with a dark palette: private living rooms, bars, lounges, studies, restaurants with subdued light.
LC0328.style: Dark Art Nouveau and brutal opulence: wood, brass, leather, deep tones. The message is drama — the composition works like a shadow that has been given a form.
LC0328.madeToOrder: The length, the depth of the bends and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A gesture rather than an object. A broad band is thrown into the air, twisted and left in the position it was caught in — the whole composition is one movement carried through to the end.
The model holds an international award. The intent is concision: one form, one substance, one gesture — and nothing beyond that.

By day the ribbing works as an optical grating: from one angle the ribbon is almost transparent, from another it flares gold, and as the viewer moves waves run along it. In the evening the light travels the length of the band, emphasising the twist — the gesture becomes a glowing stroke of the pen.
LC0329.whereItWorks: A horizontal format for large spaces: above a long table, in a lobby, in a meeting room, in a gallery, in a restaurant hall.
LC0329.style: Contemporary minimalism and gallery aesthetics: empty walls, large planes, no small-scale decor. The message is confidence — a piece that has nothing to prove in order to be the main thing in the room.
LC0329.madeToOrder: The length of the ribbon, the character of the bend and the tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same system stripped of contrast — and denser in sound because of it. The white is removed and only a warm metallic tone remains, with deep shadows in the gaps.

The shade wanders from light to dark module by module, and that unevenness makes the surface alive, like old bronze that hands have touched. The gloss catches any source and scatters soft highlights across the wall.
The system can be built to any opening — from a full wall to a pier half a metre wide. This is not a product of fixed size but a language in which a border is constructed.

By day the shade wanders from light to dark module by module, and the surface lives like old bronze that hands have touched. In the evening the gloss catches any source and scatters soft highlights across the wall — the bronze lacework begins to shimmer.
LC0330.whereItWorks: A wide panel between zones or a narrow vertical section in a pier: a living room, an entrance hall, a restaurant, a boutique, a private study.
LC0330.style: Art Deco and Eastern opulence: dark wood, deep colours, an abundance of metal. The message is restrained luxury — bronze lacework that works as a background rather than taking the solo.
LC0330.madeToOrder: The dimensions, the tone of the links and the configuration of the sections are all made to order.

paragraphs: A border the gaze passes through. The screen does not cut a space off, it separates it into layers: movement is visible behind it but not detail — exactly as much as is needed to keep the zones connected.

The modules are assembled into a rigid grid, but the surface of each is slightly convex and glossy, so the wall shimmers as you move along it. Alternating pale and dark links set a diagonal rhythm — a static structure reads as fabric.
By day the screen draws diamond shadows on the floor; in the evening, lit from the side, the gloss turns it into a wall of mother-of-pearl.
LC0331.whereItWorks: Zoning without walls: between a living room and a dining room, in an entrance hall, in a restaurant, in a showroom, beside a staircase, behind a reception desk.
LC0331.style: Contemporary classic and softened Art Deco: the composition likes the company of velvet, brass and mirrors. The message is delicacy — dividing a space without cutting it apart.
LC0331.madeToOrder: The dimensions of the panel, the palette of the links and the density of the weave are all made to order.

paragraphs: Ice from a river shallow, set on edge. The surface is rough, chipped, full of inclusions — the substance is deliberately left imperfect, because perfect ice does not exist.
The light enters from above and gets caught in the mass rather than passing through. The plate glows not against the light but from within, diffusely, like a real floe under a low sun.
The ring form closes the composition on itself: it has no front and no back, it is equally composed from any side. A crown with every point alight.

By day it is ice from the shallows: a rough chipped surface with inclusions, a piece read through texture and irregularity. In the evening the light enters from above and gets caught in the mass rather than passing through — the plate glows from within, diffusely, like a real floe under a low sun.
LC0332.whereItWorks: The ring form is made for round tables, rotundas, the zone above a kitchen island, private dining rooms.
LC0332.style: Nordic minimalism and eco-modern: pale wood, linen, stone, a muted palette. The message is natural honesty — the composition does not pretend to be precious, it pretends to have been found.
LC0332.madeToOrder: The diameter of the ring, the number of plates and the height of the candles are all made to order.

paragraphs: One floe, stood against the wall. A single plate is taken out of the ring — rough, chipped, full of inclusions in its depth — and hung vertically: what was a point of the crown in the composition has become a shard of its own here.
The device stays as it was: the light enters from above and lodges in the depth without passing through. The plate glows not against the light but from within, diffused.

By day it is texture and nothing besides: the uneven surface, the chipped edge, the inclusions read close to. In the evening the depth fills with diffused glow while the edge stays dark — a floe under a low sun, set upright.
LC0332-1.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, bathrooms, bedrooms at the bedhead, corridors. Soft diffused light without highlights suits places where the light must not dazzle. It also works as a companion to composition LC0332 — the same ice on the walls around a round table.
LC0332-1.style: Nordic minimalism and eco-modernism: pale wood, linen, stone, a muted palette. The message is natural honesty — the piece does not pretend to be precious, it pretends to have been found.
LC0332-1.madeToOrder: The size of the plate, the depth of the texture and the colour temperature are all made to order.

paragraphs: A collection of vessels that never held anything. Bellied flasks, drawn-out decanters, squat retorts — the forms are taken from craft and released from function.

Light pours into each cavity from below, like a liquid, and stops at the neck. The vessel turns out to be full — not of a substance but of a glow, and that substitution is what the whole thing was conceived for.
No form repeats another: the asymmetry here is a signature rather than carelessness.

By day it is a workshop shelf lifted into the air: the forms read as silhouettes and no two are alike. In the evening light pours into each cavity from below, like a liquid, and stops at the neck — the vessels turn out full, not of a substance but of a glow.
LC0333.whereItWorks: The cascade narrows downward — a format for stairwells, bay windows, double-height living rooms, wine rooms and restaurant halls.
LC0333.style: Eclecticism and artisan luxury: exposed brick, wood, antiques mixed with the contemporary. The message is collectorly — a piece for someone who gathers objects with a history and values the trace of a hand.
LC0333.madeToOrder: The number of vessels, their forms and the depth of the cascade are all made to order.

paragraphs: Hoarfrost enlarged to the size of a palm. Inside each plate needles radiate from the centre — the drawing winter makes on a window overnight and erases by noon.
Here it is arrested. The light stands exactly at the centre of the pattern and ignites the whole of it, turning every element into a snowflake under a magnifier.
A crumpled edge and a gold border argue with the coldness of the drawing. The piece lives off that argument: ice graphics in a warm setting.

By day the thickness produces powerful distortion: through one plate you see the next, refracted and enlarged — a depth that should not exist in a flat object. In the evening the light stands exactly at the centre of the pattern and ignites the whole of it, turning every element into a snowflake under a magnifier.
LC0334.whereItWorks: The horizontal format suits a long table, an entrance hall, a meeting room with a high ceiling, a living room with a fireplace.
LC0334.style: Contemporary classic and softened Art Deco: pale walls, gilded fittings, mirrors. The message is a winter marvel — the composition brings a festive note into an interior without descending to festive decor.
LC0334.madeToOrder: The number of plates, their calibres and the density of the cloud are all made to order.

paragraphs: A polar sky carried into a room. The colour moves from deep emerald at the top to clear at the bottom — the way a real aurora melts toward the horizon, having no lower edge at all.

The composition puts itself out. By day it is a dense green-and-blue curtain; in the evening the mass disappears and only thousands of sparks remain, hanging in layers at different depths. An object that loses its body in the evening and leaves the light behind.
The model holds an international award. The intent lies in refusing an edge: the composition does not end, it dissolves.
LC0335.whereItWorks: A format for large verticals — atriums, stair shafts, panoramic lobbies, double-height living rooms, wherever the height can be shown in full.
LC0335.style: Contemporary luxury and Nordic Art Nouveau: a cold palette, panoramic glazing, dark noble surfaces. The message is contemplative — the composition gives not light but the state of a northern night.
LC0335.madeToOrder: The height, the density of the threads and the depth of the gradient are all made to order.

paragraphs: A form impossible to repeat twice. The lines do not follow the rules of a sphere, they fall as thread falls — freely, overlapping, with hollows and thickenings.

This is a composition about the hand-made: behind the apparent chaos stands exact calculation, but the eye reads not calculation but a nest, a cocoon, a ball of yarn — something wound rather than drawn.

The light is born at the knots of the weave and scatters in hundreds of points. The honey tone takes away the cold, and the sphere begins to seem warm to the touch — an illusion the whole object rests on.

By day it is a tangle of overlapping lines with hollows and thickenings: behind the apparent chaos stands calculation, but the eye reads a nest rather than a drawing. In the evening the light is born at the knots of the weave and scatters in hundreds of points, the honey tone takes away the cold — the sphere begins to seem warm to the touch.
LC0336.whereItWorks: A spherical form has no front: it works in the centre of a space, above a round table, in a double-height living room, in an entrance hall, in a restaurant.
LC0336.style: Eco-modern and comfortable minimalism: wood, linen, rattan, warm walls. The message is domestic warmth — honey light and the form of a nest read as a promise of comfort.
LC0336.madeToOrder: The diameter of the sphere, the density of the weave and the tone of the threads are all made to order.

paragraphs: Three spheres threaded vertically — and three different views of one object: from the ground floor you see the lowest sphere, from the first the middle one, from above the whole row at once.
The structure is openwork throughout: through the weave you see both the neighbouring sphere and the space beyond it. The volume here is declared but not occupied — a form consisting mostly of air.
The intent is in the vertical. The composition does not hang above the viewer, it accompanies them on the way up, opening in parts — light tied to movement.

By day the structure is openwork throughout: through the weave you see both the neighbouring sphere and the space beyond it — the volume is declared but not occupied. In the evening light is born inside the spheres and comes out through the weave as a net of rays — three glowing cocoons threaded on a vertical.
LC0337.whereItWorks: Ideal for a stairwell: the spheres read from different floors in turn. Also good in a narrow double-height entrance hall and in a shaft between floors.
LC0337.style: Contemporary Art Nouveau and soft high-tech: open staircases, glass balustrades, spare finishes. The message is upward movement — three steps of light leading the eye along a vertical.
LC0337.madeToOrder: The number of spheres, their diameters and the density of the weave are all made to order.

paragraphs: Rain with neither a beginning nor an end. Dense gold at the top, clearer and clearer toward the bottom — the composition dissolves into the air instead of ending at an edge.

Inside every thread a chain of lights runs, and no thread repeats the rhythm of its neighbour. From a distance it is one continuous radiance; close up you see that it is assembled from thousands of separate sparks, each in its place.
The model holds an international award. The intent is simple and strong for that reason: the object does not depict rain, it occupies all the space that rain would occupy.

By day it is a gold gradient dissolving toward the bottom — a piece read through density and transition. In the evening a chain of lights runs inside every thread and no thread repeats the rhythm of its neighbour: continuous radiance from a distance, thousands of separate sparks up close, each in its place.
LC0338.whereItWorks: The format was made for large verticals: atriums, stair shafts, panoramic lobbies, double-height living rooms, banqueting halls.
LC0338.style: Contemporary luxury and glamour: the composition was made to make an impression and works in interiors that are not embarrassed by that. The message is celebration — it turns any space into a formal one.
LC0338.madeToOrder: The height, the density of the threads and the gradient of the coating are all made to order.

paragraphs: White on white — the hardest task in product design: with the colour taken away, form has nothing left to hide behind.
Here it holds. You can see how the thickness of a petal changes from base to tip, how it catches light with its gloss, how the double tier gives volume without a single hint of colour.

The glow shows through at the edges and the flower becomes half-transparent — not a glowing object but an object that light passes through. The difference is fundamental, and the whole piece rests on it.

By day you can see how the thickness of a petal changes from base to tip and how it catches light with its gloss: the double tier gives volume without a single hint of colour. In the evening the glow shows through at the edges and the flower becomes half-transparent — not a glowing object but an object that light passes through.
LC0339.whereItWorks: The most universal version of the series: above a table, in a bedroom, in a hallway, in a meeting room, in a study — anywhere that needs an accent without colour.
LC0339.style: Suits almost any interior — from strict minimalism to classicism with mouldings. The message is restrained perfection — the piece declares taste through quiet rather than through brightness.
LC0339.madeToOrder: The diameter, the number of petals and the colour temperature of the light are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same flower, brought down to human height. The bloom is tilted slightly — like a real one reaching for the light — and the floor lamp stops being an object and becomes company beside an armchair.

The proportions rest on a risk: a heavy head, the finest of stems, a substantial base. The object looks fragile while remaining perfectly stable — a deliberate illusion, and everything was calculated for it.
The light goes up and to the side, leaving the floor in shadow. This is not general lighting but personal lighting — a circle you sit in.

By day it is a sculpture on the finest of stems: the tilted bloom reads as a silhouette, the base carries the weight. In the evening the light goes up and to the side, leaving the floor in shadow — one lit circle appears around the armchair, personal rather than general.
LC0340.whereItWorks: Beside an armchair in a living room, at the head of a bed, in the corner of a study, in a hotel lounge. Works solo and in a pair flanking a sofa — in two colours it reads at once as a pair of different flowers.
LC0340.style: Contemporary classic and feminine Art Nouveau: a soft line, nothing technical. The message is intimacy — the floor lamp does not light the room, it makes one comfortable corner.
LC0340.madeToOrder: The height, the colour of the bloom and the finish of the base are all made to order.

paragraphs: A flower caught at the moment of opening. The petals are not fully unfurled — the movement is stopped a little before it finished, and the whole life of the object is in that.

Blue and white alternate in layers, so the sphere looks solid even switched off. The light is hidden in the core and pushes out between the petals, lifting their edges — what glows is not the surface but the gaps.
The composition received an international award. It is built on a rare balance: a recognisable natural form with not one naturalistic detail.

By day the sphere looks solid even switched off — the blue and white layers alternate and give light and shade. In the evening the light from the core pushes out between the petals and lifts their edges: what glows is not the surface but the gaps, and the flower turns out to be outlined in light.
LC0341.whereItWorks: Above a round table, in a bedroom over the bed, in an entrance hall, in a dressing room — wherever a whole silhouette and soft shadowless light matter.
LC0341.style: Contemporary classic and soft Art Nouveau: rounded furniture, velvet, pale walls. The message is flowering — a note of spring in an interior, kept strict in form.
LC0341.madeToOrder: The diameter of the sphere, the number of petals and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: There is no natural form here — only pure structure. The object is built like a thought: a horizontal, a vertical, a node, a pause.

The light lives inside the lines and never comes out as a patch — it rules the space, leaving air and shadow between the rods. By day the frame reads; in the evening only a glowing drawing remains, suspended with no support.
The intent is built on a contradiction: a rigid orthogonal grid filled with a texture that resists it — sparks inside the rods make the strict geometry alive.
LC0342.whereItWorks: Contemporary spaces with high ceilings: lofts, open-plan offices, atriums, galleries, showrooms, meeting rooms.
LC0342.style: High-tech, constructivism, industrial minimalism: concrete, metal, exposed services. The message is intellectual: this is a structure rather than an ornament, and it declares the rationality of its owner.
LC0342.madeToOrder: The dimensions of the lattice, the density of the rods and the finish of the capsules are all made to order.

paragraphs: A pond lifted to the ceiling. The bowls open upward rather than down — and that inverts the usual logic: the light here does not pour onto the table, it lies in the leaves like water after rain.
The green mass works as a filter: light passes through it and tints the air beneath the composition a soft grass tone. The white bowls keep the colour from going monotonous — they hold the pause.
The composition holds an international award. What won it was the honesty of the device: form and optics here do not argue, they do one job.

By day the bowls read green against the light — water lying in leaves after rain. In the evening the green mass works as a filter: light passes through it and tints the air beneath the composition a grass tone, while the white bowls remain a pause in the colour.
LC0343.whereItWorks: Above a round or oval table, in a winter garden, in a spa area, in a living room facing a garden — where the green outside will pick up the green of the composition.
LC0343.style: Art Nouveau and eco-modern: the line of nature, no geometry at all. The message is living water — the composition brings in the sense of a pond, damp coolness and slow time.
LC0343.madeToOrder: The number of bowls, the balance of green to white and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A branch that was not cut but grown again. The leaves are twisted and turned out of step with each other — there is no garland rhythm here, there is the disorder of a real canopy.

Half the foliage transmits light and half reflects it. Because of that the canopy shimmers the way a tree shimmers in the sun: some leaves burn against the light, others stay dark, and the drawing changes with every step.
The composition is deliberately horizontal: it does not descend on the viewer, it reaches out above them — like a branch over a garden path that you want to stand under.

By day the canopy shimmers the way a tree shimmers in the sun: some leaves burn against the light, others stay dark, and the drawing changes with every step. In the evening the light comes from inside the branch, the clear leaves fill and the gold ones flare — the branch lights up every other leaf.
LC0344.whereItWorks: A linear format for a long dining table, a bar counter, a kitchen island, a reception desk, an elongated meeting room.
LC0344.style: Contemporary classic with an Eastern note: warm wood, brass fittings, quiet walls. The message is hospitality — a branch above a table reads as the sign of a table laid and a guest invited.
LC0344.madeToOrder: The length of the branch, the number of leaves and the balance of clear to gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: The man-made pretending to have been found. The crystals are split irregularly, the facets meet at random angles, and the object looks lifted out of rock rather than assembled in a workshop.
Light enters at the bases and turns every facet into a prism: some crystals burn from within, others only reflect their neighbours. A depth arises between them that exists in no single element.
That is the device: the composition is built from repeating modules and reads as a one-of-a-kind mineral. Order pretends to be chance — deliberately and all the way through.

By day it is rock: the split facets catch daylight unevenly and the cluster looks lifted out of the ground. In the evening light enters at the bases and every facet becomes a prism — some crystals burn from within, others only reflect their neighbours, and a depth opens inside the mass.
LC0345.whereItWorks: The vertical cluster asks for height: a staircase, an atrium, a double-height entrance hall, a study with double light.
LC0345.style: Contemporary luxury and brutal opulence: rough stone, dark metal, leather, coarse texture. The message is the primordial — the piece speaks of the force of nature in the language of precise work.
LC0345.madeToOrder: The number of crystals, their calibres and the finish of the branches are all made to order.

paragraphs: Water frozen together with everything that was in it. Inside each element there is a suspension: bubbles, sparks, grains, as though the sea had frozen before it could let go of the plankton.

The form is reduced to a minimum — a smooth cylinder, a smooth lens, not one gesture. All the work is given to the depth: the blue elements damp the light and hold shadow, the clear ones multiply it, and the field comes out layered, with hollows and flares.
The intent here is not in the form but in the state: the composition does not depict water, it reproduces the sensation of looking through a body of it.

By day it is a clear mass with a suspension inside — a piece read through depth and layers, calm and cold. In the evening the blue elements damp the light and hold shadow, the clear ones multiply it, and the field comes alive with hollows and flares: a look through water at dusk.
LC0346.whereItWorks: A format for large horizontal spaces: above a long table, in a lobby, in a panoramic living room, in a meeting room, in a spa and beside a pool.
LC0346.style: Contemporary minimalism and Nordic Art Nouveau: concrete, glazing, dark wood, muted tones. The message is depth and quiet — the composition works like a window into water; it calms rather than entertains.
LC0346.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the balance of blue to clear and the area of the field are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a fragility that turns out to be stronger than stone. A dragonfly lives one season, but its silhouette has not changed in two hundred million years — that paradox became the intent of the object.

The wings hold their transparency to the limit: light does not bounce off them, it goes through, developing the drawing of the veins the way film is developed. The bodies stay dense and dark — they do not glow, they give the wings their support.

The vertical is assembled without symmetry: each figure is turned its own way, and the swarm reads not as a formation but as an instant — what came before and what comes after is left outside the frame.

By day it is graphic work — the fine drawing of veins on a transparent wing, the bodies read as dark strokes. In the evening the wings light up against the light while the bodies stay blind: the swarm glows by its wings, suspended in the dark.
LC0347.whereItWorks: The narrow vertical format suits stair flights, wall piers, zones beside a window, studies and private libraries — wherever the object is looked at closely and for a long time.
LC0347.style: Art Nouveau: the composition comes from the same aesthetic as Tiffany's stained glass and Lalique's jewelled brooches. The message is collectorly — a piece for someone who values a naturalistic detail and is willing to study it.
LC0347.madeToOrder: The number of dragonflies, the height of the column and the finish of the bodies are all made to order.

paragraphs: An object about a shell being a house built along a spiral. The form is coiled so that it has neither a beginning nor an end: the gaze is drawn inside and finds no floor.

The light is hidden deep in the whorl and comes out not straight but in a circle, drawing the curve. The result is not a luminaire but a find — something raised from the sea bed that goes on glowing by itself.
The birds between the shells keep the composition from the literal: sea and air in one scene — a device that stops the object becoming a seaside corner in the souvenir sense.

By day it is a sculptural find — a spiral read through plasticity and the highlights along the whorl. In the evening the light comes out in a circle, drawing the curve, and the shell begins to glow of its own accord, like something raised from the sea bed that will not go out.
LC0348.whereItWorks: A dense vertical format — for staircases, bay windows, tall entrance halls, spa areas and poolside spaces where the theme of water sounds natural.
LC0348.style: Mediterranean classicism and resort luxury: white walls, natural stone, pale textiles. The message is calm — the composition brings the sense of a coastline into a house without a single literal shell on a shelf.
LC0348.madeToOrder: The number of shells and birds and the depth of the cascade are all made to order.

paragraphs: A flock with no leader. Every bird is generalised to the limit — two wings and a body, not one surplus detail — and precisely for that reason the eye sees movement rather than figures.

The composition is built by the laws of a real flock: a dense core, thinned edges, individual birds that have broken ahead. The formation never repeats itself, and a shimmer arises out of that — the gaze reads flight where nothing moves.
The intent is concision: the less that is said about a bird, the more is left to the viewer. This is a composition as hint, not as illustration.

By day the flock reads as graphic work on the ceiling — generalised silhouettes, not one detail. In the evening the light reveals it in layers: the near birds flare, the far ones stay shadow, and the flight acquires a depth it does not have by day.
LC0349.whereItWorks: The horizontal format is ideal above a long dining table, in a lobby, in a meeting room, over a reception desk — anywhere that needs span without mass.
LC0349.style: Contemporary minimalism and Scandinavian restraint: white walls, pale wood, panoramic glazing. The message is freedom — the flock reads as open sea beyond the window, even when the window gives onto a city.
LC0349.madeToOrder: The number of birds, the span of the arc and the balance of white to clear are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition with a plot — the rare case of an object that does not decorate a space but tells a story.

The birds are held in different phases of movement: one is diving, another hovers, a third is only approaching. The flowers wait. Between them is that instant before contact for which the whole thing was assembled.

The dusty lilac was not chosen for prettiness. The muted colour pushes the blossom into the background and brings the birds forward; in the evening the roles reverse — the flowers light up from within and become the stage while the birds go to silhouette. One object, two performances.

By day it is fine botanical graphic work: dusty lilac blossom and gold birds read as silhouettes. In the evening the stage turns over — the flowers fill with light from inside, the birds go into shadow, and the object becomes a theatre with the stage lit.
LC0350.whereItWorks: The vertical format was made for stairwells and double-height living rooms: the stage has to be seen whole, top to bottom. Also good in a bay window, a winter garden, a generous bedroom.
LC0350.style: Contemporary classic and neoclassicism — pale walls, mouldings, soft furniture in pastel tones. The message is romantic: a piece for someone who wants a plot in the house, not simply a source of light.
LC0350.madeToOrder: The height of the cascade, the number of flowers and hummingbirds and the tone of the blossom are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same story in white. The absence of colour shifts the accent onto plasticity: you can see how each flower is coiled along a spiral, how the edge turns, how light flows out of the depth of the bowl. Nothing distracts from form.
Dark birds against a white ground read graphically, like silhouettes on paper: they give the composition rhythm and keep it from turning sugary. That one contrast carries the whole piece.

By day the object looks refined, expensive, faintly museum-like — white gloss and dark metal, nothing surplus. In the evening the flowers fill with warm light and the birds begin to reflect that glow, and the scene comes alive: the white stops being cold.
LC0351.whereItWorks: The most universal of the three versions — light interiors, bedrooms, living rooms in a neutral palette, stairwells. White works in any register, so the composition does not dictate a colour to the interior.
LC0351.style: Art Nouveau and contemporary classic: white with a graphic accent. The message is restrained and expensive — a piece for an interior that chooses quiet.
LC0351.madeToOrder: The height of the cascade, the number of flowers and birds and the finish of the birds are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same scene in a green register. Flowers of two kinds — clear olive-green and milky white — open as wide bowls; between them hover chrome hummingbirds with white breasts.

The green bowls work as stained glass: light passes through and tints the air beneath the composition a grass tone, while the white ones stay neutral and balance the colour. The chrome birds reflect everything around them and seem almost liquid — the only elements with no appearance of their own.

By day the object reads as a botanical study in the transparent: green on chrome, a fresh and light piece. In the evening the light burns deep in each bowl, the air beneath the composition turns green, and the garden turns out to be lit from within with the birds held still inside it.
LC0352.whereItWorks: Vertical and compact in footprint — a stairwell, a bay window, a narrow double-height space. Coloured light noticeably changes the tone of a room: neutral surfaces are needed nearby.
LC0352.style: Art Nouveau and botanical modern: a transparent garden. The message is fresh and natural — a piece for an interior that loves greenery.
LC0352.madeToOrder: The number of flowers and birds and the balance of green to white are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition with a plot of its own. The birds here are not decoration but participants in a scene: one dives, another hovers, a third is only approaching, and the beaks are turned toward the flowers. The wisteria cascade descends as a vertical cluster, the hummingbirds hang around it on separate cables — the composition tells a story rather than decorating a ceiling.
Every corolla carries a warm point of light, the branches are golden, the flowers a cold blue-grey.

By day the combination of dusty blue and matte gold looks noble and restrained: the piece reads through colour and silhouette. In the evening the flowers light up from within and the hummingbirds begin to throw highlights — the scene comes alive and the birds seem genuinely to move.
LC0353.whereItWorks: A vertical format — stairwells and double-height living rooms where the scene is visible entire. The composition tells its story only in full view: cropped in height, it loses its point.
LC0353.style: Art Nouveau and the Japanese school: wisteria with a bird is a classic subject of the woodblock print. The message is narrative — a piece for someone who values a story and not only a form.
LC0353.madeToOrder: The height of the cascade, the number of flowers and birds and the depth of the blue-grey tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a dandelion. Hundreds of tubular elements radiate in every direction from a central sphere, and at the end of each is a gold ball, like a seed on a parachute. The form is spherical but not rigid: the tubes vary slightly in length, so the silhouette is a little downy, alive.
The glow is split into two parts: a soft milky light along the whole length of the tubes and gold points of highlight on top of it. Neither gets in the way of the other.

By day it is a white sculpture with gold accents — clean, almost souvenir-clear in its image. In the evening the sphere becomes a source of even diffused light that throws no shadows and fills the room entirely, while the gold balls hold the eye.
LC0354.whereItWorks: The compact format makes the piece universal — above a dining table, in a bedroom, in a child's room, in a meeting room. Shadowless light is convenient where people work and eat.
LC0354.style: Scandinavian minimalism and mid-century: the sphere as the purest of forms. The message is light and friendly — a piece for an interior with no pretension.
LC0354.madeToOrder: The diameter of the sphere, the number of tubes and the finish of the details are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same scaling gathered into a cascade. The cones are threaded in tiers on rings of differing diameter: the upper rows are wide, the lower ones narrow, and the composition ends in a sharp wedge. The form of a mountain rather than a cloud.
The density of the tiers gives the principal effect: the far elements show through the near ones, and the depth seems endless.

By day it is a mountain of honey with a rich geometric texture — a heavy piece read through silhouette and relief. In the evening each cone is lit at its base and the light runs down to the point; the multi-layered glow overlays itself. A glowing hive with a pulsing core.
LC0355.whereItWorks: The composition is formal and substantial in image — an entrance hall, a dining room with a high ceiling, a stairwell. The wedge below sets the lowest point: clearance is needed under it.
LC0355.style: Art Deco and Eastern opulence: tiering as a symbol of wealth. The message is representative — a piece for a space that receives a guest.
LC0355.madeToOrder: The number of tiers, the diameter of the upper ring and the depth of the honey tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about scales. Cones are threaded in rows so that each is turned point outward and its neighbour points back: the result is dense scaling, like the skin of a pine cone or a coat of mail. The device is protective in origin — the author makes it decorative.
A smoky tea-brown tone mutes the light to amber. The floor lamp deliberately does not light the room — it tints it.

By day it is a dense dark column with a rich texture, almost an architectural detail: a piece read through relief and the shadow between the scales. In the evening the light pushes out between the cones — each tip catches fire, and the whole vertical is covered with a net of warm sparks. A column with a fire inside it.
LC0356.whereItWorks: Corners, wall piers, the zone beside a staircase. In a pair the floor lamps work as a portal — flanking an entrance, a fireplace, a sofa. The muted light means a separate source is needed for reading.
LC0356.style: Dark luxe and Art Deco: texture and muted amber instead of shine. The message is intimate and evening-bound — a piece for an interior in a dark palette.
LC0356.madeToOrder: The height, the diameter of the column, the depth of the smoky tone and the finish of the frame are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same water lily taken out of the composition. A single disc with a fractured texture on a short curved bracket that comes out of the wall and holds the leaf at an angle, like a real stem. The piece is reduced to a minimum — and the texture reads more clearly for it than it does in the cluster.
Close up the essential thing is visible: the cleavage is deep, the facets number in the dozens, and no two lie in the same plane.

By day the wall light works as a wall sculpture: a relief catching daylight from the window, a quiet piece. In the evening light from the core goes into the mass and comes out around the whole perimeter, tracing the disc with a glowing contour — a soft background source that neither dazzles nor throws hard shadows.
LC0357.whereItWorks: Solo beside a mirror, in a pair flanking a bedhead, in a series along a corridor — in a row the tilts of the discs can be alternated. The absence of hard shadows suits bedrooms and zones beside a mirror.
LC0357.style: Art Nouveau and natural modern: one leaf instead of a composition. The message is intimate — a piece for a wall that does not need an accent.
LC0357.madeToOrder: The diameter of the disc, the length of the bracket and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about frozen water. The surface of the discs looks fractured — not decorative hatching but a deep cleavage yielding dozens of facets. The author takes a state rather than a form: a leaf covered in hoarfrost, and ice cracked and seen against the light.
The branch reaches out horizontally, the discs tilted at different angles — like lily pads on the surface of a pond. No fracture repeats another.

By day it is a collection of ice sections on a curved golden branch — a piece read through texture, every facet catching light its own way. In the evening light enters the disc from the central core and runs out across the texture: each facet lights up as a separate spark and the leaf glows like frozen water against the light. From a distance, a chain of radiant circles.
LC0358.whereItWorks: Long tables, bar counters, reception desks — wherever rhythmic light is needed along an axis. The tilts of the discs set a direction: the composition is oriented to the movement of the gaze.
LC0358.style: Art Nouveau and natural modern: the water lily as a classic motif, ice as a device. The message is cool and clean — a piece for an interior in a cold palette.
LC0358.madeToOrder: The length of the branch, the number of discs and their tilt are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about vanishing. A thick form rolled into a shell with a wavy edge — an orchid petal, a rolled leaf, a sea shell. Entirely clear, without colour, with powerful optical distortions inside: a piece that exists by virtue of what it does to light rather than by its own appearance.
The sphere is dense at the centre and sparse at the edges, so it has no defined boundary — a cloud rather than a sphere.

By day the object all but dissolves, leaving only contours and flares along the edges: in a light room it is easy to overlook. In the evening light from the depth reflects off the inner surfaces of the petals, breaks up and comes out as soft highlights — the source cannot be located by eye. A glowing sphere with no edge.
LC0359.whereItWorks: Light interiors with high ceilings — living rooms, lobbies, dining rooms, bedrooms. The composition adds volume without adding weight: it suits places that must not be made heavier.
LC0359.style: Contemporary classic and minimalism: transparency as the principal quality. The message is lightness — a piece for an interior that does not want a dominant.
LC0359.madeToOrder: The diameter of the sphere, the number of petals and the density of the cloud are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about rain through foliage. Two tiers work toward one image: above, a dense ring of leaves with the sources hidden between them; below, dozens of faceted clear drops. Light from the canopy passes through them and ignites them from within — the effect of rain lit by a setting sun through branches.
The contrast is set firmly: warm matte foliage above, cold transparency below. Neither repeats the other; they complement each other in temperature.

By day it is a wreath with a clear fringe — gold and transparency, a piece read as silhouette. In the evening it becomes a glowing cloud with water pouring out of it; the drops sway with the movement of air and the highlights run about constantly.
LC0360.whereItWorks: A round form — above a dining table, in an entrance hall, in the centre of a living room. The fringe sets the lower boundary: the composition hangs higher than its diameter would suggest.
LC0360.style: Art Nouveau and formal classicism: a wreath with pendants in a contemporary reading. The message is ceremonial and warm — a piece for the table people gather at.
LC0360.madeToOrder: The diameter of the wreath, the number of drops and the depth of the rain are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a cluster. The branches hang down in a dense cone, narrowing toward the bottom and ending in a few solitary sprigs — like a real cluster pulled toward the ground by its own weight. The form is set by weight rather than by drawing.
Every leaf is elongated, slightly curved, with a sharp tip, veining and an uneven edge — taken from a real tree and gilded.

By day the object works as a sculpture in a bronze register: matte patina, deep shadows between the leaves, a heavy and calm piece. In the evening the light comes out of the depth of the canopy in warm rays and lifts the foliage from below — the gold begins to glow from inside, the shadows turn velvet. A burning bush.
LC0361.whereItWorks: Double-height living rooms, stairwells, the zone above a low coffee table in a lounge — wherever the composition is looked at from below. The light goes downward: bright under the cluster, dim around it.
LC0361.style: Art Nouveau and natural opulence: gold foliage as a classic motif of abundance. The message is generous and warm — a piece for an interior that receives.
LC0361.madeToOrder: The height of the cluster, the density of the foliage and the finish of the patina are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about ripple. Thousands of narrow plates of varying length fold into a spiral that twists downward through several floors. Polished mirror, matte and clear are intermixed — three behaviours of light within one mass.

The device is separation: the light lives only in the ends of the clear strips, runs their whole length and breaks out below as a bright point. The mirrored ones do not transmit it at all — they only reflect their neighbours.

By day it is strict graphic work: vertical strokes of varying density, almost a draft drawing read through lines. In the evening the spiral comes alive — light runs from level to level, the composition shimmers like scales or like ripple under a lamp, and seems to be turning slowly.
LC0362.whereItWorks: Very tall spaces — stair shafts, atriums, panoramic lobbies with double or triple height. The spiral is designed for a specific height and a specific route of ascent.
LC0362.style: Contemporary sculptural installation and kinetic art: movement with no mechanism. The message is monumental — a piece that sets the scale of a building.
LC0362.madeToOrder: The height of the spiral, the ratio of mirrored to clear plates and the density are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a bush in bloom. Fine rods spread in every direction, interlacing into a volumetric sphere, and on each tip sits a pointed flower with a gold core. The branching is honest — into three or four shoots, as on a real bush, rather than into equal rays.

Close up it is a botanical study: you can see how the bud attaches to the branch, how the gold of the core is reflected in the whiteness. From a distance it is a glowing sphere woven out of sparks, like sea buckthorn in the sun.

By day the composition is graphic: white on silver, a clean line, no colour at all. In the evening hundreds of point sources turn it into a cloud of fireflies suspended above the table — the form disappears and the swarm remains.
LC0363.whereItWorks: A spherical form has no front — the object is equally good in the centre of a room, above a round table, in an opening between floors. Point sources give sparkling rather than diffused light.
LC0363.style: Art Nouveau and natural modern: the branch as a classic motif. The message is alive and festive — a piece for an interior that loves detail.
LC0363.madeToOrder: The diameter of the sphere, the number of branches and buds and the finish of the rods are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a stroke of the pen. The ribbons are coiled into rings and loops — as though someone had written in the air in one continuous movement and left the trace. The form is not assembled, it is drawn.

The device is that the ribbon has two layers: a polished mirror surface outside, a ribbed glowing band within. The light is visible only from the inside of a coil, and the composition changes constantly as you walk around it — from one point you see the blind backs of the rings, from another their open glowing interiors.

By day it is metallic graphic work in the air: mirrored coils living off reflections, a dense dark piece. In the evening it acquires a second face — a fiery one: the warm bronze version reads as a melt, the cold silver one as a ribbon of magnesium burning in the dark. An object with two characters at once.
LC0364.whereItWorks: A strictly vertical format several metres tall — stair flights, atriums, narrow tall entrance halls where the composition is visible from several levels at once. The change of faces reads only when the viewer moves.
LC0364.style: Contemporary sculpture and brutal opulence: one gesture instead of a composition. The message is artistic — an object-piece for a space that wants a statement.
LC0364.madeToOrder: The height, the number of coils, the finish and the temperature of the glow are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about what has not yet opened. The bud is coiled into a spiral: a sharp point at the top, a soft shell below, the edge running inward on a smooth twist — an unopened tulip or a rolled calla leaf. The author takes the form at the moment before flowering, when everything is ready and nothing has been shown.

The field is dense with a sagging centre, so the composition reads equally well from below and from the side — from an upper floor or from the stairs. Volume is built not by the number of sources but by cross-reflections: every element is mirrored in the gloss of its neighbours.

By day it is a white cloud with cold highlights — pure plasticity, a quiet and graphic piece. In the evening the buds fill with warmth and the fine spires above them disappear, and the flowers seem to hang in the air by themselves.

There is a mirrored version of the same element: a smoky silver surface with gold spires. The same silhouette turns from a tender cloud into a graphite storm cloud with gold sparks — an entirely different temperament.
LC0365.whereItWorks: Double-height living rooms, lobbies, stairwells, banqueting halls. The sagging centre sets the lower boundary — clearance is needed beneath the composition.
LC0365.style: Art Nouveau and contemporary classic: a botanical motif without ornament. The message is tender in the white version and dramatic in the smoky one — one piece for two different interiors.
LC0365.madeToOrder: The number of buds, the depth of the field and the finish of the buds and spires are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about smoke caught and frozen. Inside every tube the finest fibrous texture is visible — arrested streams, like a feather in the body of ice. The texture is the protagonist here: it exists inside, it cannot be touched, only seen.
The field is gathered into a wave with a sagging centre — a stand of reeds in the wind. Every tube is caught by a gold collar.

By day, switched off, the composition remains a collection of clear rods with a silver drawing inside — a piece to be examined close up. In the evening light enters through the collar and runs down the fibres all the way to the end: the streams flare and turn into glowing threads. Smoke that has caught fire.
LC0366.whereItWorks: In the compact version, four or five tubes above a table; at scale, hundreds of rods covering the whole ceiling of a stairwell. The texture is visible close up, so the composition is not hung higher than it needs to be.
LC0366.style: Natural minimalism and Japanese aesthetics: a drawing inside the substance instead of decor on the outside. The message is contemplative — a piece you look into.
LC0366.madeToOrder: The number of tubes, their lengths, the shape of the field and the finish of the collars are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same shoal in a matte execution. Here the light does not pass right through as it does in the clear version — it comes out from under the wing as a soft halo, and every figure seems lit from below, like a fish above a sandy bottom. One substitution changes the whole character of the scene.
The shoal moves in a wave, rising and falling on cables of differing length, drawn out in a long arc.

By day white against a dark background reads with maximum clarity: the silhouette works as graphic art, without one highlight. In the evening the figures fill with a soft glow and gold points at the fixings — the calmest of the brand's shoals: no glare, no colour, only form and light.
LC0367.whereItWorks: Bedrooms, spas, light living rooms, spaces beside water. The absence of glare makes the composition comfortable where people rest and where calm matters.
LC0367.style: Marine Art Nouveau and Scandinavian minimalism: movement without shine. The message is quiet — a piece for an interior that does not raise its voice.
LC0367.madeToOrder: The number of figures, the length of the arc and the drop heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same image without light. Three white figures on fine rods on a shared base: one ahead, two following, all in different phases of movement. The author removes the electricity and leaves the plasticity alone — a test of the form's strength.
The smooth curve of a wing, a drawn-out tail, an edge lifted slightly — the moment of a turn in the body of water, caught in three positions at once.

By day the glossy surface gathers the light of the room and lights itself: the sculpture looks luminous with not a single lamp. In the evening, under directed light, it is chiaroscuro that works — a highlight along the edge of a wing, a deep shadow beneath it — and the figures acquire a volume invisible by day.
LC0368.whereItWorks: A console in an entrance hall, a long chest of drawers, a meeting room — wherever an accent is needed without colour and without electricity. No wiring is required: it can be placed anywhere.
LC0368.style: Contemporary sculpture and minimalism: white, form, nothing more. The message is restrained — a piece for an interior for which one detail is enough.
LC0368.madeToOrder: The size, the number of figures and the finish of the base are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a shoal going round an obstacle. The shoal moves diagonally, deeper and lower — not as a formation and not as a cloud but as a trajectory: the way large sea creatures pass an obstruction without breaking the group.
Every ray is cast whole: a thick body with a lens inside and a wing edge so fine it is almost a thread. The difference in thickness is the principal device — a dense body against a vanishing edge.

By day the object all but dissolves: only highlights and contours are visible, the shoal guessed at rather than read. In the evening light from the fixing points floods the wing from within — a wave of light runs along the clear body, the tip of the tail flares as a point — and the shoal appears entire, "swimming" slowly as the viewer moves.
LC0369.whereItWorks: Long spaces — above a table, along a staircase, in a gallery. The diagonal is designed for a specific volume and a specific point of entry.
LC0369.style: Marine Art Nouveau and contemporary installation: movement as subject. The message is narrative — a piece that creates a scene.
LC0369.madeToOrder: The number of figures, the trajectory of the shoal and the spread are all made to order.

paragraphs: A development of the ring theme at a formal scale. The rings are larger and thicker, with a scattering of bubbles inside: the mass looks aerated, alive, as though the movement in it had not yet finished.

They are held by broad bands of polished gold that curve around the rings the way a setting holds a stone. The device is a jeweller's, and it sets the whole logic of the piece: the transparent here is the gem, the metal only the setting.

By day it is a jeweller's work: gold, transparency, precision of joints — an object to be examined close up. In the evening light travels from the gold clasps into the ring, the bubbles flare, and each ring becomes a glowing hoop with a sparkling core. The separate elements become indistinguishable — what remains is a dense radiant cloud.
LC0370.whereItWorks: The scale allows large spaces to be covered — lobbies, atriums, restaurant halls. The sagging centre demands height: the composition is built downward.
LC0370.style: Art Deco and jewelled Art Nouveau: the setting as a device rather than as a fixing. The message is formal and expensive — a piece for a representative space.
LC0370.madeToOrder: The number of rings, the dimensions of the cloud and the finish of the settings are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a stone with a hole in it. The rings are thick, irregular, slightly skewed — as though turned by water rather than cast. There is not one true circle: the form belongs to the elements, not to a pair of compasses.

The rings are linked by gold pins with glowing ends and assembled into a dense field several layers deep. The mass is optically complex: through it you see the neighbouring rings, distorted as though through a lens.

By day it is a field of transparent sections — a piece read through distortions and overlays, the depth visible right through. In the evening light enters through the pins and spreads through the whole volume, and every ring glows along its inner contour. What remains is a net of glowing ovals hanging inside one another.
LC0371.whereItWorks: Equally good in two formats — a compact circle above a table or an elongated band along a counter. It reads both close up and from a distance, so it suits intimate rooms and large halls alike.
LC0371.style: Natural minimalism and contemporary sculpture: the water-worn stone as a form. The message is calm and tactile — a piece for an interior that values substance.
LC0371.madeToOrder: The number of rings, the shape of the field and the density of the linking are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same spiral stood upright. The ribbon twists around an invisible axis from the floor to the top; the base is a simple ring out of which the vortex literally grows. The support is reduced to a minimum so that nothing holds the movement back.
The structure reads as DNA or as the trace left by a spinning torch: the movement here is completely obvious although the object does not move.

By day the floor lamp works through silhouette and reflections — a clean line twisted in the air. In the evening the light is distributed evenly over the whole height: it lights the space softly, creating neither glare nor dark zones. The black version with cold light looks technological, almost museum-like; the gold one with warm light like a formal column.
LC0372.whereItWorks: The corners of a living room, the zone beside a staircase, wall piers, reception rooms. Even light over the full height makes the floor lamp a genuine source rather than only an accent.
LC0372.style: Contemporary sculpture and parametric design: the spiral as pure mathematics. The message is intellectual — a piece for an interior with contemporary taste.
LC0372.madeToOrder: The height, the number of coils and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a vortex laid on its side. Flat polished ribbons are twisted into spirals and threaded on a straight axis — movement fixed in the horizontal, where it does not usually occur.

Inside the coils sit faceted inserts lit along their whole length. The insert works as a prism: light travels inside it and breaks into sparks facet by facet, while the ribbon by contrast reflects the neighbouring coils — an endless multiplication of highlights arises inside the composition.

By day it is a metal spiral read through reflections: the drawing changes with every step the viewer takes. In the evening, from a distance, the composition reads as an unbroken ribbon of light twisted like a corkscrew. Gold gives a formal warm reading; black graphite with chrome a hard technical one.
LC0373.whereItWorks: The linear format sits above a long table, a bar counter, a reception desk — wherever light is needed as a band rather than a pool. Even distribution along the length gives uniform light across the whole zone.
LC0373.style: Art Deco in gold and industrial modernism in graphite — one form for two different interiors. The message is dynamic — a piece for a space that moves.
LC0373.madeToOrder: The length, the number of coils and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a candle with no flame. Every clear petal is coiled along a spiral — a form somewhere between a calla leaf, a sail and a tongue of fire; below, a sharp point with a gold tip, above, a fine tube with a point of light. One form reads three ways, and the author does not choose between them.
The cascade is triangular: long elements at the centre, short ones at the edges, the lower edge converging into a sharp wedge.

By day the cascade reads as a cloud of transparent highlights — an almost invisible mass living off reflections. In the evening light enters from above and travels the whole length: a vertical glowing vein flares inside every petal while the form itself stays invisible. A swarm of candles suspended in the air; as you walk around, the elements overlap and the drawing changes constantly.
LC0374.whereItWorks: Stairwells, double-height living rooms, the zone above a round table. The wedge below sets the lowest point — clearance in height is needed under the composition.
LC0374.style: Contemporary classic and minimalism: light as the only material. The message is ceremonial and quiet — a piece for a formal space without shine.
LC0374.madeToOrder: The number of petals, the height of the cascade and the depth of the wedge are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a cob. The leaves sit in layers, overlapping, by the dozen — a dense vertical where every row covers the one before. The form reads as a cob, as a cone and as a cypress: everything that grows upward inside a tight wrapping.
The leaves work against the light: being thin, they do not block it, they diffuse it.

By day it is a sculptural column with rich plasticity — white on gold, a dense and calm piece. In the evening the glow pushes out of the depth of the column, tracing every leaf along its edge: the whole vertical shines with an even milky radiance without one dazzling spot, while the gold between the leaves gives warm vertical sparks. A glowing trunk around which a space gathers itself.
LC0375.whereItWorks: In a pair flanking an entrance or a sofa, in a row along a long wall. Soft light without glare suits rest areas and reception rooms where people stay for a while.
LC0375.style: Organic Art Nouveau and contemporary classic: a natural form carried through to an architectural one. The message is calm and representative — a piece that is a column rather than an accent.
LC0375.madeToOrder: The height, the density of the foliage and the finish of the rods are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a bouquet in a narrow vase. From a massive cylindrical base rises a bundle of fine tubes, each finishing in a trumpet with a wavy rim. The flowers look in different directions and are raised to different heights — the way callas stand, not the way an artificial arrangement does.

It is a rare case of an art object delivering full functional lighting: light comes out of the depth of the trumpets in soft cones — up, sideways, onto the wall — and the direction of each flower is chosen at assembly.

By day the floor lamp reads as a silhouette: white gloss or mirrored trumpets on fine stems, the polished base reflecting the floor and making the piece visually lighter. In the evening the flowers throw light around the room in exactly the directions the client set — a bouquet that illuminates.
LC0376.whereItWorks: Beside an armchair, in a bedroom, in an entrance hall — anywhere that needs light and silhouette at once. The aimed cones let you light reading, a wall or a picture.
LC0376.style: Art Nouveau and mid-century: a botanical motif with technical precision. The message is practical and elegant — a piece for those who want both beauty and function.
LC0376.madeToOrder: The height, the number of flowers and the finish of the stems and trumpets are all made to order.

paragraphs: A development of the theme: the ribbons are twisted upward and fly apart more freely, like tongues of a bonfire caught by the draught. Between them sit short glowing inserts, so the fire seems to burn inside the structure itself rather than to light it from outside.
The surface is deliberately uneven, slightly coarse: clear to the point of invisibility in one place, clouded and filled with warmth in another. There are no identical stretches.

By day it is a transparent sculpture on a stem — a piece to be examined close up, built entirely on texture. In the evening the upper part literally catches fire while the lower stays a dark strict vertical: a bonfire on a stand. The gold finish reinforces the association with fire; chrome takes it into another register — shards of ice thrown upward.
LC0377.whereItWorks: Beside an armchair, in a winter garden, in a lounge — wherever the object is seen close up and the texture will be appreciated. The light is gathered at the top: the floor lamp gives an accent rather than general lighting.
LC0377.style: Organic Art Nouveau and contemporary art: irregularity as a virtue. The message is tactile — a piece you want to study.
LC0377.madeToOrder: The height, the number and spread of the elements and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about order breaking. Below, strict graphic work: the even verticals of a bundle, a clean line, nothing surplus. Above, the form explodes — clear "tongues" with ragged, seemingly fractured edges twist upward and fly apart, like flame or spray in a freeze frame.
The contrast of order and chaos is the model's principal device, and it reads instantly: one piece showing two states at once.

By day the floor lamp works as silhouette: a strict base, a dishevelled top, transparent fractures catching daylight. In the evening light travels from the ends of the tubes straight into the tongues and ignites every fracture — the gold version reads as a warm torch, the chrome one as a fountain of icy water. In both finishes the tongues themselves stay clear: the temperature is set by the rods.
LC0378.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, the zone beside a staircase, meeting rooms — wherever a strong vertical accent is needed that takes up no floor area. The spread of the upper part requires clearance to the sides.
LC0378.style: Contemporary sculpture and brutal opulence: destruction as a form. The message is bold — a piece for an interior with character.
LC0378.madeToOrder: The height, the number of tubes and clear elements and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same language, assembled more densely. The leaves are threaded one above another along a spiral and form a single twisted trunk; the tubes rise in a bundle around it, some above the foliage, some lost in its depth. Instead of a grove, one plant.
The thick form produces powerful optics: each leaf holds an inverted reflection of the neighbouring elements, and sharp highlights flare on the cut edges.

By day it is a transparent trunk read through highlights and distortions — a piece with no weight. In the evening light from the bases of the tubes rises and lights the trunk from within: a plant that glows from the root. Chrome gives an icy, almost aqueous reading; the gold finish turns the same form into a warm amber column — the leaves do not change, the temperature of the whole piece does.
LC0379.whereItWorks: The corner of a living room, the zone beside a window, a pier between cabinets — wherever a vertical without mass is needed. Transparency requires a dark or saturated background: against a white wall the floor lamp loses its silhouette.
LC0379.style: Organic Art Nouveau and minimalism: the spiral as the single device. The message is lightness — a piece for a tight space that must not be made heavier.
LC0379.madeToOrder: The height, the density of the spiral and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a grove. Fine tubes of differing height rise from the floor — a stand of bamboo or a rank of organ pipes; between them, threaded on rods, hover large leaves twisted helically, with a wavy edge and a deep lens inside.
The thickness here behaves like water: the reflections of the neighbouring tubes gather in the leaf, and the object never looks the same from two positions.

By day the floor lamp reads as a transparent sculpture — all but invisible, only highlights and contours. In the evening the light enters at the end of the rod, travels its whole length and flares at the bends: the leaves fill with warmth and a soft radiance spreads around the base. The transparent becomes more noticeable at night than by day.
Two finishes change the character of the piece completely. Chrome — cold, technical, for glass and concrete. Gold — warm, enveloping, for wood, leather and muted tones.
LC0380.whereItWorks: Solo beside an armchair, in a pair flanking a sofa or a portal. In a pair of differing heights the floor lamps read as a small grove — a device for generous living rooms and entrance halls.
LC0380.style: Natural Art Nouveau and contemporary classic: a plant taken apart into verticals. The message is calm — a piece for an interior that loves form without colour.
LC0380.madeToOrder: The height, the number of tubes and leaves and the finish of the rods are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about armour. The leaves hang in dense tiers, overlapping like plumage or like plates of armour, and the cone narrows downward: the form reads now as a folded wing, now as a fir cone, now as a suit of armour. The ambiguity works toward the image of protection — everything listed covers something of value.
Graphite-grey and matte outside, polished gold within. The most dramatic contrast in the brand's catalogue.

By day it is a dark sculptural mass — a blind, heavy piece that absorbs light. In the evening the light hidden under the feathers reflects off the gold reverse and only a warm radiance from the depth escapes: a dark exterior, a glowing interior. Armour with a fire under it.
LC0381.whereItWorks: Interiors with character — dark walls, wood, warm metal, subdued light. Against a pale ground the contrast stops working: the composition needs a dark context.
LC0381.style: Dark luxe and brutal modernism: graphite with gold. The message is masculine and strong — a piece for an interior that does not flirt.
LC0381.madeToOrder: The number of feathers, the depth of the cone and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about geometry arguing with ornament. The same baroque pendant is set in dialogue with flat rectangles of polished gold: strict facets against shaped transparent contours. The character of the piece is born of that argument — classical and sharply contemporary at once.
Clear and mirrored alternate through the cascade, overlapping one another; the form narrows downward into a wedge.

By day it is a play of two surfaces: the gold reflects the room, the clear pendants let it pass through, and the composition reads as an overlay. In the evening light from the gold candles reflects in the plates and passes through the faceting — the piece plays on shine and transparency at once, choosing neither.
LC0382.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, staircases, reception rooms, banqueting halls. The formal wedge form requires height and a frontal view.
LC0382.style: Postmodernism in the best sense: a classical quotation next to pure geometry. The message is bold — a piece for an interior that knows how to join eras.
LC0382.madeToOrder: The ratio of clear to gold and the size of the cascade are made to order.

paragraphs: A composition as quotation. The silhouette of an old chandelier pendant is enlarged and cleared of everything surplus: the shaped, almost lacework contour remains and everything that made it tinsel is removed. The form is recognisable, the execution minimal.

The faceting runs only along the edge and catches light, scattering it as rainbow sparks; the smooth centre stays clear and the neighbouring pendants are visible through it. The cascade is assembled in tiers and converges into a sharp wedge.

By day it is clear lacework graphic with gold candles between the elements — a piece read through contours and overlays. In the evening the faceted edges flare into rainbow while the smooth centres stay dark: the cascade glows around its edges and remains transparent within.
LC0383.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, dining rooms, stairwells, reception rooms. The wedge below sets the lowest point — clearance is needed under the composition.
LC0383.style: Contemporary classic: baroque retold in the language of minimalism. The message is representative — a piece for an interior that respects tradition without copying it.
LC0383.madeToOrder: The number of pendants, the depth of the cascade and the finish of the candles are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about flight. Every plate is bent its own way — origami that has almost sprung open: the form is caught at the moment when the fold no longer holds. Individual figures have broken away from the main stream, and it is exactly those that make the flock alive.
The vortex is vertical: a dense core at the centre, sparse birds at the edges. Three finishes give three temperatures — cold transparency, matte whiteness and warm gold.

By day it is a flock read through folds and overlays: clear, white and gold intermixed. In the evening points of light are dissolved through the flock and lift the folds from within — the form appears through the ribs of the creases, and the flight becomes obvious.
LC0384.whereItWorks: Stairwells and double-height spaces where flight can be shown at full height. The vortex is designed for a specific height.
LC0384.style: Japanese minimalism and contemporary sculpture: the fold as form, flight as subject. The message is poetic — a piece that tells a story.
LC0384.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the balance of the finishes and the height of the vortex are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a section. A dense concentric cutting — the section of a shell or a fingerprint enlarged to the size of a platter. A drawing that in nature is unique to every specimen is repeated here by the dozen, and that is the paradox of the piece.
The discs hang in tilted tiers, overlapping like scales. As you walk around, the grooves play a moiré — the drawing seems to rotate.

By day it is clear sections on gold spokes: pure texture, no colour, a piece for those who value optics over decor. In the evening light enters along the spoke and spreads through the grooves, turning every disc into a glowing spiral. The composition starts to rotate before your eyes.
LC0385.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms. The moiré reads in movement: the composition is placed where people walk past.
LC0385.style: Optical art and contemporary minimalism: a pattern without ornament. The message is intellectual — a piece for an interior that loves precision.
LC0385.madeToOrder: The number of discs, the tiering and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the sun in a drop. Light reflects off the inner surface of every hemisphere and gathers into one bright point — the same optical focus a dew drop gives in the sun. The author builds the whole piece on it.
The shell is so thin that it reads only through highlights and contours: the composition is astonishingly light, almost absent.

By day, close up, it is a collection of lenses each holding its own reflection of the interior — a piece to be studied; from a distance it is all but invisible, only an iridescent cast along the edges. In the evening a point of its own flares in each hemisphere, and the cloud begins to shimmer with hundreds of small suns.
LC0386.whereItWorks: Light spaces — white walls, panoramic windows, minimalist living rooms and lobbies. Against a pale ground the composition argues with nothing, because it has almost no colour of its own.
LC0386.style: Contemporary minimalism and optical art: transparency as a device. The message is lightness — a piece for an interior that does not want to add weight.
LC0386.madeToOrder: The number of hemispheres, their calibres and the density of the cloud are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about rings on water. The concentric waves on every disc are arrested in the mass — a drawing that lives for a second on water and is held here for good.

The composition is minimal to the limit: only discs, only cables, only light. All the dynamics come from the tilts and the differences in height — the cloud seems suspended in the middle of a slow movement.

By day it is smoky amber circles at differing heights — a piece read through form and inner drawing, without one surplus element. In the evening light burns at the centre of every disc and the waves run out from it as glowing rings: the warm amber and the soft glow make the composition comfortable despite the strictness of the form.
LC0387.whereItWorks: Above a table, in a meeting room, in a lounge. The flat discs steal no height — the composition suits medium ceilings too.
LC0387.style: Scandinavian minimalism and mid-century: the circle as the only form. The message is calm — a piece for an interior that does not want volume.
LC0387.madeToOrder: The number of discs, their diameters and the depth of the cloud are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about April. The flowers vary in size — fully open, half-opened, tight buds — as on a real magnolia branch, which flowers before the leaves and does it unevenly.
The composition is dense and generous without being heavy: white dominates, gold only holds the structure. The proportion is chosen so that the metal does not argue with the flowering.

By day it is a branch in bloom — broad white petals with a pinkish reverse, a light and formal piece. In the evening light at the heart of every flower makes the petals translucent, like a fine shell against the light: the pink reverse comes through from inside and the white stops being flat.
