LC0388.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, living rooms, lobbies, banqueting halls. The horizontal vine lies along a table or across a volume — the composition adapts to the plan.
LC0388.style: Art Nouveau and romantic classicism: the magnolia as a brand classic in its most formal execution. The message is festive — a piece for a ceremonial interior.
LC0388.madeToOrder: The length of the vine, the number of flowers and the density of the flowering are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about wisteria on a pergola. The flowers are set densely and turned every way, the cascade descending as a dense vertical cluster — the way an overgrown vine hangs when nobody has pruned it.
Saturated violet on gold is the boldest colour pairing in the catalogue. The author softens it with nothing: no white, no clear.

By day it is a deep blue-violet on gold stems — a dense colour read as a mass. In the evening light burns in the throat of every flower and lifts the petals from within: the violet becomes almost luminous and the gold beneath it goes white-hot. A waterfall on fire.
LC0389.whereItWorks: Staircases, double-height spaces, window displays, interiors that are not afraid of colour. The saturated tone tints the air: neutral surfaces are needed nearby.
LC0389.style: Art Nouveau and Eastern opulence: wisteria as a classic subject. The message is bold and regal — a piece for an interior with character.
LC0389.madeToOrder: The height of the cascade, the number of flowers and the depth of the violet tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about autumn. Colour decides everything: burnt ochre, ash, warm bronze — a muted autumnal register, rare in light compositions, where white and gold usually prevail.
The petals go deep in layers, by the hundred, and the flower reads as a volume even from a distance. At the core of each is a matte white sphere, the nucleus around which the whole mass is gathered.

By day it is a branch in terracotta and ash: warm, earthy, read through the volume of the petals. In the evening the white cores light up and the layers of petals around them are lit layer by layer — from a bright centre to a blind edge. Flowers with a burning core.
LC0390.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, libraries, interiors with wood and leather, studies. The earthy register asks for warm finishes around it — against a white wall the composition looks foreign.
LC0390.style: Natural Art Nouveau and autumnal classicism: fading as an aesthetic. The message is warm and adult — a piece for a lived-in interior.
LC0390.madeToOrder: The number of flowers, the palette and the length of the branch are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about opening. Some flowers are fully open, some are only beginning — the cascade shows the process rather than the result. The spiral twists, the flowers look in different directions, and the stream reads as growing upward or descending depending on where you stand.
The pink here is powdery, almost flesh-toned: it makes the composition warm and alive rather than decorative.

By day it is a vertical stream of soft pink on gold stems — a piece read through colour and the plasticity of the turned-back petals. In the evening light inside every flower shows through the fine petals and makes them glow from inside: the cascade fills from within, like skin against the light.
LC0391.whereItWorks: A vertical format — stairwells, double-height living rooms, tall niches, bay windows. The spiral reads as you climb and as you walk around it.
LC0391.style: Art Nouveau and Eastern classicism: the lotus as a symbol of opening. The message is warm and feminine — a piece for an interior that loves softness.
LC0391.madeToOrder: The height of the cascade, the number of flowers and the depth of the pink tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an orchestra before a concert. Trumpets of differing calibre look up, down and sideways — that is how a brass section looks while the players tune up: the directions are random, but everyone is doing one job.
The branches wind into a dense tangle, the green elements are used sparingly — they enliven the white mass and add a botanical note without turning the piece into a plant.

By day it is white with olive on chrome: a matte surface, polished metal, a composition read through the form of the trumpets. In the evening light comes out of the depth of each one as a soft cone — the composition delivers genuine working light rather than only an image, and the different directions wash the room from several sides.
LC0392.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms. The trumpets are aimed at assembly: the composition can light the table, the wall or the ceiling as chosen.
LC0392.style: Art Nouveau and modernism: botany and mechanics in one form. The message is practical and alive — a piece for the image and for the light alike.
LC0392.madeToOrder: The number of trumpets, the share of green and the dimensions of the tangle are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the sky before a storm. The lilac tone fills from within — the colour the air takes on a few minutes before rain. The author takes exactly that state rather than the flower as such.
The branches divide freely, the flowers look down and to the side, the blossoms gather in clusters: this is not a strict composition but a fragment of a living hedge lifted to the ceiling.

By day it is smoky lilac on silver — a restrained, almost monochrome piece read through the ribbing of the petals. In the evening a warm point lights inside every flower, the lilac fills from within, and the composition gives a soft, faintly cool light. Dusk hung from the ceiling.
LC0393.whereItWorks: Bedrooms, boudoirs, lounges, private living rooms. Soft diffused light without glare suits rest areas; the lilac register asks for restrained surroundings.
LC0393.style: Art Nouveau and romantic modern: the living hedge as a motif. The message is intimate and lyrical — a piece for a private space.
LC0393.madeToOrder: The spread of the network, the number of flowers and the saturation of the lilac are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about different phases of flowering. The buds are turned in different directions, some open, some only just parted — a thicket rather than a bouquet: a real plant never flowers in unison.
The matte surface kills highlights and makes the colour deep, almost watercolour; chrome rules a cold graphic between the flowers. Cut petals open up the interior of the bud.

By day it is a dense turquoise-green with occasional whites — a fresh, resort register read through colour. In the evening light comes out of the opened buds as an even warm radiance, and the cold turquoise acquires a warm core: a thicket lit from within.
LC0394.whereItWorks: Light interiors, spas, winter gardens, pools, dining rooms. Coloured light tints the air slightly — neutral surfaces are needed nearby.
LC0394.style: Art Nouveau and Mediterranean classicism: the tulip in a cool register. The message is fresh and resort-bound — a piece for an interior at rest.
LC0394.madeToOrder: The number of buds, the balance of turquoise to white and the length of the vine are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a night sky. Large stars of the first magnitude, a fine gold scattering between them, thinned edges and a dense core — the distribution is taken from a real sky, where the bright is always scarce and the small is plentiful.
The four-pointed elements with sharp, slightly curved rays are each turned their own way: not one repeats the orientation of its neighbour. The swarm is alive.

By day it is a clear scattering with gold sparks — a piece read through contours and highlights, almost without colour. In the evening the light flares at the tips of the rays and dissolves into the mass, and the composition becomes a patch of sky carried up to the ceiling. A minimal and ceremonial register.
LC0395.whereItWorks: Formal spaces — lobbies, atriums, banqueting halls, double-height living rooms. A night sky reads against a dark ground: on a white ceiling the effect is lost.
LC0395.style: Contemporary classic and minimalism: the star as the purest of signs. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a space that has to impress.
LC0395.madeToOrder: The number of elements, their calibres and the area of the sky are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a single movement. A square plate is pressed in at the centre and turned up at the corners — a figure folded with one push, with no pattern and no second step. The simplicity of the device is its strength.
The cloud is very flat in silhouette and deep in layers: the plates hang at different heights, and as you move through the room it constantly reassembles itself.

By day it is a field of folded figures — clear intermixed with smoky amber, read through folds and overlays. In the evening light burns beneath each plate and flows down the folds, and the field shimmers at two temperatures at once, cold and warm. Origami that has caught fire.
LC0396.whereItWorks: Lobbies, meeting rooms, dining rooms, panoramic living rooms. The flat silhouette suits rooms of medium height, where a bulky composition would be heavy.
LC0396.style: Japanese minimalism and contemporary design: the fold instead of the form. The message is light and intellectual — a piece for an interior that likes simple solutions.
LC0396.madeToOrder: The area of the cloud, the number of plates and the balance of clear to amber are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a dragonfly's wing. The finest longitudinal hatching on every leaf is not decor but structure: on a real wing these are the veins that hold the transparent film. The author uses that literally — in the evening the light travels along exactly that hatching.
The branches interlace, the feathers point in different directions, the density grows toward the centre: the composition reads as a thicket rather than a bouquet.

By day, from a distance, it is a pink cloud; up close a collection of separate feathers, each at its own angle, lilac-pink intermixed with smoky and clear. In the evening light from the joints lifts the feathers from below, the hatching flares, and every leaf comes to resemble a dragonfly's wing.
LC0397.whereItWorks: Living rooms, boudoirs, bedrooms, reception areas, boutiques. The dusty pink register is rare in light objects and needs neutral surroundings so as not to argue with the finishes.
LC0397.style: Art Nouveau and romantic modern: the insect and the plant as classic motifs. The message is feminine and expensive at once — a piece for an interior with fine taste.
LC0397.madeToOrder: The length of the vine, the palette and the density of the thicket are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a city seen from above. The mass reads as blocks of differing height, narrow alleys between them, a light in every window. The lower edge is not levelled — it steps downward like the terrain the city was built on.
Inside every block lives a flowing texture, and above it rises a fine candle of light: the light enters from the top and passes right through the block.

By day it is an architectural model under the ceiling: pink-cognac blocks read through volume and inner drawing. In the evening the facets light up amber and the mass turns into a city seen at night from a plane. A second execution is clear instead of smoky: the same architecture, but cold, glacial, almost technical.
LC0398.whereItWorks: Lobbies, meeting rooms, long dining rooms, reception desks. The stepped underside gives different heights above a zone — the composition is designed for a specific plan.
LC0398.style: Urban modernism and brutal opulence: the city as an ornament. The message is contemporary — a piece for an interior with an urban agenda.
LC0398.madeToOrder: The number of blocks, the depth of tone and the dimensions of the mass are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a bonfire drawn out along the ceiling. Every element is twisted helically: a white gloss face on one side, polished gold on the other. The light hides in the bend itself, and either the white flank or the gold reverse lights up — depending on where you look from.
The field is horizontal, dense, with a sagging centre. The alternation of white and gold creates a shimmer even in a motionless composition.

By day it is graphic work: white and gold bands read through the light and shade of the bends, a dense and dressy piece. In the evening the composition begins to seem alive, crackling — the light runs about the flanks, and no two viewpoints give the same drawing. A bonfire drawn out above the table.
LC0399.whereItWorks: A long table, a bar counter, a lobby — anywhere that needs a warm horizontal accent. The light goes down and to the side: the composition lights the table and the faces.
LC0399.style: Contemporary Art Deco and Hollywood glamour: white with gold, no geometry. The message is hospitable — a piece for a table people sit at for a long time.
LC0399.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the balance of white to gold and the length of the field are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the last drops. The cascade is gathered into a heart: a dense core at the centre, sparse elements at the edges and solitary spindles hanging lower than the rest — like the last drops of a retreating rain. It is exactly those strays that make the form alive.

Faceted lozenges with sharp noses repeat the finials of old balusters; between them rise fine gold candles. The classic formula of a formal chandelier is translated into a contemporary language: no tinsel, only facets, light and a precise line.

By day it is a crystalline mass — dense from one position, an airy scattering from another; a piece read through faceting and highlights. In the evening every spindle catches the light of the candle beside it and flares from within with a cold brilliance — the cascade acquires a depth invisible by day.
LC0400.whereItWorks: Formal spaces — entrance halls, dining rooms, stairwells, banqueting halls. The heart form requires a view from the front and from below: the composition is hung on the axis of the room.
LC0400.style: Contemporary classic with an Art Deco note: a quotation from a formal chandelier, cleared of ornament. The message is representative — a piece for an interior that greets a guest.
LC0400.madeToOrder: The number of spindles, the depth of the cascade and the density of the candles are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the plan of a city in three dimensions. The bars are fixed at right angles: horizontals and verticals fold into a volumetric grid in which there is not one accidental line. This is not a chandelier but a spatial frame of light.
Inside every bar runs a veined texture — the only living thing in a strict orthogonal system.

By day it is an architectural grid: clear bars on black rods, read through lines and inner drawing, a technical and precise piece. In the evening the light burns in the ends as cold points — the grid is marked out by its nodes and the volume becomes legible right through. A city plan lifted into the air.
LC0401.whereItWorks: Lofts, offices, meeting rooms, contemporary interiors with character. The orthogonal geometry needs straight lines around it: in a classical interior the piece argues with the finishes.
LC0401.style: Bauhaus and industrial modernism: structure instead of decor. The message is rational — a piece for a space that values order.
LC0401.madeToOrder: The dimensions of the grid, the number of bars and the depth of the layers are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a branch above a bench. The vine winds as a horizontal line and reaches out above the table exactly as a real branch reaches out above a garden bench — along it, not down onto it.

Leaves of two kinds, white gloss and gold, are intermixed; the points of light are hidden at the stalks. White-and-gold botany is the brand's most recognisable formula: the composition is formal without being heavy, rich without being loud.

By day it is clean graphic work: white on gold, read through the silhouette of a leaf. In the evening the light lifts the foliage from below in a warm tone — the gold leaves flare sharply, the white ones glow evenly, and the vine comes alive the way a real one comes alive under a lamp.
LC0402.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, living rooms, lobbies, restaurant halls, reception desks. The horizontal line is calculated for the length of the table or the zone.
LC0402.style: Art Nouveau and contemporary classic: the vine as a classic motif. The message is hospitable — a piece for an interior that receives.
LC0402.madeToOrder: The length of the vine, the density of the foliage and the balance of gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an explosion stopped at its best moment. From a vertical axis, stem-rays break out in every direction, and at the end of each a bud opens with a sparkling core: a dense core above, elements flying apart at the edges. The firework is caught exactly in the phase of opening, before it began to fade.
The light is born inside every bud — hundreds of shimmering points in a clear centre.

By day it is a white vertical with a gold axis: a piece read through its rays and silhouette, graphic and clean. In the evening the buds light from within with a scattering of sparks, the axis goes into the dark, and what remains is a firework suspended in the air.
LC0403.whereItWorks: A vertical format — staircases, entrance halls, double-height living rooms, atriums. The spread of the rays extends beyond the footprint of the axis: clearance is needed to the sides.
LC0403.style: Art Deco and formal classicism: the firework as the form of celebration. The message is ceremonial and bright — a piece for a space that greets.
LC0403.madeToOrder: The height, the number of buds and the density of the firework are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an upturned basket. Large faceted fruits hang in clusters beneath gold capitals, from which bundles of fine rods project — ears of grain above the fruit. The composition reads as a basket of precious harvest tipped over above the table.
The monochrome of transparency and gold makes the piece formal without being gaudy: two substances, not one surplus colour.

By day it is clear fruit beneath gold capitals — a piece read through faceting and highlights, dense and generous. In the evening the light comes from the capitals and fills every fruit, breaking up in the facets: the cluster fills with light from within the way a real one fills with juice.
LC0404.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, banqueting halls, lobbies, reception rooms. The dense cluster requires height — clearance is needed beneath it.
LC0404.style: Art Deco and formal classicism: the harvest as a symbol of abundance. The message is generous — a piece for the table people are received at.
LC0404.madeToOrder: The number of fruits, the tiering and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about seeds filled with light. White valves open to reveal a clear core with a scattering of points shimmering inside it — a fruit shown in section, at the moment when everything inside is already ready. Above every bud is a comb of fine plates, like a crown.
Hundreds of buds at differing heights form a living relief — a wave rather than a plane.

By day it is white on white: the composition reads through the plasticity of the valves and combs, through light and shade, without one patch of colour. In the evening sparks flare inside the cores and the opened valves begin to glow from within — a fresh, clean register acquires a second layer.
LC0405.whereItWorks: Light interiors — living rooms, dining rooms, spas, wedding and banqueting halls. The wave relief requires area: compressed, the composition loses its plasticity.
LC0405.style: Natural Art Nouveau and contemporary classic: the opened fruit as a motif of abundance. The message is bright and festive — a piece for an interior in a white register.
LC0405.madeToOrder: The number of buds, the shape of the wave and the density are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a staircase of light. The arcs twist into a spiral from top to bottom, and on each hangs a dense fringe of faceted rods. The form quotes a spiral staircase outright: turns, treads, ascending movement.
The light is woven into the arcs rather than hung from them: the structure itself burns.

By day it is a gold spiral with a clear fringe — a piece read through its turns and the highlights on the facets, alive as you walk around it. In the evening every turn lights from within, the fringe breaks the light into sparks, and the spiral becomes a staircase leading up. Movement seen from below and from every floor differently.
LC0406.whereItWorks: Formal verticals — atriums, stairwells several floors high, shafts between levels. The spiral reads whole only at full height: cropped, it loses its point.
LC0406.style: Art Deco and formal classicism: the spiral as a symbol of ascent. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a building rather than for a room.
LC0406.madeToOrder: The height, the number of turns and the density of the fringe are all made to order.

paragraphs: One turn of the spiral, taken off the staircase. An arc with its dense fringe of faceted rods is lifted out of the great vertical and hung on the wall — a fragment that was one step in the composition has become a piece in its own right.
The device is kept: the light is woven into the arc rather than hung from it. The structure itself burns, and the fringe only passes the light on.

By day it is a golden arc with a clear fringe: the piece reads through its line and the highlights on the facets, compact and precise. In the evening the arc lights up from within, the rods break the light into sparks, and a glowing step appears on the wall — a fragment of ascent with neither beginning nor end in sight.
LC0406-1.whereItWorks: Staircase flights, halls, corridors, reception rooms. Especially apt beside composition LC0406: on a staircase the wall lights carry the spiral along the wall, repeating its pitch.
LC0406-1.style: Art Deco and formal classicism: the step as a module. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a formal wall.
LC0406-1.madeToOrder: The width of the arc, the density of the fringe and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a night garden. The flowers read as silhouettes and the light as their core: a dark register is rare in light compositions, and the piece looks found rather than made because of it. The branch might have been cut in a garden after sunset.
The trumpets are graphite-grey with a white glow inside, sitting on dark curved branches and spreading horizontally.

By day it is dark graphic work against a pale ground — a piece read through contour, almost like an ink drawing. In the evening light leaves the bowls as directed warm beams while the bodies stay dark: only the glowing mouths are visible, hanging in the air. Callas that opened at night.
LC0407.whereItWorks: Interiors with dark walls, lofts, restaurants, bars, private studies. The directed beams let a table or a counter be lit precisely.
LC0407.style: Dark luxe and Art Nouveau: a botanical motif in a graphite register. The message is dramatic — a piece for an evening interior.
LC0407.madeToOrder: The number of flowers, the length of the branch and the depth of the graphite tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a wave of sails. The cones, opening downward, are gathered into a relief: a dense crest at the centre, sparse elements at the edges. The composition does not simply cover a space — it draws its shape, setting the height with light.
Two characters in one mass: matte white and honey amber, intermixed without order.

By day it is a wave of pale cones — a piece read through silhouette and the changes in height, calm and plastic. In the evening the white ones glow evenly, the amber ones fill with a dense sunset tone, and the wave acquires a relief of temperature on top of its relief of form: where there is more amber, it is warmer.
LC0408.whereItWorks: Lobbies, dining rooms, panoramic living rooms, restaurant halls. The cones are aimed downward — the light is soft and diffused, suitable for zones where people stay a while.
LC0408.style: Scandinavian minimalism and mid-century: the cone as the purest of forms. The message is warm and calm — a piece for an interior that does not argue.
LC0408.madeToOrder: The number of cones, the balance of white to amber and the area of the wave are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the moment between botany and fireworks. Hundreds of fine stems break out from a single centre and fall away into a full sphere — the form can be read as a flower head, a firework or a shower of sparks arrested in the air. The author does not choose: it is exactly that duality that makes the piece universal.
The stems are bronze in tone, with a drop at the end of each.

By day it is a graphic sphere: fine lines radiating from a point, a piece read as silhouette with almost no mass. In the evening a warm drop lights at every end, the stems go into the dark, and what remains is a swarm of lights hanging as a cloud — an explosion stopped at its best phase.
LC0409.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms, and covered outdoor spaces — verandas and terraces. A spherical form has no front: it is placed at the centre of a zone.
LC0409.style: Mid-century and natural Art Nouveau: the dandelion as a classic of twentieth-century design. The message is festive and light — a piece for an interior without heaviness.
LC0409.madeToOrder: The diameter of the sphere, the number of stems and the density of the flower head are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a crown. Thick hoops with an inner bubbled texture catch on one another through gold collars — dozens of rings entered into each other like the links of a mail coat. The form is assembled not by suspensions but by its own linkages: it holds itself up.
The bubbles in the mass make the substance alive — it looks arrested at a moment when the movement inside it had not yet finished.

By day it is a massive precious volume: close up you see the precision of the form and the joints, from a distance a dense transparent mass. In the evening light burns in the collars and spreads through the rings, tracing each with a radiant contour: what remains is a glowing crown with not one source in sight.
LC0410.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, reception rooms, dining rooms, banqueting halls. The dense volume needs height and clear surroundings — other accents beside it are surplus.
LC0410.style: Jewelled Art Nouveau and Art Deco: the link as a unit of luxury. The message is representative — a piece that sets the level at first glance.
LC0410.madeToOrder: The number of rings, the diameter of the crown and the finish of the collars are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about mass. Hundreds of identical capsules — streamlined like grains, caught by a gold band — fold into a wave field with a deep relief. No single element matters here: only quantity works.
The grain form was chosen for its neutrality: it refers to nothing in particular and lets the mass read as a surface rather than as a set of objects.

By day it is a breathing relief beneath the ceiling: identical forms at differing heights read through light and shade, a field with not one accent. In the evening the light burns in the band and fills both halves of every grain with a soft radiance — the surface comes alive entire. A harvest of light suspended above a space.
LC0411.whereItWorks: Generous rooms — lobbies, atriums, conference halls, retail galleries. The field is designed for an area: the composition covers a ceiling rather than occupying a point.
LC0411.style: Parametric design and contemporary minimalism: an array instead of an object. The message is architectural — a piece that is a surface rather than a luminaire.
LC0411.madeToOrder: The number of grains, the shape of the wave and the area of the field are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a constellation. The stars are scattered along the branches rather than set on a grid: the branches gather them into a figure the way imagination gathers random points of sky into a drawing. The arrangement is free — the constellation can run horizontally, wrap a corner, descend as a cascade.
Three-rayed elements with a core of light at the centre sit on dark bronze branches curving through space.

By day it is dark graphic work with clear accents — a piece read through the lines of the branches and the silhouettes of the stars. In the evening the dark finish of the branches goes into shadow and only the stars' own lights remain, hanging in emptiness: the drawing of the constellation appears entire.
LC0412.whereItWorks: Living rooms, lobbies, stairwells, private studies. The free arrangement allows the composition to be assembled for a specific room geometry.
LC0412.style: Art Deco and contemporary sculpture: the constellation as a motif. The message is poetic — a piece for an interior that loves stories.
LC0412.madeToOrder: The number of stars, the configuration of the branches and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a flowering branch above a path. The vine reaches out horizontally and the flowers look down — exactly as a real magnolia branch leans over a garden path. The piece does not depict a tree, it reproduces a situation.
White flowers with large lifelike petals sit on gold branches; a source is hidden at the heart of each. White and gold — the brand's classic in its most botanical reading.

By day it is a branch in bloom: large petals read through light and shade, the gold only holding the structure. In the evening the light in the cores makes the petals translucent from inside and the white stops being flat — the flowering turns out to be full.
LC0413.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, living rooms, lobbies, restaurant halls. The horizontal vine is calculated for the length of the table.
LC0413.style: Art Nouveau and romantic classicism: the magnolia as a signature motif. The message is tender and formal — a piece for a light interior.
LC0413.madeToOrder: The length of the vine, the number of flowers and the density of the flowering are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same loop stood upright and rendered in gold. The cascade is gathered into a heart, the loops linking into a living mail coat — the same logic of the invisible chain, but now it streams rather than hangs.
The change of orientation and finish changes the character of the piece: the horizontal bronze version reads as engineering, the vertical gold one as ceremony.

By day it is a gold cascade with clear contours — a piece read through its linkages and the highlights on the collars. In the evening the glowing segments ignite the contours and the cascade streams as a waterfall of clear links: the form disappears and only downward movement remains.
LC0414.whereItWorks: Staircases and double-height spaces: the composition reads from any floor. The heart form requires a frontal view along the axis of the opening.
LC0414.style: Art Deco and jewelled Art Nouveau: the link as a unit of luxury. The message is formal — a piece for a representative vertical.
LC0414.madeToOrder: The height of the cascade, the number of loops and the density are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an invisible chain. Clear loops catch on one another like links — the structure holds by its own linkages, and where metal should be there is emptiness.
The collars are bronze in tone with glowing segments inside them; the cloud is horizontal. The dark finish gives the composition graphic quality and weight.

By day it is strict engineering graphic work: clear contours on dark nodes, a piece read through lines and overlays. In the evening light runs along the tubes from the collars and traces every loop with a radiant contour — the chain appears entire while remaining transparent.
LC0415.whereItWorks: Studies, meeting rooms, lofts, reception areas. Strict graphic work suits working spaces that do not need a decorative accent.
LC0415.style: Industrial minimalism and brutal opulence: structure as an aesthetic. The message is rational — a piece for an interior that values how a thing is made.
LC0415.madeToOrder: The number of loops, the dimensions of the cloud and the finish of the collars are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a branch under the weight of a harvest. The sprigs bend into crescents — not for beauty but because they carry a load: the form follows the weight of the clusters.
The crystals are amber and clear intermixed — large grains and shards of ice in one bunch, the warm next to the cold.

By day it is a precious branch: the faceted clusters catch daylight and scatter it, a piece read through brilliance. In the evening points at the joints ignite the crystals from within — the amber ones fill with warmth, the clear ones flare cold, and the clusters begin to wink at one another. A harvest that glows.
LC0416.whereItWorks: Above a long table, in a dining room, in a banqueting hall, above a bar counter. The crescent bend gives different heights above the table — the composition adapts to the zone.
LC0416.style: Art Deco and formal classicism: the cluster as a symbol of abundance. The message is generous and festive — a piece for the table people celebrate at.
LC0416.madeToOrder: The length of the branch, the mix of crystals and the proportion of amber are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an inverted city. Plates with a cellular honeycomb texture descend in tiers, and the composition reads as a stalactite cave — architecture grown from the top down, with no foundation.
Three finishes lead three parts: whiteness for purity and structure, transparency for depth, gold for warmth and accent. The white upper tier melts into clear, the gold burns at the core.

By day it is a cellular mass read through texture and the transition of tones — a dense, almost architectural piece. In the evening the light lives between the plates and inside the cells: the honeycomb flares as a net, the clear tiers recede into depth, the gold goes white-hot at the centre. A cave of treasure built with a jeweller's precision.
LC0417.whereItWorks: Generous rooms with high ceilings — lobbies, atriums, double-height living rooms, banqueting halls. Tiering only exists where there is height to spare.
LC0417.style: Art Deco and natural architecture: the cave as a formal motif. The message is rich — a piece for a space that has to astonish.
LC0417.madeToOrder: The tiering, the share of gold and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a rising vortex. Crescent ribbons wind around a vertical axis like petals caught in a current — the movement is directed upward rather than down, which for a suspended composition is unnatural and therefore noticeable.
White and dusty blue are intermixed, the surface glossy; a chrome axis rules the vertical right through.

By day it is fresh white-and-blue graphic work on chrome — a light, airy piece read through the silhouette of the crescents. In the evening points of light in the bends lift the gloss from inside the stream, and the vortex begins to read as a direction: the glow runs upward, as though the current were accelerating.
LC0418.whereItWorks: Light interiors — staircases, bay windows, double-height living rooms, spa areas. The vertical requires height: the vortex is built upward and does not read in a low room.
LC0418.style: Scandinavian minimalism and contemporary sculpture: a cold register, pure movement. The message is fresh and light — a piece for an interior in a cool palette.
LC0418.madeToOrder: The height of the vortex, the number of crescents and the balance of white to blue are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a bow. Broad mirrored bands are tied into loose loops and knots that hover in the air — a gesture from the world of wrapping and gifts, enlarged to the size of a chandelier and stripped of its occasion.
The surface is broken into thousands of triangular facets, so the composition does not reflect, it multiplies: points of light hide in the bends and are multiplied without end.

By day the piece gathers all the light of a space and returns it as a salute of highlights — it works with not one lamp switched on, living only on what is around it. In the evening the sources in the bends add a glow of their own, and the facets begin to fire sharp sparks in every direction.
LC0419.whereItWorks: Above a table, in a window display, in an entrance hall, in a boutique. The composition depends on its surroundings: it is placed where there is something to reflect and where directed light will strengthen the facets.
LC0419.style: Hollywood glamour and contemporary Art Deco: shine as a subject in its own right. The message is festive — a piece for a space that wants an effect.
LC0419.madeToOrder: The number of bands, their widths and the choreography of the knot are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a colony. White tees link into a porous vertical structure with voids, bends and inner passages — coral grows exactly like this: not to a plan but by addition. No section repeats another.
The light does not pour out directly — it pushes through in fragments from the depth, through openings and pores.

By day it is a snow-white sculpture read through relief and the shadows inside its voids — a quiet and complex piece. In the evening it begins to breathe: the light comes out unevenly, in patches, and the colony looks like a living organism glowing from within. The floor lamp works solo or as a family of differing heights — and then a whole reef grows up against the wall.
LC0420.whereItWorks: Entrance halls, living rooms, spa areas, showrooms, winter gardens. Fragmented light gives atmosphere rather than illumination: a second source is needed nearby.
LC0420.style: Bio-design and organic Art Nouveau: growth as a form-making principle. The message is natural and contemporary — a piece for an interior with character.
LC0420.madeToOrder: The height, the density of the colony and the number of glowing pores are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about coral grown in air. The tees link into an extended structure hovering horizontally, and the differing orientation of the elements makes it alive and fluid — growth never goes in one direction.
The light lives inside and comes out through the openings — it is aimed nowhere in particular, it breathes out of the pores in soft warm patches.

By day it is a white glossy colony: a piece read through relief, voids and inner passages, complex when examined close up. In the evening the pores light up, the light is distributed unevenly, and the structure turns into a living organism for good.
LC0421.whereItWorks: Lobbies, restaurants, spa areas, showrooms, gallery spaces. The horizontal extension requires length — the composition is built along rather than deep.
LC0421.style: Bio-design and organic Art Nouveau: the colony as a form with no author. The message is natural and contemporary — a piece for an interior with an agenda.
LC0421.madeToOrder: The length of the colony, the density of the linking and the number of glowing modules are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a flare. Curved tusks break out in every direction from a mirrored core — the sun at the moment of a prominence, a dandelion enlarged to a chandelier, a firework that will not go out. Three readings of one form, and all three about a release of energy.
There are bubbles in the mass of the tusks, some clear, some smoky. The core is mirrored — it gathers and returns everything around it.

By day it is an explosion caught in a freeze frame: clear rays and a mirrored centre, a piece living off reflections and changing with every step. In the evening every tusk is lit from its base — the rays run along the curves to the points, and the flare turns out to be lasting. The composition holds a room single-handed.
LC0422.whereItWorks: Lobbies, atriums, double-height living rooms, showrooms. The spread in every direction requires free volume: nothing should be near the composition.
LC0422.style: Art Deco and cosmic modernism: the explosion as a form. The message is powerful — a piece for a space that has to astonish.
LC0422.madeToOrder: The diameter, the number of tusks and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about heat under ash. The light burns only inside the clear stones while the red ones merely reflect it: the ruby mass does not glow on its own, it is heated by its neighbours. That is how coals smoulder — the light comes not from everywhere but from inside the heap.
Hundreds of faceted stones are gathered into a crescent bowl on the finest of cables: a piece of jewellery at the scale of an interior, treasure poured out into the air.

By day it is a scattering of deep ruby and clear — a piece read through faceting and colour, dense and rich. In the evening the clear crystals flare, the red ones pick up their light, and the scattering begins to shimmer unevenly. The red is metered out by the light — the composition is deep rather than loud.
LC0423.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, private living rooms, bars, restaurants, reception rooms. The saturated colour asks for restrained surroundings.
LC0423.style: Art Deco and Eastern opulence: a scattering of gemstones as a motif. The message is rich and warm — a piece for an interior that is not afraid of colour.
LC0423.madeToOrder: The number of stones, the proportion of ruby to clear and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about kelp in a column of light. The ribbons wind around a vertical frame — they do not wrap it decoratively, they reach upward, as weed reaches for the surface. The vertical is full of movement: the ribbon seems to be still growing.
Sparks are scattered through the mass of the amber ribbons — the suspension you find in water lit from above.

By day it is a warm amber spiral on cold chrome: a contrast of two temperatures read through highlights. In the evening light travels down the ribbons, igniting the sparks in the mass and the gloss of the bends — the light descends into the depth as it does in real water.
LC0424.whereItWorks: Staircases, bay windows, tall wall piers, atriums. The vertical takes little floor area and works where there is no room for a bulky composition.
LC0424.style: Marine Art Nouveau: the weed as a natural motif without stylisation. The message is warm and organic — a piece for an interior that avoids straight lines.
LC0424.madeToOrder: The height, the number of ribbons and the saturation of the amber tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about handwriting. Hundreds of commas written by one hand, and not one of them the same: each is curved by its own movement — a rise, a turn, a fall. A form on the edge of calligraphy, where what matters is not the letter but the pressure.
The flock is dense, glossy white intermixed with matte gold.

By day it is calligraphy in the air: white and gold read through curves and overlays, a formal piece without heaviness. In the evening warm points of light are scattered deep inside the flock — they light the elements from within the mass, and the handwriting appears in layers: the near lines sharp, the far ones blurred.
LC0425.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, reception rooms, reception desks. The dense flock reads from a distance: the composition is calculated for the view from the entrance.
LC0425.style: Contemporary Art Deco and calligraphic aesthetics: the gesture instead of the form. The message is light and graceful — a piece for an interior that values a line.
LC0425.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the proportion of gold and the spread of the flock are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about lace. Openwork discs with honeycomb perforation read as a frost pattern or a hand-made doily — but are executed with machine precision. Joining airiness to precision is the device: a cloud from a distance, a jeweller's work up close.
At the centres of the discs, flowers open with light in them; the bowl is wide, the discs white intermixed with gold.

By day it is a field of lace: the perforation reads as graphic work, light from the window passes through it and draws a second composition on the ceiling. In the evening the light leaves through the perforation as hundreds of highlights — a small cloud of points appears around every bowl, and the lace turns out to be glowing.
LC0426.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, boudoirs, wedding halls, boutiques. The perforation gives patterned shadows — quiet surfaces are needed nearby so the drawing can be seen.
LC0426.style: Art Nouveau and jewelled Art Nouveau: lace as a classic decorative motif. The message is dressy and feminine — a piece for an interior that loves detail.
LC0426.madeToOrder: The number of discs, the balance of white to gold and the dimensions of the bowl are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about passion and restraint. The white flowers burn, the burgundy ones keep silent: the light lives only in the pale bowls while the dark ones hold colour and depth. One composition speaks in two voices at once.
The petals are crumpled, uneven, alive; the cluster is assembled on a vertical gold axis. Red and white on gold is a classic operatic register.

By day it is a dense cluster of cream and burgundy on gold — a saturated piece read through colour and the plasticity of the petals. In the evening the white bowls fill with warm light and the burgundy ones go into deep shadow: the composition turns dramatic, like a stage where not everyone is lit.
LC0427.whereItWorks: Staircases, tall niches, bay windows, private living rooms. The vertical format takes little floor area and requires height.
LC0427.style: Art Nouveau and operatic classicism: the poppy as a symbol of passion and oblivion. The message is dramatic — a piece for an interior with character.
LC0427.madeToOrder: The number of flowers, the balance of burgundy to white and the height are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about weight pretending to be vapour. Every dome is crumpled its own way, like a cloud sculpted by wind — and it looks weightless although it is a dense glossy volume. The play of weight against weightlessness is the piece's principal trick.
The flock hovers at differing heights, white intermixed with smoky blue.

By day it is glossy clouds beneath the ceiling: the crumpled surfaces catch light and give uneven highlights, and the composition reads through plasticity. In the evening a soft light comes on inside the domes and leaves the folds as a warm radiance — the dense mass turns into vapour for good.
LC0428.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, children's rooms, spa areas, lobbies. A multi-level flock requires height — pressed to the ceiling, it loses its volume.
LC0428.style: Contemporary minimalism and pop aesthetics: the cloud as a form, without irony. The message is light and friendly — a piece for an interior with no pretension.
LC0428.madeToOrder: The number of clouds, the palette and the area of the flock are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a seed. A smooth drop — a form in which everything is compressed and nothing is shown; on some elements there is the finest engraving of patterns, like carving on a shell. The difference between smooth and carved gives the composition a second plane that is visible only close up.
The wave is broad and the suspensions invisible: the mass reads as hovering.

By day it is a quiet pastel — white and turquoise, smooth matte, the rhythm of the drops. The composition does not argue with an interior, it gives it room to breathe. In the evening points of light hidden in individual seeds shine downward in warm beams: not all of them burn, only the chosen ones, and the field acquires accents it did not have by day.
LC0429.whereItWorks: Bedrooms, living rooms, spa areas, meeting rooms, reception rooms. The meditative rhythm and soft light suit zones where people stay a while.
LC0429.style: Scandinavian minimalism and natural Art Nouveau: pastel and a smooth form. The message is calm — a piece for an interior that calms.
LC0429.madeToOrder: The number of seeds, the balance of white to turquoise and the shape of the wave are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a wave that has passed through an organ. A strict vertical of elements and a free curve of suspension — the whole piece rests on that contrast: the tubes hang plumb while the carrying branches bend in waves, and the field of pipes looks disturbed.
The surface of the tubes is alive, run down — like a candle that has already burned.

By day it is a milky field on dark branches: the composition reads through the rhythm of the verticals and the relief of the suspension. In the evening light fills the tubes from top to bottom in a warm gradient — from peach to milk — and each begins to look like a candle lit from inside. An organ whose pipes have caught fire.
LC0430.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms, restaurant halls. The undulating suspension gives different heights above a zone: the composition is designed for a specific plan.
LC0430.style: Organic Art Nouveau and contemporary classic: the candle as the oldest image of light. The message is warm — a piece for an interior where people gather.
LC0430.madeToOrder: The number of tubes, the curve of the branches and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a banking turn. The dynamics are built into the structure: the lines of the frame draw the movement and the elements pick it up. The branches curve through space, and on them sit flocks of wings caught mid-turn.
The points of light stand on the branches rather than in the figures: the flock is lit from within and the source is never read directly.

By day it is a gold line with clear and white wings — a piece read through the graphic of the frame and the silhouettes of the birds. In the evening the light lifts the flock from below and from inside, the branches go into shadow, and only the wings remain, suspended in their turn. There are executions in contrasting black-and-white enamel — more graphic and more severe.
LC0431.whereItWorks: Living rooms, lobbies, stairwells, restaurant halls. The frame is designed for a specific geometry: the composition can wrap a corner, run along a wall, descend as a cascade.
LC0431.style: Art Nouveau and contemporary sculpture: flight as a classic motif. The message is alive and poetic — a piece for an interior that loves movement.
LC0431.madeToOrder: The number of birds, the configuration of the branches and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an inverted organ. Ribbed columns with capitals descend in a V-shaped cascade — pipes taken out of the instrument and hung in the air. The form has kept its solemnity and lost its support.
Light fills the ribbing along the whole length: every column sings with its own light, and together they give a chord rather than a unison.

By day it is strict vertical graphic work: cylinders with gold capitals, read through rhythm and ribbing. In the evening the ribbing fills with light over its full height and the cascade turns cathedral-like — the piece gives a space its vertical and its rhythm the way music gives it tempo.
LC0432.whereItWorks: Lobbies, atriums, banqueting and conference halls, double-height living rooms. The V-shaped cascade requires height and a frontal view.
LC0432.style: Art Deco and cathedral classicism: the organ as a symbol of solemnity. The message is monumental — a piece for a formal hall.
LC0432.madeToOrder: The number of columns, their lengths and the depth of the cascade are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a spinning top. A top exists only while it spins — here there is a swarm of them, stopped mid-spin, tilted in different directions the way real ones stop.
The tilts decide everything: the composition is full of movement with not one moving part. Highlights slide along the lenses with every step the viewer takes.

By day it is a swarm of clear lenses on gold axles — a piece read through faceting and reflections, alive as you walk around it. In the evening light enters through the axle and runs out across the concentric faceting in rings: every disc begins to glow from the centre outward, and the rotation becomes visible.
LC0433.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms. The movement reads as the viewer moves: the composition is placed where people walk past.
LC0433.style: Optical art and contemporary classic: rotation as subject. The message is intellectual and playful — a piece for an interior that loves paradoxes.
LC0433.madeToOrder: The number of tops, their calibres and their tilts are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an element caught and made to shine. Ribbons of thousands of vertical rods twist into a giant spiral narrowing toward the bottom — the form of a funnel, which in nature means destruction and here means light.
The light is woven into the arcs rather than hung from them: the structure itself burns, every turn from within.

By day it is a metal funnel with dense hatching of rods — a piece read through lines and twist, strict and monumental. In the evening every turn lights up and the funnel begins to rotate in light: the spiral reads as movement although nothing moves.
LC0434.whereItWorks: Atriums and grand staircases several floors high. One of the brand's largest verticals: the composition is designed for a specific shaft and reads differently from every level.
LC0434.style: Contemporary sculptural installation and Art Deco: the element as a formal motif. The message is monumental — a piece for a building rather than for a room.
LC0434.madeToOrder: The height of the funnel, the number of turns and the direction of the twist are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a repeated gesture. One and the same form — a disc with soft concentric waves — is taken in different calibres, from a saucer to a tray. Rings on water arrested in an object, and then multiplied across scales.
The tiers overlap like the roofs of a pagoda: the East read in the language of modernism.

By day it is milky discs on mirrored funnels — a piece read through the silhouette of the tiers and the soft waves on the surface. In the evening light burns in the funnel and spreads across the waves of the disc, tracing every ring: the rings on water begin to glow from the centre out.
LC0435.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms. The pyramidal assembly requires height — pressed to the ceiling, it loses its tiering.
LC0435.style: Oriental modernism and mid-century: a pagoda kept from the literal. The message is calm and Eastern — a piece for an interior that values rhythm.
LC0435.madeToOrder: The number of discs, the tiering and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a natural phenomenon. Every drop is a complete luminaire, yet on its own it means nothing: only mass turns a set of objects into rain.
The form is double: a mirrored tip flowing into a matte milky body. The flock is dense, narrowing toward the bottom.

By day it is silver and milk: the mirrored tips catch light, the matte bodies stay calm, and the composition reads through the difference between two surfaces. In the evening the milky bodies fill with an even glow while the tips go on reflecting — rain in which only the drops glow and the whole mass does not glitter.
LC0436.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, stairwells. The monochrome does not argue with an interior — the composition crowns a space without dictating a palette to it.
LC0436.style: Contemporary classic and minimalism: silver with milk, nothing surplus. The message is calm and formal — a piece for an interior that chooses restraint.
LC0436.madeToOrder: The number of drops, the depth of the flock and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a surface grown by nature. The deep cellular texture reads as crystallisation or as cell structure — a drawing with no author. At the centre is a glossy sphere, a core, the only smooth detail in the whole piece.
The contrast is set simply: chaos around, order in the middle.

By day the object works as a wall sculpture: the relief catches daylight, every cell gets a shadow of its own, and the bowl looks volumetric with not one lamp on. In the evening the core gives a soft glow that spreads across the relief and does not dazzle — the moon and a pearl in the white version, a Martian crater with a warm interior in the terracotta one.
LC0437.whereItWorks: Hallways, corridors, bedrooms at the bedhead, bathrooms, private living rooms. The light is soft and reflected — the wall light does not dazzle and suits rest areas. It works switched off as well.
LC0437.style: Natural minimalism and bio-design: texture as the principal content. The message is tactile — a piece you want to stand close to.
LC0437.madeToOrder: The diameter, the colour of the bowl and the colour temperature of the light are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a winter forest. The two-colour formation reads directly: the white cones are trunks in snow, the dark green ones are conifer. The form is one; the colour turns it into a landscape.
The texture is alive, slightly crumpled, catching shadows like hand-cast paper. The cones stand points up in dense formation, with light burning in the cut of each.

By day it is graphic work in two colours: white and deep green read through texture and the play of light on a crumpled surface. In the evening light goes down from every cut — the composition delivers genuine working illumination, a rarity among art objects — and the forest turns into a field of lights.
LC0438.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, kitchen islands, meeting rooms, restaurants, reception desks. The downward light lets the composition be used as the main lighting of a working zone.
LC0438.style: Scandinavian minimalism and natural Art Nouveau: the forest as a motif without stylisation. The message is warm and domestic — a piece for an interior that loves nature.
LC0438.madeToOrder: The number of cones, the balance of white to green and the format are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about repetition. Hundreds of identical gestures differing only in height and tilt — the botany here is strict, almost architectural, and that is the strength of the piece: a forest reads through quantity rather than variety.
Every flower is drawn out into a tube: a green stem flowing into a white bowl, the light sitting in the cut itself. The direction is firm — downward.

By day it is a dense forest on invisible suspensions: a green gradient passing into white, a piece read through the rhythm of the verticals. In the evening every calla becomes a living spotlight — the light goes down in narrow cones, and a field of light pools appears beneath the composition.
LC0439.whereItWorks: Lobbies, dining rooms, meeting rooms, restaurant halls. The downward light gives working illumination of a zone rather than only atmosphere.
LC0439.style: Art Nouveau and modernism: a botanical motif with architectural rigour. The message is clear and functional — a piece for the image and for the light alike.
LC0439.madeToOrder: The number of callas, the green gradient and the area of the forest are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a mercury icicle. A mirrored funnel draws out into the finest of tails — a form in which everything runs downward and ends in a point. The cluster is assembled points down, densely, without a single gap.
The composition is monochrome and hypnotic for it: only shine, light and the vertical. Not one colour, not one texture — a piece reduced to three qualities.

By day it is a mirrored mass that shows not itself but the room: the neighbouring stems reflect in one another and the drawing changes with every step. In the evening the light burns in the funnels and runs down the mirrored surface, breaking up in the reflections — the cluster begins to seem liquid.
LC0440.whereItWorks: Contemporary interiors with high ceilings — lobbies, double-height living rooms, showrooms, boutiques. A mirror works where there is something to reflect: the composition needs surroundings.
LC0440.style: Contemporary minimalism and high-tech: pure shine without decor. The message is strict and technical — a piece for an interior of straight lines.
LC0440.madeToOrder: The number of icicles, their lengths and the density of the cluster are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a liana. The spiral grows from the top down, putting out large leaves — the way a plant reaches in a conservatory when it has nothing to catch on and can only hang.
The leaves with their lifelike turns face in different directions; the points of light sit on the spiral between them.

By day it is white and gold on a vertical axis — botany rendered in two finishes, a graphic and formal piece. In the evening the light lifts the underside of the leaves in a warm tone: the gloss catches fire from below while the spiral goes into shadow — what remains is a liana glowing from its reverse.
LC0441.whereItWorks: Stairwells, bay windows, tall niches, winter gardens. The vertical requires height and reads as you walk around it.
LC0441.style: Art Nouveau and conservatory classicism: the liana as a motif. The message is alive and warm — a piece for an interior with greenery.
LC0441.madeToOrder: The height of the vine, the density of the foliage and the number of lights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a frost star on a window. Sharp faceted spindles are gathered into burrs — a prickly, radiant form, exactly what hoarfrost draws: from a point in every direction, without symmetry.
The burrs are linked by gold arcs into a horizontal garland: ice on gold, cold on warm.

By day it is clear spiky stars on gold — a piece read through facets and highlights, sharp and festive. In the evening light burns at the base of every spike and the burrs begin to glitter with hundreds of rays: the composition charges a space with energy without overloading it with colour.
LC0442.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, living rooms, lobbies, banqueting halls. Faceted spikes give a great deal of glare — the composition is formal rather than working.
LC0442.style: Art Deco and winter classicism: the crystal as a motif of celebration. The message is bright — a piece for an interior that wants brilliance.
LC0442.madeToOrder: The number of burrs, the spread of the garland and the density of the spikes are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an explosion in slow motion. Ribbon-strips — bent, twisted, alive — sit as dense crowns on rings descending in a vertical spiral. The piece reads as a flower flying apart frame by frame.
Every ribbon is bent separately: there are no two alike in a crown.

By day it is a vortex of white gloss on gold rings — the composition reads through the plasticity of the ribbons and their overlays, light and mobile. In the evening light stitches the rings with points and reflects in the gloss: the highlights leap from ribbon to ribbon and the vortex begins to turn.
LC0443.whereItWorks: Staircases, entrance halls, double-height living rooms, atriums. The spiral reads as you climb — the composition is calculated for a viewer moving upward.
LC0443.style: Contemporary Art Deco and sculptural modernism: movement instead of ornament. The message is dynamic — a piece for a vertical that has to lead the eye.
LC0443.madeToOrder: The number of rings, the density of the ribbons and the height are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a firework held in the act of opening. Bundles of tubes sit as stars on a branch — these are both fir boughs in hoarfrost and a firework caught at its best phase. Two readings, both wintry and both festive.
The composition is built without one surplus colour: white and gold, nothing more.

By day it is matte white stars on a gold branch — a piece read through the silhouette of the bundles and the rhythm of their placing. In the evening light in the cores ignites the tubes, each glowing with an even milky light, and the stars open fully. A winter celebration in warm gold.
LC0444.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, living rooms, lobbies, restaurants. The horizontal branch lies along a table; soft milky light without glare is convenient where people eat.
LC0444.style: Contemporary classic and Scandinavian winter aesthetics. The message is ceremonial and joyful — a piece for an interior that loves a celebration.
LC0444.madeToOrder: The number of stars, their calibres and the length of the branch are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the spiral of life. The axis grows dozens of tendrils, each ending in a drop: the form reads both as a molecule and as a flower head turning toward the sky. The double reading — biological and botanical — works toward one meaning: growth along a spiral.
The tendrils curve in different directions, and rings of light on the axis ignite them tier by tier.

By day it is a gold vertical with clear drops at the tips — a piece read through lines and highlights, light and mobile. In the evening the rings light up tier by tier, the drops flare at the ends, and the spiral reads as growing: the light climbs it from the bottom up.
LC0445.whereItWorks: Stairwells, bay windows, tall niches, double-height living rooms. The vertical takes little floor area and requires height.
LC0445.style: Art Nouveau and scientific aesthetics: the spiral as the universal form of life. The message is intellectual and alive — a piece for an interior with an idea.
LC0445.madeToOrder: The height of the spiral, the number of tiers and tendrils are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a garland that stayed for good. The branch spreads above the table as one continuous line — a festive gesture stripped of its occasion and therefore fit for every day.
The leaves have a lifelike curve, as though they had just unfurled; between them, points of light burn in the branch.

By day it is white on polished gold — the clean graphic of a leaf, a dressy and light piece. In the evening the points lift the gloss from below and the leaves begin to throw warm highlights onto one another: the garland comes alive the way a real branch comes alive under a lamp.
LC0446.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, living rooms, lobbies, restaurants, reception desks. The horizontal line is calculated for the length of the table or the counter.
LC0446.style: Art Nouveau and contemporary classic: white-and-gold botany as the signature formula. The message is festive and hospitable — a piece for the table people are received at.
LC0446.madeToOrder: The length of the branch, the density of the foliage and the number of lights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition as gesture. One continuous ribbon woven of thousands of the finest tubes winds in free waves — a silk scarf thrown into flight, or an aurora tinted by sunset. A piece as long as a conversation, passionate and fluid.
Red on dark, light on red — pure drama, without one softening element.

By day it is a scarlet wave beneath the ceiling: a dense colour read through folds and amplitude, a loud and whole piece. In the evening points of warm light flare along the crests of the folds — they emphasise the relief and set the ribbon moving before your eyes: an aurora that has acquired a rhythm.
LC0447.whereItWorks: Lobbies, restaurants, banqueting halls, showrooms, gallery spaces. Saturated red takes command of a room's palette — neutral surfaces are needed nearby.
LC0447.style: Contemporary sculptural installation and theatrical aesthetics: colour as the principal argument. The message is passionate — a piece for a space that wants to speak.
LC0447.madeToOrder: The length of the ribbon, the amplitude of the waves and the saturation of the red are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a pirouette. The ribbed funnels read as pleated skirts in a dance — a form that exists only in movement: a stopped skirt does not hold its folds.
The clusters hang as a free group, in tiers on gold cylinders — a dance stopped halfway through a turn.

By day it is a pale group of funnels: the pleating catches daylight and gives a soft vertical hatching. In the evening light enters from above and spreads through the folds — every skirt glows from waist to hem, and the group begins to seem to be turning.
LC0448.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, living rooms, reception rooms, banqueting halls. The free group is assembled for a specific plan: the composition can hang compactly or stretch along a table.
LC0448.style: Art Deco and the dance aesthetics of the twenties: movement as decor. The message is festive and light — a piece for an interior that loves joy.
LC0448.madeToOrder: The number of skirts, the tiering and the format of the group are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a curtain of scarves. Hundreds of ribbed "kerchiefs", bent at a free break, descend as a dense vertical volume — an almost textile gesture repeated at the scale of a building.
Gold capsules of light stitch the curtain right through: the sources are neither under the composition nor above it but inside it.

By day it is a waterfall of clear and smoky folds — a piece read through overlays and depth, pale and all but weightless. In the evening light runs along the ribbing of every kerchief as along strings, and the curtain sounds entire: hundreds of glowing strokes at differing depths.
LC0449.whereItWorks: One of the brand's largest verticals — atriums, stair shafts, double-height lobbies several storeys tall. The composition is designed for a specific opening.
LC0449.style: Contemporary sculptural installation: a textile gesture in a rigid substance. The message is monumental and soft at once — a piece for a building that wants warmth.
LC0449.madeToOrder: The number of kerchiefs, the height of the curtain and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a fan. The pleated disc reads both as a scallop shell and as the cap of a mushroom — what they have in common is that the folds radiate from one point: a structural principle rather than an ornament.
The colour decides everything: ashen rose makes the piece warm and adult at once — a rare shade for light and a precious one for an interior.

By day it is a tilted field of dusty pink fans: the pleating reads through light and shade, the composition soft and almost monochrome. In the evening a warm light comes on at the heart of every disc, and the folds radiate from it as rays of shadow — the fan acquires a drawing of its own that is invisible by day.
LC0450.whereItWorks: Living rooms, boudoirs, bedrooms, boutiques, reception areas. The dusty pink register asks for neutral surroundings so as not to argue with the finishes.
LC0450.style: Art Deco and marine Art Nouveau: the fan as a classic motif. The message is feminine and expensive — a piece for an interior with fine taste.
LC0450.madeToOrder: The number of fans, their calibres and their tilts are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a ring on water. The rays radiate from one point, and even a static form reads as movement — a drawing that always has a source and a direction.
The contour is deliberately imperfect: a live asymmetry makes the form natural rather than drafted. No disc repeats its neighbour.

By day it is clear cushions with a radial texture: the drawing reads against the light, and the uneven edge keeps the composition from turning mechanical. In the evening light from the gold capsules runs along the rays from centre to edge, and every disc begins to breathe — an impulse repeating over and over.
LC0451.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, meeting rooms, lobbies. The flat discs steal no height: the composition suits medium ceilings too.
LC0451.style: Optical art and natural minimalism: the wave as a pure form. The message is calm — a piece for an interior that likes the simple.
LC0451.madeToOrder: The number of discs, their calibres and the density of the cloud are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a regatta in the dark. Triangular prisms hang from chrome yard-bars — the form quotes a sail outright and the bars read as spars: a fleet held still before the start.
Geometry and colour make the piece graphic: this is the most architectural of the brand's green series.

By day it is emerald triangles on chrome — the radial carving reads as hatching, the composition strict and clean. In the evening light comes from the bars and fills the sails, the facets flaring cold emerald: the fleet catches fire in green.
LC0452.whereItWorks: Lobbies, meeting rooms, restaurants, showrooms, contemporary living rooms. The saturated green tints the air: neutral surfaces are needed nearby.
LC0452.style: Modernism and marine classicism: the sail as a geometric sign. The message is graphic and contemporary — a piece for an interior of straight lines.
LC0452.madeToOrder: The number of sails, the depth of the green tone and the spacing are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a leaf stalk. The gold capsule here is fixing and source at once: the rays of the texture radiate from it exactly as the veins radiate from the stalk of a real leaf. Structure and botany have coincided.
Clear, smoky and cognac leaves hang as a dense canopy at differing heights.

By day it is a canopy in three tones: the texture reads as rays, the layers of canopy overlaid and visible right through. In the evening the light enters the leaf from within and runs out along the rays — every leaf glows from stalk to edge, and the canopy burns like a tree at sunset.
LC0453.whereItWorks: Living rooms, lobbies, winter gardens, restaurant halls. The layered canopy requires height — pressed to the ceiling, it loses its depth.
LC0453.style: Art Nouveau and botanical modern: the leaf as a classic motif. The message is warm and natural — a piece for an interior in a natural register.
LC0453.madeToOrder: The number of leaves, the palette and the shape of the canopy are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a meadow after rain. Discs with a radial texture and a live wavy edge read as mushroom caps or as angelica flower heads — the sort of thing that appears in a meadow suddenly and all at once.
The composition brings a clearing, a meadow, a forest into an interior — and does it without one literal leaf.

By day it is a cloud of milky and amber umbrellas: the radial texture reads through light and shade, the edge lives by its irregularity. In the evening the light hides under the caps and lifts the rays from within — the meadow lights up from below, as under a low sun.
LC0454.whereItWorks: Living rooms, winter gardens, restaurants, lobbies, spa areas. The cloud is built wide: it needs area rather than height.
LC0454.style: Natural Art Nouveau and bio-design: a meadow instead of a bouquet. The message is alive and fresh — a piece for an interior that loves nature without stylisation.
LC0454.madeToOrder: The number of umbrellas, the balance of milky to amber and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about rain turned into jewellery. The light is hidden inside long stems and descends the shaft, filling the drop right to its tip: the source is not hung from the drop, it leads to it.
Differing tube lengths gather the composition into a three-dimensional cloud; the rhythm of gold verticals and clear drops makes the piece strict and jewel-like at once.

By day it is graphic work: gold lines with clear drops at their ends, a composition read through rhythm and with almost no mass. In the evening the light descends the stems and ignites in the drops — the stems stay dark and only the ends glow. Rain with burning drops.
LC0455.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms. The differing stem lengths give three-dimensionality — the composition needs height to spare.
LC0455.style: Jewelled Art Nouveau and contemporary classic: the suspension as a detail in its own right. The message is graceful — a piece for an interior that loves precision.
LC0455.madeToOrder: The number of drops, the lengths of the stems and the format of the cloud are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a downpour under a spotlight. Narrow faceted lancets descend in a dense vertical cascade several storeys deep — hundreds of arrows with one direction and differing lengths.
The cathedral solemnity here comes not from decor but from scale and repetition.

By day it is a clear and smoky amber cascade: the facets catch daylight and scatter it, a piece read through brilliance and depth. In the evening light enters from above and runs down the facets — the cascade glitters entire, like rain caught in a beam.
LC0456.whereItWorks: Staircases and atriums. A large formal piece: the composition is designed for a specific height and reads differently from every floor.
LC0456.style: Formal classicism in a contemporary execution: a cascade without a single conventional faceted pendant. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a building that greets.
LC0456.madeToOrder: The number of arrows, the height of the cascade and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about pebbles. The form is deliberately simple — a smooth stone with rounded sides and a live, uneven surface: something a river rolled rather than a craftsman turned. The author adds nothing to it.
The magic comes from the mass: a field of stones on fine needle suspensions shimmers like a shallow in the sun.

By day it is clear cobbles suspended in the air — a piece read through the irregularity of the form and its refractions, calm and quiet. In the evening light comes on at the crown of each and runs down through the mass: the stones fill from within, and the field begins to shift like water over a shallow.
LC0457.whereItWorks: Spa areas, pools, living rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms. The field is designed for an area: the composition covers a ceiling rather than occupying a point.
LC0457.style: Natural minimalism and wabi-sabi: the simplest of forms, without intervention. The message is contemplative — a piece for an interior that values calm.
LC0457.madeToOrder: The number of stones, their calibres and the area of the field are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about fur made of hoarfrost. Semicircular fans are built from a dense needled texture — what grows on branches over a frosty night: not smooth ice but a prickly pile.
The fans overlay each other in waves, like the scales or feathers of a giant bird; the arcs alternate gold and steel.

By day it is northern opulence: the needled mass catches daylight in thousands of points, a ceremonial and cold piece. In the evening light from under the arcs floods the needles, and every fan burns with a prickly radiance — hoarfrost that has caught fire from within.
LC0458.whereItWorks: Lobbies, banqueting halls, reception rooms, showrooms. The wave assembly requires area: the composition is built wide rather than deep.
LC0458.style: Art Deco and Nordic Art Nouveau: fur and hoarfrost as motifs of luxury. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a formal space with a cold palette.
