LC0458.madeToOrder: The number of fans, the balance of gold to steel and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about laundry in the wind. Every leaf is bent twice — not once, as in a static form, but with a second fold of the kind only cloth gets when a current takes it. Hence the soft movement through the whole mass.
The matte texture kills highlights and makes the light velvet: white and smoky grey waves with occasional burgundy hang as a vertical forest.

By day it is a quiet mass of pale waves — a piece read through plasticity and soft chiaroscuro, without one hard highlight. In the evening gold rods glow between the leaves like candles in a garden while the leaves themselves stay matte — the sources are visible and the mass around them stays calm.
LC0459.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, lobbies, spa areas, meeting rooms. Velvet light without glare suits zones where people stay a while.
LC0459.style: Natural Art Nouveau and Japanese aesthetics: cloth and petal in one gesture. The message is quiet — a piece for an interior that does not raise its voice.
LC0459.madeToOrder: The number of leaves, the palette and the density of the forest are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about direction. This flock has no top and no front — only a direction of flight, and that is set at assembly. The composition has no orientation of its own: it takes one from the room.
Ribbed boat-shapes fly in a wide crescent, each at its own angle; clear ones are intermixed with olive green, the tips gilded.

By day it is light graphic work in the air: the ribbing reads as hatching and the composition has almost no mass. In the evening points of light are scattered through the flock and ignite the ribbing — the feathers flare as they do under a low sun, when the light travels along rather than from above.
LC0460.whereItWorks: Living rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms, restaurant halls. The direction of flight is chosen along the route of movement from the entrance — the composition leads the eye.
LC0460.style: Natural Art Nouveau and contemporary sculpture: the feather as a motif of lightness. The message is alive — a piece for an interior that dislikes stasis.
LC0460.madeToOrder: The number of feathers, the balance of green to clear and the spread are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about weight that does not press. Voluminous folded forms drawn together at a gold knot read as pouches tied with a cord, or as buds an instant before opening — as something full and heavy. And they hover all the same.
The play of weight against weightlessness is the piece's principal trick, and it rests on one detail: the knot at the top looks like a gathering rather than a suspension.

By day it is dense folded volumes — clear and smoky, read through the plasticity of the folds, a piece that looks substantial. In the evening the light traces every fold along its edge, and the mass becomes outlined rather than filled: the heavy turns out to be empty.
LC0461.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, reception rooms, boutiques. Voluminous forms require height — pressed to the ceiling, they lose their plasticity.
LC0461.style: Contemporary sculpture and Art Deco: drapery as a form. The message is expressive — a piece for an interior that needs a gesture.
LC0461.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the balance of clear to smoky and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a sunset cloud. The field is gathered into a relief: large veils at the centre, small ones at the edges — the way a real cloud is built, with the mass growing toward the middle.
Corrugated disc-flowers in an amber-gold tone read as mushroom caps or as opened silk parasols — a soft form despite the density.

By day it is a warm field overhead: the corrugation reads through folds and soft chiaroscuro, the composition calm and uniform. In the evening light comes on at the centre of every disc and the corrugation drives it out along the folds in warm rays: the cloud fills with a sunset tone from within.
LC0462.whereItWorks: Living rooms, lobbies, restaurants, spa areas, banqueting halls. The field is built wide: the composition covers the ceiling of a zone.
LC0462.style: Art Deco and natural Art Nouveau: the parasol and the cloud as motifs. The message is warm — a piece for an interior in a gold register.
LC0462.madeToOrder: The number of veils, their calibres and the area of the field are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a whirlpool. Faceted plates of differing length descend in a spiral cascade along a frame — a vortex twisted from ceiling to floor. The spiral leads the eye downward and does not let go.
The light is woven into the spiral: the points hide between the prisms rather than hanging separately.

By day it is a gold frame with clear faceted pendants — a piece read through its twist and the highlights on the facets, alive as you walk around it. In the evening the whole whirlpool glitters with cold fire: the light breaks up in the facets and is passed from level to level, and the spiral begins to turn before your eyes.
LC0463.whereItWorks: Staircases and double-height halls. The spiral is designed for a specific height and reads differently from every floor.
LC0463.style: Art Deco and formal classicism: the vortex as a formal motif. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a vertical that has to impress.
LC0463.madeToOrder: The height of the spiral, the number of prisms and the direction of the twist are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a cut fruit. The scaled shell is built petal by petal, and in the cut a milky interior glows — the piece shows what on a real lychee is visible only once it has been opened.
The branches wind as a horizontal vine, the fruits facing in different directions; pomegranate red is intermixed with white.

By day it is a cluster of tropical fruit on gold — a dense red read through the scaled texture, a bold and rare register. In the evening the milky cuts light up, the red shell stays dark, and the composition burns from within: fruit filled with light.
LC0464.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, restaurants, bars, private living rooms. Saturated red takes command of a palette — neutral surfaces are needed nearby.
LC0464.style: Eastern opulence and Art Deco: the exotic fruit as a symbol of abundance. The message is bright and generous — a piece for an interior that is not afraid of colour.
LC0464.madeToOrder: The number of fruits, the balance of red to white and the length of the vine are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a nest woven out of gold. An oval wreath of interlaced branches carries clusters of drop-flowers — the form reads both as an upturned basket and as a nest: something plaited rather than assembled.
Every drop is tilted at its own angle, and a source looks downward out of each.

By day it is gold plaiting with white clusters — a piece read through the interlacing of the branches and the rhythm of the drops. In the evening light goes down from every flower: the composition delivers genuine illumination and not only an image, and a field of light pools of differing strength appears beneath it.
LC0465.whereItWorks: Above a table in a dining room, in a meeting room, in a restaurant, in a reception room. The downward light makes the piece a formal chandelier rather than a decorative object.
LC0465.style: Art Nouveau and formal classicism: the nest and the basket as motifs of abundance. The message is hospitable — a piece for the table people gather at.
LC0465.madeToOrder: The diameter of the wreath, the number of drops and their tilts are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a bundle of kindling. The rods are laid as a loose armful and cross at live angles — the way branches lie when caught by a cord: the chaos is judged but not drafted.
Fine ring engraving along every rod reads as threads of hoarfrost grown overnight.

By day it is a clear armful with gold ends: the engraving reads as hatching, and the composition looks wild and jewel-like at once. In the evening light enters at the ends and runs along the engraving in sparks — every rod acquires a dotted glowing line, and the bundle catches fire from within.
LC0466.whereItWorks: Living rooms, lobbies, dining rooms, restaurant halls. The horizontal cloud is built wide and requires no height.
LC0466.style: Natural minimalism and jewelled Art Nouveau: kindling presented as treasure. The message is a contrast — a piece for an interior that loves paradoxes.
LC0466.madeToOrder: The number of rods, their lengths and the dimensions of the cloud are all made to order.

paragraphs: A thinned-out version of the same meadow. The trefoils hover more freely, there is air between the elements, and the cloud breathes — instead of a wall there is a swarm.
The principal difference is in the light: it is now in the bowl of every flower rather than between the leaves. Each becomes a small lantern.

By day it is a light white cloud with occasional gold accents — the composition reads through the silhouettes of individual elements rather than as a mass. In the evening light from the cores ignites every flower from within, and the composition becomes a swarm of fireflies above a meadow.
LC0467.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, dining rooms, meeting rooms. The thinning gives soft diffused light: the composition is comfortable where people stay a while.
LC0467.style: Natural Art Nouveau and Scandinavian minimalism: the meadow in a thinned reading. The message is light and bright — a piece for an interior in a white register.
LC0467.madeToOrder: The number of trefoils, the density and the share of gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a meadow lifted into the air. Thousands of trefoils gather into a dense vertical cloud, uniform from a distance and breaking up close to into thousands of live leaves, each at its own angle.
Among the whiteness, as occasional sparks, are gold clovers: four-leaf charms hidden in the mass. They have to be found, and that is the whole point.

By day it is a dense white wall read as a texture — a monolithic and quiet piece. In the evening points of warm light come on between the leaves, the gold clovers flare, and rare accents appear in the uniform mass: a meadow with individual blades of grass alight.
LC0468.whereItWorks: Lobbies, atriums, stairwells, double-height living rooms, reception desks. The vertical cloud is designed for a specific opening and reads from several levels.
LC0468.style: Bio-design and natural minimalism: mass instead of a bouquet. The message is alive and warm — a piece for a space that wants nature.
LC0468.madeToOrder: The area of the cloud, the density and the number of gold accents are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a setting for a firefly. In every drop a round opening is cut, and through it passes a cable with a point of light: the source hangs inside the form without touching it. Light and shell exist separately — the signature gesture of the series.
Hundreds of drops gather into a wave: matte white intermixed with clear green.

By day it is a calm wave of flat forms with windows — a piece read through silhouette and the depth of the bottle tone in the green ones. In the evening the white ones glow softly with borrowed light, the green ones fill with colour, and inside every opening a point of its own burns: the drop becomes a setting rather than a lamp.
LC0469.whereItWorks: Living rooms, lobbies, meeting rooms, restaurants. The wave is built wide: the composition covers a zone rather than occupying a point.
LC0469.style: Contemporary minimalism and optical art: form and light as separate entities. The message is intellectual — a piece for an interior that values a device.
LC0469.madeToOrder: The number of drops, the balance of white to green and the shape of the wave are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an explosion stopped in the moment. Faceted boulders — like uncut diamonds — hover among crumpled petals as thin as foil, with live creases. There is no symmetry at all: the piece lives by the laws of nature rather than of composition.
The cables dissolve into the air, leaving pure suspension: the structure is taken out of sight entirely.

By day it is a scattering of gold and silver with clear boulders between them — the mirrored surfaces catch the room and multiply it, and the composition never looks the same twice. In the evening light burns inside the faceting and reflects in the mirrored surfaces, flying apart in rainbows and sharp highlights: it seems the light was detonated from inside and then stopped.
LC0470.whereItWorks: Lobbies, atriums, double-height living rooms, showrooms, gallery spaces. The chaotic assembly requires free volume — there should be no other accents nearby.
LC0470.style: Contemporary art and brutal opulence: destruction as a form. The message is bold — a piece for a space that wants to speak.
LC0470.madeToOrder: The number of boulders and petals, the balance of gold to silver and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about scales. Three-dimensional pyramids hang as a dense swarm, facet to facet — that is how scales lie: element against element, without gaps, with the planes all facing one way.
Milky facets in a gold setting: two substances divided by role — one glows, the other outlines.

By day it is a dense swarm of geometric forms: the gold frames read as graphic work, the milky facets through light and shade, a piece strict and warm at once. In the evening the milky facets glow evenly, the gold frames flare with reflections, and the swarm begins to shift like scales turning.
LC0471.whereItWorks: Above a table, in an entrance hall, in a lift lobby, in a meeting room. The dense swarm requires no great height — the composition is compact vertically.
LC0471.style: Art Deco and contemporary minimalism: strict geometry in a warm register. The message is restrained and expensive — a piece for an interior that values order.
LC0471.madeToOrder: The number of elements, their calibres and the density of the swarm are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about shoots. The ribbons are tied into loose loops and waves and gathered into a dense garden of vertical gestures — the movement here is directed upward, as in spring growth.
The green is metered like a seasoning: it enlivens the white mass and gives the composition a botanical mood without turning it into a plant.

By day it is a garden of glossy ribbons — creamy white with olive, read through the plasticity of the loops and their overlays. In the evening a warm point comes on at the top of every ribbon and runs down the gloss: the light descends the curl, repeating its line, and the garden begins to glow from the top down.
LC0472.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, winter gardens, reception desks. Vertical gestures need height to spare — otherwise the composition flattens.
LC0472.style: Art Nouveau and natural modern: the shoot as a motif of growth. The message is fresh and spring-like — a piece for an interior that loves movement.
LC0472.madeToOrder: The number of curls, the balance of white to green and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an ornament torn loose. Carved acanthus leaves — the very ones that grow on Corinthian capitals — have been torn off by the wind and circle in a free vortex. Ornament separated from architecture and let go.
Every element is independent, yet together they form a complex, almost natural rhythm — asymmetric, alive, new every time you walk around it.

By day the gold leaves burn with reflected light even with no lamps on while the white ones hold purity and rhythm: the piece works on daylight alone. In the evening the mirrored gold picks up artificial light and flares sharply, the white diffuses it softly — the vortex acquires a rhythm of temperature on top of its rhythm of form.
LC0473.whereItWorks: Living rooms, lobbies, reception rooms, stairwells, boutiques. The free vortex is designed for a specific volume and has no front.
LC0473.style: Baroque and contemporary sculpture: a classical ornament lifted out of its context. The message is bold — a piece for an interior that knows how to quote.
LC0473.madeToOrder: The number of leaves, the proportion of gold and the scale of the vortex are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a canopy and a flock at once. White feathers with a wavy, live plasticity are intermixed with dark green leaves — the shadow of foliage within plumage, and the composition reads two ways at once, choosing neither.
Warm points of light hide deep in the mass and lift the feathers from within.

By day it is a fresh white-and-green mass: the gloss multiplies daylight, the green gives depth, and the piece reads through the plasticity of individual elements. In the evening light from the depth lifts the feathers from inside, the green leaves stay dark, and the cloud acquires volume — what glows is not the surface but the interior.
LC0474.whereItWorks: Living rooms, winter gardens, lobbies, restaurants, spa areas. The dense cloud requires height — pressed to the ceiling, it loses its depth.
LC0474.style: Natural Art Nouveau: plumage and foliage as paired motifs. The message is fresh and alive — a piece for an interior with greenery.
LC0474.madeToOrder: The number of feathers, the share of green and the dimensions of the cloud are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a state rather than an object. There is no lighting here in the ordinary sense — there is light coming apart, weightlessness and quiet dynamics: the space around the composition turns into air.
Every feather is unique: its own curve, its own plasticity, its own moment of flight. The vortex is dense, circling.

By day it is a gust of air set in a body: clear fluid forms read through highlights and have almost no mass. In the evening points of light dissolved in the vortex flare along the edges — the mass itself stays invisible, only the edges glow, and the movement appears as contours.
LC0475.whereItWorks: Living rooms, lobbies, spa areas, boutiques, gallery spaces. The composition creates atmosphere — separate functional light is needed with it.
LC0475.style: Contemporary sculptural installation: air as a material. The message is poetic — a piece for a space that wants a mood.
LC0475.madeToOrder: The number of feathers, the scale of the vortex and the density are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a scattering of diamonds. Faceting of jewel precision is repeated hundreds of times: what usually exists as a single specimen kept in a safe is here poured out into the air.
The field is gathered into a wave: a deep centre, light edges. From a distance a diamond cloud, close up a collection of individual gems.

By day it is a clear field with gold tips: the facets catch daylight and scatter it, a piece read through brilliance. In the evening light enters through the gold and fills the faceting — every crystal flares from within, breaking the rays into rainbow sparks.
LC0476.whereItWorks: Lobbies, banqueting halls, reception rooms, boutiques, dining rooms. The breaking light gives a great deal of glare: the composition is formal rather than working.
LC0476.style: Art Deco and jewel classicism: faceting as a subject in its own right. The message is rich — a piece for an interior that declares its level.
LC0476.madeToOrder: The number of crystals, their sizes and the shape of the cloud are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a stroke of the pen. Every curl is twisted its own way — as a hook, a loop, a comma: the gesture of a nib left in the air and set. Not one repeated line.
The composition joins baroque plasticity to contemporary minimalism: only form and the gold of the suspension points, no surplus detail.

By day it is a cluster of clear curls on gold capsules — a piece read through the plasticity of the bends and the highlights on the edges. In the evening light enters from above and runs along the curve: every curl glows along its edge, like a stroke made in luminous ink.
LC0477.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, reception rooms. The hanging cluster sets the lower boundary — clearance is needed beneath the composition.
LC0477.style: Baroque retold in the language of minimalism: the curl without ornament. The message is expressive — a piece for an interior that needs a gesture.
LC0477.madeToOrder: The number of curls, their calibres and the shape of the cluster are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an inverted colonnade. Turned spindles of spheres, rings and cones descend as a dense forest — a balustrade taken out of a palace and hung from the ceiling. Architecture deprived of its support and turned into light.
This is not a chandelier in the classic sense but a light environment with optical depth: the rhythm of the details and the pure geometry hold a space on their own.

By day it is a gold and clear forest: the turned profiles read as silhouettes and highlights, a dense and formal piece. In the evening light lives in the clear segments and the gold ends — the composition shimmers with warm brilliance and faceted transparency, and the colonnade turns out to be glowing right through.
LC0478.whereItWorks: Lobbies, atriums, banqueting and conference halls, double-height living rooms. The dense forest requires height and area: the composition covers a ceiling entire.
LC0478.style: Art Deco and classical architecture: the baluster as a decorative module. The message is monumental — a piece for a formal hall.
LC0478.madeToOrder: The number of spindles, the proportion of gold to clear segments and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about lily of the valley at the scale of a chandelier. A small woodland flower is enlarged to the size of a formal piece — a device that changes the relationship: what used to be examined bending down now looks down from above.
The plasticity of the petals is alive: some flowers are open, others have barely unfurled — the bouquet breathes, because flowering is never synchronous. Gold pin fixings set fine accents.

By day it is a full white heart-shaped cascade: the flowers read through the plasticity of the petals, a bright and dressy piece. In the evening light burns in the bowl of every flower, the petals are lit from within, and the cascade glows a creamy warm white — bells whose cups have caught fire.
LC0479.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, living rooms, stairwells, wedding and banqueting halls. The heart form requires a frontal view: the composition is hung on the axis of the room.
LC0479.style: Art Nouveau and romantic classicism: lily of the valley as a motif of spring. The message is tender and festive — a piece for a light interior.
LC0479.madeToOrder: The number of flowers, the shape of the cascade and the height are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about split ice. The radial frost texture on the triangular plates reads unambiguously: that is how cracks run out from a single blow — from a point, in rays, not to a plan.
At the centre of every plate is a mirrored disc with the light hidden behind it: the source is covered by its own reflector and is never seen.

By day it is a silver horizon beneath the ceiling: the texture reads as rays, the mirrored centres catch the room, and the composition is strict and festive at once. In the evening the rays run out along the grooves and every shard shines with a rose of light of its own — an aurora cut into facets.
LC0480.whereItWorks: Lobbies, dining rooms, meeting rooms, showrooms, banqueting halls. The broad field is built wide: the composition covers a zone rather than occupying a point.
LC0480.style: Nordic Art Nouveau and Art Deco: ice as a formal motif. The message is ceremonial and cold — a piece for an interior in a silver register.
LC0480.madeToOrder: The number of shards, their calibres and the width of the field are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about wealth hidden inside. Stone outside, sun within: the split geodes show a dark mercury surface on the outside and a hot gold in the break. The device comes from nature — that is how real geodes are built, and everything of value in them opens only after the split.
Every element is unique: its own break, its own relief, its own drawing of the melt.

By day it is dark mirrored stones on copper rods — a piece read through reflections, with the gold interior visible only from certain positions. In the evening light comes out of the breaks in warm flashes and reflects in the dark facets of the neighbours: the stones begin to wink at each other while the mass around stays dark.
LC0481.whereItWorks: Private living rooms, studies, bars, lounges, showrooms. The dark mass requires dark surroundings: against a pale wall the contrast stops working.
LC0481.style: Brutal opulence and natural aesthetics: the mineral as it is. The message is strong and collectorly — a piece for an interior with character.
LC0481.madeToOrder: The number of geodes, their sizes and the composition of the swarm are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about equilibrium. A disc on a fine needle axis — a spinning top stopped in perfect balance: a position that in reality lasts fractions of a second.
The swarm hovers at differing heights; the monochrome makes it light and strict at once: the composition plays on light and form alone, without one colour.

By day it is clear parasols on needles — a piece read through silhouettes and ribbing, light and almost graphic. In the evening light burns in the axis beneath the disc, and the ribbed surface drives it round in a silver radiance: every top acquires a glowing halo, and the swarm begins to seem to be turning.
LC0482.whereItWorks: Contemporary spaces — above a table, in a meeting room, in an entrance hall, in a lobby. The flat discs steal no height: the composition suits medium ceilings too.
LC0482.style: Contemporary minimalism and optical art: rotation as subject. The message is technical and playful — a piece for an interior of clean geometry.
LC0482.madeToOrder: The number of tops, their calibres and their heights are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an oyster with fire instead of a pearl. White valves open in pairs, and between them hang amber "mussels" — what the shell is opened for has been replaced with light.
The clusters gather into a free cloud: the whiteness gives a matte rhythm, the amber warm flares in the depth.

By day it is white valves with a wavy relief and amber bodies between them — a piece read through the plasticity of the shell, a marine theme kept from the literal. In the evening the amber "mussels" light from within while the valves stay matte: the light comes not from everywhere but from the depth of every pair. A precious find from the shore.
LC0483.whereItWorks: Living rooms, spa areas, restaurants, reception rooms, interiors beside water. The free cloud is assembled for a specific plan.
LC0483.style: Marine Art Nouveau and Mediterranean classicism: the shell as a symbol of hidden value. The message is warm — a piece for an interior in a light register.
LC0483.madeToOrder: The number of valves and inner elements and the scale of the cloud are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same wave stood upright. Clear blocks are assembled into a strict column inside which a fluid form rolls: strict outside, alive within.
The light does not come out directly — it slides along the bends, refracts and fills the mass with depth.

By day it is a clear column with a bubbled texture: a piece read through distortions and inner drawing, almost without mass. In the evening the light reveals the depth — the mass fills and the wave inside becomes visible entire. A black frame with turquoise light gives a nocturnal, electric reading; a gold one with warm light an intimate, jewel-like one.
LC0484.whereItWorks: The corner of a living room, a study, a bedroom, a reception room. The vertical takes little floor area and works both as a source and as a sculpture.
LC0484.style: Contemporary minimalism and optical art: refraction as the content. The message is technical and mesmerising — a piece for an interior with contemporary taste.
LC0484.madeToOrder: The height, the finish of the frame and the colour of the light are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about water in a frame. A strict contour and free plasticity within — a formula that makes the object architectural and alive at once: the frame holds, the wave moves.
Clear ribbons with a bubbled mass roll inside the frame, and glowing strips light every crest.

By day, from below, the composition reads as the surface of water raised above the table: the bubbles are visible against the light, the crests catch light from the window. In the evening light lifts every crest from within, and the water begins to move before your eyes — the frame stays still while the contents live.
LC0485.whereItWorks: Above a long table, a kitchen island, a reception desk. The linear format is calculated for the length of the zone; the light is directed downward and gives working illumination.
LC0485.style: Contemporary minimalism and architectural design: the frame as a device. The message is rational and beautiful at once — a piece for an interior that loves order.
LC0485.madeToOrder: The length, the number of waves and the finish of the frame are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an underwater landscape dissolved in air. The piece lights less than it creates depth: curved plates swim in a funnel through the body of the space, and above them shimmers a scattering of white points — plankton near the surface.
The finest drawing of coral veining on the turquoise and smoky plates reads close up and disappears at a distance.

By day it is a calm turquoise-and-smoke mass: the colour reads against the light, and the composition creates a sense of depth in daylight already. In the evening the points above the funnel flare as suspension, the plates go into shadow, and a body of water appears in the room where only what is nearer the surface can be seen.
LC0486.whereItWorks: Spas, pools, bathrooms, interiors in a marine register. The composition is atmospheric rather than working — separate functional light is needed with it.
LC0486.style: Marine modern and bio-design: coral and plankton as motifs. The message is contemplative — a piece for a space where people unwind.
LC0486.madeToOrder: The number of plates, the balance of turquoise to smoke and the dimensions are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about lace turned by the sea. The organic perforation in the white plates reads as coral lace — a pattern nobody drew: the water left it.
Between the layers, coloured butterflies flit — blue, amber, gold. The colour is metered like a brooch on a white dress: the composition is festive without being gaudy.

By day it is a three-dimensional white cloud with occasional coloured accents: the perforation reads as graphic work, the butterflies as points of colour. In the evening light burns inside the lace and shows through the openings as hundreds of warm points, while the butterflies' wings pick it up and flare — a white field in which precious details have lit up.
LC0487.whereItWorks: Living rooms, bedrooms, children's rooms, wedding halls, boutiques. The layered cloud requires height — pressed to the ceiling, it loses its depth.
LC0487.style: Art Nouveau and marine modern: lace and butterfly as paired motifs. The message is festive and tender — a piece for a light interior.
LC0487.madeToOrder: The number of plates, the mix of butterflies and the scale are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition with no light of its own. The piece works exclusively on borrowed light: the gloss and the gold border gather a room's illumination and shift with every step. A sculpture made of highlights that needs no wiring.
The elements are bent like a petal in the wind or a sweet in an opened wrapper; the cascade is triangular, narrowing downward, the edge traced in gold.

By day the cascade lives on daylight from the window: the white gloss reflects it softly, the gold border sharply, and the drawing of highlights changes as the sun moves. In the evening directed lamplight makes the cascade flare entire — the piece catches fire the more strongly the harder you light it from the side.
LC0488.whereItWorks: Grand staircases, entrance halls, the zone above a round table. The composition gives volume and luxury with no lighting technology — suitable where wiring is impossible but directed light is available nearby.
LC0488.style: Hollywood glamour and contemporary Art Deco: shine as the content. The message is dressy — a piece for a space that wants an effect.
LC0488.madeToOrder: The number of elements, the shape of the cascade and the share of gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a current stopped mid-movement. Every ribbon has a plasticity of its own: here a wave, there stretched cloth, there a jet of air. There are no two alike, because a current does not repeat itself.
In the mass there are hundreds of air bubbles; gold clasps catch the ribbon along its whole length. The fine suspensions dissolve into the dark, and the columns hover.

By day it is a clear forest of verticals: the bubbles read against the light, the ribbons as smooth waves, a piece light and almost invisible. In the evening light enters through the clasps and ignites the bubbles — the mass fills with sparks and the columns become luminous right through.
LC0489.whereItWorks: Staircases, double-height living rooms, window displays, atriums. The forest of verticals is designed for a specific height and reads from several levels.
LC0489.style: Contemporary sculptural installation: the movement of water as a motif. The message is light and fluid — a piece for an interior that avoids stasis.
LC0489.madeToOrder: The number of ribbons, their heights and the density of the forest are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the phases of a wave. Every element is arrested in its own: crest, fall, run-up — together they give not a drawing but the storyboard of a single movement.
White gathers the mass into one cloud: strict, architectural, almost graphic. The light comes from the bends rather than from above.

By day it is an even white field overhead — a piece read through the plasticity of the bends and soft chiaroscuro, calm and uniform. In the evening light comes out of every bend and the field begins to shimmer like a sea under a low sun: the crests burn, the falls stay dark.
LC0490.whereItWorks: Large spaces — lobbies, conference halls, retail galleries, panoramic living rooms. The composition covers a hall in an even layer of light and movement: it works as the main lighting.
LC0490.style: Parametric design and contemporary architecture: an array instead of an object. The message is monumental — a piece that is a surface, for a building.
LC0490.madeToOrder: The area of the field, the number of waves and the density are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about rigging. A ship's tackle is translated into the language of luxury: some columns keep a genuine rope texture in a warm flax tone, others are twisted and faceted with light inside. Coarse fibre next to faceted radiance, craft next to jewellery.
The contrast decides everything, and it is underlined by one detail: the ends of all the columns are caught identically in polished gold.

By day it is a dense bundle of ropes: the flax texture reads tactilely, the faceted columns through highlights, an honest and heavy piece. In the evening the glowing ropes light the corded ones and the whole bundle smoulders like rigging at sunset — the light comes from inside the bundle rather than from outside it.
LC0491.whereItWorks: Lobbies, restaurants, bars, lounges, interiors on a marine theme. The dense bundle is built downward: the composition needs height to spare.
LC0491.style: Brutal opulence and marine classicism: tackle as a decorative motif. The message is honest and artisan — a piece for an interior with character.
LC0491.madeToOrder: The number of ropes, the ratio of textured to faceted and the lengths are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a vine on a column. The branches climb the wall from bottom to top, and the composition turns a plane into a flowering relief — a gardener's device: a plant is trained up a support so that the wall stops being a wall.
Along the branches grow glossy domes ranging from the size of a palm to the size of a saucer, and between them clusters of clear bubbles and curls.

By day it is a painterly relief in a powdery pink register — tender and rare for light decor; the composition reads through the silhouette of the vine and the calibres of the domes. In the evening a warm light comes on inside the domes, the bubbles pick it up and scatter it in sparks, and the vine begins to flower in light.
LC0492.whereItWorks: Accent walls — entrance halls, living rooms, boudoirs, bedrooms, boutiques. The vertical vine sits on a pier or runs alongside a stair flight.
LC0492.style: Art Nouveau and romantic modern: the vine as a classic wall motif. The message is feminine and tender — a piece for an interior with a soft palette.
LC0492.madeToOrder: The height of the vine, the number of domes and the density of the scattering are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a stamen made of pure light. A gold needle with a glowing filament passes through every bud — the light burns along the whole axis, exactly where a real flower has its stamen. Structure and botany have coincided.
The cluster is dense, matte white intermixed with clear amber; needle pins above the buds stitch the composition with a gold rhythm.

By day it is a cluster of buds running from cream to honey — a piece read through the form of the drop and the transition of tones. In the evening the white ones give a matte, calm glow and the amber ones a deep, warm one, and the cluster shifts along its whole height while the gold axes show through it as vertical threads.
LC0493.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, stairwells, reception rooms. The dense cluster is built downward: clearance is needed beneath the composition.
LC0493.style: Art Nouveau and jewelled Art Nouveau: a flower with a metal core. The message is warm and expensive — a piece for an interior in a gold register.
LC0493.madeToOrder: The number of buds, the balance of white to amber and the shape of the cluster are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a leaf fall twisted by wind. The funnel narrows downward, the elements circling densely — the form of a vortex that has drawn fallen leaves into it.
The light hides in the gold: points of warm radiance are scattered through the vortex like sparks in a fire of leaves. Clear green among the whites works as a fresh accent.

By day it is a white funnel with gold tips and occasional green — a piece read through its twist and silhouettes, light and mobile. In the evening the points light up inside the vortex and it begins to turn before your eyes: the light runs down the spiral from the top.
LC0494.whereItWorks: Stairwells and double-height halls. The funnel form requires height — the composition is built downward and reads from several levels.
LC0494.style: Natural Art Nouveau and contemporary sculpture: the vortex as a form of movement. The message is alive and spring-like — a piece for a space with character.
LC0494.madeToOrder: The number of petals, the share of green and the height of the vortex are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about reflected space. Rounded mirrored boulders crumple like liquid metal and reflect an interior as a circular panorama — the piece does not show itself, it multiplies everything around it.
Light here is an accent rather than the main thing: gold points flare in the folds of every lens.

By day the composition lives exclusively on borrowed light: every lens gives its own distorted panorama of the room, and the drawing changes with every step. In the evening the gold points in the folds light up and the mirrored field acquires lights of its own — the reflection gets an anchor.
LC0495.whereItWorks: Accent walls and ceilings — entrance halls, living rooms, lobbies, reception desks, showrooms. The composition depends on its surroundings: it is placed where there is something to reflect.
LC0495.style: Contemporary art and minimalism: an object with no image of its own. The message is conceptual — a piece for an interior that values an idea.
LC0495.madeToOrder: The number of lenses, their calibres and their layout across a surface are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the body of water. This is the brand's most numerous shoal: hundreds of figures circle in a giant ring, filling a space the way a real shoal fills water — as a dense current with thinnings and thickenings.
Every fish is simple, but the magic comes from the mass: on its own an element means nothing.

By day it is a ring of silhouettes beneath the ceiling: the composition reads through form and density, alive as you walk around it. In the evening light shimmers on hundreds of gold backs, the cables go into the dark, and the whole ring begins to swim slowly — movement appears with not one moving part.
LC0496.whereItWorks: Large spaces — atriums, lobbies, restaurants with high ceilings, double-height living rooms. The ring reads only from above and from a distance.
LC0496.style: Marine modern and contemporary installation: the shoal as a natural phenomenon. The message is narrative — a piece that turns a room into a stage.
LC0496.madeToOrder: The number of fish, the diameter of the ring and the density of the shoal are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a branch found in a forest. The composition spreads horizontally, repeating the curve of a real branch — not straightened and not symmetrical, but as it grew.
Points of warm light hide in the thick of the leaves like berries: they have to be spotted, they are not put on show.

By day it is white with occasional gold on the cold shine of the branches — a fresh, spring note, a piece read through the silhouettes of the leaves. In the evening the garland glows through the foliage like a window through a canopy: the sources are invisible, and the light pushes through in patches between the leaves.
LC0497.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, living rooms, winter gardens, restaurant halls, reception desks. The horizontal garland is calculated for the length of the table.
LC0497.style: Art Nouveau and Scandinavian minimalism: the branch as a motif without stylisation. The message is fresh and spring-like — a piece for a light interior.
LC0497.madeToOrder: The length of the garland, the density of the foliage and the share of gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a formula written in the air. Hexagonal honeycomb frames are linked into a horizontal chain — a structure out of a chemistry textbook carried into space. At the nodes of the lattice, white loop-petals open: strict geometry and living organics work off each other.
That contrast is exactly what carries the piece: the lattice sets the order, the petals break it.

By day it is gold graphic work with white accents — the chain reads through the lines of the cells, an elongated and strict piece. In the evening light comes on inside the petals, the cells go into shadow, and a row of glowing points remains, threaded on an invisible formula.
LC0498.whereItWorks: Dining tables, bar counters, reception desks — long spaces that need holding with one continuous line. The chain is calculated for the length of the zone.
LC0498.style: Bauhaus and natural Art Nouveau: the lattice against the plant. The message is intellectual — a piece for an interior that loves a contradiction.
LC0498.madeToOrder: The length of the chain, the number of cells and the density of the petals are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a knot. The knot is an ancient sign of connection and of infinity; here it is turned into sculpture and repeated by the dozen, each with its own plasticity and its own bend. Tying the same knot twice is impossible.
The cloud is dense, on gold needle pins: it reads whole from a distance and opens into the plasticity of each knot close up.

By day it is a white cloud of free loops — a piece read through curves and overlays, bright and mobile. In the evening a soft light comes on inside the loops: it slides along the gloss and floods the core of every knot with warmth — what glows is not the mass but the middle of each linkage.
LC0499.whereItWorks: Living rooms, dining rooms, lobbies, reception rooms, wedding halls. The dense cloud requires height — pressed to the ceiling, it loses its plasticity.
LC0499.style: Contemporary sculpture and Art Deco: the knot as a symbol. The message is expressive — a piece for an interior that needs a gesture.
LC0499.madeToOrder: The number of knots, the density of the cloud and the scale are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a game stopped on the winning move. Cubes assemble into a structure with setbacks, cantilevers and towers — a construction set with no final appearance: the composition is built like a building and can take any number of storeys and any configuration.
Between the clear cubes, gold modules with light are set in — they are part of the structure rather than a pendant attached to it.

By day it is transparent architecture: the undulating lens surface distorts everything behind it, and the structure reads through setbacks and refractions. In the evening the gold modules light up inside the construction and the light is multiplied in the facets of the neighbouring cubes — the building glows from within, storey by storey.
LC0500.whereItWorks: Contemporary interiors — lofts, lobbies, meeting rooms, showrooms, offices. The strict geometry needs straight lines around it; the configuration is chosen for a specific room.
LC0500.style: Bauhaus and architectural minimalism: the module instead of the ornament. The message is rational — a piece for a space that values structure.
LC0500.madeToOrder: The number of cubes, the proportion of gold modules and the shape of the assembly are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a shaving off a cutting tool. Springy rings and half-rings of ribbed ribbon repeat a form that arises by itself — as a by-product of work. The author makes it the main thing.
Every curl carries a gold capsule of light; the cloud is vertical and dense.

By day it is a vortex of ribbed coils: the composition reads through plasticity and hatching, alive and mobile. In the evening light runs along the spirals, slips off the coils and fills the space with dancing highlights — the cloud begins to turn.
LC0501.whereItWorks: Stairwells, the zone above a round table, bay windows. The composition is flexible in mood: assembled densely it reads as baroque, thinned out as light calligraphy.
LC0501.style: Baroque and industrial minimalism in one piece: the curl without ornament. The message is expressive — a piece for an interior that needs character.
LC0501.madeToOrder: The number of curls, the height of the cloud and the density are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition as an event. This is not a luminaire but the central object of a space: giant wings opened to their full span, holding a hall single-handed.
Feather by feather, from the flight feathers to the down — the form is worked entire, with no generalisations. The mass with its air bubbles makes every feather alive.

By day it is a transparent sculpture: the bubbles read against the light, the feathers catch daylight along their edges, and the wings seem almost weightless. In the evening light flows along the edges from within, flares at the tips and runs down as needles of ice — the wings catch fire in gold while staying cold to the eye.
LC0502.whereItWorks: Above a grand piano, in an atrium, above a formal staircase, in a double-height lobby. The composition requires complete openness: there should be no other accents near it.
LC0502.style: Art Nouveau and monumental sculpture: the wing as a symbol. The message is ceremonial, almost sacred — a piece for a space that has to astonish.
LC0502.madeToOrder: The span, the number of feathers and the colour temperature of the light are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a migration over a northern sea. Birds of a smoky blue shade fly in a vertical stream — calmly and steadily, without drama: this is neither a flight nor a take-off but a long journey.
The muted blue-grey is a rare guest in light decor and precious for that reason: it ties the interior to the sky beyond the window. The gold breasts are the only warm accent.

By day the colour works at full strength: the smoky blue answers the sky, and the composition seems a continuation of the view. In the evening, under directed light, the matte surface gives deep shadows, the gold flares as points, and the stream becomes gathered and graphic.
LC0503.whereItWorks: Bedrooms, studies, staircases, interiors in a Scandinavian or Japanese aesthetic. The composition is decorative — it works without lamps but gains from side light.
LC0503.style: Scandinavian minimalism and the Japanese school: the migration as a classic subject. The message is quiet — a piece for an interior that does not raise its voice.
LC0503.madeToOrder: The number of birds, the depth of the shade and the height of the stream are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about snow in headlights. The dense bubbled texture on V-shaped wings reads as frost on a window, and in the evening it gives the principal effect: the light breaks up in thousands of bubbles and shimmers like snow caught in a beam.
The column is vertical, and the body of every pair of wings carries a source that traces the contours in gold.

By day it is a column of ice: the texture reads against the light, the wings fold into a vertical rhythm, a cold and graphic piece. In the evening the texture takes the leading part — the light breaks up and shimmers over the whole height, and the column begins to tremble.
LC0504.whereItWorks: Stairwells and narrow verticals. The composition takes no floor area but fills a height — ideal where there is no room for a bulky piece.
LC0504.style: Nordic Art Nouveau: the butterfly and the hoarfrost as paired motifs. The message is poetic and cool — a piece for an interior in a cold register.
LC0504.madeToOrder: The number of butterflies, the height of the column and the density are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a runway. The ribbing on a broad single wing turns it in the evening into a strip of light — the same marking that rules an airfield runway, only carried into the air.

The wings read as gliders or as rays: whole, without division into feathers. Beneath each is a gold keel-cone with light. The white ceiling rails are part of the aesthetic: the installation looks technological, like a light-aviation hangar.

By day it is an almost colourless flock: the wings read through ribbing and form, and the composition is very airy. In the evening light floods the wing from below, the ribbing drives it along, and the flock covers a space with an even warm radiance — a hundred runways overhead.
LC0505.whereItWorks: Lobbies, conference halls, meeting rooms, retail galleries, panoramic living rooms. The even radiance makes the composition the main source of lighting.
LC0505.style: Industrial modernism and aviation aesthetics: engineering as beauty. The message is rational — a piece for a contemporary space.
LC0505.madeToOrder: The number of gliders, the area of the flock and the drop height are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a feather cast in mercury. Mirrored crescents with the finest ribbed texture circle in a vortex around an invisible centre — the movement is set by the arrangement rather than by the form.

The mirrored surface gathers the interior and the light around it: the composition is always the colour of its own space — cold in the morning, warm in the evening. Gold finials place the full stops in the whirl.

By day the vortex lives on daylight: the crescents reflect the window, the walls, one another, and the drawing changes as the sun moves. In the evening warm lamplight tints the mirror and the same composition turns golden — the piece has no permanent colour, it takes one from the room.
LC0506.whereItWorks: Contemporary interiors — above a staircase, in a dining room, on an accent wall, in an entrance hall. It fixes to a wall or a ceiling and works as graphic art in three dimensions.
LC0506.style: Contemporary sculpture and minimalism: the mirror as a device. The message is conceptual — a piece for an interior that values an idea.
LC0506.madeToOrder: The diameter of the vortex, the number of wings and the finish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about flight in all its phases at once. The wings are open, folded, turned — one movement broken into frames and gathered into a single vertical.
Snow-white ones with gold bodies alternate with occasional graphite blue: gulls and petrels in one flock. The dark wings give depth and rhythm.

By day the white feather texture gathers light from the space and looks luminous with no lamps at all — the piece works on daylight alone. In the evening, under directed light, the texture gives a relief of light and shade while the dark wings drop into hollows: the flock becomes more contrasted than it is by day.
LC0507.whereItWorks: Interiors where the lighting is already resolved and what is needed is volume, movement and character — living rooms, entrance halls, staircases, reception rooms. The composition requires no wiring.
LC0507.style: Marine modern and contemporary sculpture: the flock as graphic art in three dimensions. The message is alive — a piece for an interior that lacks movement.
LC0507.madeToOrder: The number of wings, the share of dark ones and the scale are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the time of day. The gradient of the flock reads as the passage of a day: from daylight above to dusk below — from white through dusty rose to deep violet. The flock is not flying, it is darkening.

This is a decorative composition with no light of its own: it works through plasticity, colour and shadow. The matte surface kills highlights nobly, and the gold of the beaks and breasts sets the accents.

By day the gradient reads in full: colour is the piece's principal argument, and daylight shows it more precisely than any lighting. In the evening, under directed light, the matte surface gives deep soft shadows while the gold details flare as points — the flock acquires a volume invisible by day.
LC0508.whereItWorks: Staircases, entrance halls, wall piers, living rooms — wherever a coloured vertical accent is needed without lighting technology. It requires no wiring but gains from directed light nearby.
LC0508.style: Contemporary sculpture and natural Art Nouveau: the gradient as subject. The message is poetic — a piece for an interior that loves colour.
LC0508.madeToOrder: The number of birds, the stretch of the gradient and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: The same flock twisted into a vertical column. The birds rise in a spiral, like a current caught by a draught — and the composition fills a vertical with movement from the bottom up.
Every bird is unique in its turn and its tilt: the vortex does not repeat itself from any angle.

By day it is a clear spiral with gold bodies — a piece read through its twist and its silhouettes, alive as you walk around it. In the evening light shimmers in the feathers as the sun shimmers in the flight feathers of a real flock: some individuals flare, others stay shadow, and the current seems to be moving.
LC0509.whereItWorks: Staircases and double-height spaces. The vortex is designed for a specific height and reads differently from every level.
LC0509.style: Art Nouveau and contemporary installation: the rising current as subject. The message is dynamic — a piece for a vertical that has to lead the eye upward.
LC0509.madeToOrder: The height of the vortex, the number of birds and the density of the spiral are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a double temperament. The wings are clear, the bodies gold: the cold anatomy of flight and a warm heart inside every bird. The source is hidden in the body and the light comes out through the mass of the wing.
Every wing is worked down to the individual feather — a detailed form rather than a silhouette.

By day it is a clear flock with gold bodies spread across a wide front: the composition reads through anatomy and the highlights on the feathers. In the evening the light comes out through the mass and the feathers catch an icy fire — the bodies stay warm points, the wings turn cold.
LC0510.whereItWorks: A long table, a bar counter, a reception desk, a meeting room. The horizontal front covers a space the way a flock covers a field: the composition is oriented along the length of the zone.
LC0510.style: Art Nouveau and contemporary sculpture: the bird as a classic motif of flight. The message is alive and narrative — a piece that creates a scene.
LC0510.madeToOrder: The number of birds, the spread of the flock and the direction of flight are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an object let go. A table lamp is a thing whose name says everything: it stands on a table. The author takes that silhouette, multiplies it and lifts it into the air. The move is ironic and therefore instantly recognisable.
Dozens of small "lamps" hang as a dense cloud, each with its own tilt and height — as though they had only just been released and had not yet fallen into line.

By day it is recognisable silhouettes beneath the ceiling: ribbed skirts on fine gold stems, a piece read through form and repetition. In the evening light burns in the stem and floods the skirt, turning each into a glowing pleated bell — a swarm of table lamps with no table.
LC0511.whereItWorks: Above a long table, in cafés and bar spaces, in lofts, in meeting rooms — wherever a joke is welcome. The dense swarm gives even light along the whole length of a zone.
LC0511.style: Postmodernism and contemporary design: the quotation of an object instead of an ornament. The message is witty — a piece for an interior with a sense of humour.
LC0511.madeToOrder: The number of "lamps", their sizes and the density of the swarm are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a piece of jewellery at the scale of an interior. Large faceted links are joined by gold bushings into live vertical chains — literally a jewel enlarged to the size of a chandelier.
The palette runs as a gradation: from pale lavender to deep amethyst, and the chains chime with one another in shades.

By day it is faceted lilac links catching daylight and scattering it across the walls — a piece read through colour and faceting. In the evening light enters the link through the bushing and leaves the facets in lilac flashes: the chain lights from within, link by link.
LC0512.whereItWorks: Boudoirs, dressing rooms, boutiques, private living rooms. The saturated colour asks for neutral surroundings; lilac highlights tint the walls — the background should be quiet.
LC0512.style: Art Deco and jewelled Art Nouveau: the gemstone chain as a classic of adornment. The message is bold and feminine — a piece for an interior that is not afraid of colour.
LC0512.madeToOrder: The length of the chains, the number of links and the palette are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about swirled syrup. The bubbled mass in the green-and-amber "rings" reads as a viscous liquid with bubbles caught in it — movement stopped halfway.

Every element is threaded on a gold funnel axis and resembles a spinning top frozen mid-turn. The swarm hangs at differing heights, narrowing downward: the sense of rotation survives in complete stillness.

By day it is warm amber volumes with bubbles seen against the light — a piece read through form and inner drawing, dense and comfortable. In the evening light burns in the axis and floods the volume from within: the bubbles flare like sparks in swirled syrup, and the tops begin to turn.
LC0513.whereItWorks: Spaces with a retro-futurist character — bar counters, kitchen islands, studies, lounges. The dense swarm requires no great height.
LC0513.style: Retro-futurism and mid-century: a sixties form without quotation. The message is playful and warm — a piece for an interior with humour.
LC0513.madeToOrder: The number of tops, their calibres and the depth of tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a rain of its own. Every parasol is tilted its own way, as though catching something of its own — and the swarm stops being a formation: every cap has a task of its own.
The form is simple: a fine stem, a wide pleated skirt, a mirrored surface.

By day the monochrome and the mirroring make the composition graphic — it reflects an interior and dissolves into it, leaving only contours. In the evening light burns under the skirts, the pleating takes it apart into silver rays, and all that remains of the swarm is a set of glowing coronets.
LC0514.whereItWorks: Contemporary spaces — concrete, panoramic glazing, minimalist living rooms and lobbies. A mirror works where there is something to reflect.
LC0514.style: Contemporary minimalism and high-tech: the mushroom as pure geometry. The message is technical — a piece for an interior of straight lines.
LC0514.madeToOrder: The number of parasols, their diameters and their angles of tilt are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about two layers. Outside, a full flower head of dozens of curved petals — from honey to cognac; inside, a white branching frame, a bone coral that glows through the amber. The piece shows the flower and its skeleton at once.
The spherical form has no front: the composition is equally beautiful from any side.

By day it is an amber sphere with a white frame showing through between the petals — a piece read through colour and structure. In the evening points in the core light up, the frame comes through as a silhouette against the amber, and the light turns honeyed — the interior around it becomes evening-like and comfortable.
LC0515.whereItWorks: The centre of a space — above a round table, in a rotunda, in a bay window, in an entrance hall. Having no front means it is viewed in the round.
LC0515.style: Art Nouveau and natural modern: the dahlia as a motif of abundance. The message is warm — a piece for an interior in a honey register.
LC0515.madeToOrder: The diameter of the sphere, the density of the petals and the depth of the amber tone are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an inverted canopy. Gold trunks with forked joints carry a harvest: white petal-fruits and clear faceted drops. The tree grows downward, and the fruit hangs where the roots would usually be.

Three textures are gathered into one volume: matte whiteness gives softness and weight, faceting gives brilliance and transparency, gold gives structure. The canopy opens in layers as you walk around it.

By day it is a dense rich mass with not one surplus colour — a piece read through the overlay of three surfaces. In the evening the faceted drops light from within and scatter the light, the white petals diffuse it softly, and the gold picks it up and traces the structure: abundance without gaudiness.
LC0516.whereItWorks: Dining rooms, living rooms, lobbies, banqueting halls. The dense canopy requires height — pressed to the ceiling, it loses its layers.
LC0516.style: Art Deco and formal classicism: the harvest as a symbol of plenty. The message is generous — a piece for an interior that receives.
LC0516.madeToOrder: The scale of the canopy and the number of petals and drops are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about sparks over a coal. Below, a large core of deep red; above it a plume of crystals rises — what flies up at the moment a white-hot thing is struck.

The red here is dramatic rather than decorative: the composition works on emotion and keeps a space under tension. Smoky mirrored crystals damp and set off the heat — without them it would be unbearable.

By day it is a ruby core with a plume of faceted shards — a dense colour read through faceting and depth. In the evening the core lights from within like heat in rock, while the smoky crystals above it only reflect it and stay dark: one point burns and everything else merely catches the glow.
LC0517.whereItWorks: Interiors with a bold palette — bars, wine rooms, private cinemas, living rooms with dark walls. Against a pale ground the drama is lost.
LC0517.style: Dark luxe and theatrical aesthetics: colour as emotion. The message is passionate — a piece for a space with character.
LC0517.madeToOrder: The size of the core, the length of the plume and the proportion of red are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a rising seam. The eye reads a movement from the bottom up: a large nugget below, and above it a scattering of shards rising on invisible threads — a flare stopped at the moment of its ascent.
The nugget is built as a geode in reverse: a mirrored gold core inside a clear shell, with the light coming from the middle.

By day it is a faceted stone with a gold interior and a scattering of amber shards above it — a piece read through faceting and vertical movement. In the evening the core burns with a dense warm light, the shards shimmer with reflections, and the whole seam begins to rise: the light thins toward the top the way it thins through a body of water.
LC0518.whereItWorks: Stairwells and narrow tall niches — where a vertical is cramped. The composition is built upward and takes little floor area.
LC0518.style: Natural aesthetics and Art Deco: the mineral as a formal motif. The message is rich and warm — a piece for an interior in a gold register.
LC0518.madeToOrder: The height of the ascent, the number of shards and the scale of the core are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about an inverted city. Faceted obelisks descend in dense formation — the towers of a Gothic city turned spires down. The formation reads as ceremonial, almost musical: an organ assembled out of light.

The double temperature is the composition's signature move: light enters through the gold pin and runs out along the facets, the clear mass flares cold while the finial stays warm. Gold and ice argue and balance each other.

By day it is a formation of clear spires with gold tops — a piece read through facets and rhythm, strict and formal. In the evening the cold and the warm separate for good: the mass fills with ice, the pins burn gold, and the city glows in two colours at once.
LC0519.whereItWorks: Formal verticals — staircases, atriums, entrance groups, double-height lobbies. The formation is designed for a specific height.
LC0519.style: Gothic in a contemporary reading and Art Deco: the spire as a symbol of aspiration. The message is ceremonial — a piece for a building that greets.
LC0519.madeToOrder: The number of spires, their lengths and the proportion of gold are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a face and a reverse. Outside the petals are deep graphite, inside milky white: the dark contour holds the form, the pale interior fills it. That one device makes the sphere volumetric with no relief at all.
The flower heads are built from dozens of narrow petals and hang as a cluster, turned in different directions as on a real bush.

By day it is graphite spheres with glimpses of white in the depth — a dense piece read through silhouette and contrast. In the evening the light comes out of the core between the petals, and every flower becomes a soft lantern with a petal filter: dark outside, burning within.
LC0520.whereItWorks: Above a table, in a bedroom, in a private living room; in large spaces it gathers into whole flowerbeds. The dark outer side asks for a pale background so the silhouette can read.
LC0520.style: Dark luxe and natural Art Nouveau: the chrysanthemum in a graphite register. The message is intimate and evening-bound — a piece for an interior with a mood.
LC0520.madeToOrder: The number of flower heads, their calibres and the balance of graphite to white are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about foam and water. The matte tenderness of the opal rays and the cold shine of the chrome tail-spikes work as a pair: a soft body and a mirrored needle stitching the flight together.
The flock reassembles with every step the viewer takes — now a dense shoal, now sparse solitary silhouettes.

By day it is milky figures with a warm gradient inside and silver tails — a piece read through silhouette and soft transitions. In the evening the light inside the wings comes on evenly and calmly, without sharp highlights: the composition glows entire. The quietest of the brand's flying pieces.
LC0521.whereItWorks: Bedrooms, living rooms in a light register, spas, spaces beside water. Even light without glare is comfortable where people stay a while.
LC0521.style: Marine modern and Scandinavian minimalism: flight without shine. The message is calm — a piece for an interior that does not raise its voice.
LC0521.madeToOrder: The number of figures, the density of the flock and the balance of white to chrome are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a dive. A wing with a bubbled mass flows into a long gold tail-spike — the form of a swallow at the moment it folds its wings and drops.
The composition is built on diagonals: the tails rule the space with swift lines. No element repeats the tilt of its neighbour — the flock is alive.

By day it is gold lines with clear wings: a piece read through diagonals and bubbles seen against the light, sharp and mobile. In the evening light from the gold body floods the wings from within — the flock flies glowing, and the tails remain dark strokes between the patches of light.
LC0522.whereItWorks: Spaces with movement — staircases, entrance halls, rooms with high ceilings, galleries. The direction of flight is set along the route from the entrance.
LC0522.style: Art Nouveau and contemporary sculpture: the swallow as a classic motif of speed. The message is dynamic — a piece for a space people move through.
LC0522.madeToOrder: The number of birds, the direction of flight and the spread of the flock are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition in two tempos. The strict architecture of rings — and the weightless, melting dust of rain around it: the piece is a draft drawing and a cloud at once.
Bands of polished gold curve into wide rings, faceted rods hang from them as a dense fringe, and from above the finest beads descend on hundreds of threads.

By day, close up, the precision of the contour and the faceting is visible; from a distance a radiant cloud: two scales of perception in one piece. In the evening light comes from the gold bands and floods the fringe from within, the facets burn warm, and the rain of beads catches the reflections and scatters them — the architecture dissolves into dust.
LC0523.whereItWorks: Formal spaces — an atrium, a lobby, a restaurant with a high ceiling, a banqueting hall. The rain of beads requires height: it is built downward from the rings.
LC0523.style: Art Deco and formal classicism: the ring and the pendant as a classic pairing. The message is a statement of status — a piece for a space that declares its level.
LC0523.madeToOrder: The diameters of the rings, the density of the fringe and the area of the rain are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about miniature tornadoes. Cones with pleated skirts read as inverted glasses or as the funnels of a whirlwind — a form in which everything converges to a point below.
The composition is monochrome and architectural for it: only transparency, steel and light. The pleating breaks the rays into hundreds of facets.

By day it is a strict triangular swarm: the faceted surface catches light on all its planes, and the piece reads through brilliance and rhythm. In the evening the light inside every funnel is driven along the folds and comes out as a silver radiance — the swarm shimmers like frosty air under a street lamp.
LC0524.whereItWorks: Above a long table, in a meeting room, in an entrance hall — wherever strict but living light is needed. The triangular swarm is calculated for the length of the zone.
LC0524.style: Contemporary minimalism and Art Deco: pleating instead of ornament. The message is strict — a piece for an interior that holds its form.
LC0524.madeToOrder: The number of funnels, their calibres and the format of the swarm are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a bouquet with no front. The flowers face in different directions and the cluster is equally beautiful from any position — this is how you gather a bouquet meant to stand in the middle of a room, not one arranged for a photograph.
Large glossy flowers with live crimped edges are threaded on gold rods into a dense vertical.

By day it is white gloss: the composition reads through the plasticity of the crimped edge and the volume of the blooms. In the evening the light fills the petals the way the sun fills a fine shell, and the cluster glows with a peach interior — the white turns warm.
LC0525.whereItWorks: Staircases, double-height spaces, corners that need a soft formal accent. The vertical format takes little floor area.
LC0525.style: Art Nouveau and romantic classicism: the hibiscus as a tropical motif. The message is dressy and warm — a piece for a light interior.
LC0525.madeToOrder: The number of flowers, the height of the cluster and the colour temperature of the light are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about the solid pretending to be silk. The plasticity is deliberately textile: folds, ruffles, softness — the ribs of the domes work as the spokes of a parasol, the frills of the tentacles as foam.
The layered cloud reassembles itself from every angle: now domes, now skirts, now glowing cores.

By day it is a dusty lilac mass with textile plasticity — a piece read through folds and soft colour. In the evening a warm peach light shows through the frills and paints the composition with a sunset gradient: lilac above passing into peach below, and the light quite literally embraces.
LC0526.whereItWorks: Bedrooms, boudoirs, window displays, boutiques, private living rooms. Soft warm light without glare suits zones where people rest.
LC0526.style: Romantic modern and Art Nouveau: drapery as a form. The message is tender and feminine — a piece for an interior with a soft palette.
LC0526.madeToOrder: The number of parasols, the degree of pink in the light and the scale of the cloud are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a slow pulse. Some domes are open, others contracted — the colony is shown in different phases of one movement, the very movement by which jellyfish swim.
Colour is the protagonist: a dense ultraviolet and inky blue, a matte velvet surface, full frills below with the light hidden in their folds.

By day it is a sculptural colony of matte domes: the deep blue-violet reads as volume, a dense and quiet piece. In the evening warm gold lights in the folds of the frills, and the colony turns into a deep-sea garden glowing from under its skirts — darkness above, light below.
LC0527.whereItWorks: Interiors that are not afraid of the dark — a lounge, a bar, a bedroom with character, a private study. Against a pale ground the deep colour loses its drama.
LC0527.style: Dark luxe and marine modern: ultraviolet as a palette. The message is intimate and evening-bound — a piece for an interior with a mood.
LC0527.madeToOrder: The number of jellyfish, the shade and the density of the colony are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition as a scene. One piece contains a whole underwater episode: a ribbed dome the colour of a sea wave, clear tentacles arrested like jets, and a shoal of silver fish scattering from the centre. Not an object but a moment.
The light is built into the dome itself: it descends the tentacles.

By day it is a turquoise dome with a clear fringe and mirrored flashes around it — a piece read through colour and the composition of the scene. In the evening the turquoise lights up as a lagoon, the tentacles carry the light downward, and the fish flare with reflected highlights: the scene comes alive entire.
LC0528.whereItWorks: Children's rooms, bathrooms, poolside zones, spas. It works solo as an art object or in a group at differing heights — like a bloom of jellyfish in the body of the water.
LC0528.style: Marine modern and narrative sculpture: the underwater world kept from the literal. The message is playful and alive — a piece for a space that tells a story.
LC0528.madeToOrder: The size of the dome, the length of the tentacles and the number of fish are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about germination. Out of a faceted cocoon shoots break upward — twisted, with the texture of a stem just watered; around them, on invisible threads, clear bubbles rise, air released by the root. The moment when a seed stops being a seed.
The cocoon is dense and radiant, like a druse: something that opened rather than something that was opened.

By day it is green shoots above a faceted core with a scattering of bubbles — a piece read through the vertical and the colour, fresh and alive. In the evening light from the cocoon floods the shoots from below and the green catches fire — spring-like, almost edible — while the bubbles catch the highlights and dissolve the composition into the space.
LC0529.whereItWorks: Staircases, double-height halls, full-wall niches, winter gardens. The vertical story requires height: the shoot has to have room to stretch.
LC0529.style: Bio-design and Art Nouveau: germination as subject. The message is fresh and optimistic — a piece for an interior that loves life.
LC0529.madeToOrder: The height of the shoots, the size of the cocoon and the density of the bubbles are all made to order.

paragraphs: A composition about a creature that answers the air. Long trains of tentacles — fine threads strung with pearl beads of differing calibre — respond to any movement of air: the object lives even when there is nobody in the room.

The domes with their soft iridescent cast look as though they had only just risen from the deep. The composition is assembled as a shoal: two or three jellyfish at differing heights above a bedside zone, a family of domes above a staircase.

By day it is white with mother-of-pearl — a quiet, almost monochrome piece read through the plasticity of the domes and the rhythm of the beads. In the evening a warm light comes on inside the domes and the pearls shimmer along the whole length of the trains: the jellyfish glows not itself but through what it draws behind it.
LC0530.whereItWorks: Bedrooms, bathrooms, spa areas, children's rooms, spaces beside water. The trains set the lower boundary and need somewhere they will not be brushed against.
LC0530.style: Marine modern and romantic classicism: pearl and iridescence as a palette. The message is tender and quiet — a piece for a private space.
LC0530.madeToOrder: The number of jellyfish, the length of the trains and the density of the beads are all made to order.
